units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 16
units.deva:
समवायकृतं तच्चेन्न भेदस्यापरिच्युतेः । न तावद्द्वे वस्तुनी सामान्यविशेषौ, प्रख्याभेदात् । समानाधिकरणत्वेन हीमे प्रख्ये जायेते ‘सन् घटः, गौः स्वस्तिमतीऽ; इति । न व्यधिकरणत्वेन यथा नीलपीतप्रख्ये, यथा वा ‘दण्डो देवदत्तःऽ; इति । नापि विशेषणविशेष्यभावेन यथा ‘दण्डीऽइति, संबन्धस्याप्रतिभासनात् । न च वस्तुभेदविषयत्वे सामानाधिकरण्यमवकल्पते सत्यपि संबन्धे । संबन्धिद्वयं विशेषणविशेष्यत्वेन द्वाभ्यामेकया वा बुद्ध्या गृह्यते, न तु परस्परात्मत्वेन । परस्परात्मत्वेन चेह प्रतिपत्तिः प्रत्यात्मवेदनीया । विप्रतिपत्तेश्च सामान्यविशेषयोर् [क्क्स्_61] भेदे । नान्यथा विप्रतिपद्येरन् । सामान्यप्रत्यक्षे च विशेषप्रत्यक्षाभिमानात् । अन्यथा धूमदृष्टाविवाग्नौ परोक्षाभिमानः स्यात् । स्यादेतत् --- न संबन्धमात्राद्भेदप्रतिपत्तिः, अपि तु संबन्धविशेषात्समवायात् । स हि वस्तुसंश्लेषात्मकः । तन्न, समवाये ऽपि ताभ्यां रूपभेदस्यानपायात्, अन्यथा भेदाभावादसंबन्धात् । तथा च नैकात्म्येन प्रख्या युज्यते । अस्ति चेयम् । अतस्तया विरुद्धः प्रख्याभेदो न वस्तुभेदव्यवस्थायै प्रभवति । स्वयं वा व्याहतत्वात्, एकाधिकरणत्वेनोत्पत्तेः (एकाधिकरणत्वेनोपपत्तेः एदितिओन्) । ननु भेदे ऽपि परस्परात्मत्वेन प्रतिपत्तेर्निमित्तं समवायः । तस्य खल्वेष सामर्थ्यातिशयः, येन भेदवतामर्थानां भेदं तिरोदधाति । तथा च ते ऽभेदेन प्रकाशन्ते । अत्रोच्यते ---
भेदान्तर्धानसामर्थ्यं तस्य भेदे ऽपि चेन्मतम्
units.iast:
samavāyakṛtaṃ taccenna bhedasyāparicyuteḥ /
na tāvaddve vastunī sāmānyaviśeṣau, prakhyābhedāt / samānādhikaraṇatvena hīme prakhye jāyete ‘san ghaṭaḥ, gauḥ svastimatī'; iti / na vyadhikaraṇatvena yathā nīlapītaprakhye, yathā vā ‘daṇḍo devadattaḥ'; iti / nāpi viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvena yathā ‘daṇḍī'iti, saṃbandhasyāpratibhāsanāt / na ca vastubhedaviṣayatve sāmānādhikaraṇyamavakalpate satyapi saṃbandhe / saṃbandhidvayaṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyatvena dvābhyāmekayā vā buddhyā gṛhyate, na tu parasparātmatvena / parasparātmatvena ceha pratipattiḥ pratyātmavedanīyā / vipratipatteśca sāmānyaviśeṣayor [kks_61] bhede / nānyathā vipratipadyeran / sāmānyapratyakṣe ca viśeṣapratyakṣābhimānāt / anyathā dhūmadṛṣṭāvivāgnau parokṣābhimānaḥ syāt / syādetat --- na saṃbandhamātrādbhedapratipattiḥ, api tu saṃbandhaviśeṣātsamavāyāt / sa hi vastusaṃśleṣātmakaḥ / tanna, samavāye 'pi tābhyāṃ rūpabhedasyānapāyāt, anyathā bhedābhāvādasaṃbandhāt / tathā ca naikātmyena prakhyā yujyate / asti ceyam / atastayā viruddhaḥ prakhyābhedo na vastubhedavyavasthāyai prabhavati / svayaṃ vā vyāhatatvāt, ekādhikaraṇatvenotpatteḥ (ekādhikaraṇatvenopapatteḥ edition) /

nanu bhede 'pi parasparātmatvena pratipatternimittaṃ samavāyaḥ / tasya khalveṣa sāmarthyātiśayaḥ, yena bhedavatāmarthānāṃ bhedaṃ tirodadhāti / tathā ca te 'bhedena prakāśante / atrocyate ---
bhedāntardhānasāmarthyaṃ tasya bhede 'pi cenmatam
units.translation:
If this non-difference is produced by inherence, difference has not disappeared. General and particular features are not two separate objects, because their appearance is not different. They appear in the same grammatical locus, as in “the pot is existent” and “the cow is fortunate,” not in different loci as blue and yellow do, or as in “the staff is Devadatta.” Nor are they related as qualifier and qualified, as in “the staff-bearer,” because no relation is perceived. Even when a relation exists, a shared grammatical locus is not possible if the cognition concerns distinct objects. Two related things are apprehended as qualifier and qualified, by two cognitions or by one, but not as identical with each other. Here, by contrast, they are apprehended as identical with one another, as each person can directly know. And people disagree about whether the general and particular are different; they would not disagree otherwise. When the general feature is directly perceived, one supposes that the particular is directly perceived too. Otherwise, as with fire inferred from smoke, one would suppose that it was indirectly known.

One might object: the apprehension of non-difference does not arise merely from a relation, but from the particular relation of inherence, which is a joining of things. No: even in inherence, their difference of form does not disappear. If it did, there would be no difference and hence no relation between them. Thus they cannot properly appear as one. Yet they do appear that way; therefore this appearance of non-difference, which contradicts difference, cannot establish that the objects are different. Or else it contradicts itself, since it arises in one locus.

One might say that inherence is what makes different things be apprehended as identical; that is its special power, by which it conceals the difference between things that are in fact distinct. Thus they shine forth as non-different. The reply is:

“If it is held that inherence has the power to conceal difference even when difference is present…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 17
units.deva:
हन्तैकस्यैव तत्किं न यदेवमवभासते । समवायसामर्थ्याच्चेद्भेदवतोरभेदवतोरभेदावभासः, हन्तैकस्यैव वस्तुनः सामर्थ्यविशेषान्नानावभासो ऽभ्युपेयताम् । व्यर्था वस्तुभेदकल्पना । न ह्यस्ति विशेषः --- यतो भिन्नयोरभेदप्रकाशसंभवः, नैकस्य नानावभाससंभव इति । ननु ज्वलनायोगुडादिषु दृष्टमेवंविधं संसर्गस्य सामर्थ्यम् । तत्र दर्शनात्संभवी संसर्गाद्भेदवत्स्वभेदावभासः । नैकस्मिन्नानावभासः, अदर्शनात् । उच्यते ---
दृष्टः संसर्गधर्मो ऽयं यद्येकमपि वै तथा
units.iast:
hantaikasyaiva tatkiṃ na yadevamavabhāsate /
samavāyasāmarthyāccedbhedavatorabhedavatorabhedāvabhāsaḥ, hantaikasyaiva vastunaḥ sāmarthyaviśeṣānnānāvabhāso 'bhyupeyatām / vyarthā vastubhedakalpanā / na hyasti viśeṣaḥ --- yato bhinnayorabhedaprakāśasaṃbhavaḥ, naikasya nānāvabhāsasaṃbhava iti /

nanu jvalanāyoguḍādiṣu dṛṣṭamevaṃvidhaṃ saṃsargasya sāmarthyam / tatra darśanātsaṃbhavī saṃsargādbhedavatsvabhedāvabhāsaḥ / naikasminnānāvabhāsaḥ, adarśanāt / ucyate ---
dṛṣṭaḥ saṃsargadharmo 'yaṃ yadyekamapi vai tathā
units.translation:
Then why should one not accept that a single thing appears in just this way? If the power of inherence makes distinct things appear non-different, why not accept that the special power of a single object makes it appear as many? The imagined difference between objects would then be pointless. There is no reason to think that different things can appear as non-different through a special power of inherence, while one thing cannot appear as many.

Someone may object that this kind of power in association is observed in fire and balls of iron: since it is observed there, it is possible for things that are different to appear non-different through association. But there is no observation of many appearances in a single thing. We reply:

“If a property of association is observed in this way even when there is one thing…”

gloss.en: because of the power of inherence
the possibility of appearing as many
in fire and heated iron balls and the like

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 18
units.deva:
नानावभासते चित्रं रूपमेकं तथा मतिः । दृष्टं खल्वेकमपि विविधावभासम्, यथा चित्रं रूपम् । तद्धि खलु न नीलादिसमाहारमात्रम् । तेषामवयवसमवाये रूपान्तरानभ्युपगमे चावयविनो नीरूपत्वप्रसङ्गात् । न च नीरूपत्वमेवावयविनः । रूपसंस्काराभावे हि न स चाक्षुषः स्यात् । न च रूपिसमवायात्संख्याकर्मादिवच्चाक्षुषत्वम् । एवं ह्युक्तम् --- ‘महत्यनेकद्रव्यसमवायाद्रूपाच्चोपलब्धिःऽ; इति । सर्वश्चेत्थमवयवी नीरूपः स्यात् । अथ नारूपः प्रतीयत इति नायं प्रसङ्गः, [क्क्स्_62] चित्रो ऽपि तथेति नारूपः । तच्चास्य रूपं नीलपीतादिनिर्भासः । तथा नगरत्रैलोक्यादिबुद्धयो विविधविषयाकारा निर्भासन्ते भेदाभावे ऽपीति विषयाकारज्ञानवादिनो मन्यन्ते । न चैकबुद्धितत्त्वाव्यतिरेकाद्विषयाकाराः परस्परतो ऽपि व्यावर्तन्ते, प्रागेव बुद्धेः । स्यादेतत् --- चित्रमपि रूपं संसर्गादेवैकार्थसमवेतसमवायलक्षणात्तथावभासते । तदसत् । यतः ---
न च संबन्धिसंबन्धः संसर्गो व्यवधानतः
units.iast:
nānāvabhāsate citraṃ rūpamekaṃ tathā matiḥ /
dṛṣṭaṃ khalvekamapi vividhāvabhāsam, yathā citraṃ rūpam / taddhi khalu na nīlādisamāhāramātram / teṣāmavayavasamavāye rūpāntarānabhyupagame cāvayavino nīrūpatvaprasaṅgāt / na ca nīrūpatvamevāvayavinaḥ / rūpasaṃskārābhāve hi na sa cākṣuṣaḥ syāt / na ca rūpisamavāyātsaṃkhyākarmādivaccākṣuṣatvam / evaṃ hyuktam --- ‘mahatyanekadravyasamavāyādrūpāccopalabdhiḥ'; iti / sarvaścetthamavayavī nīrūpaḥ syāt / atha nārūpaḥ pratīyata iti nāyaṃ prasaṅgaḥ, [kks_62] citro 'pi tatheti nārūpaḥ / taccāsya rūpaṃ nīlapītādinirbhāsaḥ /

tathā nagaratrailokyādibuddhayo vividhaviṣayākārā nirbhāsante bhedābhāve 'pīti viṣayākārajñānavādino manyante / na caikabuddhitattvāvyatirekādviṣayākārāḥ parasparato 'pi vyāvartante, prāgeva buddheḥ / syādetat --- citramapi rūpaṃ saṃsargādevaikārthasamavetasamavāyalakṣaṇāttathāvabhāsate / tadasat / yataḥ ---
na ca saṃbandhisaṃbandhaḥ saṃsargo vyavadhānataḥ
units.translation:
One cognition can present a single, variegated form in many ways, just as a painting does. A painting is not merely a collection of blue and other colored parts: if colors inhered only in its parts and no form of the whole were admitted, the whole would have no color. Yet the whole is not colorless, for then it could not be seen. Nor is its visibility due simply to inherence in colored things, as number and motion are visible; it has been said that perception arises from magnitude, inherence in many substances, and color. On that account every whole would be colorless. If one says that it does not appear colorless and so this consequence does not follow, the same is true of a painting: it is not colorless. Its color is what appears as blue, yellow, and the like.

Likewise, cognitions of a city, the three worlds, and so on appear with the forms of diverse objects, even though there is no difference in the object; so think those who hold that cognition takes the form of its object. Since the forms of objects are not different from the one reality of cognition, they do not differ from one another, much less from cognition itself.

One might object that the painting appears as it does because of a relation: the relation of inherence of something inhering in something that itself inheres in one object. That is unsound, because—

“An association that involves a relation between relations cannot be the connection, since it is interrupted…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 19
units.deva:
संश्लेषो हि संसर्गः । ततश्च परस्पररूपावभासः । स चाव्यवधाने युज्यते । न तु स्वाश्रयाभ्यां व्यवधाने । अवयवावयविरूपयोरेकव्यवधाने ऽप्यसंश्लेषः, किमु द्वयव्यवधाने । किं च

व्यवहारे परोपाधौ सर्वा धीर्व्यावहारिकी । अयथार्था यदा भावभेदकल्पस्तदा मुधा
units.iast:
saṃśleṣo hi saṃsargaḥ / tataśca paraspararūpāvabhāsaḥ / sa cāvyavadhāne yujyate / na tu svāśrayābhyāṃ vyavadhāne / avayavāvayavirūpayorekavyavadhāne 'pyasaṃśleṣaḥ, kimu dvayavyavadhāne /

kiṃ ca

vyavahāre paropādhau sarvā dhīrvyāvahārikī /
ayathārthā yadā bhāvabhedakalpastadā mudhā
units.translation:
Association is a joining, and from that follows an appearance of reciprocal forms. It is possible when there is no intervening thing, but not when the two objects are separated from their own supports by something between them. Even the form of a part and the form of a whole are not joined when one thing intervenes; how much less when there are two intervening things? Moreover—

“When, in ordinary usage, every cognition depends on an external condition, all practical cognition is inaccurate. If one imagines differences among things, then such usage is pointless.”

gloss.en: between the form of a part and the form of a whole
a difference among things is imagined

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 20
units.deva:
यस्य खलु ‘शुक्लो गौःऽ; इत्यादिबुद्धयो व्यवहाराङ्गभूता द्रव्येषु गुणजात्युपाधिनिबन्धनाः तस्यैता न यथावस्तु, जातिगुणद्रव्याणामन्योन्यमर्थान्तरत्वात् । तथा च न वस्तुनिबन्धनो व्यवहारः, बुद्ध्यानुपदर्शितस्याव्यवहाराङ्गवाद्बुद्ध्युपदर्शितस्य च तथाभावात् । एवं च प्रत्ययविरचितेनैवायमर्थेन व्यावृत्तो व्यवहारो ऽनुवृत्तश्चेति व्यर्था वस्तुभेदकल्पना, कल्पितस्यापि तस्य व्यवहारे ऽनुपयोगादितरस्य चोपयोगात् । यथार्थत्वाय हि व्यावहारिकीणां बुद्धीनां वस्तुभेदः कल्प्यते । कल्पिते च तस्मिन् परोपाधित्वात्तासां नायथार्थत्वपरिहारः । स्यादेतत् --- असति वस्तुभेदे ऽयथार्थमप्यनुवृत्तव्यावृत्तावग्रहं व्यावहारिकं विज्ञानं नोदेतुमर्हति, बीजाभावात् । न खलु स्थाणुशकलादिषु पुरुषरजतादिविभ्रान्तयो निर्बीजाः, सामान्यनिबन्धनत्वात् । उच्यते ---

अयथार्थधियो बीजमवश्यं बाह्यमेव न । दृष्टस्तिमिरकामादिरान्तरो ऽपि ह्युपप्लवः
units.iast:
yasya khalu ‘śuklo gauḥ'; ityādibuddhayo vyavahārāṅgabhūtā dravyeṣu guṇajātyupādhinibandhanāḥ tasyaitā na yathāvastu, jātiguṇadravyāṇāmanyonyamarthāntaratvāt / tathā ca na vastunibandhano vyavahāraḥ, buddhyānupadarśitasyāvyavahārāṅgavādbuddhyupadarśitasya ca tathābhāvāt / evaṃ ca pratyayaviracitenaivāyamarthena vyāvṛtto vyavahāro 'nuvṛttaśceti vyarthā vastubhedakalpanā, kalpitasyāpi tasya vyavahāre 'nupayogāditarasya copayogāt / yathārthatvāya hi vyāvahārikīṇāṃ buddhīnāṃ vastubhedaḥ kalpyate / kalpite ca tasmin paropādhitvāttāsāṃ nāyathārthatvaparihāraḥ /

syādetat --- asati vastubhede 'yathārthamapyanuvṛttavyāvṛttāvagrahaṃ vyāvahārikaṃ vijñānaṃ nodetumarhati, bījābhāvāt / na khalu sthāṇuśakalādiṣu puruṣarajatādivibhrāntayo nirbījāḥ, sāmānyanibandhanatvāt / ucyate ---

ayathārthadhiyo bījamavaśyaṃ bāhyameva na /
dṛṣṭastimirakāmādirāntaro 'pi hyupaplavaḥ
units.translation:
For someone who holds that cognitions such as “the cow is white,” which are part of ordinary usage, depend on substances being qualified by qualities and universal kinds, those cognitions do not correspond to things as they are, since a universal, a quality, and a substance are distinct things. Thus ordinary usage is not based on the object itself: what cognition does not present cannot contribute to ordinary usage, while what it does present can.

In that case, since usage both distinguishes and connects things through objects constructed by cognition, the imagined difference between real things is pointless. Even if such difference is imagined, it contributes nothing to ordinary usage, while the other, cognition-constructed difference does. A difference among real things is imagined in order to make practical cognitions truthful. But once that difference is imagined, it is an additional condition imposed upon those cognitions, and it does not remove their inaccuracy. Someone may object that without differences among real things, practical cognition—although it apprehends both continuity and distinction inaccurately—could not arise, since it would have no basis. Illusions such as mistaking a tree stump for a person or mother-of-pearl for silver do not arise without a basis; they depend on a general feature. We reply:

“The basis of inaccurate cognition need not always be external; inner disturbances such as eye disease and desire are also observed.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 21
units.deva:
[क्क्स्_63] न विषयदोषादेव सादृश्यादेरयथार्थज्ञानम्, आध्यात्मिकेभ्यो ऽपि तु दोषेभ्यस्तिमिरकामशोकादिभ्यः । तत्रासति वस्तुभेद आध्यात्मिको दोषो ऽविद्यालक्षणो व्यावहारिकज्ञानबीजमिति नार्थो वस्तुभेदेन । अस्तु तर्ह्येकं द्व्यात्मकम् । एवं हि परस्परात्मप्रतिपत्तिश्च सामान्यविशेषयोः कल्पते । वस्तुविपरीतश्च नार्थसामर्थ्यातिशयः कल्पयितव्यः । वस्तुनिबन्धनो व्यवहारः, न व्यावहारिकज्ञानानामयथार्था वृत्तिः । स्यादेतत् --- एकस्य द्व्यात्मकता विरोधवती । एकं च द्व्यात्मकं चेति विप्रतिषिद्धम् । अपि च सामान्यं भेदान्तरानुयायि । ततो व्यावृत्तस्वभावो भेदः । तयोरेकत्वं हि विरोधादशक्यावहम् । नैतत्सारम् । विरुद्धमिति नः क्व संप्रत्ययः? यत्प्रमाणविपर्ययेण वर्तते । यत्तु यथा प्रमाणेनावगम्यते तस्य तथाभावे विरुद्धत्वाभिधाने कं बतायमाश्रित्य हेतुं विरुद्धत्वाविरुद्धत्वे व्यवस्थापयेत्? प्रमाणं चैकस्य सामान्यविशेषात्मकतामवगमयति, व्यावृत्त्यनुवृत्तिभ्यां प्रख्यारूपभेदात्सामानाधिकरण्यावगमाच्च (ऐकाधिकरण्यावगमाच्च एदितिओन्) । तदिदमसांप्रतम्, यतो नेदृशां विप्रतिषिद्धार्थज्ञानानां प्रामाण्यमेव युज्यते संशयज्ञानवत् । अन्यथा संशयविषयो ऽपि द्व्यात्मा स्यात्, द्व्याभासत्वात्तस्य सामानाधिकरण्याच्च तदवभासयोः । अथ मतम् --- न संशयिते रूपसमुच्चयावगमः, यथा सामान्यविशेषवति, ‘अयं वा, अयं वाऽइति प्रतीतेः । मा भूत्समुच्चयः, विकल्पः स्यात् । सो ऽपि न, वस्तुनो विकल्पानुपपत्तेः । एकमपि तर्हि न द्व्यात्मकम्, एकस्य द्व्यात्मकताविरोधात् । तत्र यथा संशयज्ञानं विप्रतिषेधादप्रमाणं तथा सामान्यविशेषप्रतिपत्तिरपि, ऐकाधिकरण्यात् । स्यादेतत् --- न संशयज्ञानं विप्रतिषेधादप्रमाणम्, निर्णयज्ञानेन तु बाधनात् । यत्र तर्हि न निर्णयस्तत्र विकल्पात्मता स्यात् । अपि च यथा बाधायामेकस्याप्रामाण्यं निराकरणात्, एवं विरोधे ऽपि द्वयोरेकस्य वा ज्ञानस्य विरुद्धरूपोपग्रहे तद्रूपाधिगत्योरन्योन्यनिराकरणात् । तत्रैकनिराकरणे [क्क्स्_64] इतरस्मान्निश्चयः । परस्परनिराकृतौ तुल्यबलत्वे सन्देह इति न संशयज्ञानादेकस्य सामान्यविशेषप्रतिपत्तिर्विशिष्यते । तस्मादिहानैकान्तिकं वस्त्वित्येवं ज्ञानं सुनिश्चितमिति स्वपक्षोपवर्णनम् । अपि च

एकत्वमविरोधेन भेदसामान्ययोर्यदि । न द्व्यात्मता भवेदेकतरनिर्भक्तभागवत्
units.iast:
[kks_63] na viṣayadoṣādeva sādṛśyāderayathārthajñānam, ādhyātmikebhyo 'pi tu doṣebhyastimirakāmaśokādibhyaḥ / tatrāsati vastubheda ādhyātmiko doṣo 'vidyālakṣaṇo vyāvahārikajñānabījamiti nārtho vastubhedena /

astu tarhyekaṃ dvyātmakam / evaṃ hi parasparātmapratipattiśca sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ kalpate / vastuviparītaśca nārthasāmarthyātiśayaḥ kalpayitavyaḥ / vastunibandhano vyavahāraḥ, na vyāvahārikajñānānāmayathārthā vṛttiḥ / syādetat --- ekasya dvyātmakatā virodhavatī / ekaṃ ca dvyātmakaṃ ceti vipratiṣiddham / api ca sāmānyaṃ bhedāntarānuyāyi / tato vyāvṛttasvabhāvo bhedaḥ / tayorekatvaṃ hi virodhādaśakyāvaham / naitatsāram / viruddhamiti naḥ kva saṃpratyayaḥ? yatpramāṇaviparyayeṇa vartate / yattu yathā pramāṇenāvagamyate tasya tathābhāve viruddhatvābhidhāne kaṃ batāyamāśritya hetuṃ viruddhatvāviruddhatve vyavasthāpayet? pramāṇaṃ caikasya sāmānyaviśeṣātmakatāmavagamayati, vyāvṛttyanuvṛttibhyāṃ prakhyārūpabhedātsāmānādhikaraṇyāvagamācca (aikādhikaraṇyāvagamācca edition) / tadidamasāṃpratam, yato nedṛśāṃ vipratiṣiddhārthajñānānāṃ prāmāṇyameva yujyate saṃśayajñānavat / anyathā saṃśayaviṣayo 'pi dvyātmā syāt, dvyābhāsatvāttasya sāmānādhikaraṇyācca tadavabhāsayoḥ /

atha matam --- na saṃśayite rūpasamuccayāvagamaḥ, yathā sāmānyaviśeṣavati, ‘ayaṃ vā, ayaṃ vā'iti pratīteḥ / mā bhūtsamuccayaḥ, vikalpaḥ syāt / so 'pi na, vastuno vikalpānupapatteḥ / ekamapi tarhi na dvyātmakam, ekasya dvyātmakatāvirodhāt / tatra yathā saṃśayajñānaṃ vipratiṣedhādapramāṇaṃ tathā sāmānyaviśeṣapratipattirapi, aikādhikaraṇyāt /

syādetat --- na saṃśayajñānaṃ vipratiṣedhādapramāṇam, nirṇayajñānena tu bādhanāt / yatra tarhi na nirṇayastatra vikalpātmatā syāt / api ca yathā bādhāyāmekasyāprāmāṇyaṃ nirākaraṇāt, evaṃ virodhe 'pi dvayorekasya vā jñānasya viruddharūpopagrahe tadrūpādhigatyoranyonyanirākaraṇāt / tatraikanirākaraṇe [kks_64] itarasmānniścayaḥ / parasparanirākṛtau tulyabalatve sandeha iti na saṃśayajñānādekasya sāmānyaviśeṣapratipattirviśiṣyate / tasmādihānaikāntikaṃ vastvityevaṃ jñānaṃ suniścitamiti svapakṣopavarṇanam /

api ca

ekatvamavirodhena bhedasāmānyayoryadi /
na dvyātmatā bhavedekataranirbhaktabhāgavat
units.translation:
Error arising from similarity and the like is not due only to defects in the external object; it also arises from internal defects such as cataracts, desire, sorrow, and the like. If there is no real difference between objects, then an internal defect in the form of ignorance is the seed of practical cognition; no difference among objects themselves is needed. Let one thing, then, have two aspects. In this way it is possible for the universal and particular to be understood in relation to one another. There is no need to imagine a power that is contrary to the nature of the object. Practical dealings are grounded in objects, not in incorrect modes of practical cognition.

Someone may object that one thing having two aspects is contradictory: “one” and “having two aspects” are incompatible. Moreover, a universal follows many distinct things, while a particular has the nature of exclusion; because the two conflict, they cannot be one. That is not sound. What is the criterion by which we decide that something conflicts? It is that it goes against a means of knowledge. But if something is as it is understood by a means of knowledge, what could anyone rely on to determine that it is contradictory or not? A means of knowledge establishes that one thing has the nature of both universal and particular through its different appearances as continuity and distinction, and through their being understood in one locus.

This is not acceptable, since cognitions of things with mutually contradictory meanings cannot themselves be valid, just like cognition in doubt. Otherwise the object of doubt would also have two natures, because both appearances occur in one locus. Someone may say that a doubt does not grasp a combination of forms in one object, as it does for a universal and particular; its form is “this or that.” Let there be no combination; then there is only an alternative. But that too is impossible, since an object cannot itself be an alternative. Then nothing is two-aspected, since there is a contradiction in one thing having two natures. Thus, just as cognition in doubt is invalid because its forms conflict, cognition of a universal and particular is invalid for the same reason, since it assigns both to one object.

Someone may reply that cognition in doubt is not invalid because of contradiction; it is invalid only because a later decisive cognition sublates it. In that case, where there is no decisive cognition, it would be an alternative cognition. Moreover, just as one cognition is invalid when it is sublated by another, so in a contradiction one or both cognitions that grasp incompatible forms are invalid, since each cancels the other. If one is cancelled, certainty follows from the other; if both are cancelled and have equal force, there is doubt. Thus the cognition of a universal and particular in one object does not differ from cognition in doubt.

Therefore, the claim that an object is both one and two-aspected is inconclusive; this is how their position should be described. And:

“If unity of universal and particular is possible without contradiction,
then the one does not have a twofold nature, like a part from which one aspect is separated.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 22
units.deva:
अवश्यमनेन पदार्थानां भेदाभेदौ व्यवस्थापयता --- यथा तावत्सामान्यमभिन्नं विशेषा भिद्यन्त इति --- भेदाभेदयोर्लक्षणं वाच्यम् । तत्र रूपविरोधो ऽन्योन्याभावो भेदलक्षणम् । विपर्ययो ऽभेदलक्षणम् । रूपविरोधाद्ध्यन्योन्याभावपर्यायाद्विशेषा भिद्यन्ते । भिद्यमानेष्वपि तेषु सामान्यमभिन्नम्, विपर्ययात् । तत्र सामान्यविशेषयोर्यदि स्वरूपविरोधो ऽन्योन्याभावः, नैकत्वं भेदानामिव परस्परम् । अथ सामान्यविशेषबुद्ध्येरैकाधिकरण्येनोत्पत्तेः स्वरूपविरोधो ऽभ्युपेयते, न तर्ह्येकं द्व्यात्मकम् । सामान्यविशेषयोः स्वरूपविरोधाभावादसति भेदे द्वित्वानुपपत्तेः । यथा न सामान्यांशो द्विरूपो विशेषांशो वा रूपविरोधाभावात् --- तत्रैकस्मिन्निर्भक्ते द्वित्वाभावात् --- तथा सामान्यविशेषयोरपि सामानाधिकरण्यबुद्धेर्यदि न रूपविरोधः, न परस्परात्माभावः (म्स् ब्; परस्पराभावः एदितिओन्) । द्वित्वं न युज्यते । अथ रूपविरोधः, नैकत्वमिति । यदि मतम् --- न स्वरूपविरोधान्नानात्वम्, तदभावाच्चैकत्वम्, येन सामान्यविशेषयोः स्वरूपविरोधाभावाद्द्वित्वं न स्यादन्यतरस्येव भागस्य । किं तु बुद्धे रूपभेदाभेदाभ्याम् । सामान्यविशेषयोश्च परस्परात्मत्वेन प्रतिपत्तेरसत्यप्यन्योन्याभावलक्षणे स्वरूपविरोधे बुद्धे रूपभेदाद्द्वित्वम् । अंशे तु रूपाभेदादेकत्वम् । अतो वस्तुनो द्विरूपबुद्धिग्राह्यत्वाद् द्व्यात्मतेति । तत्रोच्यते ---

ऐकात्म्यबुद्धेर्भागे चेदेवं वस्तुनि तर्ह्यसौ । न चेत्कुतस्त्यमेकत्वमस्ति चेद् द्व्यात्मता कथम्
units.iast:
avaśyamanena padārthānāṃ bhedābhedau vyavasthāpayatā --- yathā tāvatsāmānyamabhinnaṃ viśeṣā bhidyanta iti --- bhedābhedayorlakṣaṇaṃ vācyam / tatra rūpavirodho 'nyonyābhāvo bhedalakṣaṇam / viparyayo 'bhedalakṣaṇam / rūpavirodhāddhyanyonyābhāvaparyāyādviśeṣā bhidyante / bhidyamāneṣvapi teṣu sāmānyamabhinnam, viparyayāt / tatra sāmānyaviśeṣayoryadi svarūpavirodho 'nyonyābhāvaḥ, naikatvaṃ bhedānāmiva parasparam / atha sāmānyaviśeṣabuddhyeraikādhikaraṇyenotpatteḥ svarūpavirodho 'bhyupeyate, na tarhyekaṃ dvyātmakam / sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ svarūpavirodhābhāvādasati bhede dvitvānupapatteḥ / yathā na sāmānyāṃśo dvirūpo viśeṣāṃśo vā rūpavirodhābhāvāt --- tatraikasminnirbhakte dvitvābhāvāt --- tathā sāmānyaviśeṣayorapi sāmānādhikaraṇyabuddheryadi na rūpavirodhaḥ, na parasparātmābhāvaḥ (ms b; parasparābhāvaḥ edition) / dvitvaṃ na yujyate / atha rūpavirodhaḥ, naikatvamiti /

yadi matam --- na svarūpavirodhānnānātvam, tadabhāvāccaikatvam, yena sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ svarūpavirodhābhāvāddvitvaṃ na syādanyatarasyeva bhāgasya / kiṃ tu buddhe rūpabhedābhedābhyām / sāmānyaviśeṣayośca parasparātmatvena pratipatterasatyapyanyonyābhāvalakṣaṇe svarūpavirodhe buddhe rūpabhedāddvitvam / aṃśe tu rūpābhedādekatvam / ato vastuno dvirūpabuddhigrāhyatvād dvyātmateti / tatrocyate ---

aikātmyabuddherbhāge cedevaṃ vastuni tarhyasau /
na cetkutastyamekatvamasti ced dvyātmatā katham
units.translation:
One who establishes that things are both different and non-different—saying, for example, that the general feature is non-different while particulars are different—must state the defining marks of difference and non-difference. A conflict of form, or mutual exclusion, defines difference; its opposite defines non-difference. Particulars are different because their forms conflict, which amounts to mutual exclusion; even though the particulars are different, the general feature is non-different from them, because the opposite holds.

If a conflict of nature, or mutual exclusion, is admitted between general and particular features, they cannot be one, just as distinct particulars are not mutually identical. But if their conflict of nature is explained by the cognition of the general and the particular arising in the same locus, they cannot then constitute one thing with two aspects. For there would be no conflict of nature between general and particular features; and without difference, their being two cannot be explained. Just as the general aspect alone is not double-form, nor the particular aspect alone, because there is no conflict of form within either one—and there are not two aspects within one undivided thing—so too, if the cognition of general and particular features in the same object involves no conflict of form, they do not exclude one another. Their being two would then be untenable. But if there is a conflict of form, they cannot be one.

Someone may object: multiplicity does not result from a conflict of nature, nor unity from its absence, which would otherwise make the general and particular features not two, just like one aspect. Rather, multiplicity and unity depend on whether cognition has different or identical forms. Since the general and particular are apprehended as identical with one another, they may be two despite the absence of mutual exclusion or conflict of nature: the cognition has two forms, while the parts themselves are one because their cognitive form is identical. Thus the object has two aspects because it is apprehended through a cognition with two forms.

We reply:

“If so, then when the object is apprehended as one in its aspect, that [unity] is present in the object. If not, where would the unity come from? And if it is present, how could the object have two aspects?”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 23
units.deva:
यदि तर्हि बुद्धेरेकरूपोपग्राहित्वादभेदों ऽशस्य, वस्तु विचार्यम् --- [क्क्स्_65] तत्रापि बुद्धिः किमेकरूपोपग्राहिणी न वेति । तत्र यदि नैकरूपोपग्राहिणी वस्तुनि बुद्धिः --- सामान्यविशेषात्मकं हि वस्तु --- तद्द्विरूपबुद्ध्युपग्राह्यम्, कथमेकत्वं वस्तुनः? बुद्धिरूपाभेदस्याभेदलक्षणस्याभावात्, रूपभेदस्य च भेदलक्षणस्य भावात् । अथैकरूपोपग्राहिण्येव वस्तुनि बुद्धिः, न द्व्यात्मकत्वमंशवदेव । अथ मतम् --- बुद्धिरूपभेदः परस्परात्माभावश्च (म्स्स् अब्; परस्परात्मताभावश्च -- एदितिओन्) भेदलक्षणम् । तत्र गवादयो भेदा भिन्नरूपबुद्ध्युपग्राह्याः परस्परानात्मानश्च, न तु सामान्यविशेषौ, बुद्धिरूपभेदे ऽपि परस्परात्मत्वेन प्रतिपत्तेः । एवमपि सामान्यविशेषयोर्भेदलक्षणेन विरहान्न द्व्यात्मता, अंशवदित्युक्तम् । यदि मन्येत --- बुद्धिरूपाभेदः (म्स् ब्; बुद्धेः रूपाभेदः -- एदितिओन्) परस्परात्मप्रतिपत्तिश्च द्वे अभेदलक्षणे । तत्रांशस्य रूपाभेदादेकत्वम्, उभयोस्तु परस्परात्मत्वप्रतीतेः । विशेषाणां तु न बुद्धे रूपाविभागः, न परस्परात्मप्रतिपत्तिरिति भिन्ना इति । एवमप्यभेदलक्षणे सति परस्परात्मप्रतिपत्तौ, उभयाभावे च भेदलक्षणे ऽविद्यमाने, न द्व्यात्मता । न चैकस्याभेदस्य द्वे लक्षणे युज्येते । लक्षणाभेदो ह्यभेदं व्यवस्थापयति, तद्भेदश्च भेदम् । लक्षणभेदे ऽपि चेत्तत्त्वम्, अन्यत्वं च लक्षणाभेदे ऽपि यदि, व्यर्थतैव लक्षणस्य स्यादिति । अपि च सामान्यविशेषयोरभेदे,

बुद्ध्यन्तरस्य वैयर्थ्यमेकांश इव चापतेत् । नानात्वादर्थवत्ता चेदेकत्वाद्व्यर्थता न किम्
units.iast:
yadi tarhi buddherekarūpopagrāhitvādabhedoṃ 'śasya, vastu vicāryam --- [kks_65] tatrāpi buddhiḥ kimekarūpopagrāhiṇī na veti / tatra yadi naikarūpopagrāhiṇī vastuni buddhiḥ --- sāmānyaviśeṣātmakaṃ hi vastu --- taddvirūpabuddhyupagrāhyam, kathamekatvaṃ vastunaḥ? buddhirūpābhedasyābhedalakṣaṇasyābhāvāt, rūpabhedasya ca bhedalakṣaṇasya bhāvāt / athaikarūpopagrāhiṇyeva vastuni buddhiḥ, na dvyātmakatvamaṃśavadeva / atha matam --- buddhirūpabhedaḥ parasparātmābhāvaśca (mss ab; parasparātmatābhāvaśca -- edition) bhedalakṣaṇam / tatra gavādayo bhedā bhinnarūpabuddhyupagrāhyāḥ parasparānātmānaśca, na tu sāmānyaviśeṣau, buddhirūpabhede 'pi parasparātmatvena pratipatteḥ / evamapi sāmānyaviśeṣayorbhedalakṣaṇena virahānna dvyātmatā, aṃśavadityuktam /

yadi manyeta --- buddhirūpābhedaḥ (ms b; buddheḥ rūpābhedaḥ -- edition) parasparātmapratipattiśca dve abhedalakṣaṇe / tatrāṃśasya rūpābhedādekatvam, ubhayostu parasparātmatvapratīteḥ / viśeṣāṇāṃ tu na buddhe rūpāvibhāgaḥ, na parasparātmapratipattiriti bhinnā iti / evamapyabhedalakṣaṇe sati parasparātmapratipattau, ubhayābhāve ca bhedalakṣaṇe 'vidyamāne, na dvyātmatā / na caikasyābhedasya dve lakṣaṇe yujyete / lakṣaṇābhedo hyabhedaṃ vyavasthāpayati, tadbhedaśca bhedam / lakṣaṇabhede 'pi cettattvam, anyatvaṃ ca lakṣaṇābhede 'pi yadi, vyarthataiva lakṣaṇasya syāditi /

api ca sāmānyaviśeṣayorabhede,

buddhyantarasya vaiyarthyamekāṃśa iva cāpatet /
nānātvādarthavattā cedekatvādvyarthatā na kim
units.translation:
If, then, the intellect grasps a single form, and this is what makes something non-different, the matter must be examined: does the intellect grasp a single form in the object or not? If it does not, the object is constituted by general and particular features, and is grasped by cognitions of two forms. How, then, is the object one? The defining mark of non-difference, identity of cognitive form, is absent, while the defining mark of difference, diversity of form, is present. If the intellect does grasp a single form in the object, then the object is not constituted by two aspects; there is only one aspect, as was said.

Someone may object: diversity in the forms of cognition and the absence of mutual identity define difference. Cows and other distinct things are grasped by cognitions with different forms and are not identical with one another; but the general and particular are not so, because even when the forms of cognition differ, they are apprehended as identical with one another. Even so, since general and particular features lack the defining mark of difference, they are not two aspects; as already explained, the object is not constituted by both.

Suppose one says that there are two marks of non-difference: identity in the form of cognition and apprehension of mutual identity. The aspect is one because its cognitive form is identical, and the two are also one because they are apprehended as identical with one another. Particulars, however, are different because they have neither an undivided cognitive form nor apprehension of mutual identity. Even so, when the marks of non-difference are present—apprehension of mutual identity—and the marks of difference are absent, there cannot be a dual constitution. Nor can a single kind of non-difference reasonably have two defining marks. A difference in defining marks establishes non-difference, while a difference in those marks establishes difference. If the truth of a thing held despite a difference in its defining mark, and its otherness held despite identity of that mark, then the mark would be pointless.

Moreover, if general and particular features are non-different, the need for a separate cognition would become pointless, just as if they were a single aspect. If one says that diversity makes cognition meaningful, why would unity not make it pointless?

units.deva:
बुद्ध्यन्तरप्रवृत्तिरेव सामान्यविशेषयोरेकवस्त्वात्मतामपाकरोति । सा हि नानात्मत्वे भेदेष्विवार्थवती, अनधिगताधिगमात् । एकत्वे तु यथा सामान्यविशेषविभागयोः स्वबुद्धिसमधिगतयोर्न विलक्षणं बुद्ध्यन्तरमर्थ्यते, तथा सामान्यबुद्धेर्न बुद्ध्यन्तरं विलक्षणं विशेषाधिगमाय प्रार्थ्येत । तथा विशेषबुद्धेर्न सामान्याधिगमाय । अथ नात्यन्तमव्यतिरेकः सामान्यविशेषयोः, व्यतिरेको ऽपि तु । तत्र व्यतिरेकादर्थवत्तेति । तदसत् । एवमपि कुत एतत् --- व्यतिरेकादर्थवत्त्वं भेदवत्, न पुनरव्यतिरेकादेकांशवद्वैयर्थ्यम्? [क्क्स्_66] तुल्ययोर्हि भेदाभेदयोः कुत एतत् --- भेदादेकया बुद्ध्या न ग्रहणम्, न पुनरभेदाद्ग्रहणमिति बुद्ध्यन्तरवैयर्थ्यम्? औत्सर्गिकश्च हेत्वभावे फलाभावः स्वभावसिद्धः । तस्य हेतुभावे फलभावो ऽपवादः । तत्राभेदे हेतुभावादेकयैव बुद्ध्योभयाधिगमो युक्तः । नैकत्वे ऽन्यतराधिगमहेतुर्नास्तीति शक्यं वक्तुम् । अथापि कथञ्चिन्नास्तीत्युच्येत । तथाप्यस्ति तावत्, एकत्वात् । तत्र हेतुभावात् फलभावः स्यात्, तस्य कारणत्वात् । न त्वभावो ऽभावस्य कारणम् । स्वभावसिद्धस्त्वभावः फलस्य । तस्य हेतुनिबन्धनः फलभावो निवर्तकः । स च हेतुरुभयत्रास्ति तावत् । असत्त्वं त्वनुपयोगम्, अकारणत्वादिति । अपि च

सामान्यं न हि वस्त्वात्मा न भेदश्चित्र एव सः । तस्यानन्वयतो भेदवादः शब्दान्तरादयम्
units.iast:
buddhyantarapravṛttireva sāmānyaviśeṣayorekavastvātmatāmapākaroti / sā hi nānātmatve bhedeṣvivārthavatī, anadhigatādhigamāt / ekatve tu yathā sāmānyaviśeṣavibhāgayoḥ svabuddhisamadhigatayorna vilakṣaṇaṃ buddhyantaramarthyate, tathā sāmānyabuddherna buddhyantaraṃ vilakṣaṇaṃ viśeṣādhigamāya prārthyeta / tathā viśeṣabuddherna sāmānyādhigamāya / atha nātyantamavyatirekaḥ sāmānyaviśeṣayoḥ, vyatireko 'pi tu / tatra vyatirekādarthavatteti / tadasat / evamapi kuta etat --- vyatirekādarthavattvaṃ bhedavat, na punaravyatirekādekāṃśavadvaiyarthyam? [kks_66] tulyayorhi bhedābhedayoḥ kuta etat --- bhedādekayā buddhyā na grahaṇam, na punarabhedādgrahaṇamiti buddhyantaravaiyarthyam? autsargikaśca hetvabhāve phalābhāvaḥ svabhāvasiddhaḥ / tasya hetubhāve phalabhāvo 'pavādaḥ / tatrābhede hetubhāvādekayaiva buddhyobhayādhigamo yuktaḥ / naikatve 'nyatarādhigamaheturnāstīti śakyaṃ vaktum / athāpi kathañcinnāstītyucyeta / tathāpyasti tāvat, ekatvāt / tatra hetubhāvāt phalabhāvaḥ syāt, tasya kāraṇatvāt / na tvabhāvo 'bhāvasya kāraṇam / svabhāvasiddhastvabhāvaḥ phalasya / tasya hetunibandhanaḥ phalabhāvo nivartakaḥ / sa ca heturubhayatrāsti tāvat / asattvaṃ tvanupayogam, akāraṇatvāditi /

api ca

sāmānyaṃ na hi vastvātmā na bhedaścitra eva saḥ /
tasyānanvayato bhedavādaḥ śabdāntarādayam
units.translation:
The very fact that a distinct cognition is required rules out the general and particular being the nature of one and the same object. If they were distinct, as different objects are, a separate cognition would be meaningful because it would apprehend what had not yet been apprehended. But if they were one, then, just as no different cognition is needed to apprehend a division into general and particular features already grasped by a single cognition, a separate cognition of a different kind should not be sought in order to apprehend the particular after apprehending the general, or the general after apprehending the particular.

One might object: the general and particular are not completely identical; there is also some difference, and it is that difference that makes a separate cognition meaningful. That is unsound. Even so, why should difference make a separate cognition meaningful, as it does for distinct objects, while identity does not make it pointless, as with a single aspect? If difference and non-difference are equally present, why should one cognition fail to grasp both because of their difference, while a separate cognition is not pointless because of their identity? In the absence of a cause, the absence of an effect follows by default; when a cause is present, the result occurs—this is established by their natures. Therefore, if identity is the cause, it is reasonable that one cognition apprehend both. One cannot say that unity provides no cause for apprehending one or the other. Even if it were said somehow to provide none, unity is still there. Since the cause is present, its result should follow. For the absence of a cause cannot cause an effect not to occur; that absence is natural, and the arising of the effect when its cause is present removes that natural absence. The same cause is present in both cases. Nonexistence, however, is irrelevant, since it is not a cause.

Furthermore:

“The general feature is not the nature of a real object, nor is the particular; they are a variegated [composite]. Because it is not shared, this is the doctrine of difference, based on another word and the like.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 25
units.deva:
यस्यैकमुभयात्मकं वस्तु न तस्य सामान्यमात्रं वस्तुन आत्मा न विशेषमात्रम् । तन्मात्रत्वे वस्तुभेदप्रसङ्गात् । तस्मात् संभिन्नोभयरूपः शबलो वस्त्वात्मा । न च शबलस्यान्यत्रानुगमः । यस्य त्वनुगमः स वस्तुरूपं न भवति । तथा च शब्दान्तरमवलम्ब्य भेदा एव सत्या इत्येतत्प्रतिपाद्यते शब्दान्तरेण वा हेतुना द्व्यात्मकमेकमिति । अनुगन्तुरवस्तुस्वभावत्वे कल्पनाविषयत्वात् । स्यादेतत् --- मा भूद्वस्तु तदंशत्वं तु न वार्यते । अन्यथा निर्बीजा कल्पनापि न भवेत् । कः पुनरयमंशो नाम । न तावद्वस्त्वेव । तन्मात्ररूपत्वे वस्तुनो भेदप्रसङ्ग इत्युक्तम् । नापि वस्तुनो ऽन्यत्स्वयं वस्तु, सामान्यविशेषतद्वतां त्रयाणां वस्तूनां प्रसङ्गात् । अथ न वस्त्वेव नान्यत्स्वयं वस्तु । परिशेषात् कल्पनाविषयस्तत्त्वान्यत्वाभ्यामनिर्वचनीयः । ननु नांशों ऽशिनो ऽर्थान्तरं नापि स एव, उभयथानंशत्वात् । नाप्यवस्तु, अत एव । न हि खपुष्पं कस्यचिदंशो भवति । तत्रांशानुगमे वस्त्वेवानुगतं भवति तस्य तदव्यतिरेकात् । नैतत्सारम् । [क्क्स्_67] अननुगमादंशान्तरस्य किं न वस्तुनो ऽननुगमः । अपि त्वननुगम (अपि त्वननुगम -- एदितिओन्) एव तस्य समुदायात्मकत्वादेकाभावे ऽप्यभावात् । तथा हि --- इतरेतरापेक्षौ वा सामान्यविशेषौ वस्तु, तत्समाहारो वा । उभयथार्थान्तरे विशेषस्याभावान्न वस्त्वन्वयः । प्रत्येकमनपेक्षयोर्वस्तुत्वे नोभयात्मकमेकं वस्तु स्यादिति सुष्ठूच्यते ---

तस्यानन्वयतो भेदवादः शब्दान्तरादयमिति । यदि वाखिलभावानामभेदात्तदतत्त्वतः । अभेदवादाश्रयणं स्यादन्यविधया गिरा
units.iast:
yasyaikamubhayātmakaṃ vastu na tasya sāmānyamātraṃ vastuna ātmā na viśeṣamātram / tanmātratve vastubhedaprasaṅgāt / tasmāt saṃbhinnobhayarūpaḥ śabalo vastvātmā / na ca śabalasyānyatrānugamaḥ / yasya tvanugamaḥ sa vasturūpaṃ na bhavati / tathā ca śabdāntaramavalambya bhedā eva satyā ityetatpratipādyate śabdāntareṇa vā hetunā dvyātmakamekamiti / anuganturavastusvabhāvatve kalpanāviṣayatvāt /

syādetat --- mā bhūdvastu tadaṃśatvaṃ tu na vāryate / anyathā nirbījā kalpanāpi na bhavet / kaḥ punarayamaṃśo nāma / na tāvadvastveva / tanmātrarūpatve vastuno bhedaprasaṅga ityuktam /

nāpi vastuno 'nyatsvayaṃ vastu, sāmānyaviśeṣatadvatāṃ trayāṇāṃ vastūnāṃ prasaṅgāt / atha na vastveva nānyatsvayaṃ vastu / pariśeṣāt kalpanāviṣayastattvānyatvābhyāmanirvacanīyaḥ / nanu nāṃśoṃ 'śino 'rthāntaraṃ nāpi sa eva, ubhayathānaṃśatvāt / nāpyavastu, ata eva / na hi khapuṣpaṃ kasyacidaṃśo bhavati / tatrāṃśānugame vastvevānugataṃ bhavati tasya tadavyatirekāt / naitatsāram / [kks_67] ananugamādaṃśāntarasya kiṃ na vastuno 'nanugamaḥ / api tvananugama (api tvananugama -- edition) eva tasya samudāyātmakatvādekābhāve 'pyabhāvāt / tathā hi --- itaretarāpekṣau vā sāmānyaviśeṣau vastu, tatsamāhāro vā / ubhayathārthāntare viśeṣasyābhāvānna vastvanvayaḥ / pratyekamanapekṣayorvastutve nobhayātmakamekaṃ vastu syāditi suṣṭhūcyate ---

tasyānanvayato bhedavādaḥ śabdāntarādayamiti /

yadi vākhilabhāvānāmabhedāttadatattvataḥ /
abhedavādāśrayaṇaṃ syādanyavidhayā girā
units.translation:
For someone who holds that one object has both aspects, neither the general feature alone nor the particular feature alone is the nature of the object. If it were only one of these, different objects would result. Therefore the nature of the object is a variegated unity, combining both features. But such a variegated feature is not shared by other things. Whatever is shared in this way is not the nature of an object. Thus, by relying on another word, or by some other reason, one may establish that only differences are real; or, by another word or reason, that one thing is constituted by two aspects. If what is shared has no real nature, it is merely an object of conceptual thought.

Someone may object: let it not be an object, but one cannot deny that it is a part of the object. Otherwise, even conceptual thought would be without a basis. But what is this thing called a “part”? It is not the object itself; as already said, if the object consisted only of that part, different objects would follow. Nor is it a separate real thing that is other than the object, since that would entail three real things: the general feature, the particular feature, and the thing possessing them. If it is neither the object itself nor another independently real object, then by elimination it is an object of conceptual thought, indescribable as either identical with or different from reality.

But a part is neither something other than the whole nor the whole itself, since in either case it would not be a part. Nor is it unreal, for the same reason: a sky-flower is not a part of anything. If the whole is shared through its parts, then it is the very object that is shared, since the whole is not separate from them. This is not sound. If one part is not shared, why should the object itself not be unshared? Indeed, it is simply not shared, since it is constituted by a collection and is absent even if one member is absent. For either the general and particular features are the object by depending on each other, or the object is their aggregate. In either case there is no connection of the object with something else, because there is no separate particular feature. If each were a real thing independently, then there would not be one object constituted by both. Therefore it is correctly said:

“Because it is not shared, this is the doctrine of difference; but another account, based on another word and the like, is this: since all existents are non-different in their unreality, nondualism is accepted, expressed in another way.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 26
units.deva: अंशानुवृत्त्या वा वस्त्वनुगमे ऽद्वैतवादः । तथा हि --- गौः स्वतस्तावद्गौः, सद्द्रव्यादिरूपानुगमादश्ववस्तुनो ऽनुगमादश्वः । तदेवं गौर्गौश्चाश्वश्च । अश्वो ऽपि तावदश्वः सद्द्रव्यादिरूपानुगमेन गोवस्तुनो ऽन्वयाद्गौः । तदेवमश्वो ऽप्यश्वो गौश्च । तदेवं सर्वभावानां तद्भावान्यभावाभ्यामभेद इत्यद्वैतं जगदित्युक्तमन्यप्रकारया वाचा । सत्यम्, द्वैतमप्यस्ति । यतस्तद्भावान्यभावाभ्यामभेदः । नैतत्सारम् । गौरपि चेदश्वो गौश्चाश्वश्च । तत्कुतो ऽन्यत्वम्? गौरश्व इत्यपि (गौश्चाश्वश्चेत्यपि -- एदितिओन्) भेदाभिधानमनिबन्धनमेव । सिद्धे हि गवाश्वभेदे एतदुपपद्यते । गवाश्वस्य तु प्रत्येकं गवाश्वत्वे भेदाभावादनिबन्धनमेव तत् । ननु विशेषांशानां व्यावृत्तेरन्यत्वसिद्धिः । तथा च द्वैताद्वैतात्मकं जगदिति । अथ विशेषव्यावृत्तेरन्यत्वसिद्धिः । किमुभयरूपत्वाद्वस्तुनो वस्त्वन्तरे ऽनुगमो नास्ति? अश्ववस्तु गोवस्तु न भवति । अथास्त्यनुगमः, अश्वो ऽपि गौर्भवति? तत्र पूर्वस्मिन्कल्पे वस्तुनो ऽनन्वयादनुयतश्चावस्तुत्वाद्भेदवाद इत्युक्तम् । अथ विशेषव्यावृत्तावपि तद्वस्त्वनुगतम्, भवत्यश्वो गौः (भवत्यश्वो ऽपि -- एदितिओन्) । कुतो ऽन्यत्वसिद्धिः? यदि मतम् --- अनुगतं चाननुगतं चाश्वे गोवस्तु । भवति चाश्वो गौः । गौस्तु गौरेव । भवत्येव हि तत्र गोवस्तु । ततो ऽन्यत्वसिद्धिरिति । अथ गोवस्तु कथं वक्तव्यम्? किं यद्गौर्भवत्येव, अथ यन्न भवत्यपि? तत्र पूर्वस्यां कल्पनायां न वस्तुनो ऽनुगम इत्यनन्वितानि वस्तूनि । द्वितीयस्यां [क्क्स्_68] वस्तुनो वस्त्वन्तरे ऽन्वयादद्वैतम् । सर्वथा येन विशेषेणायमश्वाद्गोवस्तु व्यवस्थापयत्यन्यत् तद्विशेषयुजस्तु तस्यानन्वयाद्भेदवादः । अथानन्वयदोषान्न विशेषमाश्रयति अभेदवाद इति न द्वैताद्वैतकल्पनोपपद्यत इति । द्रव्यपर्यायार्थकानां नय एतेन वारितः । तेषामपि द्रव्यनयः पर्यायनय एव वा
units.iast:
aṃśānuvṛttyā vā vastvanugame 'dvaitavādaḥ / tathā hi --- gauḥ svatastāvadgauḥ, saddravyādirūpānugamādaśvavastuno 'nugamādaśvaḥ / tadevaṃ gaurgauścāśvaśca / aśvo 'pi tāvadaśvaḥ saddravyādirūpānugamena govastuno 'nvayādgauḥ / tadevamaśvo 'pyaśvo gauśca / tadevaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ tadbhāvānyabhāvābhyāmabheda ityadvaitaṃ jagadityuktamanyaprakārayā vācā / satyam, dvaitamapyasti / yatastadbhāvānyabhāvābhyāmabhedaḥ / naitatsāram / gaurapi cedaśvo gauścāśvaśca / tatkuto 'nyatvam? gauraśva ityapi (gauścāśvaścetyapi -- edition) bhedābhidhānamanibandhanameva / siddhe hi gavāśvabhede etadupapadyate / gavāśvasya tu pratyekaṃ gavāśvatve bhedābhāvādanibandhanameva tat / nanu viśeṣāṃśānāṃ vyāvṛtteranyatvasiddhiḥ / tathā ca dvaitādvaitātmakaṃ jagaditi / atha viśeṣavyāvṛtteranyatvasiddhiḥ / kimubhayarūpatvādvastuno vastvantare 'nugamo nāsti? aśvavastu govastu na bhavati / athāstyanugamaḥ, aśvo 'pi gaurbhavati? tatra pūrvasminkalpe vastuno 'nanvayādanuyataścāvastutvādbhedavāda ityuktam / atha viśeṣavyāvṛttāvapi tadvastvanugatam, bhavatyaśvo gauḥ (bhavatyaśvo 'pi -- edition) / kuto 'nyatvasiddhiḥ? yadi matam --- anugataṃ cānanugataṃ cāśve govastu / bhavati cāśvo gauḥ / gaustu gaureva / bhavatyeva hi tatra govastu / tato 'nyatvasiddhiriti / atha govastu kathaṃ vaktavyam? kiṃ yadgaurbhavatyeva, atha yanna bhavatyapi? tatra pūrvasyāṃ kalpanāyāṃ na vastuno 'nugama ityananvitāni vastūni / dvitīyasyāṃ [kks_68] vastuno vastvantare 'nvayādadvaitam / sarvathā yena viśeṣeṇāyamaśvādgovastu vyavasthāpayatyanyat tadviśeṣayujastu tasyānanvayādbhedavādaḥ / athānanvayadoṣānna viśeṣamāśrayati abhedavāda iti na dvaitādvaitakalpanopapadyata iti /

dravyaparyāyārthakānāṃ naya etena vāritaḥ /
teṣāmapi dravyanayaḥ paryāyanaya eva vā
units.translation:
Alternatively, nondualism may be defended by saying that a thing persists through a common part. Consider this: a cow is, in itself, a cow; because it shares the form of an existent substance and so on, it also shares in the reality of a horse. Thus a cow is both a cow and a horse. A horse too is, in itself, a horse; through sharing the form of an existent substance and so on, it participates in the reality of a cow and is therefore a cow. Thus a horse is both a horse and a cow. In this way, because every existent is identical through the presence and absence of its respective nature, the world has been called nondual, though expressed in a different way.

Granted, duality also exists, since things are alike through the presence and absence of their natures. This is not sound. If a cow is both a horse and a cow, where is their difference? Even saying “cow and horse” would then have no basis; such a statement is meaningful only when a difference between cow and horse is established. But if each is, in every respect, both cow and horse, there is no difference between them and the statement lacks a basis.

One might object that difference is established by excluding the particular features of each thing, and that the world is therefore both dual and nondual. But does the fact that a thing has both forms prevent one thing from sharing in another? A horse is not a cow; or, if there is such sharing, does the horse become a cow as well? In the first case, it has already been shown that there is no relation between things, so, being unrelated, they would be unreal; that is the dualist position. But if, despite the exclusion of particular features, the one thing is shared by another, then the horse is a cow too. How then is difference established?

Suppose one says that the reality of a cow is both shared and unshared in a horse: the horse is a cow, but a cow is only a cow; the reality of the cow is indeed present there, and from this difference follows. But what should “the reality of a cow” mean? Does it mean what is only a cow, or what is also not only a cow? On the first interpretation, no reality is shared by one thing with another, and things are unrelated. On the second, one thing is related to another, and nonduality follows. In any case, the particular feature by which one establishes that the reality of a cow is different from a horse does not connect them; because of that lack of connection, this is the dualist position. If the nondualist avoids relying on a particular feature because that would entail the defect of nonrelation, then the proposed theory of a world that is both dual and nondual cannot be sustained. This also refutes the positions that treat substance and its modes as separately meaningful principles, whether as substance or as modes.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 27
units.deva:
ये च --- द्रव्यं नित्यं मृत्सुवर्णादि । तस्य (तस्य तु म्स् अ; तस्य च -- एदितिओन्) घटरुचकादयः पर्याया विशेषाख्या अपायिन उपायिनश्चाव्यतिरेकाः । न च ते द्रव्यमेव, तस्य स्थितिमत्त्वात् । न च ततो ऽत्यन्तं व्यावर्तन्ते, भेदेनानुपलब्धेः । द्रव्यस्यैव रुचकादिरूपेण प्रत्ययात् । एवं द्रव्यपर्यायरूपं वस्तु । अथ (म्स् ब्; अथ -- एदितिओन्) तु द्रव्यमेव स्यात्, वर्धमानकभङ्गेन रुचकक्रियायां न किञ्चिदुत्पन्नं नष्टं वेति प्रीतिशोकौ तदर्थिनोर्न स्याताम् । अथ तु पर्यायमात्रम्, हेमार्थिनो मध्यस्थता न स्यात् । पर्यायमात्रे हि हेम्नि हेम्नो विनाशात्पर्यायविनाशे कथं मध्यस्थता? उत्पादे वा? तस्माद्द्रव्यपर्यायरूपत्वाद्वस्तुन उत्पत्तिस्थितिभङ्गानामेकत्र संभवाद्द्रव्यरूपस्थितेर्माध्यस्थ्यम्, पर्याययोरुत्पत्तिविनाशाभ्यां प्रीतिशोकाववकल्पेते इति --- मन्यन्ते । तन्नीतिरप्यनेनैव निराकृता प्रकारेण । तथा हि --- तेषामपि वस्तुनो वस्त्वन्तरान्वये ऽपि भागाभावाद्द्रव्यमात्रं स्यात् । अथ न वस्त्वन्वेति द्रव्यपर्यायरूपत्वाद्वस्तुनः, पर्यायान्तरे च पर्यायान्तरस्याननुगमादनन्वितानि तर्हि व्यावृत्तस्वभावानि वस्तूनि । यस्यानुगमः कल्प्यते तन्मात्ररूपस्यावस्तुत्वात्पर्यायमात्रम् । अवस्थितं हि द्रव्यमुच्यते । न चैवमवस्थितं किञ्चिदेकं वस्त्वस्ति । वस्तुनस्त्वपोद्धृतस्यांशस्यावस्थानकल्पना कल्पनैव । वस्तुनश्चित्रत्वात्, तस्य चातथाभावादिति । अपि च

उत्पादस्थितिभङ्गानामेकत्र समवायतः । प्रीतिमध्यस्थताशोकाः स्युर्न स्युरिति दुर्घटम्

ye ca --- dravyaṃ nityaṃ mṛtsuvarṇādi / tasya (tasya tu ms a; tasya ca -- edition) ghaṭarucakādayaḥ paryāyā viśeṣākhyā apāyina upāyinaścāvyatirekāḥ / na ca te dravyameva, tasya sthitimattvāt / na ca tato 'tyantaṃ vyāvartante, bhedenānupalabdheḥ / dravyasyaiva rucakādirūpeṇa pratyayāt / evaṃ dravyaparyāyarūpaṃ vastu / atha (ms b; atha -- edition) tu dravyameva syāt, vardhamānakabhaṅgena rucakakriyāyāṃ na kiñcidutpannaṃ naṣṭaṃ veti prītiśokau tadarthinorna syātām / atha tu paryāyamātram, hemārthino madhyasthatā na syāt / paryāyamātre hi hemni hemno vināśātparyāyavināśe kathaṃ madhyasthatā? utpāde vā? tasmāddravyaparyāyarūpatvādvastuna utpattisthitibhaṅgānāmekatra saṃbhavāddravyarūpasthitermādhyasthyam, paryāyayorutpattivināśābhyāṃ prītiśokāvavakalpete iti --- manyante / tannītirapyanenaiva nirākṛtā prakāreṇa / tathā hi --- teṣāmapi vastuno vastvantarānvaye 'pi bhāgābhāvāddravyamātraṃ syāt / atha na vastvanveti dravyaparyāyarūpatvādvastunaḥ, paryāyāntare ca paryāyāntarasyānanugamādananvitāni tarhi vyāvṛttasvabhāvāni vastūni / yasyānugamaḥ kalpyate tanmātrarūpasyāvastutvātparyāyamātram / avasthitaṃ hi dravyamucyate / na caivamavasthitaṃ kiñcidekaṃ vastvasti / vastunastvapoddhṛtasyāṃśasyāvasthānakalpanā kalpanaiva / vastunaścitratvāt, tasya cātathābhāvāditi /

api ca

utpādasthitibhaṅgānāmekatra samavāyataḥ /
prītimadhyasthatāśokāḥ syurna syuriti durghaṭam
units.translation:
Some hold that the substance is permanent, as with clay or gold, while pots, ornaments, and other modes, called particular forms, arise and disappear without being separate from it. They are not the substance itself, since the substance continues; nor are they entirely distinct from it, since no separate difference is perceived. The substance itself is cognized in the form of a pot, an ornament, and so on. Thus a real thing is constituted by both substance and mode.

If it were only substance, then when a bracelet is broken and made into an ornament, nothing would have arisen or perished, so the person who desired one or the other could feel neither joy nor sorrow. But if it were only a mode, the person who desires gold could not remain indifferent. If the gold consisted only of modes, when the gold perished through the destruction of one mode, how could the person remain indifferent to the destruction—or production—of a mode? Therefore they say that a real thing is both substance and mode: arising, continuance, and destruction coexist in one thing. Because the substance continues, indifference is possible; because its modes arise and perish, joy and sorrow are possible.

This position too is refuted by the argument already given. Even if a thing is related to another thing, there are no parts by which the substance alone could be shared. If a thing, being constituted by substance and modes, is not shared with another thing, and one mode is not shared with another mode, then things are separate and have only excluded natures. If what is shared is imagined to be nothing but the permanent substance, that alone is not real; only the modes remain. For what is called a substance is what remains constant, and no single thing exists as constant in this way. To imagine that a separated part of a variegated object persists as a real thing is merely conceptual, because an object is complex and does not actually exist in that isolated form. Furthermore:

“When arising, continuance, and destruction coexist in one thing, it is untenable that joy, indifference, and sorrow should or should not arise.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 28
units.deva:
[क्क्स्_69] यस्य खलु द्रव्यात्पर्याया भिद्यन्ते तस्य --- द्रव्यमात्रार्थिनो द्रव्यस्य स्थितेर्विनाशाभावादपूर्वस्यानुत्पादान्मध्यस्थता, रुचकार्थिनस्तस्यापूर्वस्योत्पत्तेः प्रीतिः, वर्धमानकार्थिनस्तस्य विनाशाच्छोकः --- इति व्यवस्था कल्पते । यस्य तु न पर्यायेभ्यो ऽन्यद्द्रव्यं (म्स् अ; यस्य तु पर्यायेभ्यो ऽनन्यद्द्रव्यं -- एदितिओन्) न द्रव्यादन्ये पर्यायाः, तस्य उत्पत्तिस्थितिभङ्गानामेकत्र समवाये द्रव्यार्थिनो मध्यस्थता भवेत्, न भवेच्च । प्रीतिशोकौ स्याताम्, न स्याताम् । न हि तद्द्रव्यमवतिष्ठत एव, विनश्यत्यपूर्वं चोत्पद्यते । तत्र विनाशादपूर्वोत्पत्तेश्च प्रीतिशोकौ स्याताम्, न मध्यस्थता । मध्यस्थता च स्थितेः स्यात् --- इति दुर्घटमापद्येत । तथा वर्धमानकार्थिनस्तन्नाशाच्छोकः स्यात् । न च स्यात्, स्थितेः । प्रीतिश्च तस्यापूर्वस्योत्पादात्स्यात् । न च भवेत्, पूर्वस्यैव स्थितेः । विनाशाच्च शोकः स्यादिति । अथ भेदो ऽप्यस्तीति नायं दोषः । अभेदो ऽप्यस्तीति किं न भवति? अथ नात्यन्तमभेदः, तेन न संकरः । नात्यन्तमभेद इति व्यवस्थापि न युज्यते । न चास्य किञ्चित्क्वचिदेकान्ततः सर्वत्रानेकान्तमभ्युपयतः, येनायं विशेष उच्यते --- नात्यन्तमभेद इत्यसंकर इति । तथा च

नैकान्तः सर्वभावानां यदि सर्वविधानतः । अप्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तीदं प्राप्तं सर्वत्र ही जगत्
units.iast:
[kks_69] yasya khalu dravyātparyāyā bhidyante tasya --- dravyamātrārthino dravyasya sthitervināśābhāvādapūrvasyānutpādānmadhyasthatā, rucakārthinastasyāpūrvasyotpatteḥ prītiḥ, vardhamānakārthinastasya vināśācchokaḥ --- iti vyavasthā kalpate / yasya tu na paryāyebhyo 'nyaddravyaṃ (ms a; yasya tu paryāyebhyo 'nanyaddravyaṃ -- edition) na dravyādanye paryāyāḥ, tasya utpattisthitibhaṅgānāmekatra samavāye dravyārthino madhyasthatā bhavet, na bhavecca / prītiśokau syātām, na syātām / na hi taddravyamavatiṣṭhata eva, vinaśyatyapūrvaṃ cotpadyate / tatra vināśādapūrvotpatteśca prītiśokau syātām, na madhyasthatā / madhyasthatā ca sthiteḥ syāt --- iti durghaṭamāpadyeta / tathā vardhamānakārthinastannāśācchokaḥ syāt / na ca syāt, sthiteḥ / prītiśca tasyāpūrvasyotpādātsyāt / na ca bhavet, pūrvasyaiva sthiteḥ / vināśācca śokaḥ syāditi / atha bhedo 'pyastīti nāyaṃ doṣaḥ / abhedo 'pyastīti kiṃ na bhavati? atha nātyantamabhedaḥ, tena na saṃkaraḥ / nātyantamabheda iti vyavasthāpi na yujyate / na cāsya kiñcitkvacidekāntataḥ sarvatrānekāntamabhyupayataḥ, yenāyaṃ viśeṣa ucyate --- nātyantamabheda ityasaṃkara iti / tathā ca

naikāntaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ yadi sarvavidhānataḥ /
apravṛttinivṛttīdaṃ prāptaṃ sarvatra hī jagat
units.translation:
For someone who distinguishes a substance from its changing modes, this arrangement is possible: a person who wants only the substance remains indifferent, because the substance persists and neither disappears nor gives rise to anything new; a person who wants a new ornament feels joy when that new thing is produced; and a person who wants an ornament still growing larger feels sorrow when it is destroyed. But for someone who holds that the substance is not other than its modes and that the modes are not other than the substance, the arising, continuing, and destruction all coexist in one thing. Then the person who wants the substance might either remain indifferent or not; joy and sorrow might arise or not. For the substance itself is not simply continuing: what is new is produced and what was there is destroyed. In that case, because something is destroyed and something new is produced, there should be joy and sorrow, not indifference. Indifference, however, would follow from its continuation. This leads to an untenable result. Likewise, the person who wants an ornament that is growing larger should feel sorrow when it is destroyed; but they should not, because it continues. Joy should arise from the production of a new ornament, but it should not, because the earlier one continues. And sorrow should arise from its destruction.

One might reply that there is also difference, so this defect does not apply. Why should there not also be non-difference? If it is not complete non-difference, there is no mixture of things. But the claim that it is not complete non-difference cannot be established either. Someone who accepts that nothing is wholly one way in any respect, but is in every respect partly this and partly that, cannot state any definite qualification such as “not completely non-different” to prevent mixture. Therefore:

“If no state of any existent is definite in every respect, then neither action nor cessation is possible anywhere; the whole world would be brought to a halt.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 29
units.deva:
यदा हि सर्वप्रकारेष्वनैकान्तिकत्वं भावानाम्, तथा सति --- नायं लोकः क्वचिदभिमतसाधनताप्रकारमवधार्य प्रवर्तेत, यतो नासौ तथैव । नापि निवर्तेत, यतो नासावतथैव । तथा दुःखहेतोर्न निवर्तेत, नासौ तथैव । नापि न निवर्तेत, यतो नासावतथैव --- इति कष्टां बत दशामापद्येत । अथ वा यदुक्तम् --- प्रीतिमध्यस्थताशोकाः स्युर्न स्युरिति दुर्घटमिति, तत्र ब्रूयुः --- सर्ववस्तुषु सर्वप्रकाराणामनैकान्तिकत्वात्का दुर्घटता? तथा हि --- प्रीतिमध्यस्थताशोका नैकान्ततः सन्ति, नैकान्ततो न सन्तीति । अत्रोच्यते --- नैकान्तः सर्वभावानामिति । यदि खलु प्रीत्यादीनां सदसत्त्वे [क्क्स्_70] नैकान्तिके (ऽनैकान्तिके -- एदितिओन्) --- न प्रीत्यर्थी प्रीतिसाधनेषु प्रवर्तेत, प्रीतेर्विद्यमानत्वात् । नापि न प्रवर्तेत, तस्या अभावात् । तथा दुःखनिवृत्त्यर्थी न दुःखसाधनसंपर्कं परिहरेत्, तस्यासत्त्वात् । नापि न परिहरेत्, तस्य सत्त्वात् --- इत्यप्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिकं बत विश्वमापन्नमिति । एवं तावन्न द्वे वस्तुनी, नैकं द्व्यात्मकम् । तत्र द्वयमवशिष्यते --- भेदः सत्यः, तदुपादानाभेदकल्पना । अभेदो वा सत्यः, तदुपादाना भेदकल्पनेति । तत्र ---

आपेक्षिकत्वाद्भेदो हि भेदग्रहपुरस्सरः । नैकज्ञानं समीक्ष्यैकं न भेदं तत्त्वहानतः
units.iast:
yadā hi sarvaprakāreṣvanaikāntikatvaṃ bhāvānām, tathā sati --- nāyaṃ lokaḥ kvacidabhimatasādhanatāprakāramavadhārya pravarteta, yato nāsau tathaiva / nāpi nivarteta, yato nāsāvatathaiva / tathā duḥkhahetorna nivarteta, nāsau tathaiva / nāpi na nivarteta, yato nāsāvatathaiva --- iti kaṣṭāṃ bata daśāmāpadyeta /

atha vā yaduktam --- prītimadhyasthatāśokāḥ syurna syuriti durghaṭamiti, tatra brūyuḥ --- sarvavastuṣu sarvaprakārāṇāmanaikāntikatvātkā durghaṭatā? tathā hi --- prītimadhyasthatāśokā naikāntataḥ santi, naikāntato na santīti / atrocyate --- naikāntaḥ sarvabhāvānāmiti / yadi khalu prītyādīnāṃ sadasattve [kks_70] naikāntike ('naikāntike -- edition) --- na prītyarthī prītisādhaneṣu pravarteta, prītervidyamānatvāt / nāpi na pravarteta, tasyā abhāvāt / tathā duḥkhanivṛttyarthī na duḥkhasādhanasaṃparkaṃ pariharet, tasyāsattvāt / nāpi na pariharet, tasya sattvāt --- ityapravṛttinivṛttikaṃ bata viśvamāpannamiti /

evaṃ tāvanna dve vastunī, naikaṃ dvyātmakam / tatra dvayamavaśiṣyate --- bhedaḥ satyaḥ, tadupādānābhedakalpanā / abhedo vā satyaḥ, tadupādānā bhedakalpaneti / tatra ---

āpekṣikatvādbhedo hi bhedagrahapurassaraḥ /
naikajñānaṃ samīkṣyaikaṃ na bhedaṃ tattvahānataḥ
units.translation:
If all things are indeterminate in every respect, then no one in the world could act after determining that something is a means to a desired end, since it might not be so; nor could anyone refrain from acting, since it might not be otherwise. One would neither avoid the cause of suffering, since it might not be such a cause, nor fail to avoid it, since it might be one. What an unbearable condition this would be!

Or, regarding the earlier objection that it is untenable for joy, indifference, and sorrow both to occur and not to occur, they may reply: what is untenable if every state is indeterminate in every respect? Joy, indifference, and sorrow are neither absolutely existent nor absolutely nonexistent. We reply: it is impossible for all existents to be indeterminate. If joy and the like are neither definitely present nor definitely absent, then a person seeking joy would neither pursue its means, since joy would be present, nor refrain from pursuing them, since it would be absent. A person seeking to be free of pain would neither avoid contact with what causes pain, since pain would not exist, nor fail to avoid it, since pain would exist. The whole world would therefore be left unable both to act and to refrain from action.

Thus, there are neither two separate objects nor one object constituted by both. Two possibilities remain: difference is real, and non-difference is imagined on its basis; or non-difference is real, and difference is imagined on its basis. Of these—

“Difference is relative, for it is preceded by apprehending difference; it does not, when examined, establish a single thing, since that would destroy the reality of difference.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 30
units.deva:
न भेदमुपादायाभेदकल्पना । कुतः? आपेक्षिको हि भेदो नान्यमनपेक्ष्य शक्यते ग्रहीतुम् । न चागृहीतो भेदो ऽभेदकल्पनाया उपादानं भवति । परापेक्षत्वे चास्य ग्रहणमनुपपन्नम् । यतो नागृहीते भेदे परात्मानौ व्यवतिष्ठेते । न च परात्मव्यवस्थामन्तरेण भेदग्रहो ऽस्तीति प्राक्प्रपञ्चितम् । न त्वेवम् (म्स् अ; न चैवम् -- एदितिओन्) अभेदग्रहणमभेदग्रहणापेक्षम् । नापि भेदग्रहणापेक्षम्, अभेदहानप्रसङ्गात् । न हि भेदे गृहीते ऽभेदस्यावकाशो ऽस्ति । तत्राभेदं गृहीत्वा तमुपादाय तस्य यथावन्निश्चयाशक्तौ व्यवच्छेदकल्पनोपपद्यते, यथैकबुद्धिनिर्ग्राह्येषु घटादिष्ववयवविभागकल्पना । न तत्र भेदोपादानाभेदकल्पना । भेदो हि परमाणुषु व्यवतिष्ठते । ते चातीन्द्रियाः । ननु चैकत्वमप्यनुसन्धानप्रत्ययावसेयम् । स च न भेदमन्तरेण । भेदास्पर्शे (भेदासंस्पर्शे -- एदितिओन्) हि किं केनानुसन्धीयतामिति । प्रत्युक्तमेतत् --- नेदानीमभिन्नदेशकालो ऽर्थ एकः स्यात् । असति चैकस्मिन् किमाश्रया भेदाशङ्का स्यात्, यस्यानुसंधानादेकत्वमुच्यत इति । अपि च सर्वप्रत्यात्मवेदनीयमेतदभेदोपादानो भेद इति । तथा हि ---

आलोच्यते वस्तुमात्रं ज्ञानेनापातजन्मना । अचेत्यमानो भेदो ऽपि चकास्तीत्यतिसाहसम्
units.iast:
na bhedamupādāyābhedakalpanā / kutaḥ? āpekṣiko hi bhedo nānyamanapekṣya śakyate grahītum / na cāgṛhīto bhedo 'bhedakalpanāyā upādānaṃ bhavati / parāpekṣatve cāsya grahaṇamanupapannam / yato nāgṛhīte bhede parātmānau vyavatiṣṭhete / na ca parātmavyavasthāmantareṇa bhedagraho 'stīti prākprapañcitam / na tvevam (ms a; na caivam -- edition) abhedagrahaṇamabhedagrahaṇāpekṣam / nāpi bhedagrahaṇāpekṣam, abhedahānaprasaṅgāt / na hi bhede gṛhīte 'bhedasyāvakāśo 'sti / tatrābhedaṃ gṛhītvā tamupādāya tasya yathāvanniścayāśaktau vyavacchedakalpanopapadyate, yathaikabuddhinirgrāhyeṣu ghaṭādiṣvavayavavibhāgakalpanā / na tatra bhedopādānābhedakalpanā / bhedo hi paramāṇuṣu vyavatiṣṭhate / te cātīndriyāḥ / nanu caikatvamapyanusandhānapratyayāvaseyam / sa ca na bhedamantareṇa / bhedāsparśe (bhedāsaṃsparśe -- edition) hi kiṃ kenānusandhīyatāmiti / pratyuktametat --- nedānīmabhinnadeśakālo 'rtha ekaḥ syāt / asati caikasmin kimāśrayā bhedāśaṅkā syāt, yasyānusaṃdhānādekatvamucyata iti /

api ca sarvapratyātmavedanīyametadabhedopādāno bheda iti / tathā hi ---

ālocyate vastumātraṃ jñānenāpātajanmanā /
acetyamāno bhedo 'pi cakāstītyatisāhasam
units.translation:
The imagination of non-difference is not based on difference. Why not? Relative difference cannot be grasped without relying on something else. And a difference that has not been grasped cannot serve as the basis for imagining non-difference. Since difference depends on something else, its apprehension cannot be established: when difference is not apprehended, the two things that are to be distinguished are not established as distinct. It has already been explained that difference cannot be apprehended without establishing those distinct things.

Non-difference, however, does not depend on apprehending non-difference beforehand, nor does it depend on apprehending difference, for that would destroy the possibility of non-difference. Once non-difference is apprehended, and one is unable to determine it exactly, one may then imagine distinctions within it—just as one imagines divisions among the parts of a pot, although the pot is grasped in one cognition. In that case the imagination of non-difference is not based on difference. Difference is established among atoms, but they are beyond the senses.

One might object that unity too is known only through a cognition that gathers things together, and that such a cognition requires difference; without encountering difference, what could be gathered together with what? This has already been answered: otherwise, an object whose place and time are not distinct would not be one. And if there were no one thing, what would provide the basis for suspecting difference, so that gathering it together could be called unity? Moreover, each person directly knows that difference is imagined on the basis of non-difference. For—

“Cognition, arising at first, observes the thing simply as it is; to claim that difference shines forth even though it is not apprehended is exceedingly bold.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 31
units.deva:
[क्क्स्_71] वस्तुमात्रविषयं प्रथममविकल्पकं प्रत्यक्षम् । तत्पूर्वास्तु विकल्पबुद्धयो विशेषानवगाहन्त इति सर्वप्रत्यात्मवेदनीयम् । स्यादेतत् --- विशिष्टरूपोपग्राह्येव प्रत्यक्षम् । स तु भेदः शब्देनासंस्पर्शान्न तथोपलक्ष्यते, यथा विकल्पबुद्धौ । तदयुक्तम्, विप्रतिषेधात् । न चोपलक्ष्यते प्रत्यक्षबुद्धौ विशेषः प्रकाशते चेति विप्रतिषिद्धम् । अतो ऽतिसाहसमुच्यते । यस्तु संवित्तावेव विप्रतिपद्यते सर्वानात्मव्यावृत्तस्पष्टप्रतिभासं प्रत्यक्षमिति वदन्, तस्योत्तरम् --- ‘आहुर्विधातृप्रत्यक्षम्ऽ; इत्याद्युक्तमेवेति । किं च

प्रतिष्ठितं च विज्ञानमर्थमात्रावलम्बनम् । भेदेषु त्वप्रतिष्ठत्वमस्तीन्द्रियधियामपि
units.iast:
[kks_71] vastumātraviṣayaṃ prathamamavikalpakaṃ pratyakṣam / tatpūrvāstu vikalpabuddhayo viśeṣānavagāhanta iti sarvapratyātmavedanīyam / syādetat --- viśiṣṭarūpopagrāhyeva pratyakṣam / sa tu bhedaḥ śabdenāsaṃsparśānna tathopalakṣyate, yathā vikalpabuddhau / tadayuktam, vipratiṣedhāt / na copalakṣyate pratyakṣabuddhau viśeṣaḥ prakāśate ceti vipratiṣiddham / ato 'tisāhasamucyate / yastu saṃvittāveva vipratipadyate sarvānātmavyāvṛttaspaṣṭapratibhāsaṃ pratyakṣamiti vadan, tasyottaram --- ‘āhurvidhātṛpratyakṣam'; ityādyuktameveti /

kiṃ ca

pratiṣṭhitaṃ ca vijñānamarthamātrāvalambanam /
bhedeṣu tvapratiṣṭhatvamastīndriyadhiyāmapi
units.translation:
Direct perception at first is non-conceptual and has only the object itself as its content. The conceptual cognitions that follow it grasp particular features. This is evident to everyone through their own experience. Someone may object that perception itself grasps a qualified form, but that difference is not marked by words as it is in conceptual cognition. That is unreasonable, since it is contradictory to say both that a particular is not marked and that it shines forth in perception. To claim this is exceedingly bold. As for one who disputes the nature of awareness itself, saying that perception has a clear appearance that excludes everything other than itself, the response has already been given: “The learned say that perception affirms…” and so forth. Moreover—

“Cognition is established as resting on the object alone; but with respect to differences, even cognition of things beyond the senses is not established.”

gloss.en: having only the object itself as its content
directly knowable to each person through their own experience
because it is not contacted (by words)
having a clear appearance that excludes everything other than the Self
as resting on the object alone

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 32
units.deva:
वस्तुद्वयानुपपत्तेरेकस्य च द्व्यात्मतायोगादवश्यकल्पनीये ऽन्यतरस्य मिथ्यात्वे युक्तं विशेषावभासस्य मिथ्यात्वम्, रजतादिविभ्रान्तिषु दर्शनात् । न च वस्तुमात्रावभासस्य । न हि वस्तुमात्रव्यभिचारः क्वचिज्ज्ञाने दृष्टो ऽस्ति, अन्ततस्तस्यैव वस्तुनः प्रतिभासनात् । दृष्टतद्भावस्यैव तत्कल्पना लघ्वी, क्ळ्प्तत्वाद्योग्यतायाः, इतरत्र तु कल्प्यत्वात् । स्यादेतत् --- मानस्य एव बुद्धयः क्ळ्प्तयोग्यभावा मिथ्यात्वं प्रति, नेन्द्रियजन्मानः । इन्द्रियबुद्धिसमधिगम्याश्च भेदा इति । एतच्च वार्तम् । इन्द्रियदोषानुविधायित्वाद्भ्रान्तीनामिति (@दोषविशेषानुविधायि@ -- एदितिओन्) । अपि च यस्य मतम् --- व्यावृत्तस्वलक्षणा भावाः । तेन ते ऽन्योन्याभावस्वभावा व्याकर्तव्याः, तद्विशेषणा वा । नान्यथा व्यावृत्तशब्दो ऽर्थवान् भवति, तस्येतरेतराभावनिमित्तत्वात् । तत्र

अन्योन्याभावरूपत्वं सर्वेषां न प्रकल्पते । तत्रोपाधौ प्रतीयन्तां तथा भिन्ना न रूपतः
units.iast:
vastudvayānupapatterekasya ca dvyātmatāyogādavaśyakalpanīye 'nyatarasya mithyātve yuktaṃ viśeṣāvabhāsasya mithyātvam, rajatādivibhrāntiṣu darśanāt / na ca vastumātrāvabhāsasya / na hi vastumātravyabhicāraḥ kvacijjñāne dṛṣṭo 'sti, antatastasyaiva vastunaḥ pratibhāsanāt / dṛṣṭatadbhāvasyaiva tatkalpanā laghvī, kḷptatvādyogyatāyāḥ, itaratra tu kalpyatvāt /

syādetat --- mānasya eva buddhayaḥ kḷptayogyabhāvā mithyātvaṃ prati, nendriyajanmānaḥ / indriyabuddhisamadhigamyāśca bhedā iti / etacca vārtam / indriyadoṣānuvidhāyitvādbhrāntīnāmiti (@doṣaviśeṣānuvidhāyi@ -- edition) /

api ca yasya matam --- vyāvṛttasvalakṣaṇā bhāvāḥ / tena te 'nyonyābhāvasvabhāvā vyākartavyāḥ, tadviśeṣaṇā vā / nānyathā vyāvṛttaśabdo 'rthavān bhavati, tasyetaretarābhāvanimittatvāt / tatra

anyonyābhāvarūpatvaṃ sarveṣāṃ na prakalpate /
tatropādhau pratīyantāṃ tathā bhinnā na rūpataḥ
units.translation:
Since two separate objects are untenable, and one object cannot have two natures, one of the two appearances must necessarily be imagined. It is reasonable to say that the appearance of a particular feature is false, as is observed in illusions of silver and the like, but not that the mere appearance of an object is false. There is no known cognition in which the mere object itself is absent; ultimately, that object does appear. It is more economical to suppose only a feature to be imagined when the object itself has already been seen, since the capacity for such an appearance is established; in the other case, it would have to be invented.

One might object: only mental cognitions, whose capacity for error is accepted, can be false, not those that arise from the senses; and differences are apprehended by sensory cognition. This is poorly argued, since illusions follow upon defects of the senses. Moreover, those who hold that real things are characterized by their exclusion from one another must explain that things have mutual absence as their nature, or else possess that as a qualifying property. Otherwise, the word “excluded” would have no meaning, since it is based on mutual absence. Therefore:

“It cannot be imagined that all things have mutual absence as their nature. Let them be apprehended as distinct in that way through a limiting condition; but their forms are not thereby different.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 33
units.deva:
एकस्मिन्ननपेक्षे स्थिते तदभावरूपो ऽन्यो व्यवतिष्ठते । सर्वे तु नान्योन्याभावरूपाः कल्पन्ते, परस्पराश्रयस्थितित्वात् । अथ विशेषणमन्योन्याभावः । कामम्, अतदात्मानो ऽपि विशेषणानुरागात्तथावगम्यन्ताम् । न तु स्वभावभेदः [क्क्स्_72] स्यात् । ननु नान्योन्याभावो नाम कश्चित्, यो भावानां तत्त्वं विशेषणं वा स्यात् अर्थसिद्धिरेवैषा । न चेदन्योन्याभावो कश्चित्, सिद्धस्तर्ह्यभेद इति । अपि च भेदत्वादेव विश्वस्य भेदो ऽभेदोपादान इति शक्यते ऽनुमातुम् । दृष्टो हि मणिकृपाणदर्पणादिष्वभिन्नमुखोपादानस्तद्भेदः । न च तत्र भावान्तरोत्पत्तिः, विरुद्धपरिणामत्वात् । स्यादेतत् --- अभेदो ऽपि शक्यो भेदोपादानो ऽनुमातुम्, वनाभेदस्य तरुभेदोपादानत्वात् । न, भेदाभावप्रसङ्गात् । एवं हि न कश्चिदेको ऽभिन्नः परमाणुरपि । तदभेदो ऽपि हि भेदोपादानः स्याद्वनादिवत् । तथा तदंशाभेदो ऽपीत्यनवस्थायामेकस्याभावात्तत्समुच्चयरूपो ऽभेदो न स्यात् । अथ क्वचिदवतिष्ठते स एकः । तदभेदो न भेदोपादान इति व्यभिचारः । तदिदमुच्यते ---

दपर्णादौ मुखस्येव भेदो ऽभेदावलम्बनः । भेदावलम्बनो ऽभेदो न तथा तदभावतः
units.iast:
ekasminnanapekṣe sthite tadabhāvarūpo 'nyo vyavatiṣṭhate / sarve tu nānyonyābhāvarūpāḥ kalpante, parasparāśrayasthititvāt / atha viśeṣaṇamanyonyābhāvaḥ / kāmam, atadātmāno 'pi viśeṣaṇānurāgāttathāvagamyantām / na tu svabhāvabhedaḥ [kks_72] syāt / nanu nānyonyābhāvo nāma kaścit, yo bhāvānāṃ tattvaṃ viśeṣaṇaṃ vā syāt arthasiddhirevaiṣā / na cedanyonyābhāvo kaścit, siddhastarhyabheda iti /

api ca bhedatvādeva viśvasya bhedo 'bhedopādāna iti śakyate 'numātum / dṛṣṭo hi maṇikṛpāṇadarpaṇādiṣvabhinnamukhopādānastadbhedaḥ / na ca tatra bhāvāntarotpattiḥ, viruddhapariṇāmatvāt / syādetat --- abhedo 'pi śakyo bhedopādāno 'numātum, vanābhedasya tarubhedopādānatvāt / na, bhedābhāvaprasaṅgāt / evaṃ hi na kaścideko 'bhinnaḥ paramāṇurapi / tadabhedo 'pi hi bhedopādānaḥ syādvanādivat / tathā tadaṃśābhedo 'pītyanavasthāyāmekasyābhāvāttatsamuccayarūpo 'bhedo na syāt / atha kvacidavatiṣṭhate sa ekaḥ / tadabhedo na bhedopādāna iti vyabhicāraḥ / tadidamucyate ---

daparṇādau mukhasyeva bhedo 'bhedāvalambanaḥ /
bhedāvalambano 'bhedo na tathā tadabhāvataḥ
units.translation:
When one thing is established independently, another may be established as its absence. But not all things can be conceived as the mutual absence of one another, since their establishment would depend on each other. Suppose a qualifier is simply mutual absence. Very well: even things that are not identical in nature may be understood in that way because they are associated with a qualifier. But their difference in nature would not thereby follow.

One might object that mutual absence is not some real thing that could be the nature or a qualifier of existents; it is simply a way of establishing an object. If there is no such thing as mutual absence, then non-difference is established. Moreover, one might infer that the world’s difference depends on non-difference, simply because it is difference. For example, the distinct appearances of a face in a gem, a sword, and a mirror all depend on one and the same face. No other entity arises there, because their effects are contrary transformations.

Someone may object that non-difference too can be inferred to depend on difference, since the non-difference of a forest depends on the distinct trees. No: that would entail the absence of difference. For then nothing at all would be a single, undifferentiated thing—not even an atom. Its non-difference would itself depend on difference, as with a forest. The non-difference of its parts would likewise depend on difference, and this would lead to an infinite regress. Since there would be no single thing, non-difference as an aggregate of those things could not exist. But suppose that non-difference ultimately rests in some one thing; then there is an exception: the non-difference of that thing does not depend on difference. This is the point being made:

“Difference depends on non-difference, as the face does in a mirror and the like; non-difference does not in the same way depend on difference, since it does not depend on it.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 34
units.deva:
अपि च

प्रत्येकमनुविद्धत्वादभेदेन मृषा मतः । भेदो यथा तरङ्गाणां भेदाद्भेदः कलावतः
units.iast:
api ca

pratyekamanuviddhatvādabhedena mṛṣā mataḥ /
bhedo yathā taraṅgāṇāṃ bhedādbhedaḥ kalāvataḥ
units.translation:
Moreover:

“Because each thing is pervaded by non-difference, its difference is held to be false, as with waves. Difference arises from difference, as with the parts of a whole.”

gloss.en: of a whole made of parts

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 35
units.deva:
अभेदानुविद्धत्वात्प्रत्येकं विश्वस्य भेदो मृषा । यथा जलतरङ्गेषु चन्द्रमसः । तत्र हि प्रत्येकं चन्द्रमा इत्यभेदान्वयः, तथा विश्वस्य भेदे ऽपि प्रत्येकम् ‘इदम्ऽ; ‘तत्ऽ; ‘अर्थःऽ; ‘वस्तुऽइत्यभेदान्वयः । तरुभेदस्तु यद्यपि न मृषा, वनमित्यभेदानुगमश्च न प्रत्येकम् । न हि प्रत्येकं तरुषु वनमिति बुद्धिः । अतो न तेन व्यभिचारः । एतदर्थं च प्रत्येकमित्युक्तम् । अपि च ---

एकस्यैवास्तु महिमा यन्नानेव प्रकाशते । लाघवान्न तु भिन्नानां यच्चकासत्यभिन्नवत्
units.iast:
abhedānuviddhatvātpratyekaṃ viśvasya bhedo mṛṣā / yathā jalataraṅgeṣu candramasaḥ / tatra hi pratyekaṃ candramā ityabhedānvayaḥ, tathā viśvasya bhede 'pi pratyekam ‘idam'; ‘tat'; ‘arthaḥ'; ‘vastu'ityabhedānvayaḥ / tarubhedastu yadyapi na mṛṣā, vanamityabhedānugamaśca na pratyekam / na hi pratyekaṃ taruṣu vanamiti buddhiḥ / ato na tena vyabhicāraḥ / etadarthaṃ ca pratyekamityuktam /

api ca ---

ekasyaivāstu mahimā yannāneva prakāśate /
lāghavānna tu bhinnānāṃ yaccakāsatyabhinnavat
units.translation:
Because every thing is pervaded by non-difference, the difference of each particular thing in the world is false, like the moon reflected in ripples of water. In that case, the moon’s non-difference is present in each reflection. Likewise, even amid the world’s differences, each thing is connected with non-difference through the words “this,” “that,” “object,” and “thing.” The differences among trees, however, are not false, and the shared idea “forest” is not present in each tree. We do not think of each individual tree as a forest. Therefore this example does not refute the argument; for this reason, the word “each” was used. Moreover—

“Let the greatness belong to one alone, appearing as many; this is simpler than many distinct things shining forth as though they were one.”

gloss.en: because it is pervaded by non-difference

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 1 · Tarka — reasoning about perception, difference, and nonduality
units.label: Kāṇḍa 1 · 36
