units.deva: इदं तावदयं भेदवादी प्रष्टव्यः --- कथमयं व्यावृत्तस्वलक्षणेष्वभेदावभासो ऽनुवृत्तव्यवहारश्च? यदि सादृश्यात्, तदत्यन्तमनन्वितेष्वनुपपन्नम् । अथ व्यावृत्तेरग्रहात् --- को हि गुञ्जाप्रवालादीनां रागव्यावृत्तिमवग्रहीतुं क्षमते --- [क्क्स्_73] इति । तदसत् । व्यावृत्तस्वभावस्य तदग्रहे ग्रहणमेव हि न स्यात् । अथ निश्चयप्रत्यक्षयोरात्मभेदादनिश्चयात् । तदसत्, उभयरूपव्यवहारदर्शनात् । तथा हि --- कालाक्ष्यां गोसामान्यनिबन्धनश्च व्यवहारो गवान्तरव्यावृत्तिश्च दृश्यते । न च गवान्तरव्यावृत्तेरनिश्चये स युज्यते । अथैकार्थक्रियाकारित्वादतत्क्रियाव्यावृत्तेस्तुल्यत्वात् । तदप्यसांप्रतम्, अर्थक्रियाणामपि भेदादतत्क्रियाव्यावृत्तेस्तुल्यत्वायोगात् । नैकसाध्यान्यस्यार्थक्रिया येनातत्कारिव्यावृत्तिस्तुल्या स्यात् । वस्तुस्वभावश्च व्यावृत्तिः प्रतिवस्तुभेदान्न तुल्या । अथास्वभावाः, तेषां कथं तुल्या? अथानादिवासनोपादानो न वस्तुगतविशेषापेक्षः । तदप्ययुक्तम्, नियमात् । कासुचिदेव हि व्यक्तिषु कश्चिदेवावभासः (म्स् ब्; कश्चिदेवाभेदावभासः -- एदितिओन्), स वासनामात्रोपादानत्वे न युज्यते । तस्मात्प्रकृत्यैव केचित्कस्यचिदभेदावमर्शस्य योग्याः केचिन्नेति स्वभावविपरीता भावानां सामर्थ्यातिशया कल्पयितव्याः । तथा सत्येवं गौरवात्कल्पनायाः । एकस्यैवास्तु माहात्म्यं यदेको ऽपि नानेवावभासते (नानेव भासते -- एदितिओन्), लघुत्वात्कल्पनायाः । न तु भिन्नानां ते सामर्थ्यातिशयाः, यदमी अभिन्ना इव भासन्ते (इवावभासन्ते -- एदितिओन्) । भेदव्यवहारश्च (भेदव्यवहाराश्च -- एदितिओन्) यथावभासं भेदवादिनामिवाभेदव्यवहार उपपद्यते (@व्यवहारा उपपद्यन्ते -- एदितिओन्) । तथा हि --- आत्यन्तिकभेदवादिनां यथावभासमभेदव्यवहारः, न यथावस्तु । संसर्गवादिनामपि सामान्यस्यार्थस्यार्थान्तरत्वाद्यथावभासमेव भेदेष्वभेदव्यवहारः । ये ऽप्यनर्थान्तरवादिनः, तेषामपि शबलत्वाद्वस्तुनस्तस्य चानन्वयाद्यथावभासमेवोभयव्यवहारः । न वस्त्वनुपातीति दर्शितमिति । यथानुवृत्तव्यवहारसिद्धिं यथावभासं कथयन्ति बाह्याः । तथैव भेदव्यवहारयोगं वदन्ति वेदान्तविवेकभाजः
units.iast:
idaṃ tāvadayaṃ bhedavādī praṣṭavyaḥ --- kathamayaṃ vyāvṛttasvalakṣaṇeṣvabhedāvabhāso 'nuvṛttavyavahāraśca? yadi sādṛśyāt, tadatyantamananviteṣvanupapannam / atha vyāvṛtteragrahāt --- ko hi guñjāpravālādīnāṃ rāgavyāvṛttimavagrahītuṃ kṣamate --- [kks_73] iti / tadasat / vyāvṛttasvabhāvasya tadagrahe grahaṇameva hi na syāt / atha niścayapratyakṣayorātmabhedādaniścayāt / tadasat, ubhayarūpavyavahāradarśanāt / tathā hi --- kālākṣyāṃ gosāmānyanibandhanaśca vyavahāro gavāntaravyāvṛttiśca dṛśyate / na ca gavāntaravyāvṛtteraniścaye sa yujyate / athaikārthakriyākāritvādatatkriyāvyāvṛttestulyatvāt / tadapyasāṃpratam, arthakriyāṇāmapi bhedādatatkriyāvyāvṛttestulyatvāyogāt / naikasādhyānyasyārthakriyā yenātatkārivyāvṛttistulyā syāt / vastusvabhāvaśca vyāvṛttiḥ prativastubhedānna tulyā / athāsvabhāvāḥ, teṣāṃ kathaṃ tulyā? athānādivāsanopādāno na vastugataviśeṣāpekṣaḥ / tadapyayuktam, niyamāt / kāsucideva hi vyaktiṣu kaścidevāvabhāsaḥ (ms b; kaścidevābhedāvabhāsaḥ -- edition), sa vāsanāmātropādānatve na yujyate / tasmātprakṛtyaiva kecitkasyacidabhedāvamarśasya yogyāḥ kecinneti svabhāvaviparītā bhāvānāṃ sāmarthyātiśayā kalpayitavyāḥ / tathā satyevaṃ gauravātkalpanāyāḥ / ekasyaivāstu māhātmyaṃ yadeko 'pi nānevāvabhāsate (nāneva bhāsate -- edition), laghutvātkalpanāyāḥ / na tu bhinnānāṃ te sāmarthyātiśayāḥ, yadamī abhinnā iva bhāsante (ivāvabhāsante -- edition) /

bhedavyavahāraśca (bhedavyavahārāśca -- edition) yathāvabhāsaṃ bhedavādināmivābhedavyavahāra upapadyate (@vyavahārā upapadyante -- edition) / tathā hi --- ātyantikabhedavādināṃ yathāvabhāsamabhedavyavahāraḥ, na yathāvastu / saṃsargavādināmapi sāmānyasyārthasyārthāntaratvādyathāvabhāsameva bhedeṣvabhedavyavahāraḥ / ye 'pyanarthāntaravādinaḥ, teṣāmapi śabalatvādvastunastasya cānanvayādyathāvabhāsamevobhayavyavahāraḥ / na vastvanupātīti darśitamiti /

yathānuvṛttavyavahārasiddhiṃ yathāvabhāsaṃ kathayanti bāhyāḥ /
tathaiva bhedavyavahārayogaṃ vadanti vedāntavivekabhājaḥ
units.translation:
The proponent of difference should first be asked: how can a common appearance and recurring usage arise among things whose particular natures are entirely distinct? If the answer is “through resemblance,” that makes no sense among things that are wholly unrelated. If the answer is “because their differences are not perceived,” then who is capable of perceiving the color difference between a red guñjā berry and a red coral? That is not sound. If things by nature have distinct particular characters, failure to grasp them would mean there could be no cognition at all.

Perhaps the difference lies in there being two kinds of cognition, determinate and indeterminate. That too is unsound, since both kinds of practical usage are observed. For example, in one context there is usage based on the general nature of cows, and in another there is distinction of one cow from another. The first usage would not make sense if the second distinction were not known.

Perhaps the two kinds of usage are possible because cows share a function, while things that do not have that function are distinguished from them. That is also inappropriate: functions themselves differ, so things that lack a particular function cannot all be equally excluded. The function of one thing is not accomplished by every other thing, and so their exclusion is not the same. Difference is not equal among objects, since their particular natures differ. If difference has no real nature, how can it be the same among them? Perhaps it is produced only by beginningless impressions and does not depend on any specific feature of the objects. That too is unreasonable, because cognition is restricted: only certain individuals produce a particular common appearance, while others do not. This cannot be explained by impressions alone.

Therefore, one must imagine that some objects by their nature are fit for a particular common cognition while others are not, and that things have various powers contrary to their particular natures. But this requires an elaborate construction. It is simpler to say that the one alone has the extraordinary power to appear as many. It is economical to imagine one thing appearing in many ways, rather than many distinct things appearing as one.

Transactions based on difference are also possible according to appearance, just as transactions based on non-difference are possible according to appearance for proponents of difference. Those who hold absolute difference may conduct themselves according to an appearance of non-difference, not according to reality. Those who hold that things are connected likewise treat differences as non-different according to appearance, since they hold that a universal is a separate thing. And even those who say that an object is not other than its features must accept both kinds of usage according to appearance, since the object is variegated and its features do not extend through one another. As has been shown, practical usage does not follow reality itself. Just as externalists explain recurring usage according to appearance, so too those who understand Vedānta explain the possibility of usage based on difference...

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 1
units.deva:
[इति श्रीमण्डनमिश्रविरचितायां ब्रह्मसिद्धौ तर्ककाण्डः समाप्तः ॥ ] ॥ नियोगकाण्डः ॥ [क्क्स्_74] एवं प्रत्यक्षादिविरोधात्कर्मविधिविरोधाच्च श्रुतार्थपरिग्रहे ये मन्यन्ते वेदान्तानामुपचरितार्थत्वं तत्प्रतिबोधनाय विहितः प्रयत्नः । संप्रति तु --- कार्य एवार्थे वेदस्य प्रामाण्यम्, न भूतरूपे । एवं ह्युक्तम् --- ‘चोदनालक्षणो ऽर्थो धर्मःऽ; । चोदनाप्रमाणको वेदार्थ इति यावत् । चोदना च प्रवर्तकं वचनम्, तस्मात्कार्ये ऽर्थे वेदः प्रमाणम् । वेदान्तानामपि तु प्रतिपत्तिकर्तव्यताप्रमाणभाजां तन्मुखेन तदनुगतभूतात्मतत्त्वविषयबोधकत्वम् । अतस्ते ऽपि कार्यनिष्ठतां नातिवर्तन्ते । तथा च कथं तर्हि मन्त्रार्थवादाः सोपनिषत्का इत्याशङ्क्य ‘चोदना हि भूतं भवन्तम्ऽ; इत्याद्युक्तम् । एतदुक्तं भवति --- कार्यमर्थमवगमयन्ती चोदनैव भूतादिकमप्यर्थमवगमयतीति --- ये मन्यन्ते तत्प्रतिबोधनाय प्रयत्यते । तिस्रश्च प्रतिपत्तयो ब्रह्मणि । प्रथमा तावच्छब्दात्, अन्या शब्दात्प्रतिपद्य तत्सन्तानवती ध्यानभावनोपासनादिशब्दवाच्या, अन्या ततो लब्धनिष्पत्तिर्विगलितनिखिलविकल्पा साक्षात्करणरूपा । तत्र प्रथमामधिकृत्योच्यते ---

शब्दाद्यदात्मविज्ञानं तन्न तावद्विधीयते । भवत्यधीतवेदस्य तद्धि कर्मावबोधवत्
units.iast:
[iti śrīmaṇḍanamiśraviracitāyāṃ brahmasiddhau tarkakāṇḍaḥ samāptaḥ //]

//niyogakāṇḍaḥ//

[kks_74] evaṃ pratyakṣādivirodhātkarmavidhivirodhācca śrutārthaparigrahe ye manyante vedāntānāmupacaritārthatvaṃ tatpratibodhanāya vihitaḥ prayatnaḥ / saṃprati tu --- kārya evārthe vedasya prāmāṇyam, na bhūtarūpe / evaṃ hyuktam --- ‘codanālakṣaṇo 'rtho dharmaḥ'; / codanāpramāṇako vedārtha iti yāvat / codanā ca pravartakaṃ vacanam, tasmātkārye 'rthe vedaḥ pramāṇam / vedāntānāmapi tu pratipattikartavyatāpramāṇabhājāṃ tanmukhena tadanugatabhūtātmatattvaviṣayabodhakatvam / ataste 'pi kāryaniṣṭhatāṃ nātivartante / tathā ca kathaṃ tarhi mantrārthavādāḥ sopaniṣatkā ityāśaṅkya ‘codanā hi bhūtaṃ bhavantam'; ityādyuktam / etaduktaṃ bhavati --- kāryamarthamavagamayantī codanaiva bhūtādikamapyarthamavagamayatīti --- ye manyante tatpratibodhanāya prayatyate / tisraśca pratipattayo brahmaṇi / prathamā tāvacchabdāt, anyā śabdātpratipadya tatsantānavatī dhyānabhāvanopāsanādiśabdavācyā, anyā tato labdhaniṣpattirvigalitanikhilavikalpā sākṣātkaraṇarūpā / tatra prathamāmadhikṛtyocyate ---

śabdādyadātmavijñānaṃ tanna tāvadvidhīyate /
bhavatyadhītavedasya taddhi karmāvabodhavat
units.translation:
Thus far, effort has been made to explain the intended meaning of the Upaniṣads to those who think that their meaning is figurative, because it conflicts with perception and other means of knowledge, as well as with injunctions concerning ritual action.

Now, however, some maintain that the Veda is authoritative only about what is to be done, not about what already exists. For it has been said: “Dharma is that which is characterized by an injunction”—that is, the meaning of the Veda is what is established by injunction. An injunction is a statement that prompts action; therefore the Veda is authoritative about what is to be done. The Upaniṣads too, it is held, are authoritative in prescribing acts of understanding, and through those acts they teach the already-existing nature of the Self, which is connected with them. Thus they do not go beyond prescribing actions. One might ask: how, then, do mantras and explanatory passages, including those in the Upaniṣads, have meaning? The reply has already been given: “An injunction makes known what exists, what is coming to be,” and so forth. The point is that an injunction, while making known what is to be done, also makes known objects that already exist or are yet to exist. Those who hold this view will now be instructed.

There are three kinds of apprehension of Brahman. The first comes from words. Another, arising from words and continuing that understanding, is called meditation, contemplative cultivation, or worship. A third is direct realization, which comes to completion through the preceding practice and is free from every conceptual distinction. What follows is about the first kind:

“The knowledge of the Self that arises from words is not, in the first instance, enjoined; for one who has studied the Veda it arises, just as knowledge of ritual arises.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 2
units.deva:
ब्रह्मणो हि प्रमाणान्तरानधिगमनीयरूपत्वाच्छब्दाधिगम्यस्वभावविषयं ज्ञानं विधेयम् । तत्र यच्छब्दादेव ज्ञानं तदविधेयम्, विधिमन्तरेण भावात्कर्मावबोधवत् । यथैव ‘स्वर्गकामो यजेतऽ; इति श्रुतवाक्यस्य वाक्यार्थावबोधस्तद्वाक्यप्रामाण्यादेव भवति, न विध्यन्तरमपेक्षते, तथात्मस्वरूपाभिधायिवाक्यप्रामाण्यादात्मावबोधो विध्यनपेक्षः [क्क्स्_75] संजायते, सति प्रमाणे तत्सामर्थ्येनैव प्रमेयबोधोत्पत्तेः । न खलु सोपकरणे समग्रे प्रमाणे सतीच्छापि पुरुषस्यापेक्ष्यते ज्ञानं प्रति, अनिष्टानामप्यवबोधात्, प्रागेव विधिः । तामेव विधेरनपेक्षतां कर्मावबोधे दर्शयति ---

स्वर्गकामो यजेतेति बोधे ऽस्मिन्न व्यपेक्ष्यते । विधिरन्यो ऽनवस्थानान्नायं कर्मव्यवस्थितेः
units.iast:
brahmaṇo hi pramāṇāntarānadhigamanīyarūpatvācchabdādhigamyasvabhāvaviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ vidheyam / tatra yacchabdādeva jñānaṃ tadavidheyam, vidhimantareṇa bhāvātkarmāvabodhavat / yathaiva ‘svargakāmo yajeta'; iti śrutavākyasya vākyārthāvabodhastadvākyaprāmāṇyādeva bhavati, na vidhyantaramapekṣate, tathātmasvarūpābhidhāyivākyaprāmāṇyādātmāvabodho vidhyanapekṣaḥ [kks_75] saṃjāyate, sati pramāṇe tatsāmarthyenaiva prameyabodhotpatteḥ / na khalu sopakaraṇe samagre pramāṇe satīcchāpi puruṣasyāpekṣyate jñānaṃ prati, aniṣṭānāmapyavabodhāt, prāgeva vidhiḥ /

tāmeva vidheranapekṣatāṃ karmāvabodhe darśayati ---

svargakāmo yajeteti bodhe 'sminna vyapekṣyate /
vidhiranyo 'navasthānānnāyaṃ karmavyavasthiteḥ
units.translation:
Because Brahman has a nature that cannot be known by another means of knowledge, knowledge of that nature, which is accessible through words, is said to be prescribed. But knowledge that arises from the words themselves is not prescribed, since it occurs without an injunction, just as knowledge of a ritual arises. Just as, upon hearing the sentence “One who desires heaven should sacrifice,” one understands its meaning through the authority of that very sentence, without requiring another injunction, so too knowledge of the Self arises without an injunction through the authority of sentences that declare the Self’s nature. When a valid means of knowledge is present, it produces knowledge of its object through its own power. A person’s desire is not even required for knowledge when the complete means and its supporting conditions are present, since people understand even things they do not want to know—much less is an injunction needed.

The author shows the same independence from injunction in the knowledge of ritual:

“In understanding this sentence, ‘One who desires heaven should sacrifice,’ no other injunction is required. Otherwise there would be an infinite regress; this is already established in the case of ritual action.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 3
units.deva:
न कर्मविधिवाक्यार्थज्ञानप्रवृत्तौ विधिरपेक्ष्यते ऽन्यः, न तद्गत एव वा । अन्यस्मिन्ननवस्थादोषात्, तदर्थज्ञाने ऽपि विध्यन्तरस्यापेक्षणीयत्वात्, तद्गतस्य च कर्मविषयत्वेन तद्बोधं विधातुमसामर्थ्यात् । ननु यथैषां ग्रहणे विध्यन्तरमपेक्ष्यते ‘स्वाध्यायो ऽध्येतव्यःऽ; इति, न चानवस्था, तद्वत्तदर्थबोधे ऽपि स्यात् । अस्ति च विधिः --- ‘वेदः कृत्स्नो ऽधिगन्तव्यःऽ; इति । विषम उपन्यासः --- अप्रवृत्तो ऽपि हि स्वाध्यायाध्ययनविधिवाक्याध्ययने पुरुषान्तराधीतात्ततस्तस्य चान्येषां च वाक्यानामध्ययने प्रवर्तते, शाखान्तरीयाङ्गोपसंहार इव श्रवणमात्रात् । न खलु स्वाधीतमेव वाक्यं प्रवर्तयति । यथैकस्तथा पुरुषान्तराण्यपि, अनादित्वाद्वेदवत्तदध्ययनस्यापि । अनवबुद्धार्थस्त्ववबोधविधिर्नावबोधे प्रवर्तयति । तदर्थबोधश्चेद्विध्यपेक्षः, न तत्र स एव प्रवर्तयति, अनवबुद्धार्थत्वात् । इतरेतराश्रयं स्यात् --- तदर्थबोधात्प्रवृत्तिः, प्रवृत्तस्य च तदर्थबोध इति । तस्माद्विध्यन्तरमपेक्षितव्यमित्यनवस्था । न च ‘वेदः कृत्स्नो ऽधिगन्तव्यःऽइत्यपूर्वार्थविधिः । ‘दृष्टो हि तस्यार्थः कर्मावबोधनम्ऽ; इति न्यायप्राप्तो ऽर्थः प्रदर्श्यते । अथाप्येष विधिः, स्वाध्यायाध्ययनविधिनार्थाक्षिप्तमर्थज्ञानं नोच्येत (@ज्ञानमुच्येत -- एदितिओन्, अल्तेर्नतिवे रेअदिन्ग् इन् तत्त्वसमीक्षा), तथापि ब्रह्मस्वरूपाभिधायिवेदवाक्यप्रभवे बोधे न पृथग्विधिरपेक्षितव्यः, कर्मविधिवाक्यवत् । यथैव ‘स्वर्गकामो यजेतऽ; इति सामान्यविधिना सिद्धे नान्यो ऽपेक्ष्यते, अनवस्थानात्, सत्यपि विधावन्यस्यापेक्षणात्, [क्क्स्_76] न चैतद्गत एव, कर्मविषयत्वात् । एवं तत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिपरेष्वपि वाक्येषु न विधिरपेक्षितव्यः, वाक्यसामर्थ्यादेव तत्त्वबोधोत्पादादिति । इतश्च ---

फलं विधेयावगमात्प्रवृत्तिश्चोत्तरा विधेः । अन्योन्यसंश्रयान्नैष शाब्दो बोधः स नो परः
units.iast:
na karmavidhivākyārthajñānapravṛttau vidhirapekṣyate 'nyaḥ, na tadgata eva vā / anyasminnanavasthādoṣāt, tadarthajñāne 'pi vidhyantarasyāpekṣaṇīyatvāt, tadgatasya ca karmaviṣayatvena tadbodhaṃ vidhātumasāmarthyāt /

nanu yathaiṣāṃ grahaṇe vidhyantaramapekṣyate ‘svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ'; iti, na cānavasthā, tadvattadarthabodhe 'pi syāt / asti ca vidhiḥ --- ‘vedaḥ kṛtsno 'dhigantavyaḥ'; iti /

viṣama upanyāsaḥ --- apravṛtto 'pi hi svādhyāyādhyayanavidhivākyādhyayane puruṣāntarādhītāttatastasya cānyeṣāṃ ca vākyānāmadhyayane pravartate, śākhāntarīyāṅgopasaṃhāra iva śravaṇamātrāt / na khalu svādhītameva vākyaṃ pravartayati / yathaikastathā puruṣāntarāṇyapi, anāditvādvedavattadadhyayanasyāpi / anavabuddhārthastvavabodhavidhirnāvabodhe pravartayati / tadarthabodhaścedvidhyapekṣaḥ, na tatra sa eva pravartayati, anavabuddhārthatvāt / itaretarāśrayaṃ syāt --- tadarthabodhātpravṛttiḥ, pravṛttasya ca tadarthabodha iti / tasmādvidhyantaramapekṣitavyamityanavasthā / na ca ‘vedaḥ kṛtsno 'dhigantavyaḥ'ityapūrvārthavidhiḥ / ‘dṛṣṭo hi tasyārthaḥ karmāvabodhanam'; iti nyāyaprāpto 'rthaḥ pradarśyate / athāpyeṣa vidhiḥ, svādhyāyādhyayanavidhinārthākṣiptamarthajñānaṃ nocyeta (@jñānamucyeta -- edition, alternative reading in tattvasamīkṣā), tathāpi brahmasvarūpābhidhāyivedavākyaprabhave bodhe na pṛthagvidhirapekṣitavyaḥ, karmavidhivākyavat / yathaiva ‘svargakāmo yajeta'; iti sāmānyavidhinā siddhe nānyo 'pekṣyate, anavasthānāt, satyapi vidhāvanyasyāpekṣaṇāt, [kks_76] na caitadgata eva, karmaviṣayatvāt / evaṃ tattvapratipattipareṣvapi vākyeṣu na vidhirapekṣitavyaḥ, vākyasāmarthyādeva tattvabodhotpādāditi /

itaśca ---

phalaṃ vidheyāvagamātpravṛttiścottarā vidheḥ /
anyonyasaṃśrayānnaiṣa śābdo bodhaḥ sa no paraḥ
units.translation:
No further injunction is required to bring about the understanding of a ritual injunction’s sentence and the action that follows from that understanding; nor is an injunction contained in that sentence itself required. Otherwise there would be an infinite regress, since another injunction would be needed to understand its meaning as well. And an injunction contained within it could not cause that understanding, since it would itself be an object concerning ritual action and would lack the power to produce comprehension of its own meaning.

Someone may object: just as another injunction is needed for studying the Veda—“One must study one’s own Vedic recension”—yet this does not lead to an infinite regress, so too there may be an injunction for understanding its meaning. There is, after all, the injunction “The entire Veda is to be learned.” The analogy is inapplicable. Even a person who has not yet begun studying studies the Vedic injunction to study, and from that injunction—already learned by someone else—begins studying it, as well as other sentences, simply by hearing them, just as one learns the subsidiary rites of another Vedic branch by hearing about them. It is not only a sentence one has already studied that prompts one to act. The same is true of other people, since the study of the Veda, like the Veda itself, has no beginning.

But an injunction to understand meaning cannot prompt understanding when its own meaning is not yet understood. If understanding the meaning of such an injunction itself depends on an injunction, that same injunction cannot prompt it, because its meaning has not been understood. This would be mutual dependence: understanding its meaning would lead to action, and only after acting would its meaning be understood. Therefore another injunction would have to be assumed, producing an infinite regress.

Nor does “The entire Veda is to be learned” prescribe a previously unknown purpose. It merely states a purpose already established by reasoning: its purpose is to teach the rites. Even if this is an injunction, it need not separately prescribe understanding the meaning, which is already implied by the injunction to study one’s own Vedic text. In any case, no separate injunction is needed for the knowledge produced by Vedic sentences that reveal the nature of Brahman, just as none is needed for the knowledge produced by a ritual injunction. For example, once the general injunction “One who desires heaven should perform a sacrifice” is understood, no other injunction is required; otherwise there would be an infinite regress, since even if one injunction existed, another would still be required. And an injunction contained in that sentence cannot supply it, since the sentence concerns ritual action. Likewise, sentences whose purpose is to convey the truth need no injunction: the knowledge of truth arises from the sentences’ own power.

For this further reason—

“The result is understanding what is enjoined, and action follows the injunction. Because these depend upon one another, this verbal cognition is neither that [understanding] nor a separate cognition.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 4
units.deva:
शब्दादवगम्य विधेयं या प्रवृत्तिः सा विधेः प्रयोजनम्, न तु शब्दप्रभवो विधेयावगम एव, अन्योन्यसंश्रयात् --- अवगते शब्दार्थे प्रवृत्तेः, प्रवृत्तस्य चावगमात् । शब्दार्थबोधादेव वा शब्दार्थबोध इत्यात्माश्रयः । अन्योन्यसंश्रयस्तु तुल्यानुपपत्तित्वादुक्तः । यस्तु तत्त्वावबोधपराद्वाक्यात्तत्त्वावबोधः, नासौ शब्दार्थबोधात्पराचीनः, किन्तु स एवेति । अपि च

जाते बोधे न प्रवर्त्यो नतरां खल्वबोधके । शब्दे न (शब्देन -- एदितिओन्) निश्चये तस्मादन्यस्मादन्यवाञ्छनम्
units.iast:
śabdādavagamya vidheyaṃ yā pravṛttiḥ sā vidheḥ prayojanam, na tu śabdaprabhavo vidheyāvagama eva, anyonyasaṃśrayāt --- avagate śabdārthe pravṛtteḥ, pravṛttasya cāvagamāt / śabdārthabodhādeva vā śabdārthabodha ityātmāśrayaḥ / anyonyasaṃśrayastu tulyānupapattitvāduktaḥ / yastu tattvāvabodhaparādvākyāttattvāvabodhaḥ, nāsau śabdārthabodhātparācīnaḥ, kintu sa eveti /

api ca

jāte bodhe na pravartyo natarāṃ khalvabodhake /
śabde na (śabdena -- edition) niścaye tasmādanyasmādanyavāñchanam
units.translation:
The purpose of an injunction is the action to be performed after its meaning has been understood through words, not the understanding of what is to be done that arises from the words themselves. Otherwise there would be mutual dependence: action follows understanding the meaning of the words, and understanding follows acting. Or, if understanding the meaning of a word came from another understanding of that same word, it would depend on itself. Mutual dependence has already been rejected because both directions are equally untenable. But understanding truth from a sentence whose purpose is to reveal truth does not come after understanding the word’s meaning; it is that very understanding itself. Moreover—

“When understanding has arisen, one is not someone who must be prompted to act; all the more so when the word does not reveal meaning. If certainty comes from something else, one would seek something else.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 5
units.deva: उदपादि चेत् ‘सदेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदेकमेवाद्वितीयम्ऽ; इत्युपक्रमात् ‘तत्त्वमसिऽइत्यन्ताद्वाक्यादात्मतत्त्वावबोधः, पदानां परस्परान्वितार्थत्वात्, किमन्यद्विधिः करिष्यति? न प्रवृत्त एव प्रवर्त्यः । अथ पदार्थसमन्वयमात्रान्न तत्त्वबोधोत्पादः, सुतरामप्रवर्त्यः । शाब्दस्य तत्त्वावबोधस्यासंभवात् । स्यादेतत् --- उत्पन्ने ऽपि तत्त्वावभासे शब्दात्, निश्चये प्रवर्त्यः ‘एवमिदम्ऽ; इति । तन्न । यदि तस्माच्छब्दान्निश्चयः, स जात एव । अथान्यतो निश्चयः, अन्यवाञ्छनं प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षा, न तत्र तत्त्वनिश्चयनिबन्धनं शब्दः स्यात् । एवं तावन्न तत्त्वनिश्चयाय विधिरर्थ्यते । अथाविवक्षितार्थत्वनिवृत्त्यै प्रार्थ्यते विधिः । अर्थो ज्ञातव्य इत्युक्ते ज्ञेयः स्यान्नाविवक्षितः
units.iast:
udapādi cet ‘sadeva somyedamagra āsīdekamevādvitīyam'; ityupakramāt ‘tattvamasi'ityantādvākyādātmatattvāvabodhaḥ, padānāṃ parasparānvitārthatvāt, kimanyadvidhiḥ kariṣyati? na pravṛtta eva pravartyaḥ / atha padārthasamanvayamātrānna tattvabodhotpādaḥ, sutarāmapravartyaḥ / śābdasya tattvāvabodhasyāsaṃbhavāt / syādetat --- utpanne 'pi tattvāvabhāse śabdāt, niścaye pravartyaḥ ‘evamidam'; iti / tanna / yadi tasmācchabdānniścayaḥ, sa jāta eva / athānyato niścayaḥ, anyavāñchanaṃ pramāṇāntarāpekṣā, na tatra tattvaniścayanibandhanaṃ śabdaḥ syāt / evaṃ tāvanna tattvaniścayāya vidhirarthyate /

athāvivakṣitārthatvanivṛttyai prārthyate vidhiḥ /
artho jñātavya ityukte jñeyaḥ syānnāvivakṣitaḥ
units.translation:
If knowledge of the nature of the Self has already arisen from the sentence beginning “Dear one, in the beginning this was Existence alone, one without a second” and ending “You are that,” because the words are connected with one another, what more could an injunction do? One who has not acted cannot be prompted to act if the action has already begun. If understanding the connection among the words alone does not produce knowledge of truth, then all the more is a person not someone to be prompted, since verbal knowledge of truth would be impossible.

Someone may say: even when an appearance of truth has arisen from the words, the person must be prompted to establish certainty, “This is so.” No. If certainty arises from those words, then it has already arisen. If certainty is to come from elsewhere, then one must seek another means of knowledge, and the words would not be the basis for certainty about truth. Thus an injunction is not needed to establish certainty about truth. Perhaps an injunction is desired to prevent the meaning from being left unintended. But when it is said that an object is to be known, it becomes something to be known; it cannot be left unintended…

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 6
units.deva: [क्क्स्_77] यदपि मतम् --- सत्यपि वाक्यादर्थोपप्लवे तात्पर्यं दुर्लभम्, भूतार्थपरस्य वैयर्थ्यात् । सांशयिकत्वं वा, अतात्पर्यस्यापि दर्शनाज्जपमन्त्रेषु । विधौ तु सत्यर्थज्ञानस्य चोदितत्वान्नार्थो ऽविवक्षितो भवितुमर्हति । तस्माद्विवक्षितार्थत्वाय विधिः प्रार्थ्यः । तद्वार्तमर्थपरता शब्दानां लोकवेदयोः । ‘अविशिष्टस्तु वाक्यार्थऽ; इत्युत्सर्गवती यतः
units.iast:
[kks_77] yadapi matam --- satyapi vākyādarthopaplave tātparyaṃ durlabham, bhūtārthaparasya vaiyarthyāt / sāṃśayikatvaṃ vā, atātparyasyāpi darśanājjapamantreṣu / vidhau tu satyarthajñānasya coditatvānnārtho 'vivakṣito bhavitumarhati / tasmādvivakṣitārthatvāya vidhiḥ prārthyaḥ /

tadvārtamarthaparatā śabdānāṃ lokavedayoḥ /
‘aviśiṣṭastu vākyārtha'; ityutsargavatī yataḥ
units.translation: Someone may argue: even if a sentence conveys an object, its intended purport is hard to establish, because a statement about an already existent thing would be pointless. Or it might be uncertain, since one sees statements without intended purport in mantras used for recitation. But when there is an injunction, and understanding the truth of the object is enjoined, its meaning cannot be unintended. Therefore an injunction must be assumed to establish that the words have an intended meaning. This is badly argued: the words’ meaningfulness is equally established in ordinary and Vedic usage, since the general rule is that a sentence has an undifferentiated meaning…

gloss.en: because it concerns an already existent object
so that the meaning is intended

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 7
units.deva:
औत्सर्गिकः शब्दानामर्थं प्रति शेषभावः । निमित्तान्तरात्तु स्वरूपप्रधानत्वमविवक्षितार्थत्वमपवादो लोके । तथा वेदे ऽपि, लोकावगम्यत्वाच्छब्दसामर्थ्यस्य । तदुक्तम् --- ‘अविशिष्टस्तु वाक्यार्थःऽ; इति । अपि च

दृष्टार्थता च स्वाध्यायविधेरत्र न भिद्यते । भवेदितरथा कृत्स्नः स विध्यर्थो ऽविवक्षितः
units.iast:
autsargikaḥ śabdānāmarthaṃ prati śeṣabhāvaḥ / nimittāntarāttu svarūpapradhānatvamavivakṣitārthatvamapavādo loke / tathā vede 'pi, lokāvagamyatvācchabdasāmarthyasya / taduktam --- ‘aviśiṣṭastu vākyārthaḥ'; iti /

api ca

dṛṣṭārthatā ca svādhyāyavidheratra na bhidyate /
bhaveditarathā kṛtsnaḥ sa vidhyartho 'vivakṣitaḥ
units.translation:
By default, words are subordinate to their meanings; only because of some other cause, as an exception, do they become centered on their own form and have no intended meaning in ordinary usage. The same applies to the Veda, since the power of words is established by ordinary usage. As has been said: “The meaning of a sentence is not restricted [to an injunction].” Moreover—

“The directly visible purpose of the injunction to study one’s own Veda does not differ here. Otherwise, the entire Veda would be left without an intended meaning and its injunction would be pointless.”

gloss.en: being centered on their own form
because it is understood through ordinary usage
of the injunction to study one's own Veda

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 8
units.deva: यथैव कर्मविधीनां ‘दृष्टो हि तस्यार्थः कर्मावबोधनम्ऽ; इति नाविवक्षितार्थानामध्ययनात्फलान्तरकल्पना तथा दृष्टत्वादात्मतत्त्वावबोधस्य वेदान्तानाम् । न च भूतार्थप्रतिपत्तौ वैयर्थ्यमिति वक्ष्यते । प्रतिपत्तिविधौ च तुल्यम् । अवश्यं चैतदेवं विज्ञेयम् । अन्यथा सह विधायकेन कृत्स्नस्याविवक्षितार्थता स्यात् । यतो विधायकशब्दनिबन्धनमन्येषां विवक्षितार्थत्वम्, विधायकस्य तु न तन्निबन्धनमस्ति । एवं च तस्याविवक्षितार्थत्वे इतरे ऽपि तथा स्युः । अथ विधायकः प्रकृत्या दृष्टार्थत्वेन चार्थपरः, इतरे ऽपि तथेति व्यर्थो ऽसौ विधिः । ज्ञानस्य पुरुषार्थत्वसिद्धये विधिरिष्यते । सर्वत्र पुरुषार्थत्वं विधेरित्यप्यपेशलम्
units.iast:
yathaiva karmavidhīnāṃ ‘dṛṣṭo hi tasyārthaḥ karmāvabodhanam'; iti nāvivakṣitārthānāmadhyayanātphalāntarakalpanā tathā dṛṣṭatvādātmatattvāvabodhasya vedāntānām / na ca bhūtārthapratipattau vaiyarthyamiti vakṣyate / pratipattividhau ca tulyam / avaśyaṃ caitadevaṃ vijñeyam / anyathā saha vidhāyakena kṛtsnasyāvivakṣitārthatā syāt / yato vidhāyakaśabdanibandhanamanyeṣāṃ vivakṣitārthatvam, vidhāyakasya tu na tannibandhanamasti / evaṃ ca tasyāvivakṣitārthatve itare 'pi tathā syuḥ / atha vidhāyakaḥ prakṛtyā dṛṣṭārthatvena cārthaparaḥ, itare 'pi tatheti vyartho 'sau vidhiḥ /

jñānasya puruṣārthatvasiddhaye vidhiriṣyate /
sarvatra puruṣārthatvaṃ vidherityapyapeśalam
units.translation: For injunctions concerning ritual action, it is said that their purpose is directly seen: they teach the action. One therefore does not imagine some further result from studying words whose meaning is not intended. Likewise, the purpose of the Upaniṣads is directly seen in the understanding of the Self’s nature. As will be explained, there is no pointlessness in understanding an already existent reality. The same holds for an injunction to understand. This must certainly be understood; otherwise, apart from the injunction itself, every word would have an unintended meaning. The other words count as intended because they are connected with an injunctive word, while the injunction itself is not marked in that way. If it too is taken to have no intended meaning, then the others would be unintended as well. But if the injunction is meaningful by its nature and because its purpose is directly seen, then so are the other words; the injunction would be pointless. An injunction is accepted in order to establish knowledge as a human good. Yet it is not persuasive to claim that every injunction serves a human good…

gloss.en: of words whose meaning is not intended
of understanding the truth of the Self
in understanding an already existent reality
because its purpose is directly seen
to establish it as a human good

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 9
units.deva: विध्यधीनः पुरुषार्थसाधनतावबोधः, तच्छब्दतो लब्धजन्मनो ऽप्यात्मतत्त्वावबोधस्य पुरुषार्थसाधनत्वावगमो विधेरित्येतदपि न शोभनम् । ज्ञेयाभिव्याप्तितो यस्मान्न विज्ञानात्फलान्तरम् । इष्यते मोक्ष इति चेत्साध्यस्तत्त्वच्युतेर्न सः
units.iast:
vidhyadhīnaḥ puruṣārthasādhanatāvabodhaḥ, tacchabdato labdhajanmano 'pyātmatattvāvabodhasya puruṣārthasādhanatvāvagamo vidherityetadapi na śobhanam /

jñeyābhivyāptito yasmānna vijñānātphalāntaram /
iṣyate mokṣa iti cetsādhyastattvacyuterna saḥ
units.translation: It is not reasonable to say that knowledge of truth is a means to a human goal only because an injunction makes it so, even though knowledge of the Self’s nature arises from words. For liberation is desired as a result distinct from knowledge, but if it must be accomplished, it is no longer the truth [that liberation is the Self].

gloss.en: understanding that it is a means to a human goal
of knowledge of the truth of the Self
understanding that it is a means to a human goal
because what is to be known is fully grasped
because that would depart from the truth

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 10
units.deva:
[क्क्स्_78] ज्ञानस्य हि दृष्टमेव फलम् --- ज्ञात्रा ज्ञेयाभिव्याप्तिः, ज्ञातारं प्रति तस्य प्रकाशनम् (प्रकाशता -- एदितिओन्) --- न त्वदृष्टं कालान्तरभावि, यदर्थो विधिः स्यात् । स्यादेतत् --- आत्मज्ञानस्य फलान्तरमपीष्यते मोक्षः । तन्न, असाध्यत्वात् । न हेतुजन्यो ऽसौ मोक्षः, तत्त्वच्युतेः । कार्यत्वे विनाशात्तस्य पुनःसंसारात् । आत्यन्तिकी च संसारनिवृत्तिर्मोक्ष इत्युच्यते । ननु कार्यो ऽपि नाशो न नश्यति । सत्यम्, भावरूपं तु मोक्षं निरतिशयानन्दलक्षणं निरतिशयैश्वर्यलक्षणं चाभिप्रेत्यैतदुच्यते, भावस्य कार्यस्य विनाशेनाविनाभावात् । आगामिशरीरेन्द्रियबुद्धिसंयोगाभावस्य प्रागभावस्य कार्यत्वमनुपपन्नमेव । बन्धहेतुनिवृत्तिस्तु यद्यपि कार्या, कार्यत्वे ऽपि च नास्या अनित्यत्वप्रसङ्गः, तथापि नासौ तत्त्वज्ञानात्पृथगिति न तेन साध्या । अविद्या हि बन्धहेतुः, तत्त्वज्ञानोदय एव च तन्निवृत्तिः । अथवा ‘परं ज्योतिरुपसंपद्य स्वेन रूपेणावतिष्ठतेऽ; इति स्वरूपस्थितिर्मुक्तिरुक्ता । साध्यत्वे च न स्वरूपस्थितिः स्यात् । अतो मोक्षत्वाच्च्यवेत । यत्तु --- ‘न स (न च --एदितिओन्) पुनरावर्ततेऽ; इति श्रुतेः प्रामाण्यात्कार्यस्यापि मोक्षस्य नित्यत्वमिति, दृष्टविपरीतमपि तदाश्रीयेत, अनन्यगतित्वे श्रुतेः । यदा तु विदितात्मतत्त्वस्याद्वयं विशुद्धप्रकाशमात्मानं पश्यतः समुत्खातायामनवयवेनाविद्यायां हेत्वभावात्पुनर्बन्धस्यासंभाव्यत्वात्प्राप्तमेवार्थं वर्तमानापदेशादनुवदति श्रुतिरर्थवादत्वेन, तदा कुतस्तत्प्रामाण्यादनन्तफलत्वम्? तथा हि --- वर्तमानापदेशादेव नापुनरावृत्तिः साध्यत्वेनावगम्यते । न च कामोपबन्धो ऽस्ति, यतः साध्यता गम्येत । तस्मादर्थवादः । अर्थवादादपि च या फलकल्पना, सापि ज्ञाने ज्ञेयतत्त्वावभासदृष्टफलनिराकाङ्क्षे ऽनुपपन्ना । पुरुषार्थता चास्य वक्ष्यत इति । अन्ये पुनराहुः ---

विधेर्विना कार्यशून्यं भूतार्थमनुवादकम् । वचः स्यादनुवादश्च प्रमाणान्तरगोचरे
units.iast:
[kks_78] jñānasya hi dṛṣṭameva phalam --- jñātrā jñeyābhivyāptiḥ, jñātāraṃ prati tasya prakāśanam (prakāśatā -- edition) --- na tvadṛṣṭaṃ kālāntarabhāvi, yadartho vidhiḥ syāt / syādetat --- ātmajñānasya phalāntaramapīṣyate mokṣaḥ / tanna, asādhyatvāt / na hetujanyo 'sau mokṣaḥ, tattvacyuteḥ / kāryatve vināśāttasya punaḥsaṃsārāt / ātyantikī ca saṃsāranivṛttirmokṣa ityucyate / nanu kāryo 'pi nāśo na naśyati / satyam, bhāvarūpaṃ tu mokṣaṃ niratiśayānandalakṣaṇaṃ niratiśayaiśvaryalakṣaṇaṃ cābhipretyaitaducyate, bhāvasya kāryasya vināśenāvinābhāvāt / āgāmiśarīrendriyabuddhisaṃyogābhāvasya prāgabhāvasya kāryatvamanupapannameva / bandhahetunivṛttistu yadyapi kāryā, kāryatve 'pi ca nāsyā anityatvaprasaṅgaḥ, tathāpi nāsau tattvajñānātpṛthagiti na tena sādhyā / avidyā hi bandhahetuḥ, tattvajñānodaya eva ca tannivṛttiḥ /

athavā ‘paraṃ jyotirupasaṃpadya svena rūpeṇāvatiṣṭhate'; iti svarūpasthitirmuktiruktā / sādhyatve ca na svarūpasthitiḥ syāt / ato mokṣatvāccyaveta / yattu --- ‘na sa (na ca --edition) punarāvartate'; iti śruteḥ prāmāṇyātkāryasyāpi mokṣasya nityatvamiti, dṛṣṭaviparītamapi tadāśrīyeta, ananyagatitve śruteḥ / yadā tu viditātmatattvasyādvayaṃ viśuddhaprakāśamātmānaṃ paśyataḥ samutkhātāyāmanavayavenāvidyāyāṃ hetvabhāvātpunarbandhasyāsaṃbhāvyatvātprāptamevārthaṃ vartamānāpadeśādanuvadati śrutirarthavādatvena, tadā kutastatprāmāṇyādanantaphalatvam? tathā hi --- vartamānāpadeśādeva nāpunarāvṛttiḥ sādhyatvenāvagamyate / na ca kāmopabandho 'sti, yataḥ sādhyatā gamyeta / tasmādarthavādaḥ / arthavādādapi ca yā phalakalpanā, sāpi jñāne jñeyatattvāvabhāsadṛṣṭaphalanirākāṅkṣe 'nupapannā / puruṣārthatā cāsya vakṣyata iti /

anye punarāhuḥ ---

vidhervinā kāryaśūnyaṃ bhūtārthamanuvādakam /
vacaḥ syādanuvādaśca pramāṇāntaragocare
units.translation:
The visible result of knowledge is that its object is fully manifest to the knower; it is not an unseen result to be realized at some later time, for which an injunction would be needed. Someone may object that knowledge of the Self has another result too: liberation. That is not so, since liberation is not something to be produced. It is not caused by another thing, because that would change its nature. If it were produced, it would perish and lead to renewed worldly existence. Liberation is defined as the complete cessation of worldly existence. Someone may say that even an effect such as destruction does not itself perish. That may be true, but the intended liberation here is a positive state, characterized by unsurpassed bliss and sovereignty; a positive, produced state is impermanent. The absence of a future conjunction of body, senses, and intellect cannot be an effect, since it is a prior absence. The removal of the cause of bondage may be produced and yet not be impermanent, but it is not different from knowledge of reality and is therefore not produced by it as a separate result. Ignorance is the cause of bondage; its removal occurs precisely when knowledge of reality arises.

Alternatively, scripture defines liberation as abiding in one’s own nature: “Having reached the supreme light, he remains in his own form.” If that were something to be produced, it would not be abiding in one’s own nature; it would no longer be liberation. Someone may say that scripture’s authority in “He does not return” establishes that even a produced liberation is eternal. That would mean accepting something contrary to what is observed simply on the basis of scripture, even though its subject matter lies nowhere else. But when one who knows the Self sees it as nondual and pure illumination, ignorance is completely uprooted and there is no cause from which bondage could arise again. The text, in the present tense, reports this already attained fact as praise, rather than enjoining a result to be produced. The present-tense statement itself does not show that non-return is something to be attained, and there is no desire stated from which a produced result could be inferred. It is therefore an explanatory passage. Even if a fruit is imagined from such a passage, it is not plausible when knowledge already directly manifests its object and has no need of another result. The human value of this knowledge will be explained.

Others say:

“Without an injunction, a statement about an existent thing would be merely repetition;
and repetition is valid only for what is already within the scope of another means of knowledge.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 11
units.deva: [क्क्स्_79] तत्प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षं प्रामाण्यमतिवर्तते । मानान्तरस्याविषये विध्यर्थे तु प्रतिष्ठितम्
units.iast:
[kks_79] tatpramāṇāntarāpekṣaṃ prāmāṇyamativartate /
mānāntarasyāviṣaye vidhyarthe tu pratiṣṭhitam
units.translation: Its validity goes beyond dependence on another means of knowledge; but the meaning of an injunction, which lies outside the scope of another means, is firmly established.

gloss.en: dependent on another means of knowledge
in the meaning of an injunction

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 12
units.deva: अनपेक्षं प्रमाणत्वमश्नुते कर्मवाक्यवत् । परप्रवृत्त्यभावे ऽपि प्रामाण्यायैव तद्विधिः
units.iast:
anapekṣaṃ pramāṇatvamaśnute karmavākyavat /
parapravṛttyabhāve 'pi prāmāṇyāyaiva tadvidhiḥ
units.translation: It is independent and valid like a sentence prescribing ritual action. Even when it does not prompt another person to act, an injunction is accepted only to establish its validity.

gloss.en: like a sentence about ritual action
in the absence of prompting another person's action

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 13
units.deva:
विधिमन्तरेण न कार्योपदेशप्रतीतिः । यथावस्थितं वस्तु तद्विधस्यानुवादमात्रत्वं गम्यते । अनुवादश्च प्रमाणान्तरविषय इति तदपेक्षो भूतार्थो नार्थ उच्यत इति सापेक्षत्वादप्रामाण्यम् । विध्यर्थस्य तु प्रमाणान्तराविषयत्वात्तन्निष्ठमनपेक्षं प्रमाणं कर्मविधिवाक्यवत् । प्रमाणान्तराविषयश्च विध्यर्थः । न हि ‘कुरुऽइति शब्दज्ञानादन्यतः प्रतीतिः । एवं च सति तत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिपरे वाक्ये यद्यपि वाक्यार्थबोधात्पराचीना प्रवृत्तिः, विधिफलं नास्ति । प्रामाण्यायैव तु विधिनिष्ठत्वमेषितव्यमिति । अत्रोच्यते ---

प्रमाणान्तरयातार्थभावः किमनुवादता । उत भूतार्थता तत्र सिद्धार्थमपि यद्वचः
units.iast:
vidhimantareṇa na kāryopadeśapratītiḥ / yathāvasthitaṃ vastu tadvidhasyānuvādamātratvaṃ gamyate / anuvādaśca pramāṇāntaraviṣaya iti tadapekṣo bhūtārtho nārtha ucyata iti sāpekṣatvādaprāmāṇyam / vidhyarthasya tu pramāṇāntarāviṣayatvāttanniṣṭhamanapekṣaṃ pramāṇaṃ karmavidhivākyavat / pramāṇāntarāviṣayaśca vidhyarthaḥ / na hi ‘kuru'iti śabdajñānādanyataḥ pratītiḥ / evaṃ ca sati tattvapratipattipare vākye yadyapi vākyārthabodhātparācīnā pravṛttiḥ, vidhiphalaṃ nāsti / prāmāṇyāyaiva tu vidhiniṣṭhatvameṣitavyamiti / atrocyate ---

pramāṇāntarayātārthabhāvaḥ kimanuvādatā /
uta bhūtārthatā tatra siddhārthamapi yadvacaḥ
units.translation:
Without an injunction, there is no understanding of an instruction about what is to be done. A sentence that merely states an object as it is understood is seen to be a restatement; and a restatement concerns an object known by another means of knowledge. Thus a sentence about an already existent thing depends on another means and is invalid for that reason. But an injunction concerns an object not known by another means, so a sentence whose meaning is an injunction is independent and valid, like a sentence prescribing a ritual. The meaning of an injunction is beyond the scope of other means of knowledge: the verbal cognition “Do it” is not produced from anything else.

In that case, even if a sentence intended to teach truth prompts no action until after its meaning is understood, it still has no result as an injunction. Yet it must be taken as centered on an injunction, if only to make it valid. The reply is:

“If an object is already known by another means, does its statement merely repeat that knowledge? Or, in that case, what is an already established sentence that states what exists?”

gloss.en: understanding an instruction about what is to be done
within the scope of another means
a statement about an existent object
of the meaning of an injunction
like a sentence enjoining ritual action
the fact that an object has been reached by another means
a statement of an existent fact

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 14
units.deva: न मानान्तरलब्धार्थतया तस्यावबोधकम् । न तत्सापेक्षमेषा चेदभिप्रेतानुवादता
units.iast:
na mānāntaralabdhārthatayā tasyāvabodhakam /
na tatsāpekṣameṣā cedabhipretānuvādatā
units.translation: A statement does not make its object known merely because that object has been obtained through another means of knowledge. If this is intended as a restatement, then it is dependent.

gloss.en: merely because the meaning was obtained through another means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 15
units.deva:
कः पुनरनुवादः --- अधिगमान्तरसंभिन्नार्थत्वम्, मानान्तरेणाधिगत इति प्रतिपादनम्, आहोस्विद्भूतार्थतामात्रम्? तत्र पूर्वस्मिन् कल्पे भवत्वधिगमान्तरसंभिन्नार्थं सापेक्षम् । यत्तु भूतार्थमपि न मानान्तराधिगत इति बोधयति न तदनुवादकम्, न सापेक्षम्, पूर्वाधिगमसंस्पर्शेन प्रतिपत्तेरभावात् । अथापरः कल्पः ---

सापेक्षतायाः को हेतुः शुद्धा सिद्धार्थता यदि । प्रमाणान्तरसंभेदस्तद्व्यपेक्षणकारणम्
units.iast:
kaḥ punaranuvādaḥ --- adhigamāntarasaṃbhinnārthatvam, mānāntareṇādhigata iti pratipādanam, āhosvidbhūtārthatāmātram? tatra pūrvasmin kalpe bhavatvadhigamāntarasaṃbhinnārthaṃ sāpekṣam / yattu bhūtārthamapi na mānāntarādhigata iti bodhayati na tadanuvādakam, na sāpekṣam, pūrvādhigamasaṃsparśena pratipatterabhāvāt /

athāparaḥ kalpaḥ ---

sāpekṣatāyāḥ ko hetuḥ śuddhā siddhārthatā yadi /
pramāṇāntarasaṃbhedastadvyapekṣaṇakāraṇam
units.translation:
What is meant by “restatement”? Is it that the object is blended with another cognition, or that the statement presents it as already known by another means of knowledge, or is it merely that the object is something existent? In the first case, let a statement whose object is blended with another cognition be dependent. But a statement that makes known something existent without its having been known by another means is not a restatement and is not dependent, since its cognition does not involve prior knowledge. Or perhaps the second interpretation is intended:

“If the mere statement of an established fact is independent, what is the reason for dependence? Blending with another means of knowledge would be the cause of dependence.”

gloss.en: an object blended with another cognition
the mere fact of being existent
an object blended with another cognition
mixture with another means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 16
units.deva:
अनृधीप्रभवे नास्ति भूतार्थे ऽपि स वैदिके । भूतार्थमात्रं चेदनुवादता न सापेक्षत्वहेतुरस्ति । न भूतार्थतैव सापेक्षत्वहेतुः, भूतार्थयोरपि प्रत्यक्षानुमानयोरनपेक्षत्वात् । तस्माद्भूतार्थे ऽभूतार्थे वाधिगमान्तरसंस्पर्शः प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षाहेतुः, स्मृतौ दर्शनात् । सा ह्यधिगमान्तरसंभिन्नार्थेति [क्क्स्_80] तत्साधनमपेक्षते । एवं च पुरुषबुद्धिप्रभवं भूतार्थमभूतार्थं वा वचो भवति सापेक्षम् । ततो हि तत्संभिन्न एवार्थे प्रत्ययः, न त्वनपेक्षितपूर्वाधिगमः स्वातन्त्र्येणार्थे । यथोक्तम् --- ‘अपि च पौरुषेयाद्वचनाद् ‘एवमयं पुरुषो वेदऽइति भवति प्रत्ययः, न ‘एवमर्थःऽ; इतिऽ; । अपुरुषबुद्धिप्रभवत्वाद्वेदवचसि भूतार्थे ऽपि न सापेक्षत्वहेतुः, पुरुषसंबन्धकृतत्वात्पूर्वाधिगमसंभेदस्य । स्यादेतत् --- अपौरुषेये ऽपि भूतार्थे तद्विषये प्रमाणान्तरस्य संभवात्तदपेक्षा । तथा हि --- संभवति प्रमाणान्तरे तद्विषये तद्विसंवादो ऽपि शङ्क्येत । तस्मात्तदभावाय तत्संवादो ऽपेक्षणीयः । असंभवति तु कार्ये ऽर्थे न कुतश्चिद्विसंवादाशङ्केति नापेक्ष्यमस्ति । अत्रोच्यते ---
न च संभवमात्रेण तदपेक्षावकल्पते
units.iast:
anṛdhīprabhave nāsti bhūtārthe 'pi sa vaidike /
bhūtārthamātraṃ cedanuvādatā na sāpekṣatvaheturasti / na bhūtārthataiva sāpekṣatvahetuḥ, bhūtārthayorapi pratyakṣānumānayoranapekṣatvāt / tasmādbhūtārthe 'bhūtārthe vādhigamāntarasaṃsparśaḥ pramāṇāntarāpekṣāhetuḥ, smṛtau darśanāt / sā hyadhigamāntarasaṃbhinnārtheti [kks_80] tatsādhanamapekṣate / evaṃ ca puruṣabuddhiprabhavaṃ bhūtārthamabhūtārthaṃ vā vaco bhavati sāpekṣam / tato hi tatsaṃbhinna evārthe pratyayaḥ, na tvanapekṣitapūrvādhigamaḥ svātantryeṇārthe / yathoktam --- ‘api ca pauruṣeyādvacanād ‘evamayaṃ puruṣo veda'iti bhavati pratyayaḥ, na ‘evamarthaḥ'; iti'; / apuruṣabuddhiprabhavatvādvedavacasi bhūtārthe 'pi na sāpekṣatvahetuḥ, puruṣasaṃbandhakṛtatvātpūrvādhigamasaṃbhedasya /

syādetat --- apauruṣeye 'pi bhūtārthe tadviṣaye pramāṇāntarasya saṃbhavāttadapekṣā / tathā hi --- saṃbhavati pramāṇāntare tadviṣaye tadvisaṃvādo 'pi śaṅkyeta / tasmāttadabhāvāya tatsaṃvādo 'pekṣaṇīyaḥ / asaṃbhavati tu kārye 'rthe na kutaścidvisaṃvādāśaṅketi nāpekṣyamasti / atrocyate ---
na ca saṃbhavamātreṇa tadapekṣāvakalpate
units.translation:
Even when a Vedic statement concerns something already existent, its dependence does not arise because it was produced by a human intellect. If it merely restated an existent fact, that alone would not be a reason for dependence. Nor is the fact that something is already existent itself a reason for dependence, since perception and inference, even when they concern existent things, are independent. Therefore, whether the object is existent or not, dependence on another means of knowledge arises only when the cognition is connected with a prior cognition, as is observed in memory. Memory concerns an object mixed with another cognition and therefore depends on that prior means. Accordingly, a statement arising from a human intellect—whether it concerns something existent or not—is dependent. It produces cognition only about an object already connected with prior knowledge, not independently about an object whose prior apprehension is not required. As has been said: “From a human statement, one forms the cognition, ‘This person knows in this way,’ not ‘The object is this way.’” Because Vedic statements do not arise from a human intellect, even when they concern existing things, they are not dependent for that reason; the mixture with prior knowledge is caused by their connection with a person.

One might object: even an unauthored statement concerning something existent depends on another means of knowledge, because another means could be possible for that object. For if another means is possible, one might suspect that it could disagree with the statement. To prevent that possibility of disagreement, one must check whether the two agree. But if the object is something to be done and no other means of knowledge can reach it, there can be no suspicion of disagreement, so no check is needed.

The reply is:

“Dependence on that means of knowledge cannot be established merely because it is possible.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 17
units.deva:
विशेषो न हि गम्येत सापेक्षत्वे तदा तयोः । द्वयोरेकविषयसंभवे कुत एतत् --- शब्दस्तदपेक्षः, न पुनस्तत्प्रमाणान्तरं शब्दापेक्षं स्यादिति? यदि शब्दः प्रमाणान्तराधिगतविषयो लोके दृष्ट इति, प्रमाणान्तरस्याविषये तर्हि नतरां प्रामाण्यं तस्य भवति । प्रमाणान्तरविषये हि प्रमाणान्तरसंभवादपि तावत्स्यात्, अन्यत्र तदभावाद् दुर्लभं तत् । अथ पौरुषेयत्वकारिता लोकवचसां प्रमाणान्तराधिगतार्थता, न शब्दसामर्थ्यकारिता । शब्दस्य प्रमाणान्तरासंभिन्न एवार्थे सामर्थ्यम् । न तर्हि प्रमाणान्तरसंभवाच्छब्द एव सापेक्षः, तदपि शब्दसंभवाच्छब्दापेक्षं स्यात् । किमतस्तस्य सापेक्षत्वेन? अप्रमाणं स्यात् । न शब्दस्य तत्रापेक्षा युज्यते । सति हि तस्य प्रामाण्ये तत्संवादविसंवादावपेक्ष्येयाताम् । अथ शब्दस्याप्रामाण्यान्न तत् शब्दापेक्षया प्रमाणम् । प्रमाणमेव, अनपेक्षत्वात् । शब्दस्याप्रामाण्यं कुतः? प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षत्वात् । तस्य च प्रामाण्यमनपेक्षत्वात्, अनपेक्षत्वं च शब्दस्याप्रामाण्यादितरेतराश्रयम् । प्रमाणे हि शब्दे तद्विषये संभवति तदपि सापेक्षं स्यात्तत्संभव इव शब्दः, विशेषाभावात् । [क्क्स्_81] अथ शब्दसंभवे ऽपि न तत्सापेक्षम् । तत्संभवे ऽपि न शब्दस्य सापेक्षता, विशेषाभावात् । अपि च
प्रत्यक्षानुमयोरेवं वृत्तेरन्योन्यगोचरे
units.iast:
viśeṣo na hi gamyeta sāpekṣatve tadā tayoḥ /
dvayorekaviṣayasaṃbhave kuta etat --- śabdastadapekṣaḥ, na punastatpramāṇāntaraṃ śabdāpekṣaṃ syāditi? yadi śabdaḥ pramāṇāntarādhigataviṣayo loke dṛṣṭa iti, pramāṇāntarasyāviṣaye tarhi natarāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ tasya bhavati / pramāṇāntaraviṣaye hi pramāṇāntarasaṃbhavādapi tāvatsyāt, anyatra tadabhāvād durlabhaṃ tat / atha pauruṣeyatvakāritā lokavacasāṃ pramāṇāntarādhigatārthatā, na śabdasāmarthyakāritā / śabdasya pramāṇāntarāsaṃbhinna evārthe sāmarthyam / na tarhi pramāṇāntarasaṃbhavācchabda eva sāpekṣaḥ, tadapi śabdasaṃbhavācchabdāpekṣaṃ syāt / kimatastasya sāpekṣatvena? apramāṇaṃ syāt / na śabdasya tatrāpekṣā yujyate / sati hi tasya prāmāṇye tatsaṃvādavisaṃvādāvapekṣyeyātām / atha śabdasyāprāmāṇyānna tat śabdāpekṣayā pramāṇam / pramāṇameva, anapekṣatvāt / śabdasyāprāmāṇyaṃ kutaḥ? pramāṇāntarāpekṣatvāt / tasya ca prāmāṇyamanapekṣatvāt, anapekṣatvaṃ ca śabdasyāprāmāṇyāditaretarāśrayam / pramāṇe hi śabde tadviṣaye saṃbhavati tadapi sāpekṣaṃ syāttatsaṃbhava iva śabdaḥ, viśeṣābhāvāt / [kks_81] atha śabdasaṃbhave 'pi na tatsāpekṣam / tatsaṃbhave 'pi na śabdasya sāpekṣatā, viśeṣābhāvāt /

api ca
pratyakṣānumayorevaṃ vṛtteranyonyagocare
units.translation:
If the two depend on one another, their difference cannot be understood. When both are possible in relation to the same object, why should the word depend on the other means of knowledge, rather than that other means depend on the word? If the word is observed in ordinary usage to concern an object known by another means of knowledge, then with respect to what that other means cannot know, the word is even less valid. It might be valid when another means of knowledge is possible for the object; but elsewhere, since that other means is absent, the word’s validity is hard to establish.

Perhaps ordinary statements are considered valid because they were spoken by a person, and because their objects are known through other means of knowledge, not because of the power of words. A word’s power concerns only an object not established by another means. Then the word’s dependence cannot be explained by the possibility of another means of knowledge; for if the word is possible, that other means would in turn depend on the word. What follows from its dependence? It would be invalid. Yet it is not reasonable that the other means depends on the word. If the word were valid, one could ask whether it agrees or conflicts with that other means. But if the word is invalid, then the other means, since it does not depend on the word, should be valid. Why is the word invalid? Because it depends on another means of knowledge. But that means is valid because it is independent; and its independence depends on the word’s invalidity. This is mutual dependence. For if the word is valid and its object is possible, then the other means, like the word itself, would also depend on it, since there is no difference between them.

Or perhaps the other means does not depend on the word even when the word is possible. Then, even when the other means is possible, the word does not depend on it either; there is no difference. Moreover—

“Thus perception and inference operate within each other’s domain…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 18
units.deva: परस्परव्यपेक्षत्वमविशेषं प्रसज्यते । स्यादक्षमपि सापेक्षं यदक्षान्तरगोचरे
units.iast:
parasparavyapekṣatvamaviśeṣaṃ prasajyate /
syādakṣamapi sāpekṣaṃ yadakṣāntaragocare
units.translation: Then mutual dependence would follow without distinction. Even perception would depend on another sense when its object lies within that other sense’s domain.

gloss.en: the object lies within the scope of another sense

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 19
units.deva:
संभवमात्रेण सापेक्षत्वे प्रत्यक्षानुमयोरेकस्मिन् विषये संभवादन्योन्यापेक्षत्वादप्रामाण्यप्रसङ्गः । तथा सत्तागुणत्वद्रव्येष्वनेकेन्द्रियग्राह्येष्विन्द्रियान्तराणामिन्द्रियान्तरसापेक्षत्वप्रसङ्गः । अथ शब्दस्यैव प्रमाणान्तरसंभवे सापेक्षत्वम्, विशेषहेतुर्वाच्यः । प्रमाणान्तराधिगतार्थत्वदर्शनादिति चेत्, उक्तमत्र --- यदि शब्दमात्रधर्मो ऽयमसंभवादेव तद्विषये प्रत्यक्षादेर्बुद्धादिवाक्यवदप्रामाण्यं प्राप्नोति, संभवे त्विन्द्रियविषये प्रत्ययितपुरुषवचोवद्युज्यते प्रामाण्यम् । यथोक्तम् --- ‘तच्चेत्प्रत्ययितात्पुरुषादिन्द्रियविषयं वा, अवितथमेव तत्ऽ; इति । अथ पौरुषेयधर्मो ऽयम्, न संभवत्प्रमाणान्तरविषयस्याप्यपौरुषेयस्य शब्दस्य सापेक्षत्वम् । अपि च प्रत्यक्षाधिगतविषयं किञ्चिदनुमानमिति न सामान्यतोदृष्टस्य तथा प्रत्यक्षसापेक्षता, यथा चागमपूर्वकं षड्जादिविवेकविषयं प्रत्यक्षमिति न सर्वं प्रत्यक्षं तथा, एवं पुरुषवचसां प्रमाणान्तराधिगतविषयत्वदर्शने ऽपि नापौरुषेयस्य तथाभावो भूतार्थस्यापि । अन्यथा सुतरां प्रमाणान्तरासंभवादप्रामाण्यं स्यादित्युक्तम् । अपि च

असंभवादौषधादिनियोगस्यानपेक्षता । लौकिकस्य प्रसज्येत नरप्रत्ययपूर्वकः
units.iast:
saṃbhavamātreṇa sāpekṣatve pratyakṣānumayorekasmin viṣaye saṃbhavādanyonyāpekṣatvādaprāmāṇyaprasaṅgaḥ / tathā sattāguṇatvadravyeṣvanekendriyagrāhyeṣvindriyāntarāṇāmindriyāntarasāpekṣatvaprasaṅgaḥ / atha śabdasyaiva pramāṇāntarasaṃbhave sāpekṣatvam, viśeṣaheturvācyaḥ / pramāṇāntarādhigatārthatvadarśanāditi cet, uktamatra --- yadi śabdamātradharmo 'yamasaṃbhavādeva tadviṣaye pratyakṣāderbuddhādivākyavadaprāmāṇyaṃ prāpnoti, saṃbhave tvindriyaviṣaye pratyayitapuruṣavacovadyujyate prāmāṇyam / yathoktam --- ‘taccetpratyayitātpuruṣādindriyaviṣayaṃ vā, avitathameva tat'; iti / atha pauruṣeyadharmo 'yam, na saṃbhavatpramāṇāntaraviṣayasyāpyapauruṣeyasya śabdasya sāpekṣatvam / api ca pratyakṣādhigataviṣayaṃ kiñcidanumānamiti na sāmānyatodṛṣṭasya tathā pratyakṣasāpekṣatā, yathā cāgamapūrvakaṃ ṣaḍjādivivekaviṣayaṃ pratyakṣamiti na sarvaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tathā, evaṃ puruṣavacasāṃ pramāṇāntarādhigataviṣayatvadarśane 'pi nāpauruṣeyasya tathābhāvo bhūtārthasyāpi / anyathā sutarāṃ pramāṇāntarāsaṃbhavādaprāmāṇyaṃ syādityuktam /

api ca

asaṃbhavādauṣadhādiniyogasyānapekṣatā /
laukikasya prasajyeta narapratyayapūrvakaḥ
units.translation:
If perception and inference were considered dependent on each other merely because it is possible for them to concern one object, they would then become invalid through mutual dependence. Likewise, in the case of substances such as existence, qualities, and things grasped by several senses, one sense would have to depend on another. If only a word is dependent when another means of knowledge is possible, the special reason for this must be stated. One might say that we observe words to concern objects already known by other means. This has already been answered: if this were a property of words in general, then where no other means is possible, words would be invalid, like the statements of fools; where another means is possible, words could be valid, like the statements of a reliable person concerning what the senses perceive.

As has been said: “If it comes from a reliable person, or concerns what is within the senses, it is indeed true.” But if this is a property of statements made by people, then a word that is not humanly authored would not depend on another means of knowledge, even when another means can establish its object. Furthermore, just as some inferences concern objects that perception has established, ordinary perception does not therefore depend on perception in general. Nor does all perception depend on scripture, although discrimination of the musical note Ṣaḍja may depend on prior instruction. Similarly, even if the statements of human beings are observed to concern objects established through another means, that does not mean an unauthored word shares this feature, even when it concerns an existing object. Otherwise, since no other means is possible, it would be all the more invalid, as has already been said. Moreover—

“If prescriptions about medicines and the like were not dependent [on a prior means of knowledge] merely because another means is unavailable, then ordinary statements based on trust in a person would be…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 20
units.deva: विनियोगस्तत्र तेन व्यपेक्षा वैदिके पुनः । अबुद्धिपूर्वकः सो ऽपीत्यनपेक्षत्वमुच्यते
units.iast:
viniyogastatra tena vyapekṣā vaidike punaḥ /
abuddhipūrvakaḥ so 'pītyanapekṣatvamucyate
units.translation: In ordinary speech a person’s intention directs the application of words. But in the Veda that application is not preceded by such cognition; therefore it is said to be independent.

gloss.en: not preceded by a deliberate intention

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 21
units.deva:
यदि कार्ये नियोगार्थे प्रमाणान्तरस्यासंभवाद्वेदवचसां तन्निष्ठानामनपेक्षत्वम्, ‘ज्वरवियोगकाम इदमौषधं पिबेत्ऽ, ‘स्वर्गकामः सिकता भक्षयेत्ऽ; इति [क्क्स्_82] लोकवचांस्यपि कार्यनिष्ठान्यनपेक्षाणि प्रामाण्यमश्नुवीरन् । अथ यस्तत्र साध्यसाधनभावः स पुरुषविवक्षापूर्वकः, तेन तत्र सापेक्षता, वेदे तु साध्यसाधनभावो ऽपि न पुरुषविवक्षापूर्वकः इत्यनपेक्षत्वम् । यो वा विषयनियोज्यनियोगानां संबन्धः, स पुरुषबुद्धिविरचितो लोकवाक्ये । वेदे तु केवलं नियोगो ऽपुरुषबुद्धिपूर्वकः । सो ऽपीत्यनपेक्षत्वम् । उच्यते ---

नृबुद्धिपूर्वतैवेत्थं हन्तापेक्षानिबन्धनम् । मानान्तरासंभवे ऽपि तत्र सापेक्षता यतः
units.iast:
yadi kārye niyogārthe pramāṇāntarasyāsaṃbhavādvedavacasāṃ tanniṣṭhānāmanapekṣatvam, ‘jvaraviyogakāma idamauṣadhaṃ pibet', ‘svargakāmaḥ sikatā bhakṣayet'; iti [kks_82] lokavacāṃsyapi kāryaniṣṭhānyanapekṣāṇi prāmāṇyamaśnuvīran / atha yastatra sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ sa puruṣavivakṣāpūrvakaḥ, tena tatra sāpekṣatā, vede tu sādhyasādhanabhāvo 'pi na puruṣavivakṣāpūrvakaḥ ityanapekṣatvam / yo vā viṣayaniyojyaniyogānāṃ saṃbandhaḥ, sa puruṣabuddhiviracito lokavākye / vede tu kevalaṃ niyogo 'puruṣabuddhipūrvakaḥ / so 'pītyanapekṣatvam / ucyate ---

nṛbuddhipūrvataivetthaṃ hantāpekṣānibandhanam /
mānāntarāsaṃbhave 'pi tatra sāpekṣatā yataḥ
units.translation:
If Vedic statements are independent because another means of knowledge cannot establish what is to be done, then human statements concerning what is to be done should also be independent and valid, such as “One who wishes to be free of fever should drink this medicine” or “One who desires heaven should eat sand.” Someone may say that in ordinary speech the relation between means and end is intended by a person and so depends on the speaker; but in the Veda even this relation is not intended by a person, so it is independent. Or one may say that ordinary statements have a relation, created by human thought, among the object, the person to whom an injunction is directed, and the injunction itself; whereas the Veda has only an injunction, not preceded by human thought, and so is independent.

We reply:

“Human authorship itself, then, would be the basis of dependence. Indeed, even when another means of knowledge is impossible for that object, ordinary speech would still depend on a person’s intention…”

gloss.en: in what is to be done
in the meaning of an injunction
one wishing to be free from fever
the relation between end and means
of object, one enjoined, and injunction
even when another means is impossible

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 22
units.deva:
असंभवत्प्रमाणान्तरकार्यनिष्ठे ऽपि चेद्वाक्ये पुरुषसंबन्धात्सापेक्षत्वम्, पुरुषबुद्धिपूर्वतैव तर्हि प्रमाणान्तरव्यपेक्षाकारणमन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्याम् । तद्भावे लोके सापेक्षत्वात्, तदभावे वेदे निरपेक्षत्वात् । न विषये प्रमाणान्तरसंभवः, तदभावे ऽपि लोकनियोगे सापेक्षत्वदर्शनात् । अथ मतम् ---

वेदे नियोगनिष्ठत्वं विनियोगप्रधानता । लोके वेदे न व्यपेक्षा तल्लोके च व्यपेक्षणम्
units.iast:
asaṃbhavatpramāṇāntarakāryaniṣṭhe 'pi cedvākye puruṣasaṃbandhātsāpekṣatvam, puruṣabuddhipūrvataiva tarhi pramāṇāntaravyapekṣākāraṇamanvayavyatirekābhyām / tadbhāve loke sāpekṣatvāt, tadabhāve vede nirapekṣatvāt / na viṣaye pramāṇāntarasaṃbhavaḥ, tadabhāve 'pi lokaniyoge sāpekṣatvadarśanāt /

atha matam ---

vede niyoganiṣṭhatvaṃ viniyogapradhānatā /
loke vede na vyapekṣā talloke ca vyapekṣaṇam
units.translation:
If a statement is dependent because it is connected with a person, even when it concerns something to be done that cannot be established by another means of knowledge, then human authorship itself must be the cause of dependence on another means. This follows by the method of agreement and difference: ordinary statements are dependent when they are produced by a person, while the Veda is independent because no human thought produced it. It is not that another means of knowledge is possible for the object, since ordinary injunctions are observed to be dependent even where no other means is possible. Someone may object:

“In the Veda, the injunction is primary; in ordinary usage, a direction to apply words is primary. In the Veda, the words do not depend [on a speaker]; in ordinary usage, they do.”

gloss.en: concerning an end not accessible through another means of knowledge
because of connection with a human speaker
is the cause of dependence on another means

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 23
units.deva: नियोगपर्यवसितं वैदिकं वचः, स च प्रमाणान्तरस्यागोचर इत्यनपेक्षत्वम् । साध्यसाधनभावनिष्ठं तु लौकिकं वचः, स प्रमाणान्तरविषय इति सापेक्षता । न शब्दमात्रसामर्थ्यप्रविभागो ऽयमीदृशः । लोकावगतसामर्थ्यः शब्दो वेदे ऽपि बोधकः
units.iast:
niyogaparyavasitaṃ vaidikaṃ vacaḥ, sa ca pramāṇāntarasyāgocara ityanapekṣatvam / sādhyasādhanabhāvaniṣṭhaṃ tu laukikaṃ vacaḥ, sa pramāṇāntaraviṣaya iti sāpekṣatā /

na śabdamātrasāmarthyapravibhāgo 'yamīdṛśaḥ /
lokāvagatasāmarthyaḥ śabdo vede 'pi bodhakaḥ
units.translation: Vedic statements culminate in an injunction, which is not within the scope of another means of knowledge; therefore they are independent. Ordinary statements, by contrast, concern the relation between means and end, which is within the scope of another means, so they are dependent. But this distinction in power does not belong to words alone. The power of words, established in ordinary usage, also conveys meaning in the Veda.

gloss.en: grounded in the relation of means and end
within the scope of another means
a distinction based only on the power of words
whose power is known through ordinary usage

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 24
units.deva: न तावदयं शब्दमात्रस्यानपेक्षितपुरुषसंबन्धासंबन्धस्य शक्तिप्रविभागः --- यदेकत्र नियोगः शब्दार्थः । अन्यत्र विनियोगः, यथा गोशब्दस्य सास्नादिमान्, अश्वशब्दस्य केसरादिमान् । यतो लोकाधिगतसामर्थ्यो वेदे ऽपि प्रतिपादकः । लोके चेद्विनियोगः शब्दार्थः, तत्रैवास्य सामर्थ्यमधिगतम्, न नियोगे । तत्र वेदे ऽपि विनियोग एव प्रमाणार्थः स्यात् । अथ मानान्तराज्ज्ञात्वा प्रयुङ्क्ते पुरुषो वचः । अर्थे तत्तेन तन्निष्ठमितरत्त्वन्यथा स्थितम्
units.iast:
na tāvadayaṃ śabdamātrasyānapekṣitapuruṣasaṃbandhāsaṃbandhasya śaktipravibhāgaḥ --- yadekatra niyogaḥ śabdārthaḥ / anyatra viniyogaḥ, yathā gośabdasya sāsnādimān, aśvaśabdasya kesarādimān / yato lokādhigatasāmarthyo vede 'pi pratipādakaḥ / loke cedviniyogaḥ śabdārthaḥ, tatraivāsya sāmarthyamadhigatam, na niyoge / tatra vede 'pi viniyoga eva pramāṇārthaḥ syāt /

atha mānāntarājjñātvā prayuṅkte puruṣo vacaḥ /
arthe tattena tanniṣṭhamitarattvanyathā sthitam
units.translation: The distinction in power cannot belong to words alone, independently of their relation to a speaker: in one case an injunction is the meaning, while in another a direction to apply a word is, as with “cow,” meaning an animal with a dewlap, and “horse,” one with a mane. This is because words derive their power from ordinary usage, and that power also explains Vedic language. If in ordinary usage the meaning is a direction to apply a word, then this is where its power is learned—not in an injunction. The Veda too would then be a valid means of knowledge only as a direction to apply words. But if a person uses a sentence after learning its object by another means of knowledge, then…

gloss.en: independent of any relation to a speaker
having a dewlap and the like
having a mane and the like
whose power is learned through ordinary usage

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 25
units.deva:
[क्क्स्_83] अथ मतम् --- नैष शब्दमात्रस्य सामर्थ्यविभागः । शब्दस्य हि निजं सामर्थ्यं कार्यनिष्ठतैव । तथा हि --- कार्यो नियोगार्थः । कार्याय चान्यस्यान्वयः प्रतीयते । न तु कार्यस्यान्यार्थो ऽन्वयः । तस्मात्कार्यत्वान्नियोगस्य तत्प्रधानता । पुरुषस्तु प्रमाणान्तरादवगम्यार्थं तत्र प्रयुङ्क्ते वचनम् । न च नियोगः प्रमाणान्तरगोचरः । तस्मान्न तत्र प्रयोक्तुमर्हति । विनियोगस्य तु तथाभावात्तत्र युज्यते प्रयोगः । तस्माद्विनियोगप्रधानं पुरुषवचः । वैदिकं तु सामर्थ्येन कार्यत्वान्नियोगस्य तत्प्रधानमिति । अत्रोच्यते ---

मानान्तरव्यपेक्षत्वात्संभव्यन्यप्रमाणकः । हन्तास्य गोचरो नास्मादपेक्षास्य प्रमान्तरे
units.iast:
[kks_83] atha matam --- naiṣa śabdamātrasya sāmarthyavibhāgaḥ / śabdasya hi nijaṃ sāmarthyaṃ kāryaniṣṭhataiva / tathā hi --- kāryo niyogārthaḥ / kāryāya cānyasyānvayaḥ pratīyate / na tu kāryasyānyārtho 'nvayaḥ / tasmātkāryatvānniyogasya tatpradhānatā / puruṣastu pramāṇāntarādavagamyārthaṃ tatra prayuṅkte vacanam / na ca niyogaḥ pramāṇāntaragocaraḥ / tasmānna tatra prayoktumarhati / viniyogasya tu tathābhāvāttatra yujyate prayogaḥ / tasmādviniyogapradhānaṃ puruṣavacaḥ / vaidikaṃ tu sāmarthyena kāryatvānniyogasya tatpradhānamiti /

atrocyate ---

mānāntaravyapekṣatvātsaṃbhavyanyapramāṇakaḥ /
hantāsya gocaro nāsmādapekṣāsya pramāntare
units.translation:
Someone may argue: this distinction in power is not a property of words in general. A word’s own power is directed toward what is to be done. For the meaning of an injunction is something to be done, and what is related to what is to be done is understood; but what is to be done is not understood as related to some other thing. Thus because an injunction concerns what is to be done, it is primary. A person, however, first learns the object through another means of knowledge and then uses a statement about it. An injunction is not within the scope of another means of knowledge, so it cannot be used to establish it. But a directive for applying a word does have that character and can be used in this way. Therefore statements by people are primarily directives for application, while the Veda, by its power to prescribe what is to be done, is primarily an injunction.

The reply is:

“Since it depends on another means of knowledge, it can be within the scope of a different means of knowledge. Indeed, it is not from this [word] that dependence on another means of knowledge follows.”

gloss.en: being directed toward what is to be done
is the meaning of an injunction
to what is to be done
of what is to be done
because it is something to be done
within the scope of another means of knowledge
because it concerns what is to be done
because of dependence on another means of knowledge
having another means of knowledge as its basis

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 26
units.deva: यदि पुरुषो ऽधिगते विषये वचः प्रयुङ्क्ते इति विनियोगविषयता तस्य कल्प्यते प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षत्वात्, तर्हि संभवत्प्रमाणान्तरो ऽस्य विषयः । न तु संभवत्प्रमाणान्तरविषयत्वात्पुरुषवचो ऽपि सापेक्षम्, सापेक्षत्वनिमित्तत्वात्तद्विधस्य विषयस्य । तस्मान्मानान्तराद्गत्वा परस्य प्रतिपत्तये । वचः प्रयुङ्क्ते पुरुषो नाकस्मात्तेन तद्गिरि
units.iast:
yadi puruṣo 'dhigate viṣaye vacaḥ prayuṅkte iti viniyogaviṣayatā tasya kalpyate pramāṇāntarāpekṣatvāt, tarhi saṃbhavatpramāṇāntaro 'sya viṣayaḥ / na tu saṃbhavatpramāṇāntaraviṣayatvātpuruṣavaco 'pi sāpekṣam, sāpekṣatvanimittatvāttadvidhasya viṣayasya /

tasmānmānāntarādgatvā parasya pratipattaye /
vacaḥ prayuṅkte puruṣo nākasmāttena tadgiri
units.translation: If it is imagined that statements by a person are directions for applying words, because a person uses a statement about an object already known and thus depends on another means of knowledge, then the object is one for which another means is possible. But a human statement is not dependent merely because its object is accessible to another means; that is not what causes dependence. Therefore, having first learned something through another means of knowledge, a person uses a statement to communicate it to someone else, not without reason. From the speaker’s words, the listener…

gloss.en: being a direction to apply words
because it depends on another means of knowledge
merely because its object is accessible through another means

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 27
units.deva: प्रमाणान्तरसंभेदो व्यपेक्षातो न संभवात् । स्वोपलब्धिख्यापनाय पुरुषस्य गीः, ततस्तस्यां प्रमाणान्तरसंभेदः, ‘मयोपलब्धो ऽयमर्थःऽइत्यर्थः । तेन तत्रोपलब्धे संभवासंभवावेवापेक्ष्येयाताम् । यत्रोपलब्धेर्निश्चयः ‘संभवत्यस्योपलब्धिः, न चानुपलभ्यायं ब्रवीतिऽ; इति तत्र प्रामाण्यम्, यथाप्तपुरुषस्य प्रमाणविषये । यत्र तूपलब्धेरसंभव एव यथा दृष्टार्थे बुद्धादिवाक्ये, यत्र चानुपलभ्यापि वचनप्रवृत्तिसंभावना, तत्राप्रामाण्यात् । न तु प्रमाणान्तरसंभवात्पुरुषवचने ऽपि तदपेक्षा । अपौरुषेयता तेन पौरुषेयत्वमेव च
units.iast:
pramāṇāntarasaṃbhedo vyapekṣāto na saṃbhavāt /
svopalabdhikhyāpanāya puruṣasya gīḥ, tatastasyāṃ pramāṇāntarasaṃbhedaḥ, ‘mayopalabdho 'yamarthaḥ'ityarthaḥ / tena tatropalabdhe saṃbhavāsaṃbhavāvevāpekṣyeyātām / yatropalabdherniścayaḥ ‘saṃbhavatyasyopalabdhiḥ, na cānupalabhyāyaṃ bravīti'; iti tatra prāmāṇyam, yathāptapuruṣasya pramāṇaviṣaye / yatra tūpalabdherasaṃbhava eva yathā dṛṣṭārthe buddhādivākye, yatra cānupalabhyāpi vacanapravṛttisaṃbhāvanā, tatrāprāmāṇyāt / na tu pramāṇāntarasaṃbhavātpuruṣavacane 'pi tadapekṣā /
apauruṣeyatā tena pauruṣeyatvameva ca
units.translation: Dependence does not arise merely because another means of knowledge is possible. A person’s statement reports that the person knows something; from this, the cognition is connected with another means of knowledge, and the statement means “I have known this object.” Therefore, with respect to that person’s knowing, one need consider only whether such knowledge is possible or impossible. Where it is certain that the speaker could know the object and would not speak without knowing it, the statement is valid, as with a reliable person speaking about something within the scope of a means of knowledge. Where such knowledge is impossible, as in the Buddha’s statement about an object that can be seen directly, or where a person might speak without having known the object, the statement is invalid. It is not dependent merely because another means of knowledge is possible for the object. Its being unauthored, and the other statement’s being humanly authored, are the reasons…

gloss.en: mixture with another means of knowledge
concerning an object within a means of knowledge
in the words of the Buddha and others
the possibility of making a statement

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 28
units.deva: अनपेक्षव्यपेक्षत्वनिमित्ते वर्णिते बुधैः । भूतार्थमपि सापेक्षं नातो ऽपुरुषबुद्धिजम्
units.iast:
anapekṣavyapekṣatvanimitte varṇite budhaiḥ /
bhūtārthamapi sāpekṣaṃ nāto 'puruṣabuddhijam
units.translation: The learned have explained that dependence and independence are caused by these factors. Therefore even a statement about an existent object can be dependent, if it arises from a human intellect.

gloss.en: the causes of independence and dependence

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 29
units.deva: [क्क्स्_84] अत एव पौरुषेयत्वापौरुषेयत्वे सापेक्षत्वानपेक्षत्वकारणे न्यायविद्भिर्दशिते पौरुषेयत्वनिराकरणप्रयत्नेन --- ‘औत्पत्तिकस्तु शब्दस्यार्थेन संबन्धःऽ; इति । औत्पत्तिके शब्दार्थसम्बन्धे ऽस्वातन्त्र्याच्छब्दस्य न पुरुषबुद्धिपूर्वकत्वमिति न प्रमाणान्तरसंभिन्ना शब्दादर्थावगतिरिति निरपेक्षत्वम् । ननु प्रमाणान्तरासंभवे ऽपि कृत एव यत्नः --- ‘सत्संप्रयोगेऽ; इति । सत्यम् । चोदनैव प्रमाणम्, नान्यत् --- इत्यवधारणसिद्धये । न तु प्रमाणमेव इति । अथ प्रमाणान्तरसंभवे ऽपि यदि चोदनाप्रामाण्यं न व्याहन्यते, को ऽर्थः प्रमाणान्तरनिराकरणेन? धर्मतत्त्वज्ञानम् । प्रमाणान्तरसंभवे हि सर्वज्ञाभिमतबुद्धाद्युपदिष्टो ऽपि धर्मः प्रतीयेत तत्र न धर्मतत्त्वमवधारितं स्यात् । तदवधारणार्थश्चायं यत्नः । चोदनाप्रामाण्यमपि तदर्थं मृग्यते, नादृष्टाय । अथवा तद्विरोधाच्चोदनाया बाधः स्यात्, संशयो वा तुल्यबलत्वे, तेन तस्यासंभवः प्रतिपाद्यते । न तु तत्संभवात्सापेक्षतेति । ननु तदभावो ऽपेक्षणीयः स्यात् । कामम् । न तु शब्दः प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षमर्थं प्रतिपादयति । यतः यदर्थस्य प्रतिपादकम्, न तु तदपेक्ष्यते । यदपेक्ष्यते न तदर्थं प्रतिपादयति । न हि विरोधिप्रमाणाभावः प्रतिपत्तिहेतुः । विरोधसंभवमात्रेण चाप्रामाण्ये प्रत्यक्षादीनामपि तत्स्यात् । अपि च विरोधिसंभवादप्रामाण्यं कार्यनिष्ठत्वे ऽप्यपरिहार्यम्, कर्तव्यताद्वारेण भूतार्थप्रतिपत्तेरिष्टत्वात् । तत्र तु प्रमाणान्तरविरोधिसंभावनात् । भूतार्थस्य प्रमाणान्तरविषयत्वात्तेन कार्यनिष्ठता वर्ण्यते । प्रमाणान्तरविषयत्वे किलानुवादत्वात्प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षमर्थं प्रतिपादयति --- प्रमाणान्तरेणायमधिगतः --- इति न स्वातन्त्र्येण । कार्यनिष्ठत्वे तु स्वातन्त्र्येण, तस्य प्रमाणान्तरागोचरत्वात् । उक्तेन प्रकारेण न सापेक्षत्वमिति ‘भूतार्थमपि सापेक्षं नातो ऽपुरुषबुद्धिजम्ऽइति सुष्ठूक्तम् । अथ संसर्गभाजो नो पदार्थाः क्रियया विना । किमायातं विधेः सापि त्वस्त्यादिः सुलभा क्व न
units.iast:
[kks_84] ata eva pauruṣeyatvāpauruṣeyatve sāpekṣatvānapekṣatvakāraṇe nyāyavidbhirdaśite pauruṣeyatvanirākaraṇaprayatnena --- ‘autpattikastu śabdasyārthena saṃbandhaḥ'; iti / autpattike śabdārthasambandhe 'svātantryācchabdasya na puruṣabuddhipūrvakatvamiti na pramāṇāntarasaṃbhinnā śabdādarthāvagatiriti nirapekṣatvam /

nanu pramāṇāntarāsaṃbhave 'pi kṛta eva yatnaḥ --- ‘satsaṃprayoge'; iti / satyam / codanaiva pramāṇam, nānyat --- ityavadhāraṇasiddhaye / na tu pramāṇameva iti /

atha pramāṇāntarasaṃbhave 'pi yadi codanāprāmāṇyaṃ na vyāhanyate, ko 'rthaḥ pramāṇāntaranirākaraṇena? dharmatattvajñānam / pramāṇāntarasaṃbhave hi sarvajñābhimatabuddhādyupadiṣṭo 'pi dharmaḥ pratīyeta tatra na dharmatattvamavadhāritaṃ syāt / tadavadhāraṇārthaścāyaṃ yatnaḥ / codanāprāmāṇyamapi tadarthaṃ mṛgyate, nādṛṣṭāya / athavā tadvirodhāccodanāyā bādhaḥ syāt, saṃśayo vā tulyabalatve, tena tasyāsaṃbhavaḥ pratipādyate / na tu tatsaṃbhavātsāpekṣateti / nanu tadabhāvo 'pekṣaṇīyaḥ syāt / kāmam / na tu śabdaḥ pramāṇāntarāpekṣamarthaṃ pratipādayati / yataḥ yadarthasya pratipādakam, na tu tadapekṣyate / yadapekṣyate na tadarthaṃ pratipādayati / na hi virodhipramāṇābhāvaḥ pratipattihetuḥ / virodhasaṃbhavamātreṇa cāprāmāṇye pratyakṣādīnāmapi tatsyāt / api ca virodhisaṃbhavādaprāmāṇyaṃ kāryaniṣṭhatve 'pyaparihāryam, kartavyatādvāreṇa bhūtārthapratipatteriṣṭatvāt / tatra tu pramāṇāntaravirodhisaṃbhāvanāt / bhūtārthasya pramāṇāntaraviṣayatvāttena kāryaniṣṭhatā varṇyate / pramāṇāntaraviṣayatve kilānuvādatvātpramāṇāntarāpekṣamarthaṃ pratipādayati --- pramāṇāntareṇāyamadhigataḥ --- iti na svātantryeṇa / kāryaniṣṭhatve tu svātantryeṇa, tasya pramāṇāntarāgocaratvāt / uktena prakāreṇa na sāpekṣatvamiti ‘bhūtārthamapi sāpekṣaṃ nāto 'puruṣabuddhijam'iti suṣṭhūktam /

atha saṃsargabhājo no padārthāḥ kriyayā vinā /
kimāyātaṃ vidheḥ sāpi tvastyādiḥ sulabhā kva na
units.translation:
For this reason, teachers of logic have explained authorship and authorlessness as the causes of dependence and independence, respectively, by refuting the idea that a human author is involved. “The relation of a word to its meaning is innate”: since it is innate, a word is not dependent on a person’s cognition, and verbal understanding is not mixed with another means of knowledge. Someone may object that even if another means of knowledge is absent, one still makes an effort, as in the statement “When the existing things are in contact...” That is true. The effort is made to establish the conclusion that injunction alone is the means of knowledge, and no other. It is not to prove that a means of knowledge exists at all.

If other means of knowledge are possible, and the authority of an injunction is not contradicted by them, what is gained by excluding them? Knowledge of the true nature of dharma. If another means of knowledge were possible, dharma taught by a person regarded as omniscient, such as the Buddha, might also be understood; its status as the truth about dharma would not be certain. This effort is made to establish that certainty. The authority of the injunction is sought for that purpose, not without reason. Alternatively, if another means of knowledge contradicted an injunction, it would sublate it; if they were equal in force, there would be doubt. The argument therefore establishes that another means of knowledge is impossible in this domain, not that the injunction depends on such a means.

Someone may object that the absence of a conflicting means of knowledge itself needs to be established. Granted; but a word does not convey its meaning by depending on another means of knowledge. What conveys an object is not itself dependent on that object’s being conveyed by something else; what is dependent does not convey that object. Nor does the mere possibility of conflict make a means of knowledge invalid, since the same would apply to perception and the others. Moreover, the possibility of conflict cannot be avoided even for actions: an injunction may be understood as conveying a factual meaning about a result, and another means of knowledge might conflict with it. Because a factual object is in the domain of another means, its meaning may be described as a repetition of what is already known, dependent on that other means. But an injunction has its own independent force, since its object is not known through another means.
