Perhaps the word “injunction” only makes the other words’ meanings relate to one another. What follows from that? The meanings of the words can be related without an action. The word “is,” for instance, easily conveys the reality of an object. But if one says that words do not relate meanings without action, what follows? Even the word “is” is readily understood...

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 30
units.deva:
[क्क्स्_85] यदि मतम् --- आख्यातपदार्थमन्तरेण न नामपदार्थानां संसर्गः । क्रिया हि पदार्थसंश्लेषहेतुः तदभावे साकाङ्क्षत्वात् । अतः सिद्धो ऽर्थो ब्रह्मादिर्न शब्दगोचरः पदस्याविदितसंगतित्वेनानवबोधकत्वात् । न वाक्यार्थः तस्य संसर्गात्मकत्वात् । क्रियारहितानां च पदार्थानामसंसर्गात् । एवमपि क्रियाभ्युपेयताम् । तद्द्वारेण च पदार्थसंसर्गसिद्धिराशास्यताम् । न विधेः कश्चिदर्थः । सापि च क्रिया सर्वत्र सुलभैवाश्रूयमाणाप्यस्त्यादिः ‘अस्तिर्भवन्तीपरः प्रथमपुरुषो ऽप्रयुज्यमानो ऽपि गम्यतेऽ; इति । तत्र ब्रह्मस्वरूपप्रतिपत्तिपरं वाक्यमस्त्यर्थनिष्ठम् । तन्निबन्धनस्तत्र पदार्थसंश्लेषः । सत्तायाश्च प्रकृत्यैव सत्प्रधानत्वात् तद्द्वारेण विशिष्टवस्तुसिद्धिरिति । अत्राहुः --- न प्रमाणावगम्यताया अन्या काचन सत्ता । तथा हि --- यत् प्रमाणेनावगम्यते तत्र ‘अस्तिऽ; इति व्यवहारो लौकिकानाम् विपर्यये ‘नास्तिऽ; इति । न खल्वन्यः सदसद्विभागहेतुर्लक्ष्यते । अर्थक्रियाभावाभावौ चेत् । न तयोरपि प्रमाणभावाभावाधीनत्वात् । तथा हि --- कार्ये ऽपि सद्व्यवहारो यदि कार्यान्तरनिबन्धनः अनवस्था । तस्मादन्ते ऽपि प्रमाणादेव सद्व्यवहारः तद्विपर्ययाच्चासद्व्यवहारः । एवं चेदादावेव प्रमाणाभावाभावनिबन्धनौ सदसद्व्यवहारौ स्ताम् । तथा चास्त्यर्थनिष्ठं वाक्यं प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षमेवार्थं बोधयति प्रमाणविषयताया अस्त्यर्थत्वात् । अत्रोच्यते ---

न च मानावगम्यत्वमस्तीति विषयो मतः । मानादेव यतो बुद्धिरभूदस्ति भविष्यति
units.iast:
[kks_85] yadi matam --- ākhyātapadārthamantareṇa na nāmapadārthānāṃ saṃsargaḥ / kriyā hi padārthasaṃśleṣahetuḥ tadabhāve sākāṅkṣatvāt / ataḥ siddho 'rtho brahmādirna śabdagocaraḥ padasyāviditasaṃgatitvenānavabodhakatvāt / na vākyārthaḥ tasya saṃsargātmakatvāt / kriyārahitānāṃ ca padārthānāmasaṃsargāt / evamapi kriyābhyupeyatām / taddvāreṇa ca padārthasaṃsargasiddhirāśāsyatām / na vidheḥ kaścidarthaḥ / sāpi ca kriyā sarvatra sulabhaivāśrūyamāṇāpyastyādiḥ ‘astirbhavantīparaḥ prathamapuruṣo 'prayujyamāno 'pi gamyate'; iti / tatra brahmasvarūpapratipattiparaṃ vākyamastyarthaniṣṭham / tannibandhanastatra padārthasaṃśleṣaḥ / sattāyāśca prakṛtyaiva satpradhānatvāt taddvāreṇa viśiṣṭavastusiddhiriti /

atrāhuḥ --- na pramāṇāvagamyatāyā anyā kācana sattā / tathā hi --- yat pramāṇenāvagamyate tatra ‘asti'; iti vyavahāro laukikānām viparyaye ‘nāsti'; iti / na khalvanyaḥ sadasadvibhāgaheturlakṣyate / arthakriyābhāvābhāvau cet / na tayorapi pramāṇabhāvābhāvādhīnatvāt / tathā hi --- kārye 'pi sadvyavahāro yadi kāryāntaranibandhanaḥ anavasthā / tasmādante 'pi pramāṇādeva sadvyavahāraḥ tadviparyayāccāsadvyavahāraḥ / evaṃ cedādāveva pramāṇābhāvābhāvanibandhanau sadasadvyavahārau stām / tathā cāstyarthaniṣṭhaṃ vākyaṃ pramāṇāntarāpekṣamevārthaṃ bodhayati pramāṇaviṣayatāyā astyarthatvāt /

atrocyate ---

na ca mānāvagamyatvamastīti viṣayo mataḥ /
mānādeva yato buddhirabhūdasti bhaviṣyati
units.translation:
Someone may argue: without a verb’s meaning, the meanings of nouns cannot be related. An action is what brings the meanings of words together; without it they would remain incomplete. Therefore an established reality such as Brahman is not within the range of words: because a word’s conventional relation is unknown, it cannot convey that reality. Nor can Brahman be the meaning of the sentence, since sentence meaning consists in a relation, and things without action cannot be related. Even so, one may accept an action and hope to establish the relation among the things through it. The injunction itself then has no independent meaning. Such an action is readily available everywhere, even when not heard: the verb “to be” is understood in the first person even when it is not used, as the grammatical rule says. Thus a sentence whose purpose is to establish the nature of Brahman has the verb “to be” as its meaning; the relation among the words is based on it. And since existence is primarily denoted by the verbal root, a qualified object is established through it.

The reply is that existence is not some separate thing apart from being apprehended by a means of knowledge. Ordinary people say “it exists” of what is known by a valid means of knowledge, and “it does not exist” of what is not known. No other basis for the distinction between existent and nonexistent is observed. One might propose that it is the presence or absence of practical effects. But these too depend upon the presence or absence of a means of knowledge. If an object is called existent because it produces another effect, there would be an infinite regress. Thus, ultimately, the judgment “it exists” depends on a means of knowledge, and the judgment “it does not exist” on the absence of such knowledge. In that case, the judgment of existence or nonexistence at the outset likewise depends on the presence or absence of a means of knowledge. Therefore, a sentence whose meaning is the verb “to be” conveys an object only in dependence on another means of knowledge, since being within the scope of a means of knowledge is what “existence” means.

The reply is:

“Being an object apprehended by a means of knowledge is not what is meant by ‘exists’; for cognition arises from the means of knowledge, and one says ‘it exists’ or ‘it will exist’…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 31
units.deva: धूमादिना मिते हि स्याद्वह्न्यादावियमन्यथा । भिद्येतोत्तरकाले वा भवन्ती न खलु त्रिधा
units.iast:
dhūmādinā mite hi syādvahnyādāviyamanyathā /
bhidyetottarakāle vā bhavantī na khalu tridhā
units.translation: Otherwise, as with fire known from smoke, the object would be apprehended through another means; or its threefold division into past, present, and future would be lost.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 32
units.deva: न प्रमाणावगम्यत्वमस्त्यर्थः न ‘अस्तिऽ; इति बुद्धेस्तद्विषयः । यतः प्रमाणादेव त्रिधा बुद्धिर्भवति --- ‘धूमादस्त्यत्राग्निःऽ; ‘नदीपूरविशेषादभूद्वृष्टिःऽ; ‘मेघोदयविशेषाद् [क्क्स्_86] भविष्यति वृष्टिःऽ; इति । तत्र यदि बुद्धिः प्रमाणविषयतां गोचरयति प्रमिते हि स्यात् न प्रमाणादेव । न हि प्राक् प्रमाणोत्पत्तेः सन् प्रमाणसंबन्धः । प्रमाणसंबन्धनिबन्धना चेयं बुद्धिः । अथ वैयात्यादुत्तरकालतामेवास्या ब्रूयात् । त्रैविध्यमनुपपन्नम्, प्रमाणसंबन्धस्याभेदाद्भिन्नकालेष्वप्यर्थेषु । स्वसंबन्धितया मानमथ वस्त्वधिगच्छति । तथापि नैव भिद्येत नेत्थं चान्यव्यपेक्षता
units.iast:
na pramāṇāvagamyatvamastyarthaḥ na ‘asti'; iti buddhestadviṣayaḥ / yataḥ pramāṇādeva tridhā buddhirbhavati --- ‘dhūmādastyatrāgniḥ'; ‘nadīpūraviśeṣādabhūdvṛṣṭiḥ'; ‘meghodayaviśeṣād [kks_86] bhaviṣyati vṛṣṭiḥ'; iti / tatra yadi buddhiḥ pramāṇaviṣayatāṃ gocarayati pramite hi syāt na pramāṇādeva / na hi prāk pramāṇotpatteḥ san pramāṇasaṃbandhaḥ / pramāṇasaṃbandhanibandhanā ceyaṃ buddhiḥ / atha vaiyātyāduttarakālatāmevāsyā brūyāt / traividhyamanupapannam, pramāṇasaṃbandhasyābhedādbhinnakāleṣvapyartheṣu /

svasaṃbandhitayā mānamatha vastvadhigacchati /
tathāpi naiva bhidyeta netthaṃ cānyavyapekṣatā
units.translation: Being an object of apprehension by a means of knowledge is not what “exists” means, nor is such apprehension the object of the cognition “it exists.” For from a means of knowledge itself, cognition arises in three forms: “There is fire here, from the smoke”; “It rained, as shown by the flood of the river”; “It will rain, as shown by the gathering clouds.” If cognition concerned only the fact of being within the scope of a means of knowledge, it would arise only after the object had already been known, not from the means itself. Before the means of knowledge arises, there is no connection with it; yet this cognition is based on that connection. One might arbitrarily say that it arises later, but then the threefold distinction is inexplicable, since the connection with the means of knowledge is the same even for objects at different times. Or perhaps the means of knowledge apprehends an object by relating it to itself; even so, it would not differ, and dependence on another thing would not follow.

gloss.en: being known by a means of knowledge
from the particular flood of a river
from the particular rising of clouds
being within the scope of a means
the arising of a means of knowledge
based on relation to a means

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 33
units.deva: अथ मतम् --- आत्मसंबन्धितयैव प्रमाणेनार्थो ऽवगम्यते । अतो न ‘अस्तिऽइति बुद्धेरुत्तरकालता प्रमाणसंबन्धविषयाया अपि, स्वात्मसंबन्धितयैवार्थस्य प्रतीतेः । एवमप्यस्तीत्येव सर्वत्र स्यात् । न त्रैविध्यम्, सर्वस्य प्रमितौ प्रमाणसंबन्धस्य वर्तमानत्वात् । न चेत्थं प्रमाणान्तरव्यपेक्षत्वमस्त्यर्थनिष्ठे वचसि तत्प्रमाणसंबन्धस्यैवास्त्यर्थत्वात् । अन्यमानावगम्यत्वमथ लिङ्गात्त्रिधेष्यते । स्याल्लिङ्गमपि सापेक्षं तत्सिद्धेस्तत एव चेत्
units.iast:
atha matam --- ātmasaṃbandhitayaiva pramāṇenārtho 'vagamyate / ato na ‘asti'iti buddheruttarakālatā pramāṇasaṃbandhaviṣayāyā api, svātmasaṃbandhitayaivārthasya pratīteḥ / evamapyastītyeva sarvatra syāt / na traividhyam, sarvasya pramitau pramāṇasaṃbandhasya vartamānatvāt / na cetthaṃ pramāṇāntaravyapekṣatvamastyarthaniṣṭhe vacasi tatpramāṇasaṃbandhasyaivāstyarthatvāt /

anyamānāvagamyatvamatha liṅgāttridheṣyate /
syālliṅgamapi sāpekṣaṃ tatsiddhestata eva cet
units.translation: Someone may argue: an object is apprehended by a means of knowledge precisely in relation to the means itself. Therefore there is no delay in the cognition “it exists,” even though it concerns relation to a means of knowledge, because the object is apprehended only through its relation to that means. Even so, everywhere one would have to say only “it exists”; there would be no threefold division, since the relation to a means of knowledge is present whenever anything is apprehended. And if this relation to the means of knowledge is what “exists” means, then a sentence about existence would not depend on another means: that relation itself would be existence. Or perhaps what is known by another means is distinguished in three times through inference. But the inferential sign too might be dependent, if its existence is established through that same means…

gloss.en: in relation to the means of knowledge itself
concerning relation to a means of knowledge
the relation to a means of knowledge
dependence on another means of knowledge
because that relation to a means

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 34
units.deva: नैरपेक्ष्यं यदि न तद्वेदे दण्डैर्निवार्यते । अथ मतम् --- प्रमाणान्तरगम्यतैव लिङ्गेनाधिगम्यते । तेन नोत्तरकालता । तच्च प्रमाणं त्रिकालमिति त्रैविध्यम् । किं पुनस्तत्? प्रत्यक्षम् । तथा हि --- भूतायां दृष्टौ कस्यचिद्भूतं प्रत्यक्षम्, भविष्यन्त्यां भविष्यत्, वर्तमाने ऽग्नौ वर्तमानमिति । एतच्च वार्तम्, नित्यानुमेये तस्याभावात् । अपि च लिङ्गमप्येवं प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षत्वादप्रमाणं स्यात् । अथ लिङ्गादेव प्रमाणान्तरसद्भावस्य सिद्धेर्निरपेक्षत्वम् । तथा हि --- प्रमाणान्तरसद्भाव एवेदानीं लिङ्गं प्रमाणम् । न च तत्रान्यदपेक्ष्यते । प्रमाणसद्भावद्वारा प्रमेयसिद्धिरिति । [क्क्स्_87] नायं विधिर्वेदे दण्डवारितः । वैदिकमपि वचो ऽस्त्यर्थनिष्ठं विशिष्टार्थप्रमाणसद्भाव एव प्रमाणम् । तत्र निरपेक्षम् । तत्प्रमाणद्वारा च विशिष्टार्थसिद्धिरिति समानम् । तत्संभवो ऽलौकिकार्थे (लैङ्गिके ऽर्थे --एदितिओन्) बुद्धवाक्यार्थवन्न तु
units.iast:
nairapekṣyaṃ yadi na tadvede daṇḍairnivāryate /
atha matam --- pramāṇāntaragamyataiva liṅgenādhigamyate / tena nottarakālatā / tacca pramāṇaṃ trikālamiti traividhyam / kiṃ punastat? pratyakṣam / tathā hi --- bhūtāyāṃ dṛṣṭau kasyacidbhūtaṃ pratyakṣam, bhaviṣyantyāṃ bhaviṣyat, vartamāne 'gnau vartamānamiti / etacca vārtam, nityānumeye tasyābhāvāt / api ca liṅgamapyevaṃ pramāṇāntarāpekṣatvādapramāṇaṃ syāt / atha liṅgādeva pramāṇāntarasadbhāvasya siddhernirapekṣatvam / tathā hi --- pramāṇāntarasadbhāva evedānīṃ liṅgaṃ pramāṇam / na ca tatrānyadapekṣyate / pramāṇasadbhāvadvārā prameyasiddhiriti / [kks_87] nāyaṃ vidhirvede daṇḍavāritaḥ / vaidikamapi vaco 'styarthaniṣṭhaṃ viśiṣṭārthapramāṇasadbhāva eva pramāṇam / tatra nirapekṣam / tatpramāṇadvārā ca viśiṣṭārthasiddhiriti samānam /
tatsaṃbhavo 'laukikārthe (laiṅgike 'rthe --edition) buddhavākyārthavanna tu
units.translation:
If the Veda is independent, no rule can prevent that. Someone may object: inference establishes only that another means of knowledge is available, so it does not produce knowledge later. Such a means can concern the past, present, or future: perception of something that has passed concerns the past, perception of what will occur concerns the future, and perception of a present fire concerns the present. This is unsound, for a permanent object that is to be inferred does not fit that threefold division. Moreover, an inferential sign too would be invalid because it depends on another means of knowledge. One might say it is independent because the sign itself establishes that another means of knowledge exists: at that point the sign is a means of knowledge precisely concerning the existence of another means, without relying on anything else, and the object is established through that means.

This rule does not prevent the same account of the Veda. A Vedic statement whose subject is existence is also a means of knowledge only insofar as it establishes the existence of another means of knowledge concerning a qualified object; it is independent in that respect, and through that means the qualified object is established. The two cases are alike. But the possibility of such a means concerning an extraordinary object is not like the meaning of the Buddha’s statement…

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 35
units.deva:
अत्रेति साक्षात्करणाभ्युपायादसमञ्जसम् । स्यान्मतम् --- युक्तं लिङ्गस्य प्रामाण्यमेवम्, अर्थे तस्य प्रमाणान्तरस्य संभवात् । संभवति हि वृष्ट्यादिषु प्रमाणान्तरम् । ततस्तद्द्वारार्थगतिः । न तु सर्वविशेषातीते ब्रह्मण्याम्नायैकनिबन्धने ऽभ्युपगम्यते । तत्र यथैव बुद्धादिवाक्यानाम् ‘एवमयं पुरुषो वेदऽ; इति ज्ञाननिष्ठानामतीन्द्रियार्थे ज्ञानस्यासंभवान्नार्थे प्रामाण्यमतीन्द्रियार्थोपदेशिनाम्, तथात्रापि स्यात् । संभविप्रमाणविषयाप्तवचनवत्तु लिङ्गस्य प्रमाणनिष्ठत्वे ऽपि युज्यते प्रामाण्यम् । तदसत्, ब्रह्मण्यपि साक्षात्करणस्याभ्युपगमादविद्यासंहारे । अविद्यावतां तु तदाम्नायैकनिबन्धनमुच्यते । अपि च
मेयत्वमेव सत्ता चेन्माने त्रिविधता कुतः
units.iast:
atreti sākṣātkaraṇābhyupāyādasamañjasam /
syānmatam --- yuktaṃ liṅgasya prāmāṇyamevam, arthe tasya pramāṇāntarasya saṃbhavāt / saṃbhavati hi vṛṣṭyādiṣu pramāṇāntaram / tatastaddvārārthagatiḥ / na tu sarvaviśeṣātīte brahmaṇyāmnāyaikanibandhane 'bhyupagamyate / tatra yathaiva buddhādivākyānām ‘evamayaṃ puruṣo veda'; iti jñānaniṣṭhānāmatīndriyārthe jñānasyāsaṃbhavānnārthe prāmāṇyamatīndriyārthopadeśinām, tathātrāpi syāt / saṃbhavipramāṇaviṣayāptavacanavattu liṅgasya pramāṇaniṣṭhatve 'pi yujyate prāmāṇyam / tadasat, brahmaṇyapi sākṣātkaraṇasyābhyupagamādavidyāsaṃhāre / avidyāvatāṃ tu tadāmnāyaikanibandhanamucyate / api ca
meyatvameva sattā cenmāne trividhatā kutaḥ
units.translation:
This is inappropriate, because it assumes that direct realization has an instrumental cause. One might think: inference is indeed valid in this way, because another means of knowledge is possible for its object. There can be another means of knowledge concerning rain and the like, and through it the object is known. But Brahman, beyond every particular feature and known only from scripture, cannot be admitted as an object of another means of knowledge. In that respect, one might be like the statements of the Buddha and others, which report what a person knows: “This person knows in this way.” Since knowledge of a supersensible object is impossible for them, their statements are not valid regarding the object. But an inferential sign is valid even when it concerns what is known by another means of knowledge, just as a reliable person’s statement can be valid when its object is accessible to such a means.

This is unsound, because direct realization of Brahman is admitted once ignorance has been dissolved; only for those still under ignorance is it said to rest solely on scripture. Moreover—

“If existence means only being an object of knowledge, why are there three kinds of means of knowledge?”

gloss.en: because it accepts a means for direct realization
for statements of the Buddha and others
for those whose statements rest on knowledge
about an object beyond the senses
for those who teach an object beyond the senses
like a reliable person's statement about an object accessible to another means of knowledge
even when it rests on a means of knowledge
for those still affected by ignorance

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 36
units.deva:
तत्संबन्धादतो नार्थे त्रैविध्यमवकल्पते । यदि च लिङ्गेन प्रमाणमेव मीयते, मीयमानतैव च सत्ता, तत्र प्रमीयमाणत्वात्प्रमाणं सर्वं सदेव । सच्च वर्तमानमित्युच्यते । तत्र वर्तमानत्वात्प्रमाणस्य सर्वत्रार्थे ‘अस्तिऽ; इत्येव स्यात् । न प्रमाणत्रैविध्यादर्थे त्रैविध्यम्, मीयमानस्य सत्त्वात्सतश्च वर्तमानत्वादिति । अपि च इदमयं प्रष्टव्यः --- किं वर्तमानप्रमाणयोगः प्रमाणसंबन्धः सत्ता, तद्विपर्ययो ऽसत्ता, आहोस्वित् प्रमाणयोगमात्रमनाश्रितकालविशेषम्? तत्र ---
वर्तमानप्रमायोगः सत्तासत्ता विपर्ययः
units.iast:
tatsaṃbandhādato nārthe traividhyamavakalpate /
yadi ca liṅgena pramāṇameva mīyate, mīyamānataiva ca sattā, tatra pramīyamāṇatvātpramāṇaṃ sarvaṃ sadeva / sacca vartamānamityucyate / tatra vartamānatvātpramāṇasya sarvatrārthe ‘asti'; ityeva syāt / na pramāṇatraividhyādarthe traividhyam, mīyamānasya sattvātsataśca vartamānatvāditi /

api ca idamayaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ --- kiṃ vartamānapramāṇayogaḥ pramāṇasaṃbandhaḥ sattā, tadviparyayo 'sattā, āhosvit pramāṇayogamātramanāśritakālaviśeṣam? tatra ---
vartamānapramāyogaḥ sattāsattā viparyayaḥ
units.translation:
Because of that relation, a threefold division of the object cannot be established. If an inferential sign measures only the means of knowledge itself, and being measured is what existence means, then every means of knowledge would be existent because it is being measured. What is existent is called present. Since the means of knowledge is present, every object would then have to be called existent. Thus the object is not divided into three times merely because there are three types of means of knowledge: what is being measured is existent, and what is existent is present.

Moreover, one should ask: is existence the relation to a means of knowledge operating in the present, with nonexistence the opposite; or is existence simply relation to a means of knowledge, without reference to a particular time? Of these—

“Existence is relation to present cognition; nonexistence is its opposite.”

gloss.en: relation to a means of knowledge
mere connection with a means of knowledge
without reference to a particular time

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 37
units.deva: मते यदि ततः प्राप्तमसत्त्वं स्मृतिगोचरे । [क्क्स्_88] न स्मर्यमाणस्य वर्तमानप्रमाणसंबन्धः । ननु स्मर्यमाणे विनाशसंभवान्नैव ‘अस्तिऽ; इति व्यवहारः । सत्यम् । ‘नास्तिऽ; इत्यपि नास्ति । यदि वर्तमानप्रमाणयोगः सत्ता तद्विपर्ययो ऽसत्ता, ‘नास्तिऽ; इत्येव स्यात् न च ‘अस्तिऽ; इति । तस्मादन्ये सदसत्त्वे । प्रमाणयोगमात्रं चेत्सत्तासत्ता विपर्ययः
units.iast:
mate yadi tataḥ prāptamasattvaṃ smṛtigocare /
[kks_88] na smaryamāṇasya vartamānapramāṇasaṃbandhaḥ / nanu smaryamāṇe vināśasaṃbhavānnaiva ‘asti'; iti vyavahāraḥ / satyam / ‘nāsti'; ityapi nāsti / yadi vartamānapramāṇayogaḥ sattā tadviparyayo 'sattā, ‘nāsti'; ityeva syāt na ca ‘asti'; iti / tasmādanye sadasattve /
pramāṇayogamātraṃ cetsattāsattā viparyayaḥ
units.translation: If, according to this view, a remembered object must be nonexistent, then it is not connected with a present means of knowledge. One may object that since what is remembered may have perished, people do not say “it exists.” True, but neither do they say “it does not exist.” If existence is connection with a means of knowledge operating in the present, and nonexistence its opposite, one would only say “it does not exist,” not “it exists.” Therefore existence and nonexistence must be something else. If they are simply connection with a means of knowledge and its opposite, then…

gloss.en: connection with a present means of knowledge
connection with a present means of knowledge
mere connection with a means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 38
units.deva: प्राप्ता प्रमितनष्टेन घटेन मधुधारणा । प्रमिते च न जिज्ञासा पुनः स्यात्सदसत्त्वयोः
units.iast:
prāptā pramitanaṣṭena ghaṭena madhudhāraṇā /
pramite ca na jijñāsā punaḥ syātsadasattvayoḥ
units.translation: One would have to speak of a destroyed pot, already known to be gone, as still able to hold honey. And once an object is known, there would be no further inquiry into whether it exists or not.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 39
units.deva: अनाश्रितकालविशेषे प्रमाणयोगमात्रे सत्त्वे प्रमितनष्टमपि वस्तु सदिति तेनार्थक्रियाप्रसङ्गे ऽनष्टेनेव, सत्त्वाविशेषात् । नष्टानष्टयोर्विशेषान्नैवमिति चेत्, स एव तर्हि विशेषः सदसद्व्यवहारव्यवस्थाया हेतुः कार्यव्यवस्थाया इव, न प्रमाणयोगः । तदनुसारिण्येवैषा दृश्यते लोके । न खलु प्रमितनष्टं ‘सत्ऽइत्युपचरति लोकः । किं च प्रमिते ऽर्थे सदसत्त्वे जिज्ञासेरन्न पुनर्लौकिकाः, सिद्धत्वात्प्रमाणयोगमात्रस्य तल्लक्षणत्वाच्च सत्त्वस्य । अथ प्रमाणयोग्यत्वं सत्ता (म्स्स् अब्; सत्त्वं -- एदितिओन्) नष्टाच्च तच्च्युतम् । स्मर्यमाणे प्रचलितं क्वचिदित्यप्यसुन्दरम्
units.iast:
anāśritakālaviśeṣe pramāṇayogamātre sattve pramitanaṣṭamapi vastu saditi tenārthakriyāprasaṅge 'naṣṭeneva, sattvāviśeṣāt / naṣṭānaṣṭayorviśeṣānnaivamiti cet, sa eva tarhi viśeṣaḥ sadasadvyavahāravyavasthāyā hetuḥ kāryavyavasthāyā iva, na pramāṇayogaḥ /

tadanusāriṇyevaiṣā dṛśyate loke / na khalu pramitanaṣṭaṃ ‘sat'ityupacarati lokaḥ / kiṃ ca pramite 'rthe sadasattve jijñāseranna punarlaukikāḥ, siddhatvātpramāṇayogamātrasya tallakṣaṇatvācca sattvasya /

atha pramāṇayogyatvaṃ sattā (mss ab; sattvaṃ -- edition) naṣṭācca taccyutam /
smaryamāṇe pracalitaṃ kvacidityapyasundaram
units.translation: If existence meant merely being related to a means of knowledge, without reference to a particular time, then even an object known to have been destroyed would count as existent, and practical dealings with it would be possible just as with an undestroyed thing, since both would be equally existent. One may object that the difference between destroyed and undestroyed things prevents this. Then that very difference, not relation to a means of knowledge, is what determines whether we speak of something as existent or nonexistent, just as it determines its practical use. Ordinary usage follows that difference: people do not loosely call an object they know to have been destroyed “existent.” Moreover, ordinary people would inquire whether an object already known by a means of knowledge existed or not, even though its existence is already established and existence has been defined merely as relation to a means of knowledge. If one changes the definition to “being capable of being known,” that too is lost when the object is destroyed. It is also unattractive to say that the definition shifts to something merely remembered in certain cases.

gloss.en: without depending on a particular time
in mere relation to a means of knowledge
of determining usage of existent and nonexistent
relation to a means of knowledge
an object known to be destroyed
of mere relation to a means
capacity to be known by a means

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 40
units.deva:
अथ मतम् --- न वर्तमानप्रमाणयोगः सत्ता, नानाश्रितकालं तद्योगमात्रम् । अपि तु प्रमाणं प्रति योग्यता । सा च नष्टाच्च्युतेति न तस्य सत्त्वप्रसङ्गः । स्मर्यमाणे तु कुतश्चिच्च्युता कुतश्चिन्नेति न सर्वस्यासत्त्वमिति । एतदपि न सुन्दरम्, अभ्युपगतहानात् । तथा हि --- इत्थमर्थस्वभाव एव सत्ता वर्णिता भवति । प्रमाणयोग्यो ऽर्थस्वभावः सत्ता, अर्थस्वभावनिबन्धन एव सदसद्व्यवहारविभागः, न प्रमाणतदभावोपाधिः । तस्य त्वेष कथनोपायः, न प्रमाणसंस्पर्शः, यथा ‘नीलाकारज्ञानयोग्यो ऽर्थो नीलःऽइत्याख्याते ऽपि न नीलशब्दो नीलज्ञानोपाधिः । तथा च सो ऽस्तिशब्देनाभिधीयत इत्यर्थस्वभावनिष्ठम् [क्क्स्_89] अस्त्यर्थप्रधानं वाक्यमिति कुतः सापेक्षत्वम्? प्रमाणस्यासंस्पर्शात् । स्यादेतत् --- भिन्ना एवार्थस्वभावाः प्रमाणं प्रति योग्याः सच्छब्दवाच्याः सन्तु, नैका सत्ता । मा भूत्, नैतत्साध्यम् । सर्वथार्थस्वभावाभिधाय्यस्तिशब्दो न प्रमाणयोगनिमित्त इति । प्रमाणसंस्पर्शे हि सापेक्षता स्यात् । अनेकता तु न कञ्चिद्दोषमावहति । अपि च यदि तस्यानेकत्वम्, कथमभिन्नशब्दप्रवृत्तिः? तथा हि --- भिन्नेष्वभिन्नं विशेषणमुपलक्षणं वाश्रित्यैकः शब्दो वर्तेत, भिन्ननिमित्तो वा साधारणशब्दः स्यादक्षादिवत् । तत्र न तावदनन्तार्थस्वभावेषु साधारणत्वमुपपद्यते, संबन्धग्रहणसामर्थ्यात् । परिमितजातिविषया ह्यक्षादिशब्दाः परिमितोपलक्षणलक्षिता वा स्युः । स्यादेतत् --- द्रव्यत्वादिसामान्यत्रयोपलक्षितानामर्थानां सच्छब्दः साधारण इति । तन्न । यो हि सत्तामवजानीते स द्रव्यत्वादीन्यप्यवजानीत एव । न किल तेजो दृष्टवतो ऽप्सु तदवमर्शो भवति । अपि च सामान्यविशेषसमवाया अपि सन्त एव । न तेष्वौपचारिकः सच्छब्दः प्रत्ययस्यावैलक्षण्यात् । न च सामान्याद्विनोपचारः । सति वा सामान्ये तदेव सच्छब्दार्थः । तदेव च सत्ता, तुल्यत्वात्प्रत्ययस्य । अथ मतम् --- सर्वप्रवादेषु सर्वपदार्थाः परिमितैः कैश्चिद्धर्मैरुपसंगृहीताः । तदुपलक्षणानामनन्तानामप्यर्थानां ‘सत्ऽ; इति साधारणः शब्दः । तदयुक्तम् । संग्रहो हि नैकमन्तरेण । तत्र यदि सच्छब्दार्थतया (सच्छब्दतायां -- एदितिओन्) संग्रहः ‘एतावत्प्रभेदः सच्छब्दार्थःऽइति, नार्थान्तरनिवृत्तिः स्यात् । तत्र न सर्वार्थसंग्रहः स्यात्, यथा ‘नवविधो गोशब्दार्थःऽइति नान्येषामभाव एव । तत्र न प्रवादेभ्यः काचिदर्थतत्त्वावगतिः स्यात् । ननु न प्रवादानामर्थवत्ता साध्या । न ब्रूमः प्रवादानामर्थवत्ता साध्येति । किं तु प्रतिपद्यन्ते प्रवादिनः कञ्चिदर्थस्वभावमेकम्, यस्यायं ‘पञ्च, षट्ऽइत्यादि प्रभेदसंग्रहः । यतो नैकमन्तरेणोपसंग्राहकमवान्तरसंख्यानां निवेशः । अथैतावान् प्रमाणयोग्यो ऽर्थक्रियासामर्थ्यो वेति प्रमाणयोग्यत्वे ऽर्थक्रियासामर्थ्ये वा संग्रहः, ताभ्यामेव सच्छब्दार्थ उपलक्ष्यताम्, व्यर्थः परिमितधर्मोपन्यासः । तत्र सामान्यशब्दतैव स्यात्, न साधारणशब्दता । भिन्ननिमित्तत्वे चाक्षादिशब्देभ्य इव [क्क्स्_90] निमित्तभेदात्संशयः स्यात्, न विशेषप्रतीतिः । न हि ‘सन् घटःऽ; इति निमित्तभेदेषु प्रतिपत्तारः संशेरते । यथैव ‘शुक्लः पटःऽइति निराकाङ्क्षः, तथा ‘सन् घटःऽ; इत्यपि । यस्तु द्रव्यं गुणः कर्म रूपं विज्ञानमिति वा संशयः, न स लौकिकानाम् । लौकिकास्त्वभिन्नमेव निमित्तं प्रतिपद्यन्ते । अर्थाच्च संदेहः, न शब्दात् । कुतः? विशेषप्रतीतिमन्तरेणापि प्रतिपत्तुर्नैराकाङ्क्ष्यात् । यत्र ह्यर्थसामर्थ्येन संशयः, यथा ‘वृक्षश्छिद्यताम्ऽ; इति परशुकुठारादिषु, तत्रान्यतरविशेषानवगमे ऽपि नैराकाङ्क्षम्, यस्य कस्यचिदुपादानात्, अन्यथानवस्थानात् । यत्र तु शब्दात्, तत्र विशेषावगमहेतोर्विना साकाङ्क्षत्वमेव । तदेवं न नानानिमित्तः साधारणशब्दः । विशेषणमप्येकं प्रमाणं स्यात् । तच्च प्रागपि ततः सच्छब्दानुविद्धबुद्ध्युत्पादादनुपपन्नमित्युक्तम् --- ‘मानादेव यतो बुद्धिःऽ; इति प्रपञ्चेन । अपि च कार्यादपि वृत्तमेव प्रमाणमवसीयते । तत्र कुतस्तद्विशिष्टता । न खल्वर्थो ऽसन्निहितविशेषगुणो विशिष्टो भवति । न च निश्चिते विशेषणाभावे विशिष्टाभिधानानुविद्धः संशयो भवति दण्डाभावनिश्चय इव ‘दण्डी न वाऽ; इति । भवति च शून्यनगरादिषु चिरनिखातनिधिषु प्रमाणाभावनिश्चये ऽपि ‘सन्ति नऽइति संशयः । तस्मादन्यः प्रमाणयोगात्सदर्थः, यत्रैष संशयः । नाप्युपलक्षणं प्रमाणम्, प्रमितध्वस्तेषु सच्छब्दाप्रयोगात्स्मर्यमाणे च सच्छब्दानुविद्धात्संदेहात् । वृत्तप्रमाणसंबन्धस्य प्रमाणोपलक्षितत्वात्सत्त्वमेव स्यात्, नासत्त्वम्, न संशयः । यो ऽप्यर्थक्रियया सच्छब्दार्थं विशिनष्टि उपलक्षयति वा, तस्यापि प्राक्कार्यदर्शनान्न सच्छब्दयोगः स्यात् । अथ प्रमाणजननमेवार्थक्रियां ब्रूयात्, प्रमाणादेवास्तिबुद्धिर्न स्यात् । अथ वैकल्पिकीयं प्रमाणोत्तरकालतेति मतम्, लिङ्गान्न स्यात् । अथ निर्ज्ञातकार्यसंबन्धमेव लिङ्गेनानुगम्यते, एवं तर्हि प्रमेयाभावः । तथा हि --- कार्यवत्ता ह्यस्त्यर्थः, सा चाधिगतैव । कार्यवत्तयैव कार्यवत्तावगम्यत इत्यचतुरस्रम् । कार्यकारणयोश्च यौगपद्याभावाद्विशिष्टतानुपपत्तिः । अथोपलक्षणम्, अतीतस्यापि [क्क्स्_91] सत्त्वप्रसङ्गः । स्मर्यमाणे च संशयो न स्यादित्युक्तम् । तस्माद्यथैव नीलादिशब्दार्थो ऽर्थस्वभावः, न कार्यलक्ष्यः, न प्रमाणलक्ष्यः, अनवस्थानात् । स्वरूपव्यवस्थस्तु यथाप्रमाणमवसीयते । तथा सदर्थस्वभावो ऽपीति युक्तम् । कार्यप्रमाणसदसद्भावनिबन्धने हि सदसद्व्यवहारविभागे तस्याप्रवृत्तिरेव कार्यप्रमाणसदसद्व्यवहारविभागस्यापि तन्निबन्धत्वप्रसङ्गात्, अनवस्थानात् । तस्मादर्थस्वभाव एका सत्तेति (@स्वभाव एकः सत्तेति -- एदितिओन्) ब्रह्मविदो मन्यन्ते । अथ मतम् --- नार्थस्वभावो योग्यता, प्रमाणहेतुसद्भावस्तु । न चासतां प्रमाणहेतवः सन्तीति । तदयुक्तम् ---

भूमौ निखातं निर्लिङ्गमवेद्यानुपपन्नकम् । नष्टद्रष्टृकमत्येति यत्सर्वमितियोग्यताम्

atha matam --- na vartamānapramāṇayogaḥ sattā, nānāśritakālaṃ tadyogamātram / api tu pramāṇaṃ prati yogyatā / sā ca naṣṭāccyuteti na tasya sattvaprasaṅgaḥ / smaryamāṇe tu kutaściccyutā kutaścinneti na sarvasyāsattvamiti / etadapi na sundaram, abhyupagatahānāt / tathā hi --- itthamarthasvabhāva eva sattā varṇitā bhavati / pramāṇayogyo 'rthasvabhāvaḥ sattā, arthasvabhāvanibandhana eva sadasadvyavahāravibhāgaḥ, na pramāṇatadabhāvopādhiḥ / tasya tveṣa kathanopāyaḥ, na pramāṇasaṃsparśaḥ, yathā ‘nīlākārajñānayogyo 'rtho nīlaḥ'ityākhyāte 'pi na nīlaśabdo nīlajñānopādhiḥ / tathā ca so 'stiśabdenābhidhīyata ityarthasvabhāvaniṣṭham [kks_89] astyarthapradhānaṃ vākyamiti kutaḥ sāpekṣatvam? pramāṇasyāsaṃsparśāt /

syādetat --- bhinnā evārthasvabhāvāḥ pramāṇaṃ prati yogyāḥ sacchabdavācyāḥ santu, naikā sattā / mā bhūt, naitatsādhyam / sarvathārthasvabhāvābhidhāyyastiśabdo na pramāṇayoganimitta iti / pramāṇasaṃsparśe hi sāpekṣatā syāt / anekatā tu na kañciddoṣamāvahati / api ca yadi tasyānekatvam, kathamabhinnaśabdapravṛttiḥ? tathā hi --- bhinneṣvabhinnaṃ viśeṣaṇamupalakṣaṇaṃ vāśrityaikaḥ śabdo varteta, bhinnanimitto vā sādhāraṇaśabdaḥ syādakṣādivat / tatra na tāvadanantārthasvabhāveṣu sādhāraṇatvamupapadyate, saṃbandhagrahaṇasāmarthyāt / parimitajātiviṣayā hyakṣādiśabdāḥ parimitopalakṣaṇalakṣitā vā syuḥ / syādetat --- dravyatvādisāmānyatrayopalakṣitānāmarthānāṃ sacchabdaḥ sādhāraṇa iti / tanna / yo hi sattāmavajānīte sa dravyatvādīnyapyavajānīta eva / na kila tejo dṛṣṭavato 'psu tadavamarśo bhavati / api ca sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyā api santa eva / na teṣvaupacārikaḥ sacchabdaḥ pratyayasyāvailakṣaṇyāt / na ca sāmānyādvinopacāraḥ / sati vā sāmānye tadeva sacchabdārthaḥ / tadeva ca sattā, tulyatvātpratyayasya / atha matam --- sarvapravādeṣu sarvapadārthāḥ parimitaiḥ kaiściddharmairupasaṃgṛhītāḥ / tadupalakṣaṇānāmanantānāmapyarthānāṃ ‘sat'; iti sādhāraṇaḥ śabdaḥ / tadayuktam / saṃgraho hi naikamantareṇa / tatra yadi sacchabdārthatayā (sacchabdatāyāṃ -- edition) saṃgrahaḥ ‘etāvatprabhedaḥ sacchabdārthaḥ'iti, nārthāntaranivṛttiḥ syāt / tatra na sarvārthasaṃgrahaḥ syāt, yathā ‘navavidho gośabdārthaḥ'iti nānyeṣāmabhāva eva / tatra na pravādebhyaḥ kācidarthatattvāvagatiḥ syāt / nanu na pravādānāmarthavattā sādhyā / na brūmaḥ pravādānāmarthavattā sādhyeti / kiṃ tu pratipadyante pravādinaḥ kañcidarthasvabhāvamekam, yasyāyaṃ ‘pañca, ṣaṭ'ityādi prabhedasaṃgrahaḥ / yato naikamantareṇopasaṃgrāhakamavāntarasaṃkhyānāṃ niveśaḥ / athaitāvān pramāṇayogyo 'rthakriyāsāmarthyo veti pramāṇayogyatve 'rthakriyāsāmarthye vā saṃgrahaḥ, tābhyāmeva sacchabdārtha upalakṣyatām, vyarthaḥ parimitadharmopanyāsaḥ / tatra sāmānyaśabdataiva syāt, na sādhāraṇaśabdatā / bhinnanimittatve cākṣādiśabdebhya iva [kks_90] nimittabhedātsaṃśayaḥ syāt, na viśeṣapratītiḥ / na hi ‘san ghaṭaḥ'; iti nimittabhedeṣu pratipattāraḥ saṃśerate / yathaiva ‘śuklaḥ paṭaḥ'iti nirākāṅkṣaḥ, tathā ‘san ghaṭaḥ'; ityapi / yastu dravyaṃ guṇaḥ karma rūpaṃ vijñānamiti vā saṃśayaḥ, na sa laukikānām / laukikāstvabhinnameva nimittaṃ pratipadyante / arthācca saṃdehaḥ, na śabdāt / kutaḥ? viśeṣapratītimantareṇāpi pratipatturnairākāṅkṣyāt / yatra hyarthasāmarthyena saṃśayaḥ, yathā ‘vṛkṣaśchidyatām'; iti paraśukuṭhārādiṣu, tatrānyataraviśeṣānavagame 'pi nairākāṅkṣam, yasya kasyacidupādānāt, anyathānavasthānāt / yatra tu śabdāt, tatra viśeṣāvagamahetorvinā sākāṅkṣatvameva / tadevaṃ na nānānimittaḥ sādhāraṇaśabdaḥ / viśeṣaṇamapyekaṃ pramāṇaṃ syāt / tacca prāgapi tataḥ sacchabdānuviddhabuddhyutpādādanupapannamityuktam --- ‘mānādeva yato buddhiḥ'; iti prapañcena / api ca kāryādapi vṛttameva pramāṇamavasīyate / tatra kutastadviśiṣṭatā / na khalvartho 'sannihitaviśeṣaguṇo viśiṣṭo bhavati / na ca niścite viśeṣaṇābhāve viśiṣṭābhidhānānuviddhaḥ saṃśayo bhavati daṇḍābhāvaniścaya iva ‘daṇḍī na vā'; iti / bhavati ca śūnyanagarādiṣu ciranikhātanidhiṣu pramāṇābhāvaniścaye 'pi ‘santi na'iti saṃśayaḥ / tasmādanyaḥ pramāṇayogātsadarthaḥ, yatraiṣa saṃśayaḥ / nāpyupalakṣaṇaṃ pramāṇam, pramitadhvasteṣu sacchabdāprayogātsmaryamāṇe ca sacchabdānuviddhātsaṃdehāt /

vṛttapramāṇasaṃbandhasya pramāṇopalakṣitatvātsattvameva syāt, nāsattvam, na saṃśayaḥ / yo 'pyarthakriyayā sacchabdārthaṃ viśinaṣṭi upalakṣayati vā, tasyāpi prākkāryadarśanānna sacchabdayogaḥ syāt / atha pramāṇajananamevārthakriyāṃ brūyāt, pramāṇādevāstibuddhirna syāt / atha vaikalpikīyaṃ pramāṇottarakālateti matam, liṅgānna syāt / atha nirjñātakāryasaṃbandhameva liṅgenānugamyate, evaṃ tarhi prameyābhāvaḥ / tathā hi --- kāryavattā hyastyarthaḥ, sā cādhigataiva / kāryavattayaiva kāryavattāvagamyata ityacaturasram / kāryakāraṇayośca yaugapadyābhāvādviśiṣṭatānupapattiḥ / athopalakṣaṇam, atītasyāpi [kks_91] sattvaprasaṅgaḥ / smaryamāṇe ca saṃśayo na syādityuktam / tasmādyathaiva nīlādiśabdārtho 'rthasvabhāvaḥ, na kāryalakṣyaḥ, na pramāṇalakṣyaḥ, anavasthānāt / svarūpavyavasthastu yathāpramāṇamavasīyate / tathā sadarthasvabhāvo 'pīti yuktam / kāryapramāṇasadasadbhāvanibandhane hi sadasadvyavahāravibhāge tasyāpravṛttireva kāryapramāṇasadasadvyavahāravibhāgasyāpi tannibandhatvaprasaṅgāt, anavasthānāt / tasmādarthasvabhāva ekā satteti (@svabhāva ekaḥ satteti -- edition) brahmavido manyante /

atha matam --- nārthasvabhāvo yogyatā, pramāṇahetusadbhāvastu / na cāsatāṃ pramāṇahetavaḥ santīti / tadayuktam ---

bhūmau nikhātaṃ nirliṅgamavedyānupapannakam /
naṣṭadraṣṭṛkamatyeti yatsarvamitiyogyatām
units.translation:
Someone may say that existence is neither a present relation to a means of knowledge nor merely a relation to time, which is different in different cases; rather, it is an object’s fitness to be known by a means of knowledge. That fitness ceases when the object is destroyed, so it does not follow that the object remains existent. And when something is remembered, the fitness to be known may have ceased in one case and not another, so this does not make everything nonexistent. This is not a sound account, because it abandons what had already been accepted. On this account, existence is actually described as the nature of the object itself: existence is the object’s nature of being fit for a means of knowledge. The distinction between what is and is not rests on the object’s nature, not on whether a means of knowledge happens to be present or absent. The mention of a connection with a means of knowledge is only a way of explaining it; it is not the object’s actual contact with a means of knowledge. Even when one says, “The object fit to be known by a cognition of blue is blue,” the word “blue” is not a condition that depends on blue-cognition. In this way, the sentence “It exists” has “existence” as its principal subject matter, grounded in the nature of the object. Why, then, would it depend on another means of knowledge?

Someone may say that there are many distinct natures of objects fit for a means of knowledge, and all are denoted by the word “existent”; there is no single existence. Let there be many; that is not what needs to be established. In every case, the word “existent” denotes the nature of an object, not its fitness for a means of knowledge, and so it is not dependent on one. But if existence is many, how can one undivided word apply? A single word may apply to distinct things by relying on a common qualifier or identifying mark, or it may be a common word whose meaning varies in different instances, as with the word for an axle. It is not plausible that infinitely many natures of objects could all be gathered under one common meaning, since the capacity to understand a relation between a word and its meaning would be exceeded. Words such as “axle” concern a limited class or objects identified by a limited set of marks. Someone may say that the word “existent” applies commonly to objects marked by three universals, such as substance and the like. That is not so. A person who understands existence also understands substance and the other categories; just as seeing light does not make someone reflect on water as well.

Universals, particulars, and inherence are all existent themselves; the word “existent” is not used figuratively of them, since the cognition it produces is not different. Nor is figurative use possible without a universal. If a universal does exist, that alone is what the word “existent” means, since the cognition is the same. Someone may say that in every philosophical system all objects are gathered through a limited set of properties, and the word “existent” is common to the infinitely many objects identified by those markers. This is unreasonable: gathering requires something shared. If the collection is defined as “this many distinctions are what the word ‘existent’ means,” it would not exclude other things. Then it would not gather all objects, just as saying that “the word ‘cow’ has nine kinds of meaning” does not mean that all other things do not exist. On that account, no one could understand the true nature of objects from the different philosophical systems.

One may object that the truth of the philosophical systems is not what needs to be established. We are saying that the proponents of those systems understand some common nature of an object, within which its various distinctions—“five,” “six,” and so on—are gathered. The separate distinctions cannot be placed within a collection without something that gathers them. But if the collection is based on the object’s being fit for a means of knowledge or on its capacity to produce an effect, those very features should be used to identify the meaning of “existent”; describing a limited number of other properties would be pointless. In that case the word would be a general term, not a common term applied to multiple things. If the word’s use were prompted by different things in different cases, it would produce doubt, as with words like “axle,” rather than a distinct understanding. For...

...if the word “existent” referred to different things for different reasons, listeners would be uncertain when they heard, “The pot exists.” But just as “the cloth is white” is understood without uncertainty, “the pot exists” is also understood without uncertainty. Ordinary people do not wonder whether it is a substance, a quality, an action, a form, or a cognition. They understand one and the same basis. Any doubt arises from the object, not from the word. Why? The listener does not need a particular distinction to understand it. Where a doubt arises from the force of the object itself—as in “Let the tree be cut,” when one might use an axe or a hatchet—the listener is not at a loss even without knowing which particular tool is meant, since any one of them may be used. Otherwise there would be no end to asking. But where the doubt arises from a word, one remains uncertain until one knows the particular distinction. Thus the word “existent” is not a common word whose meaning varies with different causes.

Perhaps one distinct qualifier of existence is a means of knowledge. But that does not work: even before the cognition marked by the word “existent” arises, a means of knowledge would have to be established; this has already been explained at length in the argument, “Because the cognition comes from the means of knowledge itself.” Furthermore, if the word is defined by an effect, why should it have that qualifier? An object that is not present with the particular quality is not qualified by it. And if one is certain that the particular quality is absent, there would not be the doubt that comes with a qualified statement, as in “Is he carrying a staff?” when one is certain he has no staff. Yet even when one is certain that there is no means of knowledge in a deserted city, or in the case of treasure buried long ago, one may still be unsure whether the treasure exists. Therefore the meaning of “existent” that gives rise to this doubt is different from its relation to a means of knowledge.

Nor can a means of knowledge itself be the qualifier, since the word “existent” is not used for things known to have been refuted by a means of knowledge, while doubt remains when one remembers something but is unsure whether a means of knowledge had applied to it. If the presence of a means of knowledge marks the meaning of “existent,” then the object must be existent, not nonexistent, whenever the object is marked by a means of knowledge; there should be no doubt. But, as has been said, there is doubt even about something remembered.

The same problem applies to someone who distinguishes or identifies the meaning of “existent” by an object’s capacity to produce an effect: one would have to see the effect before the word “existent” could be applied. If “producing a means of knowledge” is itself the effect, then cognition that something exists could not arise from a means of knowledge. Someone may say that the relation between a sign and its effect is understood after the effect, so that inference comes later. In that case the mark would already be connected with a known effect, and there would be no object to be inferred. The meaning of “existent” would already be established by having an effect, and to understand it from that very capacity would be inelegant. Cause and effect do not occur simultaneously, so the object cannot be qualified by an effect that has not yet occurred. If “having an effect” is merely an identifying mark, then even something in the past would count as existent, and there would be no doubt when it is remembered.

Therefore, just as the meaning of words such as “blue” is the nature of the object itself, not something identified by an effect or by a means of knowledge, since those do not remain consistently present, so too it is reasonable that the nature of the object itself is what the word “existent” means, while that nature is established in accordance with the means of knowledge. If the distinction between “existent” and “nonexistent” depended on the presence or absence of an effect or a means of knowledge, then the distinction between effects and means of knowledge would in turn depend on whether they were existent or nonexistent. This would lead to an endless regress. Therefore, the knowers of Brahman hold that existence is one nature grounded in the object itself.

Someone may object that existence is not the nature of an object but its fitness for a means of knowledge, and that a means of knowledge must have causes, which nonexistent things lack. That is unsound. As the verse says:

“What is buried in the earth, without a sign, unknowable and not established,
surpassing what is seen by a perceiver, exceeds every fitness.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 41
units.deva:
भूमौ निखातमविद्यमानेन्द्रियसंबन्धमदृश्यमानाविनाभूतमसंवेद्यमानान्यथानवकल्पमानं वस्तु प्रलीनद्रष्टृकं यत्तस्य न प्रत्यक्षानुमानार्थापत्त्यागमहेतवः सन्ति । सादृश्यविषयं ह्युपमानम्, तस्य हेतुर्दूरापेत एव । सर्वप्रमाणयोग्यतामतिक्रामति, न च तदसत् । ननु सत्त्वमप्यस्य कथम्? एवमपि संशयः । तत्र प्रमाणहेतुभावलक्षणयोग्यतारूपे सत्त्वे प्रमाणहेत्वभावस्य निश्चयात्संशयो न स्यात् । अथ स्वभावविशेषः कश्चित्प्रमाणं प्रति योग्यः सत्त्वम्, प्रकृतहानादसुन्दरमित्युक्तम् । अथ वा प्रमाणविशिष्टः सच्छब्दार्थ इत्येतदनेन निराक्रियते । न निश्चिते विशेषणाभावे विशिष्टाभिधायिशब्दानुविद्धः संशयो युक्त इति । अपि चाभावस्यापि प्रमेयत्वान्न प्रमाणयोग्यता सत्तालक्षणम् । तथा हि ---

असत्प्रमेयं च तथा यथैव स्थापयत्ययम् । अमितं हि तथा कस्मात्तथा न पुनरन्यथा
units.iast:
bhūmau nikhātamavidyamānendriyasaṃbandhamadṛśyamānāvinābhūtamasaṃvedyamānānyathānavakalpamānaṃ vastu pralīnadraṣṭṛkaṃ yattasya na pratyakṣānumānārthāpattyāgamahetavaḥ santi / sādṛśyaviṣayaṃ hyupamānam, tasya heturdūrāpeta eva / sarvapramāṇayogyatāmatikrāmati, na ca tadasat / nanu sattvamapyasya katham? evamapi saṃśayaḥ / tatra pramāṇahetubhāvalakṣaṇayogyatārūpe sattve pramāṇahetvabhāvasya niścayātsaṃśayo na syāt / atha svabhāvaviśeṣaḥ kaścitpramāṇaṃ prati yogyaḥ sattvam, prakṛtahānādasundaramityuktam / atha vā pramāṇaviśiṣṭaḥ sacchabdārtha ityetadanena nirākriyate / na niścite viśeṣaṇābhāve viśiṣṭābhidhāyiśabdānuviddhaḥ saṃśayo yukta iti /

api cābhāvasyāpi prameyatvānna pramāṇayogyatā sattālakṣaṇam / tathā hi ---

asatprameyaṃ ca tathā yathaiva sthāpayatyayam /
amitaṃ hi tathā kasmāttathā na punaranyathā
units.translation:
A thing that is buried in the ground, has no contact with the senses, cannot be seen, is inseparable from what is unseen, cannot be experienced, and cannot be explained in any other way after the observer has disappeared, has no causal relation with perception, inference, presumption, or scripture. Comparison concerns similarity, so its basis is far removed. Such a thing lies beyond the reach of every means of knowledge; yet it is not nonexistent.

One might object: how can it exist at all? That too is uncertain. If existence means being fit to be an object or a cause of a means of knowledge, then it cannot be uncertain, since the absence of any means of knowledge or causal relation has been established. If existence is some special nature that is fit to be known by a means of knowledge, that too was rejected as an unattractive departure from the issue. Or perhaps the meaning of the word “existent” is an object qualified by a means of knowledge; this argument refutes that as well. When the absence of the qualifier is established, doubt that is nevertheless shaped by a word denoting something qualified is not reasonable. Moreover, since even absence is an object of knowledge, being knowable cannot define existence. For—

“This person establishes the nonexistent as an object of knowledge in just the same way. Since what is not measured is so established, why should it not be otherwise?”

not explainable in any other way
causes through perception, inference, presumption, or scripture
the reach of every means of knowledge
when existence means fitness to be a means of knowledge or its cause
of the absence of a means of knowledge or its cause
because it abandons the subject at hand
qualified by a means of knowledge
shaped by a word that denotes something qualified
because it is an object of knowledge
fitness to be known by a means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 42
units.deva:
अवश्यं खल्वनेन सदसद्व्यवहारविभागमिच्छता असत्कथञ्चिद्व्यवस्थाप्यम्, अन्यथा व्यवहारसंकरात् । तत्र यदि प्रमाणस्याविषयः, यदि [क्क्स्_92] सर्वशक्तिविरहो वासद्बुद्धेर्विषयः । सर्वथा तथा प्रमेयम् । अपरिच्छिन्नं हि तथा प्रमाणेन किमिति तद्विधम्, न पुनरन्यथा स्यात्? न चेत्तस्य तथाभावे ऽतथाभावे वा प्रमाणव्यापारः किंनिमित्त एकपक्षानुरागः?

अपि च ---

अमित्वा कण्टकाभावं चरणं न्यस्यते कथम् । नान्यग्रहात्तस्य भावे पुरस्ताच्च प्रसङ्गतः
units.iast:
avaśyaṃ khalvanena sadasadvyavahāravibhāgamicchatā asatkathañcidvyavasthāpyam, anyathā vyavahārasaṃkarāt / tatra yadi pramāṇasyāviṣayaḥ, yadi [kks_92] sarvaśaktiviraho vāsadbuddherviṣayaḥ / sarvathā tathā prameyam / aparicchinnaṃ hi tathā pramāṇena kimiti tadvidham, na punaranyathā syāt? na cettasya tathābhāve 'tathābhāve vā pramāṇavyāpāraḥ kiṃnimitta ekapakṣānurāgaḥ?

api ca ---

amitvā kaṇṭakābhāvaṃ caraṇaṃ nyasyate katham /
nānyagrahāttasya bhāve purastācca prasaṅgataḥ
units.translation:
Anyone who wants to distinguish ordinary usage of existent from nonexistent must somehow establish what nonexistent means; otherwise usage would be confused. If nonexistent is outside the scope of a means of knowledge, or if it is the object of a cognition that lacks every power of knowing, in either case it is an object of knowledge. If it were not determined by a means of knowledge in this way, how would it be so rather than otherwise? And if no means of knowledge operates to determine whether it is or is not that way, what basis is there for favoring one side?

Moreover—

“How can one place a foot without knowing that there are no thorns? If this absence were known from perceiving something else, it would follow beforehand as well.”

gloss.en: the distinction in usage of existent and nonexistent
or when it is not so
the operation of a means of knowledge

units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 43
units.deva:
जिज्ञासा न प्रवर्तेत यदि संवित्त्यभावतः । ‘दृष्टिपूतं पदं न्यसेत्ऽ; इति कीटकण्टकाद्यभावे ऽप्रमिते कथं तन्न्यासः? तथा हि --- कीटकण्टकाद्यर्थान्तरभूतलादिपरिच्छेदात्स स्यात्, कीटाद्यपरिच्छेदात्, अभावपरिच्छेदाद्वा । तत्र न तावदर्थान्तरपरिच्छेदात्, कण्टकादिभावे ऽपि प्रसङ्गात् । तत्रापि वस्त्वन्तरपरिच्छेदस्य सत्त्वात् । प्रागपि च भूभागपरिच्छेदात् प्रसज्येत, यस्य कस्यचिद्वस्त्वन्तरस्य परिच्छित्तेर्विद्यमानत्वात् । अथ कीटकण्टकाद्यपरिच्छेदात्, न तद्भावाभावजिज्ञासा स्यात् । जिज्ञासापूर्वमपि ( जिज्ञासापूर्वकादपि -- एदितिओन्) प्रयत्नात्तदपरिच्छेदमात्रमेव प्राप्यते यस्याभावो न प्रमेयः । तच्च प्रागपि ततो ऽस्ति । अभावे तु प्रमेये ऽभावनिश्चयाय जिज्ञासा युज्यते । न चापरिच्छेद एव जिज्ञास्यः, स्वतः सिद्धत्वात् । परिच्छेदेन हि स निवर्त्यते । अप्रमेयत्वाच्च सो ऽपि खल्वभाव इत्यप्रमेयः । अथ मतम् --- सत्सूपलम्भहेतुषु प्रमाणविषयस्यापरिच्छेदात् प्रवृत्तिः । तदसत् ---
प्रमाणविषयत्वस्य नोपयोगो ऽत्र दृश्यते
units.iast:
jijñāsā na pravarteta yadi saṃvittyabhāvataḥ /
‘dṛṣṭipūtaṃ padaṃ nyaset'; iti kīṭakaṇṭakādyabhāve 'pramite kathaṃ tannyāsaḥ? tathā hi --- kīṭakaṇṭakādyarthāntarabhūtalādiparicchedātsa syāt, kīṭādyaparicchedāt, abhāvaparicchedādvā / tatra na tāvadarthāntaraparicchedāt, kaṇṭakādibhāve 'pi prasaṅgāt / tatrāpi vastvantaraparicchedasya sattvāt / prāgapi ca bhūbhāgaparicchedāt prasajyeta, yasya kasyacidvastvantarasya paricchittervidyamānatvāt / atha kīṭakaṇṭakādyaparicchedāt, na tadbhāvābhāvajijñāsā syāt / jijñāsāpūrvamapi ( jijñāsāpūrvakādapi -- edition) prayatnāttadaparicchedamātrameva prāpyate yasyābhāvo na prameyaḥ / tacca prāgapi tato 'sti / abhāve tu prameye 'bhāvaniścayāya jijñāsā yujyate / na cāpariccheda eva jijñāsyaḥ, svataḥ siddhatvāt / paricchedena hi sa nivartyate / aprameyatvācca so 'pi khalvabhāva ityaprameyaḥ /

atha matam --- satsūpalambhahetuṣu pramāṇaviṣayasyāparicchedāt pravṛttiḥ / tadasat ---
pramāṇaviṣayatvasya nopayogo 'tra dṛśyate
units.translation:
If no cognition of absence arises, there would be no inquiry. But how could one follow the instruction “Place your step after looking carefully” without first determining that there are no insects, thorns, and the like? This determination could arise from perceiving the ground as something different from insects and thorns, from not perceiving the insects and so forth, or from perceiving their absence. It cannot come merely from perceiving something else: then the same conclusion would follow even when thorns are present, since one also perceives other things there. Indeed, it would follow even before looking at the ground, since some other thing is always being perceived.

If it comes from not perceiving insects and thorns, there would be no inquiry into whether they are present or absent. Even effort preceded by inquiry would yield only their non-apprehension, and that absence is not an object of knowledge; moreover, it is already present beforehand. But if absence itself is the object of knowledge, inquiry is reasonable in order to determine that absence. Nor can mere non-apprehension be what is inquired into, since it is self-established and is removed by apprehension. And that absence too, since it is not an object of knowledge, would itself not be knowable. The opponent may say that when the conditions for perceiving something are present, one acts because the object has not been apprehended by a means of knowledge. This is unsound:

“We see no use here in making the object’s being within the scope of a means of knowledge…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 44
units.deva: असद्बोधे ऽनन्यहेतुभानेन ह्युपयुज्यते । अपरिच्छेदाच्चेत्प्रवृत्तिर्न प्रमाणविषयत्वस्योपयोगः, इतरत्राप्यपरिच्छेदस्य तुल्यत्वात्ततश्च प्रवृत्तेः । यस्य स्वभावः प्रमेयः, तत्परिच्छेदात्प्रवृत्तिः, [क्क्स्_93] तस्यानन्यनिमित्तत्वेनोपयोगवत्प्रमाणविषयत्वम् । नायमपरिच्छेदः सत्येवार्थे हेतुवैकल्यनिमित्तः, समग्रत्वात्तद्धेतूनाम् । तस्मादर्थाभावादिति । अथ यत्र प्रवृत्तिः स्यात्तत्र केवलसंविदः
units.iast:
asadbodhe 'nanyahetubhānena hyupayujyate /
aparicchedāccetpravṛttirna pramāṇaviṣayatvasyopayogaḥ, itaratrāpyaparicchedasya tulyatvāttataśca pravṛtteḥ / yasya svabhāvaḥ prameyaḥ, tatparicchedātpravṛttiḥ, [kks_93] tasyānanyanimittatvenopayogavatpramāṇaviṣayatvam / nāyamaparicchedaḥ satyevārthe hetuvaikalyanimittaḥ, samagratvāttaddhetūnām / tasmādarthābhāvāditi /
atha yatra pravṛttiḥ syāttatra kevalasaṃvidaḥ
units.translation: It is useful to explain cognition of the nonexistent by saying that it appears without any other cause. If action arises merely from non-apprehension, then being an object of a means of knowledge serves no purpose, since the same non-apprehension is present in other cases too, and action would follow there as well. Action arises from apprehending the nature of the object, and the fact that it is within the scope of a means of knowledge is useful because it is the object’s own character and has no other cause. Non-apprehension is not due to a defect in the conditions for knowing when the object really exists, since all the conditions are complete. Therefore, it is due to the object’s absence. But if there is action in the case of what is absent, then cognition alone…

gloss.en: in cognition of what is nonexistent
of being the object of a means of knowledge
because it has no other cause
being within the scope of a means of knowledge
from the absence of the object

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 45
units.deva: जिज्ञासेत न सूक्ष्मार्थं कैवल्यं संविदो यदि । केवलो विषयो नेष्टो रूपोन्मिश्रे ऽपि तद्यतः
units.iast:
jijñāseta na sūkṣmārthaṃ kaivalyaṃ saṃvido yadi /
kevalo viṣayo neṣṭo rūponmiśre 'pi tadyataḥ
units.translation: If a person who values consciousness alone did not inquire into the subtle meaning, then only an isolated object would be desired; but that is not wanted, since the object is mixed with form.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 46
units.deva: विशिष्टस्य च नास्त्यन्यदन्याभावाद्विशेषणम् । यदि मतम् --- यत्र भूभागादौ चरणन्यासादिलक्षणा प्रवृत्तिः, तस्य केवलस्य सा ज्ञानादिति । तत्रापि संप्रधार्यम् --- किमिदं ज्ञानस्य कैवल्यमभिसंहितमेकविषयप्रतिनियमो विषयान्तरासंसर्गः, आहोस्विद्विषयस्य । यदि विज्ञानस्य, प्रमिते ऽपि भूभागादौ स्थूले सूक्ष्मकीटकण्टकादिभावाभावपरीक्षा न स्यात् । प्रवर्तेतैव, केवलभूतलावग्रहज्ञानात् । अथ विषयस्य, तत्रापि संप्रधार्यम् --- स्वरूपेण वा विषयस्य कैवल्यम्, विशेषणयोगेन वा । तत्र न तावत्स्वरूपेण, मिश्रे ऽपि तस्य भावात् । विशेषणयोगेन कैवल्ये प्राप्ता कीटकण्टकाद्यभावविशिष्टपरिच्छेदात्पदन्यासादिलक्षणा प्रवृत्तिः । यतो नान्याभावाद्विशेषणमन्यादृशं किञ्चिद्दृश्यते, यद्विशेषणं वस्तु केवलं स्यादिति । नास्तीति धीव्यवहृती विषयं कमुपाश्रिते
units.iast:
viśiṣṭasya ca nāstyanyadanyābhāvādviśeṣaṇam /
yadi matam --- yatra bhūbhāgādau caraṇanyāsādilakṣaṇā pravṛttiḥ, tasya kevalasya sā jñānāditi / tatrāpi saṃpradhāryam --- kimidaṃ jñānasya kaivalyamabhisaṃhitamekaviṣayapratiniyamo viṣayāntarāsaṃsargaḥ, āhosvidviṣayasya / yadi vijñānasya, pramite 'pi bhūbhāgādau sthūle sūkṣmakīṭakaṇṭakādibhāvābhāvaparīkṣā na syāt / pravartetaiva, kevalabhūtalāvagrahajñānāt / atha viṣayasya, tatrāpi saṃpradhāryam --- svarūpeṇa vā viṣayasya kaivalyam, viśeṣaṇayogena vā / tatra na tāvatsvarūpeṇa, miśre 'pi tasya bhāvāt / viśeṣaṇayogena kaivalye prāptā kīṭakaṇṭakādyabhāvaviśiṣṭaparicchedātpadanyāsādilakṣaṇā pravṛttiḥ / yato nānyābhāvādviśeṣaṇamanyādṛśaṃ kiñciddṛśyate, yadviśeṣaṇaṃ vastu kevalaṃ syāditi /
nāstīti dhīvyavahṛtī viṣayaṃ kamupāśrite
units.translation:
There is no other kind of qualifier for a qualified object apart from the absence of something else. Someone may say: the action of placing one’s foot and the like occurs on a patch of ground simply because that ground is known. But this too must be examined. What does “simply” mean here: that the cognition is restricted to one object and does not involve another object, or that the object itself is simple? If it means the cognition, then even after the ground has been perceived, one would not examine whether tiny insects, thorns, and the like are present or absent on that large surface. One would simply act on the basis of knowing the ground alone.

If it means the object, that too must be examined: is the object simple in its own nature, or simple because it is joined to a qualifier? It is not simple in its own nature, since it is mixed with other things. If its simplicity consists in being qualified, then the action of placing one’s foot and the like depends on perceiving the ground as qualified by the absence of insects, thorns, and the like. No distinct feature is observed that could qualify an object as “simple” other than the absence of something else. On what object, then, do the cognition and everyday usage “it is absent” rely?

gloss.en: apart from the absence of something else
on a patch of ground and the like
characterized by placing the foot and similar actions
a patch of ground and the like
tiny insects, thorns, and the like
from knowing only the bare ground surface
from perceiving it as qualified by the absence of insects, thorns, and the like
characterized by placing the foot and similar actions
apart from the absence of something else

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 47
units.deva:
मानाभावं यदि क्षुण्णं मेयाभावस्य तत्र किम् । अपि चानेन ‘नास्तिऽइति बुद्धिशब्दयोर्विषयो वाच्यः । स न वस्तुस्वरूपेण, मिश्रे ऽपि प्रसङ्गात् । न केवलम्, अभावादन्यस्य विशेषणस्याभावादित्युक्तम् । ननु ‘नास्तिऽइत्ययमर्थः ‘नेदं प्रमीयतेऽ; इति, न पुनरभावो ऽवगम्यते । विरुद्धमिदम् --- नास्त्यवगम्यते चेति । यद्येवं प्रमाणाभावो विषय उक्तः स्यात् ‘नास्तिऽ; इति धीशब्दयोः, तत्र को ऽपराधः स्यात्प्रमेयाभावस्य, येन [क्क्स्_94] तमतिलङ्घ्य प्रमाणाभावो विषय उच्यते? न हि तयोर्निरुपाख्यत्वे कश्चिद्विशेषः । अथ मतम् ---
अग्रहे ऽसद्ग्रहभ्रान्तिरभावव्यवहृद्भ्रमः
units.iast:
mānābhāvaṃ yadi kṣuṇṇaṃ meyābhāvasya tatra kim /
api cānena ‘nāsti'iti buddhiśabdayorviṣayo vācyaḥ / sa na vastusvarūpeṇa, miśre 'pi prasaṅgāt / na kevalam, abhāvādanyasya viśeṣaṇasyābhāvādityuktam / nanu ‘nāsti'ityayamarthaḥ ‘nedaṃ pramīyate'; iti, na punarabhāvo 'vagamyate / viruddhamidam --- nāstyavagamyate ceti / yadyevaṃ pramāṇābhāvo viṣaya uktaḥ syāt ‘nāsti'; iti dhīśabdayoḥ, tatra ko 'parādhaḥ syātprameyābhāvasya, yena [kks_94] tamatilaṅghya pramāṇābhāvo viṣaya ucyate? na hi tayornirupākhyatve kaścidviśeṣaḥ /

atha matam ---
agrahe 'sadgrahabhrāntirabhāvavyavahṛdbhramaḥ
units.translation:
If the absence of a means of knowledge has been thoroughly established, what is left there of the absence of an object of knowledge? Moreover, one must say what the cognition and the word “it does not exist” have as their object. It cannot be the nature of an object itself, since then the same would follow for objects in which something is present. Nor can it simply be the absence of an object, since it has already been said that there is no qualifier other than absence.

One might object that the meaning of “it does not exist” is “This is not known by any means of knowledge,” and that it does not convey apprehension of an absence. This is contradictory: it is said both that something is not and that it is apprehended. If the object of the cognition and word “it does not exist” is the absence of a means of knowledge, what fault is there in saying that the object of an absence of knowledge is the absence of the object, rather than skipping over it and making the absence of a means of knowledge the object? There is no difference between them if both are utterly inexpressible. Someone may object:

“When there is non-apprehension, there is a mistaken apprehension of the nonexistent; there is confusion about speaking of absence.”

gloss.en: absence of a means of knowledge
of the absence of an object to be known
of the cognition and the word
as the nature of an object
absence of a means of knowledge
in the absence of an object to be known
the error of apprehending the nonexistent

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 48
units.deva:
अभावे च व्यवहृतेरदृष्टौ ध्वान्तदृष्टिवत् । नैव स्तां ‘नास्तिऽ; इति बुद्धिव्यवहारौ । कथमिमौ सर्वजनानां प्रतीतावपह्नूयेते? उच्यते --- भ्रमो ऽयं सद्बुद्ध्यभावे तद्विपर्ययपरिच्छेद इति । तथा सद्व्यवहाराभावे तद्विपर्ययव्यवहारभ्रमः यथालोकदर्शनाभावे ‘तमः पश्यामिऽइति विभ्रमः । न हि तमो नाम किञ्चिद्दृश्यमस्ति । नैतत्सारम् ---
इत्थं भवेत्सुषुप्तादौ त्रैलोक्याभावदृग्भ्रमः
units.iast:
abhāve ca vyavahṛteradṛṣṭau dhvāntadṛṣṭivat /
naiva stāṃ ‘nāsti'; iti buddhivyavahārau / kathamimau sarvajanānāṃ pratītāvapahnūyete? ucyate --- bhramo 'yaṃ sadbuddhyabhāve tadviparyayapariccheda iti / tathā sadvyavahārābhāve tadviparyayavyavahārabhramaḥ yathālokadarśanābhāve ‘tamaḥ paśyāmi'iti vibhramaḥ / na hi tamo nāma kiñciddṛśyamasti /

naitatsāram ---
itthaṃ bhavetsuṣuptādau trailokyābhāvadṛgbhramaḥ
units.translation:
If there were no apprehension of absence, the cognition and usage “it does not exist” would not arise, just as there is no perception of darkness when it is not seen. How can one deny the cognition and usage that everyone experiences? We reply: this is an error in which, when cognition of something existent is absent, one mistakenly apprehends its opposite. Likewise, when ordinary usage of something existent is absent, one mistakenly thinks there is usage of its opposite, just as when light is absent, one has the illusion “I see darkness.” For there is no visible thing called darkness.

This is not sound:

“Then in deep sleep and the like there would be the mistaken perception that the three worlds do not exist.”

gloss.en: when cognition of what exists is absent
when ordinary usage of what exists is absent
in deep sleep and the like
the illusion of seeing the three worlds as absent

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 49
units.deva: अपरिच्छिन्दतः किञ्चिद्विभ्रमश्च न युज्यते । आरोपविषयारोप्ये नाजानन् रजतभ्रमी
units.iast:
aparicchindataḥ kiñcidvibhramaśca na yujyate /
āropaviṣayāropye nājānan rajatabhramī
units.translation: Error is not reasonable in one who apprehends nothing at all. A person who does not know either the basis of superimposition or the imagined object cannot suffer the illusion of silver.

gloss.en: for one who does not discern
one who mistakes something for silver

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 50
units.deva: नाभावभिन्ना व्यवहृत्तदभावश्च धीपदे । तमोदृष्टिस्तु भूच्छायामालोकाभावमेव वा
units.iast:
nābhāvabhinnā vyavahṛttadabhāvaśca dhīpade /
tamodṛṣṭistu bhūcchāyāmālokābhāvameva vā
units.translation: Usage and cognition of absence are not different from absence itself. The perception of darkness, however, is merely the sight of a shadow on the earth or of the absence of light.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 51
units.deva:
आलम्बते न त्वदृष्टाविष्टो दर्शनविभ्रमः । यदि खल्वदर्शने विपर्ययदर्शनभ्रमो भवति सुषुप्ताद्यवस्थासु विश्वाभावदर्शनभ्रमः स्यादालोकादर्शनभ्रमवत् । न च किञ्चिदपरिच्छिन्दतो विभ्रमः । तथा हि --- आरोपस्य विषयं पुरोवर्ति वस्तु आरोपणीयं च रजतं ज्ञानेनानाप्नुवन् न रजतभ्रमवान् भवति । अन्यथाप्रतिपत्तिः, स्मृतिः, सामान्यप्रतिपत्तिर्वा । न च बुद्ध्यभावो ज्ञानस्य विषयो न व्यवहाराभावः, नाभावबुद्धिर्नाभावव्यवहारः, विशेषणस्याभावस्य ज्ञानाविषयत्वात् । तत्रोभयोर्विषयारोपणीययोरग्रहणे न मिथ्याज्ञानमिति । अभ्युपगम्य प्रमाणयोग्यतां सत्तां दोषाभाव उच्यते ---
[क्क्स्_95] अस्तु वा मानयोग्यत्वं सत्त्वं तच्च प्रमीयताम्
units.iast:
ālambate na tvadṛṣṭāviṣṭo darśanavibhramaḥ /
yadi khalvadarśane viparyayadarśanabhramo bhavati suṣuptādyavasthāsu viśvābhāvadarśanabhramaḥ syādālokādarśanabhramavat / na ca kiñcidaparicchindato vibhramaḥ / tathā hi --- āropasya viṣayaṃ purovarti vastu āropaṇīyaṃ ca rajataṃ jñānenānāpnuvan na rajatabhramavān bhavati / anyathāpratipattiḥ, smṛtiḥ, sāmānyapratipattirvā / na ca buddhyabhāvo jñānasya viṣayo na vyavahārābhāvaḥ, nābhāvabuddhirnābhāvavyavahāraḥ, viśeṣaṇasyābhāvasya jñānāviṣayatvāt / tatrobhayorviṣayāropaṇīyayoragrahaṇe na mithyājñānamiti /

abhyupagamya pramāṇayogyatāṃ sattāṃ doṣābhāva ucyate ---
[kks_95] astu vā mānayogyatvaṃ sattvaṃ tacca pramīyatām
units.translation:
The error in seeing what is desired does not rest on something never seen. If, in the absence of seeing, there were the error of seeing what is wrong, then in states such as deep sleep one would have the error of seeing the whole world as absent, just as one mistakes the absence of light for its presence. And there is no error in someone who apprehends nothing at all. For a person who does not encounter through cognition either the object in front that serves as the basis for superimposition or the imagined silver cannot suffer the illusion of silver. Error takes the form of apprehending something otherwise, of memory, or of apprehending a general feature. Nor is the absence of cognition itself an object of knowledge, nor is the absence of ordinary usage; there is neither a cognition of absence nor usage that reports absence, because absence as a qualifier is not an object of knowledge. Therefore, when neither the basis nor the imagined object is apprehended, there is no false cognition.

The opponent accepts that existence means being fit for a means of knowledge and denies any defect:

“Let existence be the capacity to be known by a means of knowledge; then let that itself be known…”

gloss.en: on what has not been seen
the error of seeing something wrongly
in states such as deep sleep
the error of seeing the whole world as absent
like mistaking the absence of light for its presence
one who has the illusion of silver
apprehension of something as other than it is
because it is not an object of cognition
the basis and what is superimposed
fitness to be known by a means of knowledge
fitness to be an object of a means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 52
units.deva: तस्मिन्मिते वस्तुसत्त्वं भवत्यागमगोचरे । न च सापेक्षता नास्मिन्नन्तरार्थविभिन्नताम्
units.iast:
tasminmite vastusattvaṃ bhavatyāgamagocare /
na ca sāpekṣatā nāsminnantarārthavibhinnatām
units.translation: When that object is known, its existence becomes accessible to scripture. Yet this does not make the statement dependent, nor does it make its meaning distinct from the object itself.

gloss.en: a distinction between the meaning and the object

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 53
units.deva:
प्रचक्षते ये ऽपि सत्तामन्यां न प्रतिजानते । भवतु वा प्रमाणयोग्यता सत्ता । सैव च प्रमेयास्तु । तत्प्रमेयं वस्तुसत्त्वमागमार्थः । न च प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षता दोषः, प्रमाणान्तरसंभेदस्याभावात् । ‘प्रमाणयोग्यःऽइत्येतावन्मात्राधिगतेः । तथा हि --- ये ऽपि प्रमाणयोग्यतां सत्तामाहुर्न तद्व्यतिरेकिणीम्, ते ऽपि नात्रान्तरार्थसंस्पर्शमिच्छन्ति । तत्संस्पर्शे ह्यन्यत्प्रमाणमन्वेष्यं स्यात् । कथं नान्वेष्यम्? यदा वचः प्रमाणयोग्यतायां पर्यवसितं न विशिष्टार्थसत्त्वं बोधयति, तत्र यस्य प्रमाणस्य योग्यो विशिष्टो ऽर्थस्तदवश्यापेक्षणीयम् । किमर्थं तदपेक्ष्यते? विशिष्टवस्तुसत्त्वाधिगमाय । कं पुनर्विशिष्टस्य वस्तुनः सत्त्वम्? प्रमाणयोग्यत्वम् । अधिगतमेव तर्हि तदस्त्यर्थनिष्ठाद्वचनात्, प्रमाणयोग्यताया अस्त्यर्थत्वात् । प्रमाणान्तरसंभेदाभ्युपगमे ऽपि नाप्रामाण्यप्रसङ्गदोष इति दर्शयति ---
प्रमाणान्तरभिन्नार्थमपि मानं न नो वचः
units.iast:
pracakṣate ye 'pi sattāmanyāṃ na pratijānate /
bhavatu vā pramāṇayogyatā sattā / saiva ca prameyāstu / tatprameyaṃ vastusattvamāgamārthaḥ / na ca pramāṇāntarāpekṣatā doṣaḥ, pramāṇāntarasaṃbhedasyābhāvāt / ‘pramāṇayogyaḥ'ityetāvanmātrādhigateḥ / tathā hi --- ye 'pi pramāṇayogyatāṃ sattāmāhurna tadvyatirekiṇīm, te 'pi nātrāntarārthasaṃsparśamicchanti / tatsaṃsparśe hyanyatpramāṇamanveṣyaṃ syāt / kathaṃ nānveṣyam? yadā vacaḥ pramāṇayogyatāyāṃ paryavasitaṃ na viśiṣṭārthasattvaṃ bodhayati, tatra yasya pramāṇasya yogyo viśiṣṭo 'rthastadavaśyāpekṣaṇīyam / kimarthaṃ tadapekṣyate? viśiṣṭavastusattvādhigamāya / kaṃ punarviśiṣṭasya vastunaḥ sattvam? pramāṇayogyatvam / adhigatameva tarhi tadastyarthaniṣṭhādvacanāt, pramāṇayogyatāyā astyarthatvāt /

pramāṇāntarasaṃbhedābhyupagame 'pi nāprāmāṇyaprasaṅgadoṣa iti darśayati ---
pramāṇāntarabhinnārthamapi mānaṃ na no vacaḥ
units.translation:
Even those who do not admit a distinct existence may say that existence is simply the capacity to be an object of a means of knowledge. Let that be so, and let that capacity itself be the object of knowledge. What the scripture teaches is the existence of the thing as an object of knowledge. Nor is it a defect that the statement depends on another means of knowledge, since no other means of knowledge is blended into it; all that is understood is “capable of being known.”

For even those who speak of existence as the capacity to be known do not want it to touch some other, distinct object. If it did, another means of knowledge would have to be sought. Why must it be sought? If the statement concludes only in the capacity to be known and does not teach the existence of a particular object, then the particular object must necessarily be established by the means of knowledge that can know it. Why is that means needed? To establish the existence of the particular thing. And what is the existence of that particular thing? Its being capable of being known. Then that has already been understood from the statement whose meaning is existence, since the capacity to be known is what “existence” means. It is shown that even if a statement depends on another means of knowledge, it need not therefore be invalid:

“Although our statement is a means of knowledge about an object distinct from another means of knowledge…”

gloss.en: fitness to be known by a means of knowledge
dependence on another means of knowledge
of being mixed with another means of knowledge
fit to be known by a means of knowledge
because only this much is understood
fitness to be known by a means of knowledge
if there is contact with that
in the capacity to be known
the existence of a particular object
to establish the existence of a particular thing
fitness to be known by a means of knowledge
from a statement whose meaning centers on ‘is’
because it is the meaning of ‘is’
when the blending with another means of knowledge is admitted
the defect of thereby becoming invalid
about an object distinct from another means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 54
units.deva: निरपेक्षमिहार्थे तु प्रमितं वस्त्विदं मया । अर्थमात्रे च सापेक्षमन्यापेक्षार्थबोधनात्
units.iast:
nirapekṣamihārthe tu pramitaṃ vastvidaṃ mayā /
arthamātre ca sāpekṣamanyāpekṣārthabodhanāt
units.translation: The statement “This object has been understood by me” is independent in this respect; but with respect to the object alone it depends on another, since it conveys the speaker’s understanding of the object.

gloss.en: with respect to the bare object
because it conveys the object through another's cognition

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 55
units.deva: अबाधितमपि त्वर्थे प्रमाणांशे ऽपबाधनात् । तत्राप्रमाणतामेति बुद्धानाप्तवचो यथा
units.iast:
abādhitamapi tvarthe pramāṇāṃśe 'pabādhanāt /
tatrāpramāṇatāmeti buddhānāptavaco yathā
units.translation: Even if the object itself is not contradicted, defeat of the speaker’s knowledge makes the statement invalid, as with the words of the Buddha and other unreliable speakers.

gloss.en: with respect to the reliability of the cognition
the words of the Buddha, an unreliable speaker

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 56
units.deva: न खलु प्रमाणान्तरसंभिन्नार्थमपि वचो न प्रमाणम्, प्रमाणमेव ह्याप्तवाक्यम् । कथं पुनः प्रमाणं सापेक्षमिति चेत्, उच्यते --- निरपेक्षमेव तत् ‘प्रमितो ऽयं मयार्थःऽइत्यस्मिन्नर्थे । केवले ह्यर्थे ‘एवमयमर्थःऽइत्यप्रतीतेः ‘एवमयं पुरुषो वेदऽइति च प्रतीतेः पुरुषज्ञानापेक्षम् । तत्रोपलब्धौ तावदनपेक्षत्वात्प्रामाण्यमश्नुते तत्सिद्धिद्वारश्च पश्चादर्थ इति । कथं तर्हि पुरुषवचः किञ्चिदबाधितार्थमपि सापेक्षत्वेनाप्रमाणं कथ्यते? उच्यते --- यद्यप्यर्थे बाधो नास्ति, यदपेक्षं त्वस्यार्थे प्रामाण्यं यत्सिद्धिमुखेन तं साधयति तत्र प्रमाणांशे बाध्यते । तस्यासिद्धेस्तद्द्वारेण नार्थसिद्धिरित्यर्थे ऽप्रमाणम्, यथातीन्द्रियार्थे बुद्धवचः पुरुषस्य दर्शनासंभवात् । यथोक्तम् --- ‘पुरुषाशक्तितस्तत्र सापवादत्वसंभवःऽ; । इति । यथा च विप्रलम्भकवाक्यम्, अयथादृष्टार्थवादित्वस्य प्रमाणावगतत्वात् । आप्तवाक्यं पुनर्नार्थे न मानांशे ऽपबाधितम् । निरपेक्षं प्रमाणांशे व्यवहारो ऽन्यथा कथम्
units.iast:
na khalu pramāṇāntarasaṃbhinnārthamapi vaco na pramāṇam, pramāṇameva hyāptavākyam / kathaṃ punaḥ pramāṇaṃ sāpekṣamiti cet, ucyate --- nirapekṣameva tat ‘pramito 'yaṃ mayārthaḥ'ityasminnarthe / kevale hyarthe ‘evamayamarthaḥ'ityapratīteḥ ‘evamayaṃ puruṣo veda'iti ca pratīteḥ puruṣajñānāpekṣam / tatropalabdhau tāvadanapekṣatvātprāmāṇyamaśnute tatsiddhidvāraśca paścādartha iti / kathaṃ tarhi puruṣavacaḥ kiñcidabādhitārthamapi sāpekṣatvenāpramāṇaṃ kathyate? ucyate --- yadyapyarthe bādho nāsti, yadapekṣaṃ tvasyārthe prāmāṇyaṃ yatsiddhimukhena taṃ sādhayati tatra pramāṇāṃśe bādhyate / tasyāsiddhestaddvāreṇa nārthasiddhirityarthe 'pramāṇam, yathātīndriyārthe buddhavacaḥ puruṣasya darśanāsaṃbhavāt / yathoktam --- ‘puruṣāśaktitastatra sāpavādatvasaṃbhavaḥ'; / iti / yathā ca vipralambhakavākyam, ayathādṛṣṭārthavāditvasya pramāṇāvagatatvāt /

āptavākyaṃ punarnārthe na mānāṃśe 'pabādhitam /
nirapekṣaṃ pramāṇāṃśe vyavahāro 'nyathā katham
units.translation:
A statement does not cease to be a means of knowledge merely because its object is also accessible through another means; the words of a reliable person are indeed a means of knowledge. How, then, can it be dependent and still valid? We reply: it is independent and valid with respect to the fact “This matter has been understood by me.” But it does not by itself produce the cognition “This matter is so”; rather, it produces the cognition “This person knows that the matter is so.” In this respect it depends on knowing the person’s knowledge. It is valid with regard to that knowledge; and through establishing that, one then establishes the object.

Why, then, is a human statement said to be invalid through dependence even when its object is not contradicted? We reply: although the object itself is not contradicted, the statement is defeated with respect to the aspect that is the basis for its validity concerning the object—namely, the speaker’s knowledge, through which the statement establishes it. Since that knowledge is unestablished, the object is not established through it, and so the statement is invalid with respect to the object. For instance, a person cannot see something beyond the senses, so the Buddha’s statement about such an object may be defeated by the speaker’s incapacity. As has been said: “Because of a person’s incapacity, that statement may be open to exception.” Likewise, the statement of a deceiver is invalid because it has been established by valid knowledge that he describes things contrary to how they are seen. But the statement of a reliable person is not defeated either with respect to the object or with respect to the aspect that makes it a means of knowledge. If a statement can be independent and valid with respect to the speaker’s knowledge, how could it be treated otherwise?

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 57
units.deva: आप्तवचः पुनर्नार्थे नापि प्रमाणांशे संभवत्प्रमाणगोचरं बाध्यते । प्रमाणांशे चानपेक्षं तन्मुखेन चार्थसिद्धिं विदधन्नाप्रमाणं भवितुमर्हति । अन्यथा शब्दनिबन्धनो व्यवहारो न स्यात् । मयेति वक्त्रभावेन संभेदरहितं ततः । प्रलीनज्ञानविज्ञेयविभागं स्वात्मवेदनम्
units.iast:
āptavacaḥ punarnārthe nāpi pramāṇāṃśe saṃbhavatpramāṇagocaraṃ bādhyate / pramāṇāṃśe cānapekṣaṃ tanmukhena cārthasiddhiṃ vidadhannāpramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhati / anyathā śabdanibandhano vyavahāro na syāt /

mayeti vaktrabhāvena saṃbhedarahitaṃ tataḥ /
pralīnajñānavijñeyavibhāgaṃ svātmavedanam
units.translation:
The statement of a reliable person is not defeated either with respect to the object or with respect to the aspect that makes it a means of knowledge, even when the object is within the scope of another means of knowledge. Since it is independent with respect to that aspect, and establishes the object through it, it cannot be invalid. Otherwise, ordinary usage based on words would not be possible:

“Because there is no speaker saying ‘by me,’ the Self is known without being mixed with another cognition, when the distinction between knower and known has dissolved.”

gloss.en: the statement of a reliable person
with respect to the valid-cognition aspect
when within the scope of another means of knowledge
with respect to the validity aspect
because of the absence of a speaker
with the division between knower and known dissolved

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 58
units.deva: [क्क्स्_96] प्रवेदयन्तु वेदान्ता मानान्तरमलौकिकम् । तत्सिद्धिसिद्धतार्थस्य पुंवचोवद्भविष्यति
units.iast:
[kks_96] pravedayantu vedāntā mānāntaramalaukikam /
tatsiddhisiddhatārthasya puṃvacovadbhaviṣyati
units.translation: Let the Upaniṣads teach an extraordinary means of knowledge; through its establishment, the object will be established, as with the words of a person.

gloss.en: of the object's being established through its proof

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 59
units.deva: एवं च प्रमाणान्तरसंभिन्नार्थत्वे ऽपि वेदान्तवचसां न प्रामाण्यव्याहतिः, आप्तवाक्यवत् । तथा हि --- तान्यपि ज्ञानज्ञेयविभागविकलं स्वप्रकाशरूपमलौकिकं काममवगमयन्तु प्रमाणान्तरम्, तद्द्वारा चार्थसिद्धिराप्तवचनवत् । इयांस्तु विशेषः स्यात् --- वेदे वक्तुरभावात् ‘मयाऽइति संस्पर्शो न स्यात् । अभ्युपगमवादं परिसमाप्य प्रकृतमुपसंहरति --- एवं न मेयता सत्ता परः पुनः प्रत्यवतिष्ठते --- नन्वन्यापि न युज्यते । [क्क्स्_97] न हि पूर्वावमर्शेन विना सामान्यकल्पना
units.iast:
evaṃ ca pramāṇāntarasaṃbhinnārthatve 'pi vedāntavacasāṃ na prāmāṇyavyāhatiḥ, āptavākyavat / tathā hi --- tānyapi jñānajñeyavibhāgavikalaṃ svaprakāśarūpamalaukikaṃ kāmamavagamayantu pramāṇāntaram, taddvārā cārthasiddhirāptavacanavat / iyāṃstu viśeṣaḥ syāt --- vede vakturabhāvāt ‘mayā'iti saṃsparśo na syāt /

abhyupagamavādaṃ parisamāpya prakṛtamupasaṃharati --- evaṃ na meyatā sattā paraḥ punaḥ pratyavatiṣṭhate --- nanvanyāpi na yujyate /
[kks_97] na hi pūrvāvamarśena vinā sāmānyakalpanā
units.translation:
Thus, even if the Upaniṣadic statements concern something also connected with another means of knowledge, their authority is not undermined, just as with the words of a reliable person.
