atha pramāṇarūpeṇa sa svaśabdaprakāśitaḥ
units.translation:
It is not possible to establish that special meaning as the object of knowledge merely from ordinary language. If the injunction’s meaning is inferred as a qualifier of a particular cognition that prompts action, then it is not known through words alone. If one says that the inference itself is preceded by words, the cognition from words would likewise have to be preceded by inference, so that words would be accessible only to inference. It is not possible to establish which comes first, just as it cannot be established whether the seed or the sprout is first: sometimes the word is understood through inference, sometimes an inference follows an understanding of the word whose usage is already known.

Moreover, if every person’s understanding from words were preceded by inference, then words would merely repeat what was already inferred. Everyone understands an inferred meaning whose relation to the word is known from the word; no one who is making an inference infers something already understood from the word. Someone may object that the inferred meaning is indeed what the word conveys. True, but it is conveyed by that speaker’s cognition; one person’s cognition does not make another person’s cognition a mere repetition. And if the relation of a word is learned only from its being a cause of action, only that cause would be the word’s meaning. It is not possible to posit a nonordinary cause when ordinary causes of action already suffice.

One may reply that a nonordinary cause must be posited because scriptural actions cannot arise from ordinary causes. That is not so. A word whose power has been learned in ordinary life also conveys meaning in the Veda. Thus, for Vedic action too, it should convey the very relation understood in ordinary life. If that relation were incapable of prompting the action, the word would be false. If, however, the cause of action is many-sided and can vary, the general feature that causes action would be the meaning of a word. Even then, the special Vedic cause, which is not found in ordinary cases, would be inferred by eliminating the alternatives; it would not be outside the range of other means of knowledge. And the general feature of a word’s meaning would already be established from ordinary usage, so the Veda would merely repeat it.

Someone may say that ordinary usage of words, like Vedic usage, is beginningless; in Vedic actions, the relation known by the injunction is to the distinctive, nonordinary cause of action, since an ordinary cause is absent. Nor is it inferred, because the cognition of it is inferred from the action it produces, while its establishment rests only on the capacity of that cognition. And that cognition arises from the word, so the word would be the only means of knowledge. Nor, they add, should one assume that only ordinary means of attaining good can be possible; ordinary benefit is known through other means of knowledge. The word’s meaning is determined from seeing the use of the injunctional ending and the other words; that ordinary, independently known benefit is also part of the word’s meaning.

The answer is that, even if the relation between words and meanings is learned from Vedic usage, the meaning is not thereby removed from the scope of other means of knowledge. At the time one knows the word’s capacity for a nonordinary cause of action, is that cause already known or not? If it is known, then its relation to the word must also be known through another means of knowledge. If it is not known, how can its relation to the word be known? A relation cannot be known when its two relata are not known. Someone else says that the capacity of a word is its relation. That capacity does not belong to the object, since the object is already fixed; rather, cognition is its effect, and cognition is inferred from the action that follows. The relation, defined as capacity, is therefore known in connection with the action.

Such a person must be asked: is the capacity of the word understood in any cognition whatsoever, or in a particular cognition that is a cause of action? If in cognition generally, any cognition could then follow from it. If in a particular cognition that prompts an action unlike those of ordinary life, then because that special action and cognition are inferred by eliminating alternatives, they lie within the scope of another means of knowledge. There are two ways a qualifier can function: it can be supplied from memory to qualify a particular cognition, as in “there is fire because there is smoke,” or it can be directly known by a means of knowledge that cognizes the qualified thing, as in “a white cow.” In either case, the qualifier is known through another means of knowledge, since the relation of the word to it has not been established. Thus the special cognition and its qualifier are within the scope of another means of knowledge.

Someone may object that inference establishes only the cognition, while the qualifier is merely present in it; that is enough to make it a part of the cognition of the qualified object. But this is inelegant, since the appearance of the qualifier would then fall under memory, a means of knowledge, doubt, error, or conceptual construction. It is not memory, because the special, nonordinary qualifier was not previously known. It is not doubt, because there is no contact with two alternatives. It is not a conceptual construction, since that would lead to the same conclusion about cognition of the action’s cause. Nor is it erroneous cognition: if the qualifier is actually true, how could the cognition that grasps it be empty of its object?

The conclusion is therefore that inference remains a means of knowledge. It is well said that one person understands something through the knowledge of another. Someone may reply that a person does not understand through another person’s knowledge, but through their own cognition, enabled by the other person’s knowledge. Then one must say what means of knowledge establishes that person’s cognition. It is not verbal knowledge, since verbal knowledge is defined as cognition of an object through words, and this is cognition of the speaker’s knowledge, not the object. Nor is it perception based on hearing the word. What, then, is it? It is inferred from the cognition that arises from words. If that inference is valid because the cause of action is established, and its validity comes from the absence of defects in the word that gave rise to the cognition, then the word is called a means of knowledge in that respect, and certainty about the object depends on it. That is not appropriate, because knowledge of an object from a word is precisely what is meant by verbal knowledge. A speaker’s statement is not itself a means of knowledge about the object, but only a qualifier of the cognition; and, as explained, there are two ways a qualifier may function...

...it would then be necessary to seek another means of knowledge for the object. Nor is the object established solely through the speaker’s cognition, since, as has been said, one person does not understand through another person’s cognition. As for the claim that understanding of the object depends on the speaker’s cognition: if that cognition is false, or cannot occur, then the recognition of the means of knowledge is sublated, and understanding of the object is sublated with it; if it is not sublated, the understanding is not sublated either. This does not mean that the word lacks an object. Otherwise, there would be no sense in saying that human statements depend on other means of knowledge for their meaning. It was said, “The means of knowledge is established because the cause of the speaker’s cognition is possible.” “Established” here means that it is not sublated, not that its validity itself is created. The sentence exists because the speaker’s cognition is possible; the speaker’s cognition is not the sentence’s object. A word is related to an object, not to a cognition. As it was said, “The relation of a word to its meaning is innate.” This is meant to refute those who say that a word has no contact with its meaning and is related only to cognition. The relation is the mutual fitness of word and object.

That relation cannot be understood if the object has not been understood. If it has been understood, then, as was said, it is within the scope of another means of knowledge. Nor is it understood through a bare appearance: an appearance that has a meaningful object falls under either memory or a means of knowledge. If it has no meaning, what could its relation be? If it is known through an appearance other than verbal cognition, even if that cognition is not a means of knowledge, then the possibility that the object is known by another means of knowledge cannot be ruled out. Nor is a word’s meaning established merely from affirmation or negation. Where another cause prompts a word’s use, the absence of that cause can also account for the word not being used, just as the absence of one cause of an effect matters even when other causes are present. Here, however, the word for an injunction is used when the means to a good result is intended; when that is absent, the word is not observed even when the object is known through another means. Thus the word’s meaning is at least the capacity to bring about a good result. If that capacity is understood through other means, then perhaps the word is still not an independent means of knowledge. But even if the capacity to bring about a good result is seen when the injunction is used, and is not seen when it is not used, that does not show that the word has no such meaning: the relation between the two may be uncertain when both are absent.

The capacity to produce a good result is already established as the immediate cause. That alone can account for the observed presence and absence; there is no proof that anything else is the word’s meaning. Otherwise, existence and other properties would also enter the meaning of “śiṃśapā tree,” since it is used when they are present and not used when they are absent. Someone may say that the species “śiṃśapā” is the word’s meaning, and that its absence explains the absence of the word, while its presence explains its use, so no capacity needs to be imagined. The same applies here.

One may object that the capacity to produce a good result is within the scope of another means of knowledge, and that because it cannot be established in the Veda, the Veda is invalid. This is unsound. Just because a particular means of knowledge concerns an object in one setting, it does not follow that it is false in every other setting. A nearby object may be within the scope of the external senses, while a distant one is known through scripture and inference. The capacity of sacrifices and other actions to produce results at a distant time may be known from the Veda. Another means’ failure to perceive something does not sublate a means of knowledge that concerns it, since means of knowledge operate within distinct domains.

Someone may reply that, if the Vedic meaning is in the scope of another means of knowledge, then the Veda is invalid because it conflicts with it, as no immediate result is observed. That would follow only if there were a conflict. But, as has been said, “An immediate result has not been enjoined.” Perhaps one may avoid enjoining an immediate result and still hold that the word’s meaning is established through another means; if an object is established through another means, it must be accepted just as that means established it. Otherwise, it would not be established. But it is established that ritual actions are an immediate means to a good result. That is not so: actions need not produce an immediate result by necessity, as is seen with farming, taking medicine, and the like. Intermediate effects are also established by the power of a means of knowledge, even in the case of sacrifices. Further, when a qualified meaning is established, the qualifier too is established as a means of producing good; that is all the word means. There is no conflict with the scope of another means of knowledge.

Thus, since there is no defect in ordinary causes of action, imagining a special nonordinary cause is pointless. And just as pleasure and other states are inferred from the pleasant expression of a face, the capacity to bring about action can be inferred as well. Even on the view that the meaning of a statement by a person is the speaker’s cognition, inference of the object is still not avoided: cognition cannot occur without an object, so the object is established by implication or inference. The cause of action is inferred from the action, and the cognition of the speaker is inferred along with it, just as the meaning of a statement by a trustworthy person is inferred. The fact that cognition is caused by a word does not make it a verbal means of knowledge. It is not like the meaning of a trustworthy statement being known through the senses, so that the object itself would be known through perception. Thus it is rightly said:

“If it is inferable in this way, how can it be solely within the scope of words?
No special cause can be imagined for it, since it is established through ordinary usage as well.”

If, then, it is revealed by its own word in the form of a means of knowledge...

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 86
units.deva: आक्षेप्ता निरपेक्षश्च कथ्यते ऽन्यप्रमां प्रति । अथोच्यते --- न ब्रूमो विधिरन्यथा वृथा स्यादिति तदधीनः संसर्गः । किं तु प्रमाणात्मनैव स स्वशब्देन प्रतिपाद्यते । तथा च प्रमाणत्वात्प्रमेयस्याक्षेप्तापूर्वस्य, प्रमाणान्तरानपेक्षश्च । न ह्यसौ शब्दवत्संबन्धापेक्षत्वात्पूर्वसिद्धिमपेक्षत इति । तथाप्यसिद्धे प्रागुक्तौ दोषौ सिद्धे ऽनुवादिता
units.iast:
ākṣeptā nirapekṣaśca kathyate 'nyapramāṃ prati /
athocyate --- na brūmo vidhiranyathā vṛthā syāditi tadadhīnaḥ saṃsargaḥ / kiṃ tu pramāṇātmanai sa svaśabdena pratipādyate / tathā ca pramāṇatvātprameyasyākṣeptāpūrvasya, pramāṇāntarānapekṣaśca / na hyasau śabdavatsaṃbandhāpekṣatvātpūrvasiddhimapekṣata iti /
tathāpyasiddhe prāguktau doṣau siddhe 'nuvāditā
units.translation: [It] is said to prompt the object of knowledge and to be independent of another means of knowledge. But perhaps the opponent says: we do not argue that an injunction would otherwise be pointless and that therefore the relation depends on it. Rather, it is taught in its own words as a means of knowledge itself. Thus, since it is a means of knowledge, it prompts its novel object and does not depend on another means. For unlike a word, it does not depend on knowing a word–meaning relation in advance. Even so, if its object has not been established, the two faults already stated follow; if it has been established, the statement is merely a restatement.

gloss.en: as a means of knowledge itself
because it is a means of knowledge
of the object to be known
independent of another means of knowledge
because it depends on a relation

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 87
units.deva:
प्रामाण्यमस्य यत्रास्तु श्रुतेस्तत्र वृथा त्वयम् । एवमप्यव्युत्पन्नप्रवृत्तिपदधर्मव्यतिक्रमौ प्रमाणात्मापि स यदि न प्रमाणान्तरसिद्धः । अथ सिद्धो यथावगतानुवादान्नापूर्वार्थाक्षेपः । अपि च यत्रास्य प्रामाण्यमिष्यते, शब्दस्यैव तत्रास्तु । किमनेन? ननूक्तम् --- शब्दसंगतिज्ञानापेक्षत्वादनुवादको नापूर्वार्थावगमाय प्रभवति । नैतत्सारम् । शब्दश्चेदनुवादकः । तत्प्रकाश्यं प्रमाणमप्यनूद्यमानं यथाधिगतं कथमपूर्वार्थं बोधयेत्? न प्रमेयसंस्पर्शरहिता प्रमाणावगतिः । अतो यथाधिगतप्रमेयमेव तत्प्रतीयते । [क्क्स्_111]
क्व च प्रमाणमेषो ऽर्थे न यागादौ स्वशब्दके
units.iast:
prāmāṇyamasya yatrāstu śrutestatra vṛthā tvayam /
evamapyavyutpannapravṛttipadadharmavyatikramau pramāṇātmāpi sa yadi na pramāṇāntarasiddhaḥ / atha siddho yathāvagatānuvādānnāpūrvārthākṣepaḥ / api ca yatrāsya prāmāṇyamiṣyate, śabdasyaiva tatrāstu / kimanena? nanūktam --- śabdasaṃgatijñānāpekṣatvādanuvādako nāpūrvārthāvagamāya prabhavati / naitatsāram / śabdaścedanuvādakaḥ / tatprakāśyaṃ pramāṇamapyanūdyamānaṃ yathādhigataṃ kathamapūrvārthaṃ bodhayet? na prameyasaṃsparśarahitā pramāṇāvagatiḥ / ato yathādhigataprameyameva tatpratīyate /

[kks_111]
kva ca pramāṇameṣo 'rthe na yāgādau svaśabdake
units.translation:
Where scripture is accepted as valid, this entire objection is pointless. Even so, if it is not established through another means of knowledge, it would violate the familiar principles that prompt action and that words have their own function. But if it is established, the statement merely restates what is already understood and cannot convey a novel meaning. Moreover, wherever its validity is accepted, it is enough to accept the word itself; why posit anything else?

One might object, as already stated: a restatement cannot reveal a novel meaning because knowing the conventional word–meaning relation is required. This is not sound. If the word is a restatement, how could the means of knowledge that it illuminates, which merely repeats what has already been understood, convey something new? Knowledge from a means of knowledge does not occur without contact with its object. It therefore presents precisely an object that has already been understood.

And when does such a means of knowledge operate with respect to an object—not in the case of the sacrifice or its word…

gloss.en: a violation of the usual rules of action and word-function
established by another means of knowledge
because it merely repeats what is already understood
the conveying of a novel object
because knowing the word-relation is required
without contact with the knowable object

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 88
units.deva: लौकिके ऽपूर्वसंसर्गः श्रोतुरस्त्यविधावपि । फलसाधनशक्तौ चेछब्दस्तत्र न दूष्यति
units.iast:
laukike 'pūrvasaṃsargaḥ śroturastyavidhāvapi /
phalasādhanaśaktau cechabdastatra na dūṣyati
units.translation: Even without an injunction, ordinary speech produces a novel relation for the listener. If a word has the power to bring about an effect, there is no defect.

gloss.en: if there is power to produce a result

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 89
units.deva: पदार्थान्तरतुल्यत्वाद्विध्याकाङ्क्षानिबन्धनः । न संसर्गः पदार्थानां स्वशब्दैस्तु प्रकाशिताः
units.iast:
padārthāntaratulyatvādvidhyākāṅkṣānibandhanaḥ /
na saṃsargaḥ padārthānāṃ svaśabdaistu prakāśitāḥ
units.translation: Because it is comparable to other word-meanings, the relation among the meanings does not depend on an injunction; their own words make them known.

gloss.en: because it is comparable to other word-meanings
dependent on the expectation of an injunction

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 90
units.deva: संबन्धयोग्यरूपेण तस्मात्संसर्गभागिनः । विशिष्टार्थप्रयुक्ता हि समभिव्याहृतिर्जने
units.iast:
saṃbandhayogyarūpeṇa tasmātsaṃsargabhāginaḥ /
viśiṣṭārthaprayuktā hi samabhivyāhṛtirjane
units.translation: Therefore words participate in a relation through a form fit for connection. In ordinary usage, their combination is prompted by a qualified meaning.

gloss.en: in a form fit for connection

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 91
units.deva: अतो न विद्ध्यभावेन संसर्गो न प्रकल्पते । न च नियोगस्य प्रमेयं निरूप्यते । न तावद्यागादयः प्रमेयाः, तेषां यजत्यादिशब्दविषयत्वात् । नापि तेषां प्रमाणान्तरस्यागोचरः संसर्गः । तथा हि --- अविधिष्वपि लौकिकेषु वाक्येषु श्रोतुरनधिगतो ऽपूर्वः संसर्गः प्रतीयते ‘ब्राह्मण पुत्रस्ते जातःऽइत्यादिषु । अथ फलसाधनसामर्थ्यं प्रमेयमुच्यते । न किल कामिनो नियोगो ऽकामोपाये धात्वर्थे ऽवकल्पते । अनुपायत्वे हि तस्य न स कामिन्या कृतः स्यादिति । तदप्यसंप्रतम् । न हि शब्दस्य तत्र कश्चिदपराधः, येन तमतिक्रम्यान्यत्प्रमाणं मृग्यते । प्रमाणान्तरापेक्षता प्रत्युक्ता । अनन्तरफलादर्शनेन तु विरोधो नियोगगम्ये ऽपि तस्मिन्नविशिष्टः । आनन्तर्यस्याप्रमाणार्थत्वेन तदभावः शब्दे ऽपि तुल्यः । अथ वा शब्दस्तत्र न दुष्यति फलसाधनसामर्थ्ये, नियोगस्तु दुष्यत्येव । न हि ततः पुरुषर्थसाधनावबोधः संभवति । तच्चेदं विधिविवेकभावनाविवेकाभ्यामवगन्तव्यम् । तस्मात् संबन्धज्ञानापेक्षत्वेन पदार्थान्तरैः समानत्वाद्विधायकार्थस्य न शक्यं विशेषेण वक्तुं --- तन्निबन्धनः पदार्थसंसर्ग इति । सर्व एव तु पदार्थाः संबन्धयोग्यैः कारकादिभावैः स्वपदेभ्यः प्रतीताः सन्निकर्षेण संसृज्यन्ते, यतो लोकाच्छब्दव्यापारावगमः । लोके च [क्क्स्_112] पदैः स्वार्थानां प्रतिपादनं सन्निकर्षेण विशिष्टार्थपरतया, न स्वार्थमात्रप्रतिपत्तिपरतया । तथा च सर्वपदार्थाकाङ्क्षानिबन्धन एव संसर्गः । सर्वे हि ते पदैरपर्यवसितरूपाः स्वरूपमात्रे प्रकाश्यन्ते । एवं पदार्थान्तरैस्तुल्यत्वाद्विधेः न विशेषेण तन्निबन्धनः संसर्गः । सर्वपदार्थनिबन्धने च संसर्गे न विध्यभावेन संसर्गो नोपपद्यते । तदेवं न संसर्गार्थमपि विधिरुपासनीयः । कथं नोपासनीयः, यदा नियोगपरतयैव पदानां स्वार्थेषु संसर्गज्ञानम्? प्रवर्तकवचनान्तरप्रवृत्तिदर्शनेन हि तद्धेतुप्रत्ययमनुमाय तत्र तस्य सामर्थ्यं गम्यते । नैतत्, अप्रवर्तके ऽपि वाक्ये स्वरूपनिष्ठे संबन्धग्रहणात् । सन्निधापिताग्निव्यतिरिक्तपाक्योपकरणमग्न्यर्थिनं प्रति यदोच्यते --- ‘चैत्रगृहे कृशानुःऽ; इति, तदा ततस्तेनानयनं दृष्ट्वा गम्यते --- ‘इहानेनाग्निसत्ता प्रतीता, सा चास्माद्वाक्यात्ऽ; न च शक्यं वक्तुम् --- ‘तत आनयऽ; ‘गच्छ वा तत्रऽ; इति वाक्यात्प्रत्ययः । अग्निसत्तामात्रप्रत्ययेन वाक्यात्प्रवृत्तिसिद्धेर्न वाक्यस्य नियोजने ऽपि सामर्थ्यं शक्यते कल्पयितुम् । अर्थान्तरान्वये च प्रयोगप्रत्ययोपपत्तौ न विशेषान्वये प्रमाणम् । अन्यथा वेदार्थो निष्प्रमाणक एव स्यादित्युक्तम् । अथ कर्तव्यताज्ञानाद्विनानर्थक्यमुच्यते
units.iast:
ato na viddhyabhāvena saṃsargo na prakalpate /
na ca niyogasya prameyaṃ nirūpyate / na tāvadyāgādayaḥ prameyāḥ, teṣāṃ yajatyādiśabdaviṣayatvāt / nāpi teṣāṃ pramāṇāntarasyāgocaraḥ saṃsargaḥ / tathā hi --- avidhiṣvapi laukikeṣu vākyeṣu śroturanadhigato 'pūrvaḥ saṃsargaḥ pratīyate ‘brāhmaṇa putraste jātaḥ'ityādiṣu / atha phalasādhanasāmarthyaṃ prameyamucyate / na kila kāmino niyogo 'kāmopāye dhātvarthe 'vakalpate / anupāyatve hi tasya na sa kāminyā kṛtaḥ syāditi / tadapyasaṃpratam / na hi śabdasya tatra kaścidaparādhaḥ, yena tamatikramyānyatpramāṇaṃ mṛgyate / pramāṇāntarāpekṣatā pratyuktā / anantaraphalādarśanena tu virodho niyogagamye 'pi tasminnaviśiṣṭaḥ / ānantaryasyāpramāṇārthatvena tadabhāvaḥ śabde 'pi tulyaḥ / atha vā śabdastatra na duṣyati phalasādhanasāmarthye, niyogastu duṣyatyeva / na hi tataḥ puruṣarthasādhanāvabodhaḥ saṃbhavati / taccedaṃ vidhivivekabhāvanāvivekābhyāmavagantavyam / tasmāt saṃbandhajñānāpekṣatvena padārthāntaraiḥ samānatvādvidhāyakārthasya na śakyaṃ viśeṣeṇa vaktuṃ --- tannibandhanaḥ padārthasaṃsarga iti / sarva eva tu padārthāḥ saṃbandhayogyaiḥ kārakādibhāvaiḥ svapadebhyaḥ pratītāḥ sannikarṣeṇa saṃsṛjyante, yato lokācchabdavyāpārāvagamaḥ / loke ca [kks_112] padaiḥ svārthānāṃ pratipādanaṃ sannikarṣeṇa viśiṣṭārthaparatayā, na svārthamātrapratipattiparatayā / tathā ca sarvapadārthākāṅkṣānibandhana eva saṃsargaḥ / sarve hi te padairaparyavasitarūpāḥ svarūpamātre prakāśyante / evaṃ padārthāntaraistulyatvādvidheḥ na viśeṣeṇa tannibandhanaḥ saṃsargaḥ / sarvapadārthanibandhane ca saṃsarge na vidhyabhāvena saṃsargo nopapadyate / tadevaṃ na saṃsargārthamapi vidhirupāsanīyaḥ / kathaṃ nopāsanīyaḥ, yadā niyogaparatayaiva padānāṃ svārtheṣu saṃsargajñānam? pravartakavacanāntarapravṛttidarśanena hi taddhetupratyayamanumāya tatra tasya sāmarthyaṃ gamyate / naitat, apravartake 'pi vākye svarūpaniṣṭhe saṃbandhagrahaṇāt / sannidhāpitāgnivyatiriktapākyopakaraṇamagnyarthinaṃ prati yadocyate --- ‘caitragṛhe kṛśānuḥ'; iti, tadā tatastenānayanaṃ dṛṣṭvā gamyate --- ‘ihānenāgnisattā pratītā, sā cāsmādvākyāt'; na ca śakyaṃ vaktum --- ‘tata ānaya'; ‘gaccha vā tatra'; iti vākyātpratyayaḥ / agnisattāmātrapratyayena vākyātpravṛttisiddherna vākyasya niyojane 'pi sāmarthyaṃ śakyate kalpayitum / arthāntarānvaye ca prayogapratyayopapattau na viśeṣānvaye pramāṇam / anyathā vedārtho niṣpramāṇaka eva syādityuktam /
atha kartavyatājñānādvinānarthakyamucyate
units.translation:
Thus relation among word meanings cannot be attributed to the absence of an injunction. Nor is the subject matter of an injunction clearly established. Sacrifices and other actions are not the subject matter, since they are what words such as “sacrifice” convey. Nor is the relation among their meanings something beyond the scope of other means of knowledge. Even in ordinary statements that are not injunctions, the hearer understands a relation not previously known, as in “Brahmin, your son has been born.”

Someone may say that the object is the capacity to produce a result. A person who desires a result would not be enjoined to do an action whose verbal meaning does not include that it is a means to the desired result; if it were not a means, the injunction would not have been made by someone who desires it. That is also inappropriate. There is no fault in the word that would require one to set it aside and seek another means of knowledge; dependence on another means has already been refuted. The absence of an immediate result also creates the same difficulty for something understood through an injunction as for something understood through a word. Since immediacy is not part of the subject matter of a means of knowledge, its absence is equally possible for a word. Alternatively, the word itself is not defective in conveying the capacity to produce a result, but the injunction is: it cannot convey that the action is a means to a human good. This is to be understood from the analyses of injunction and meditation. Therefore, since the meaning of an injunction depends on knowledge of a relation, just as the meanings of other words do, it is not possible to say that the relation among word meanings specifically depends on an injunction.

All meanings of words are conveyed by their respective words, and they combine when they are suited to be related, such as agent, instrument, and other factors. That is how the operation of words is understood through ordinary language. In ordinary language, words convey their own meanings in proximity to one another, with the sentence directed toward a qualified meaning; they are not directed merely toward cognition of each word’s isolated meaning. Thus a relation among the meanings arises from the expectation among all the words. Each word, considered alone, presents its meaning in an incomplete form; it is only completed in relation to the other meanings. Since injunction works in the same way as the other words, there is no special reason to say that relation among meanings depends on it. And since their relation depends on all the words, the absence of an injunction does not prevent it. Thus an injunction is not needed even to establish a relation among the meanings.

Someone may ask how an injunction can be unnecessary when the relation among words is known only because their meanings are directed toward something to be done. One observes another statement prompting activity, infers the cognition that causes it, and from that understands the word’s capacity. This is not sound, since the relation among word meanings is learned even from a statement that does not prompt action, when its meaning is taken in itself. When a person seeking fire is told, “There is fire in Caitra’s house,” while the other tools needed for cooking have already been brought, and the person then goes to fetch the fire, one understands from this that the sentence made the person aware that there was fire there. It is not possible to claim that the statement really meant “Bring it here” or “Go there.” Activity follows from the sentence’s conveying the existence of fire alone; one cannot therefore imagine that the sentence has a special power to enjoin action. If an ordinary relation among meanings explains the speaker’s use and the hearer’s understanding, there is no evidence for a special relation to action. Otherwise, as has been said, the meaning of the Veda would have no valid basis. Someone may now object that without knowledge of what should be done, the words would be meaningless...

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 92
units.deva: न प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिभ्यामन्यद्वाक्यप्रयोजनम् । प्रतिपत्तिविधौ तुल्यं यदि सैव प्रयोजनम्
units.iast:
na pravṛttinivṛttibhyāmanyadvākyaprayojanam /
pratipattividhau tulyaṃ yadi saiva prayojanam
units.translation: A sentence has no purpose other than prompting action or restraint. If that is the purpose, an injunction to understand has the same [defect].

gloss.en: apart from prompting action and restraining it

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 93
units.deva: समानमेत्तदर्थं च समर्पयति चेदयम् । प्रज्ञाक्रियोपासनाधिकारसिद्धिव्यपेक्षितम्
units.iast:
samānamettadarthaṃ ca samarpayati cedayam /
prajñākriyopāsanādhikārasiddhivyapekṣitam
units.translation: The same point applies: [a sentence] presents what is required for an injunction assigning a duty to cultivate insight, perform mental practice, or meditate.

gloss.en: what is required to establish a duty to cultivate insight, mental practice, or meditation

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 94
units.deva: हन्त तर्हि स्वरुपे तन्न वचः पर्यवसति । [क्क्स्_113] तुल्यमेतत्समाप्तं च वाक्यं वाक्यान्तरानुगम्
units.iast:
hanta tarhi svarupe tanna vacaḥ paryavasati /
[kks_113] tulyametatsamāptaṃ ca vākyaṃ vākyāntarānugam
units.translation: Then the sentence does not culminate in the thing’s own nature. The same argument applies here: a sentence whose meaning is complete joins with another sentence.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 95
units.deva: नियोगानुप्रवेशो ऽस्ति तवद्यदि वृथान्यथा । तत्त्वावबोधविध्यंशस्तावदेवं समुद्धृतः
units.iast:
niyogānupraveśo 'sti tavadyadi vṛthānyathā /
tattvāvabodhavidhyaṃśastāvadevaṃ samuddhṛtaḥ
units.translation: If it participates in an injunction, otherwise it would be pointless. The part that enjoins understanding of truth has thus been set aside.

gloss.en: the part enjoining understanding of truth

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 96
units.deva: अथ मन्यते --- वस्तुस्वरूपमात्रज्ञानं कर्तव्यताज्ञानरहितं प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिशून्यमनर्थकम् । प्रवृत्तिनिवृत्तिप्रयुक्ता हि वाक्यप्रवृत्तिः । अथो ऽर्थवत्त्वाय विधिः । अन्यथानर्थक्यम् । तत्रोच्यते --- प्रतिपत्तिविधावपि तुल्यमानर्थक्यम् । तथा हि --- ‘एवंविधः प्रतिपत्तव्यःऽइत्यपि न तत्स्वरूपज्ञानातिरिक्ता काचन प्रवृत्तिर्निवृत्तिर्वा । अथ स्वरूपज्ञानमेव प्रयोजनम्, तत्स्वरूपमात्रनिष्ठे ऽपि तुल्यम् । अथ प्रतिपत्तिविधिः ‘प्रज्ञां कुर्वीतऽ; ‘स क्रतुं कुर्वीतऽ; ‘आत्मेत्येवोपासितऽइत्यधिकारविधिव्यपेक्षितप्रज्ञोपासनाविषयसमर्पणेनार्थवान्, नावगतविषयस्वरूपा प्रज्ञा शक्येति । स्वरूपनिष्ठमपि वचस्तथार्थवत् । तस्य समर्पणे सुतरां सामर्थ्यम् । नन्वेवमस्य स्वरूपनिष्ठा हीयते नियोगानुप्रवेशिनः । स्वगतनियोगनिष्ठमपि तर्हि तन्न, नियोगान्तरानुप्रवेशात् । अथ मतम् --- स्वार्थपर्यवसितमेव वाक्यं वाक्यान्तरेणैकवाक्यतामुपैति । सो ऽयं प्राकरणिकः संबन्ध उच्यते । अन्यथा वाक्यलक्षण एव स्यात् । एतदपि समानम् । नियोगानुप्रवेशे ऽपि न स्वरूपनिष्ठता हीयते । नन्वस्ति नियोगानुप्रवेशः, अन्यथा आनर्थक्यात् । कामम् । तत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिविधिस्तु तावदानर्थक्यान्निराकृतः, विधेर्विनापि तस्माच्छब्दात्तत्वावबोधसिद्धेः । ननूत्पत्तिविधिः कर्मरूपबोधे व्यवस्थितः । यथा तत्त्वज्ञानविधिस्तथा बोधे ऽवतिष्ठताम्
units.iast:
atha manyate --- vastusvarūpamātrajñānaṃ kartavyatājñānarahitaṃ pravṛttinivṛttiśūnyamanarthakam / pravṛttinivṛttiprayuktā hi vākyapravṛttiḥ / atho 'rthavattvāya vidhiḥ / anyathānarthakyam / tatrocyate --- pratipattividhāvapi tulyamānarthakyam / tathā hi --- ‘evaṃvidhaḥ pratipattavyaḥ'ityapi na tatsvarūpajñānātiriktā kācana pravṛttirnivṛttirvā / atha svarūpajñānameva prayojanam, tatsvarūpamātraniṣṭhe 'pi tulyam / atha pratipattividhiḥ ‘prajñāṃ kurvīta'; ‘sa kratuṃ kurvīta'; ‘ātmetyevopāsita'ityadhikāravidhivyapekṣitaprajñopāsanāviṣayasamarpaṇenārthavān, nāvagataviṣayasvarūpā prajñā śakyeti / svarūpaniṣṭhamapi vacastathārthavat / tasya samarpaṇe sutarāṃ sāmarthyam / nanvevamasya svarūpaniṣṭhā hīyate niyogānupraveśinaḥ / svagataniyoganiṣṭhamapi tarhi tanna, niyogāntarānupraveśāt / atha matam --- svārthaparyavasitameva vākyaṃ vākyāntareṇaikavākyatāmupaiti / so 'yaṃ prākaraṇikaḥ saṃbandha ucyate / anyathā vākyalakṣaṇa eva syāt / etadapi samānam / niyogānupraveśe 'pi na svarūpaniṣṭhatā hīyate / nanvasti niyogānupraveśaḥ, anyathā ānarthakyāt / kāmam / tattvapratipattividhistu tāvadānarthakyānnirākṛtaḥ, vidhervināpi tasmācchabdāttatvāvabodhasiddheḥ /

nanūtpattividhiḥ karmarūpabodhe vyavasthitaḥ /
yathā tattvajñānavidhistathā bodhe 'vatiṣṭhatām
units.translation:
Someone may argue: mere knowledge of the nature of an object, without knowledge that it is obligatory, is useless, since it leads neither to action nor to refraining from action. A sentence has a purpose only insofar as it prompts action or abstention. Therefore there must be an injunction, or else the words would be meaningless.

We reply: the same meaninglessness would apply to an injunction to understand. For the injunction “One should understand it as being of this kind” produces no action or abstention beyond knowing the nature of the thing. If knowing its nature is itself the purpose, then the same is true of a sentence that simply presents the nature of the thing. The opponent may say that an injunction to understand—such as “One should cultivate insight,” “One should form an intention,” or “One should contemplate it as the Self”—has meaning because it presents the objects of insight and contemplation that are required by an injunction assigning a ritual duty, whereas insight into the nature of an already understood object cannot be so directed. A sentence that simply reveals the nature of a thing also has meaning; indeed, it is especially capable of revealing it.

One might object: in that case, the sentence loses its focus on the nature of the thing by entering into an injunction. But then an injunction itself cannot be its sole focus either, since it enters into another injunction. The opponent may say that a sentence whose meaning is complete in itself joins another sentence to form a single statement; this is the contextual relation under discussion. Otherwise it would simply meet the definition of a sentence. The same applies here. Even if a sentence participates in an injunction, it does not lose its focus on the nature of the thing.

One may say that it must participate in an injunction, or else it is meaningless. Very well; but an injunction to understand truth has already been rejected as meaningless, since understanding truth arises from those words even without an injunction. The opponent may object that an injunction to produce something has an established role in teaching the form of ritual action; likewise, let an injunction to know truth remain established in teaching cognition.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 97
units.deva: अधिकारात्प्रवृत्तिश्च मता कर्माधिकारवत् । [क्क्स्_114] अज्ञानज्ञापनमतो ऽथाप्रवृत्तप्रवर्तनम्
units.iast:
adhikārātpravṛttiśca matā karmādhikāravat /
[kks_114] ajñānajñāpanamato 'thāpravṛttapravartanam
units.translation: Action is held to arise from eligibility, just as eligibility for ritual action does. Thus it is said that [an injunction] makes the unknown known and prompts one who has not acted.

gloss.en: as in eligibility for ritual action
prompting one who has not acted

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 98
units.deva: विधिमाचक्षते धीरा इत्येतदपि तादृशम् । कर्मस्वरूपावगमस्तत्र नेष्टं विधेः फलम्
units.iast:
vidhimācakṣate dhīrā ityetadapi tādṛśam /
karmasvarūpāvagamastatra neṣṭaṃ vidheḥ phalam
units.translation: The learned say that this too is an injunction of that kind. But the result of the injunction is not the understanding of the form of ritual action.

gloss.en: understanding the nature of ritual action

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 99
units.deva: किं तु कार्यव्यपेक्षस्य फलवाक्येन संगतिः । इहाधिकारसंबन्धो यस्य तन्न विधीयते
units.iast:
kiṃ tu kāryavyapekṣasya phalavākyena saṃgatiḥ /
ihādhikārasaṃbandho yasya tanna vidhīyate
units.translation: Rather, the result is its connection with an injunction concerning what is to be done. What is connected with an assigned ritual duty is not prescribed here.

gloss.en: of what depends on what is to be done
by a sentence stating the result

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 100
units.deva: तत्त्वं तत्त्वावबोधस्य नाधिकारप्रवेशिता । न हि व्रीह्यादिविषयं प्रत्यक्षमधिकारभाक्
units.iast:
tattvaṃ tattvāvabodhasya nādhikārapraveśitā /
na hi vrīhyādiviṣayaṃ pratyakṣamadhikārabhāk
units.translation: Truth is not something that enters into an injunction assigning the act of knowing truth. Perception of rice grains and the like does not participate in a ritual duty.

gloss.en: a participant in an assigned duty

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 101
units.deva: यदपि चोद्यते --- यथोत्पत्तिविधेः कर्मरूपप्रतिपत्तिमात्रमर्थः --- ‘आग्नेयो ऽष्टकपालःऽ; इति । न ततः प्रवृत्तिः । अधिकारविधिनिबन्धनत्वात्तस्याः । तथा तत्त्वावबोधविधेस्तत्त्वावबोधमात्रमर्थः, प्रवृत्तिरधिकारविधेः --- ‘प्रज्ञां कुर्वीतऽइत्यादेः । यतश्च प्रवृत्तिप्रतिपत्तिप्रयोजनभेदो विधेः, अतो ऽस्य लक्षणद्वयमाहुः --- अज्ञातज्ञापनमप्रवृत्तप्रवर्तनमिति । एतदप्यसारम् । यतो नोत्पत्तिगतस्य विधायकस्य स्वरूपावगममात्रमिष्यते फलम् । अपि त्वधिकारवाक्यसंबन्धः । तथा हि --- विधेः पुरुषार्थमात्रसाधनत्वे ऽवबुद्धे तद्विशेषाकाङ्क्षायामधिकारसंबन्धो लभ्यते । न च तत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिविधेरपि तदेव फलम् । यतो यस्याधिकारसंबन्ध उपासनादिविषयस्यात्मतत्त्वस्य, तदक्रियात्मत्त्वान्न विधिविषयः । यत्तु तद्विषयस्तत्त्वज्ञानम्, तस्य नाधिकारसंबन्धः, व्रीह्यादिप्रत्यक्षवत् । न हि व्रीह्यादिस्वरूपग्राहि प्रमाणं प्रयोगैकदेशतां भजते । प्रमितानामधिकारसंबन्धान्निष्पन्नानामिवानोवासःप्रभृतीनाम् । वानतक्षणादिर्हि तत्क्रिया नाधिकारमनुप्रविशतीति । [क्क्स्_115] इदानीं तृतीयप्रतिपत्तिगोचरो विधिः परास्यते, तत्त्वावबोधविषयत्वेन संबन्धात् । द्वितीयप्रतिपत्तिविषयो हि न तत्त्वावबोधविषयः, किं तु तदभ्यासविषयः । सोपायमन्यत्तर्हीदं शाब्दाज्ज्ञानं विधीयते । प्रलीनग्रहणग्राह्यविभागोद्ग्राहमद्वयम्
units.iast:
yadapi codyate --- yathotpattividheḥ karmarūpapratipattimātramarthaḥ --- ‘āgneyo 'ṣṭakapālaḥ'; iti / na tataḥ pravṛttiḥ / adhikāravidhinibandhanatvāttasyāḥ / tathā tattvāvabodhavidhestattvāvabodhamātramarthaḥ, pravṛttiradhikāravidheḥ --- ‘prajñāṃ kurvīta'ityādeḥ / yataśca pravṛttipratipattiprayojanabhedo vidheḥ, ato 'sya lakṣaṇadvayamāhuḥ --- ajñātajñāpanamapravṛttapravartanamiti / etadapyasāram / yato notpattigatasya vidhāyakasya svarūpāvagamamātramiṣyate phalam / api tvadhikāravākyasaṃbandhaḥ / tathā hi --- vidheḥ puruṣārthamātrasādhanatve 'vabuddhe tadviśeṣākāṅkṣāyāmadhikārasaṃbandho labhyate / na ca tattvapratipattividherapi tadeva phalam / yato yasyādhikārasaṃbandha upāsanādiviṣayasyātmatattvasya, tadakriyātmattvānna vidhiviṣayaḥ / yattu tadviṣayastattvajñānam, tasya nādhikārasaṃbandhaḥ, vrīhyādipratyakṣavat / na hi vrīhyādisvarūpagrāhi pramāṇaṃ prayogaikadeśatāṃ bhajate / pramitānāmadhikārasaṃbandhānniṣpannānāmivānovāsaḥprabhṛtīnām / vānatakṣaṇādirhi tatkriyā nādhikāramanupraviśatīti /

[kks_115] idānīṃ tṛtīyapratipattigocaro vidhiḥ parāsyate, tattvāvabodhaviṣayatvena saṃbandhāt / dvitīyapratipattiviṣayo hi na tattvāvabodhaviṣayaḥ, kiṃ tu tadabhyāsaviṣayaḥ /

sopāyamanyattarhīdaṃ śābdājjñānaṃ vidhīyate /
pralīnagrahaṇagrāhyavibhāgodgrāhamadvayam
units.translation:
An objection may be raised: the purpose of an injunction to produce an action is merely to understand the form of the action, as in “The Agni sacrifice is performed with eight potsherds”; that does not itself prompt action, which depends on an injunction assigning a ritual duty. Likewise, the purpose of an injunction to know truth is merely to understand truth, while action depends on an injunction such as “One should cultivate insight.” Since an injunction has different purposes—understanding and prompting action—it is said to have two definitions: making known what was unknown, and prompting one who has not acted.

This too is unsound. The result of an injunction that prescribes the production of an act is not merely understanding its nature; rather, it is the connection with an injunction assigning a ritual duty. For once one understands that an injunction is a means to a person’s end, one looks for the particular end, and then one finds its connection with an injunction assigning a duty. But that is not the result of an injunction to understand truth. The Self, whose nature is the object of contemplation and the like, is not something done and therefore is not the object of an injunction. The knowledge of truth, which is the object of that injunction, has no such connection with an assigned ritual duty, just as direct perception of rice grains and the like has none. A means of knowledge that grasps the nature of rice does not become a component of a ritual performance. The rice grains and so forth are already known and established; thread, cloth, and similar things are likewise not part of a ritual act. The cutting and weaving are activities that do not enter into an injunction assigning a ritual duty.

The author now rejects an injunction whose object is a third kind of apprehension, since it is connected with knowledge of truth. The object of the second kind of apprehension is not knowledge of truth, but the practice of cultivating it. Then this would be a different knowledge, with a means, prescribed by the words:

“Nondual, which grasps what is to be grasped after the division between grasping and the grasped has dissolved…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 102
units.deva: न हि भिन्नार्थसंसर्गरूपवाक्यार्थधीपदम् । आत्मतत्त्वं निष्प्रपञ्चमित्येतदपि पेलवम्
units.iast:
na hi bhinnārthasaṃsargarūpavākyārthadhīpadam /
ātmatattvaṃ niṣprapañcamityetadapi pelavam
units.translation: It is weak to say that the meaning of a sentence is a cognition of the relation among distinct objects, and yet that the nature of the Self is free from all manifestation.

gloss.en: having the form of a relation among distinct meanings
the basis for cognition of a sentence's meaning

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 103
units.deva: अद्वयात्मप्रकाशो ऽसावनवच्छेदविभ्रमः । स्वात्मस्थितिः सुप्रशान्ता फलं तन्न विधेः पदम्
units.iast:
advayātmaprakāśo 'sāvanavacchedavibhramaḥ /
svātmasthitiḥ supraśāntā phalaṃ tanna vidheḥ padam
units.translation: That is the shining forth of the nondual Self, the illusion of limitation having ended. Its fruit is abiding in one’s own Self, utterly at peace; it is not the purpose of an injunction.

gloss.en: the shining forth of the nondual Self

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 104
units.deva: तत्साधनावबोधे हि विधातृव्यापृतिर्मता । अपेक्षितोपायतैव विधिरिष्टो मनीषिभिः
units.iast:
tatsādhanāvabodhe hi vidhātṛvyāpṛtirmatā /
apekṣitopāyataiva vidhiriṣṭo manīṣibhiḥ
units.translation: An injunction is understood to operate by teaching the means to the end. The learned accept as an injunction the teaching of a means that is needed for what is desired.

gloss.en: in understanding the means to that

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 105
units.deva:
ततो ह्यध्यवसायादिर्नाकस्मान्नाभिधानतः । न ब्रूमः --- शब्दोत्थस्तत्त्वबोधो विधीयत इति । किं तु प्रत्यस्तमितबुद्धिबोध्यभेदावग्रहः । अतश्चाद्वयो द्वितीयतद्विधबोधाभावाद्वा प्रमातृप्रमेयद्वयविरहाद्वा ततो ऽन्यः । तस्य चालौकिकस्य प्रमाणान्तरादुत्पत्त्युपायस्यानवगमात्सहोपायैः शमदममननध्यानब्रह्मचर्यादिभिर्विधानम् । यतो न शाब्दज्ञानविषय आत्मतत्त्वम् । वाक्यलक्षणो हि शब्दः प्रमाणम् । तस्य च विषयो नानापदार्थसंसर्गात्मा, तदनुगमेन प्रतीतेः । तज्ज्ञानस्य च विविधार्थमात्रसंभेदावभासस्यात्मतत्त्वं निष्प्रपञ्चं द्वैतलेशेनाप्यनवमृष्टं कथं गोचरः स्यादिति । एतदप्यसारम् । यतो यो ऽसावद्वयो द्वैतलेशसंस्पर्शविकल आत्मतत्त्वबोधः सो ऽवच्छेदविभ्रान्तिविरहात्तस्य स्वरूपावस्थानम् । अवच्छेदकलुषतया हि तदनात्मरूपेण प्रकाशते । न तु ततो ऽन्यस्तत्त्वबोधः । ‘सत्यं [क्क्स्_116] ज्ञानमनन्तम्ऽ; इति श्रुतेः । आत्मतत्त्वं च प्रशान्तशोकादिविश्वाशिवम्, अपहतपाप्मादिश्रुतेः । प्रकाशमानानतिशयानन्दम्, ‘विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्मऽ; ‘एषो ऽस्य परम आनन्दः, एतस्यैवानन्दस्यान्यानि भूतानि मात्रामुपजीवन्तिऽ; इति श्रुतिभ्यः । तथा च तत्स्वरूपस्थितिर्विश्वाशिवोपशमान्निरतिशयाह्लादावाप्तेश्च सुष्ठु प्रशान्तापरः पुरुषार्थः फलम् । उक्तं च --- ‘आत्मलाभान्न परं विद्यतेऽ; इति । न च पुरुषार्थे ऽप्यज्ञातोपाये न प्रवर्तत इति युक्तम्, यतः प्रवृत्तेः पूर्वरूपमिच्छा । तथा च तद्वारेण प्रवृत्त्युपदेश क्वचित् --- ‘अथातो धर्मजिज्ञासाऽ; । तथा ‘यो हि यदिच्छति स तत्करोतिऽ; इत्युक्तम् । अपि च अज्ञातोपाये चेन्न प्रवर्तते, अवश्यमुपायज्ञापनया तत्र प्रवर्त्यः फलमुद्दिश्य । तावता च तत्रापि प्रवृत्तिसिद्धेर्न विधायकस्य तत्र व्यापार आश्रयितव्यः । तदुक्तम् --- ‘तस्य लिप्सार्थलक्षणाऽ; इति । तस्मात्फलसाधन एव विधिव्यापारः । ननु फलवत्यप्यर्थलक्षणा प्रवृत्तिः, क्व तर्हि विधिव्यापारः? इत्थंभावे । नैतत्सारम् । यतो यथैव साधनसामान्ये ऽर्थात्, प्रवृत्तिः, तथेत्थंभावसामान्ये ऽपि । यतो नाननुग्रहकं साधनं समर्थम् । अथ तद्विशेषे प्रवर्त्यः, साधनविशेषे ऽपि तथास्तु । अपि च अपेक्षितोपायतैव विधिः, तस्या अप्रवृत्तप्रवर्तनालक्षणत्वात्, प्रवृत्तिहेतोश्च धर्मस्य प्रवर्तनाशब्दाभिधेयत्वात्, इष्टतायास्तत्साधनतायाश्चान्यस्य प्रवृत्तिहेतोरभावात्, इष्टतायाश्च प्रमाणान्तरावसेयत्वात्स्वयं प्रवृत्तेः जानात्येवासौ ‘मयैतत्कर्तव्यम्ऽ; इति नेष्टतायामप्रवृत्तप्रवर्तनात्वम् । इष्टसाधनतायां तु प्रमाणान्तरावगमाभावाच्छब्दैकगम्यायां न शब्दमन्तरेणाप्रवृत्तपुरुषप्रवृत्तिहेतुत्वम् । अतः सा शब्दप्रमाणिका सती विधिरिति गीयते । अनुतिष्ठतश् [क्क्स्_117] च साधनमनुष्ठेयं प्रवृत्तिहेतुः । न स्वभावसिद्धम् । तेनानुतिष्ठतः साधनताविधिः । अतो ऽनुष्ठानं साधनविषयमेव विधायकाच्छब्दाद्गम्यते । ननु अध्यवसायः, आकूतम्, आद्या प्रवृत्तिः, कालत्रयवियुक्तं प्रवृत्तिमात्रम्, अज्ञातक्रियाकर्तृसंबन्ध इति विधिविदो विधिं व्याचक्षते । नैतत्सारम् । यतो ऽध्यवसायादीनामेव हेतुरत्र मृग्यते । स च नान्यो ऽपेक्षितोपायतायाः । न च ते निरस्तहेतवः । स्यादेतत् --- अभिधानमेषां हेतुः । तच्च वार्तम् । अभिधानाद्धि प्रतीतिरेषां स्यात्, नोत्पत्तिः । न हि प्रतीतिमात्रेण घटादयः प्रवृत्तिहेतव इत्यादि वर्णितं विधिविवेके । अथवा --- नाभिधानतः । न च शब्दादध्यवसायादिः, ज्ञापकत्वादव्युत्पन्नप्रवृत्तिप्रसङ्गादित्यादि तत्रैवोक्तम् । अथवा ‘यो मन्यते --- ‘मयेदं कर्तव्यम्ऽ; इति यतो ऽध्यवसायः ‘नियुक्तो ऽस्मिऽइति यतो बुद्धिः स नियोगो विधिशब्दपर्याय इति, तं प्रत्युच्यते । तत एवापेक्षितोपायत्वात् ‘कर्तव्यम्ऽइत्यध्यवसायः । तथा हि --- कर्तुरिष्टाभ्युपाये ‘कर्तव्यम्ऽइति लोके बुद्धिः । तदभावे तु ‘अकर्तव्यम्ऽ; इत्यन्वयव्यतिरेकाभ्याम् । ते च तद्विषये गम्येते । तथा ‘नियुक्तो ऽस्मिऽ; इति ‘प्रवर्तितो ऽस्मिऽइति स्वात्मप्रवृत्तिहेतुप्रतीतिः । न च सो ऽन्य इष्टाभ्युपायतायाः । न खलु दृष्टसामर्थ्ये ऽकस्माद्विना हेतुनाहेतुरिति युक्तिमत् । न हि तं परित्यज्य लौकिकमलौकिककल्पने प्रमाणमस्ति । कुतश्च? नाभिधानतः । न खल्वलौकिकस्याभिधानं संभवति, संबन्धाग्रहादित्युक्तम् । अथ वा ततो ह्यध्यवसायप्रारम्भानुष्ठानपरिसमापनाः, अपेक्षितोपायत्वात् । तत्सद्भाव एव नियुक्तप्रवृत्तेः यस्य कस्यचिन्नियोगादप्रवृत्तेः । [क्क्स्_118] स्यादेतत् --- ‘कर्तव्यम्ऽ; इति प्रत्ययात्प्रवर्तते । अन्यथा कर्तव्यं न कृतं स्यात् । तच्च न, नाकस्मात्कर्तव्यप्रत्ययोत्पादः । स हि स्वार्थावाप्तिनिमित्तः । स्यादेतत् --- शब्दादेव कर्तव्यताबुद्धिः । तत्रोच्यते --- नाभिधानतः । न शब्दात्कर्तव्यताबुद्धिः । नियोगो हि शब्दार्थः । स हि नियोक्तृधर्मः स्वतन्त्रो वा स्यात् । कर्तव्यता तु विषयधर्मः । अथ विषयधर्मं नियोगं ब्रूयात्, प्राप्तमपेक्षितोपायत्वम् । अथ नियोगात्कर्तव्यता स्यात् । एवमपि न तस्यां शब्दः प्रमाणम्,साक्षात्तस्य नियोगाभिधायित्वात् । नाप्यर्थात्, अकर्तव्ये ऽप्यनाप्तनियोगदर्शनात् । अथ नियोगस्य कार्यता गम्यते । तन्निष्पत्त्यधीनेति विषये कर्तव्यतावगमः । तदसत्, विषये कार्यताप्रतीतेर्लोके । तथा हि ‘गौर्दुह्यतां त्वयाऽ; इति नियोगे अन्येन दुग्धायां न पुनर्दोहमारभते, विषयस्य कार्यताप्रतीतेः तस्य निष्पादितत्वात् । न चान्येनैव नियोगो निष्पादितः, तस्यानियुक्तत्वात् । तत्र नियोगसिद्धये पुनर्दोहारम्भः स्यात् । विस्तरेण चायमर्थो विधिविवेके विचारित इत्यलमतिप्रसङ्गेन । स्यादेतत् --- अस्य ज्ञानस्य मोक्षसाधनत्वाद्विधानम् । विद्यासाध्यो हि मोक्षः श्रूयते ‘विद्यया तदारोहन्तिऽ; ‘विद्ययामृतमश्नुतेऽयस्तमात्मानमनुविद्य विजानाति स सर्वांश्च कामान्ऽ; तथा ‘स यदि पितृलोककामो भवति संकल्पादेवास्य पितरः समुत्तिष्ठन्तिऽ; इत्यादि । न च साध्यत्वे ऽप्यन्तवत्त्वम्, शब्दगम्यत्वादनावृत्तेः --- ‘न च पुनरावर्ततेऽ; इति । न ह्येष तर्कगम्यः । येन तर्केणास्य तत्त्वं व्यवस्थाप्येत । शब्दगम्यस्य तु शब्दादेव तत्त्वव्यवस्था । [क्क्स्_119] अनन्तविद्यासाध्यत्वाद्वानन्तत्वम् । क्षणिकत्वे ऽपि च विज्ञानस्य संततिरूपेणानन्तत्वम् । तत्राहुः ---
न च मोक्षः फलं तस्य साध्यो मोक्षो न चापरः

tato hyadhyavasāyādirnākasmānnābhidhānataḥ /
na brūmaḥ --- śabdotthastattvabodho vidhīyata iti / kiṃ tu pratyastamitabuddhibodhyabhedāvagrahaḥ / ataścādvayo dvitīyatadvidhabodhābhāvādvā pramātṛprameyadvayavirahādvā tato 'nyaḥ / tasya cālaukikasya pramāṇāntarādutpattyupāyasyānavagamātsahopāyaiḥ śamadamamananadhyānabrahmacaryādibhirvidhānam / yato na śābdajñānaviṣaya ātmatattvam / vākyalakṣaṇo hi śabdaḥ pramāṇam / tasya ca viṣayo nānāpadārthasaṃsargātmā, tadanugamena pratīteḥ / tajjñānasya ca vividhārthamātrasaṃbhedāvabhāsasyātmatattvaṃ niṣprapañcaṃ dvaitaleśenāpyanavamṛṣṭaṃ kathaṃ gocaraḥ syāditi / etadapyasāram / yato yo 'sāvadvayo dvaitaleśasaṃsparśavikala ātmatattvabodhaḥ so 'vacchedavibhrāntivirahāttasya svarūpāvasthānam / avacchedakaluṣatayā hi tadanātmarūpeṇa prakāśate / na tu tato 'nyastattvabodhaḥ / ‘satyaṃ [kks_116] jñānamanantam'; iti śruteḥ / ātmatattvaṃ ca praśāntaśokādiviśvāśivam, apahatapāpmādiśruteḥ / prakāśamānānatiśayānandam, ‘vijñānamānandaṃ brahma'; ‘eṣo 'sya parama ānandaḥ, etasyaivānandasyānyāni bhūtāni mātrāmupajīvanti'; iti śrutibhyaḥ / tathā ca tatsvarūpasthitirviśvāśivopaśamānniratiśayāhlādāvāpteśca suṣṭhu praśāntāparaḥ puruṣārthaḥ phalam / uktaṃ ca --- ‘ātmalābhānna paraṃ vidyate'; iti / na ca puruṣārthe 'pyajñātopāye na pravartata iti yuktam, yataḥ pravṛtteḥ pūrvarūpamicchā / tathā ca tadvāreṇa pravṛttyupadeśa kvacit --- ‘athāto dharmajijñāsā'; / tathā ‘yo hi yadicchati sa tatkaroti'; ityuktam / api ca ajñātopāye cenna pravartate, avaśyamupāyajñāpanayā tatra pravartyaḥ phalamuddiśya / tāvatā ca tatrāpi pravṛttisiddherna vidhāyakasya tatra vyāpāra āśrayitavyaḥ / taduktam --- ‘tasya lipsārthalakṣaṇā'; iti / tasmātphalasādhana eva vidhivyāpāraḥ / nanu phalavatyapyarthalakṣaṇā pravṛttiḥ, kva tarhi vidhivyāpāraḥ? itthaṃbhāve / naitatsāram / yato yathaiva sādhanasāmānye 'rthāt, pravṛttiḥ, tathetthaṃbhāvasāmānye 'pi / yato nānanugrahakaṃ sādhanaṃ samartham / atha tadviśeṣe pravartyaḥ, sādhanaviśeṣe 'pi tathāstu / api ca apekṣitopāyataiva vidhiḥ, tasyā apravṛttapravartanālakṣaṇatvāt, pravṛttihetośca dharmasya pravartanāśabdābhidheyatvāt, iṣṭatāyāstatsādhanatāyāścānyasya pravṛttihetorabhāvāt, iṣṭatāyāśca pramāṇāntarāvaseyatvātsvayaṃ pravṛtteḥ jānātyevāsau ‘mayaitatkartavyam'; iti neṣṭatāyāmapravṛttapravartanātvam / iṣṭasādhanatāyāṃ tu pramāṇāntarāvagamābhāvācchabdaikagamyāyāṃ na śabdamantareṇāpravṛttapuruṣapravṛttihetutvam / ataḥ sā śabdapramāṇikā satī vidhiriti gīyate / anutiṣṭhataś [kks_117] ca sādhanamanuṣṭheyaṃ pravṛttihetuḥ / na svabhāvasiddham / tenānutiṣṭhataḥ sādhanatāvidhiḥ / ato 'nuṣṭhānaṃ sādhanaviṣayameva vidhāyakācchabdādgamyate /

nanu adhyavasāyaḥ, ākūtam, ādyā pravṛttiḥ, kālatrayaviyuktaṃ pravṛttimātram, ajñātakriyākartṛsaṃbandha iti vidhivido vidhiṃ vyācakṣate / naitatsāram / yato 'dhyavasāyādīnāmeva heturatra mṛgyate / sa ca nānyo 'pekṣitopāyatāyāḥ / na ca te nirastahetavaḥ / syādetat --- abhidhānameṣāṃ hetuḥ / tacca vārtam / abhidhānāddhi pratītireṣāṃ syāt, notpattiḥ / na hi pratītimātreṇa ghaṭādayaḥ pravṛttihetava ityādi varṇitaṃ vidhiviveke / athavā --- nābhidhānataḥ / na ca śabdādadhyavasāyādiḥ, jñāpakatvādavyutpannapravṛttiprasaṅgādityādi tatraivoktam / athavā ‘yo manyate --- ‘mayedaṃ kartavyam'; iti yato 'dhyavasāyaḥ ‘niyukto 'smi'iti yato buddhiḥ sa niyogo vidhiśabdaparyāya iti, taṃ pratyucyate / tata evāpekṣitopāyatvāt ‘kartavyam'ityadhyavasāyaḥ / tathā hi --- karturiṣṭābhyupāye ‘kartavyam'iti loke buddhiḥ / tadabhāve tu ‘akartavyam'; ityanvayavyatirekābhyām / te ca tadviṣaye gamyete / tathā ‘niyukto 'smi'; iti ‘pravartito 'smi'iti svātmapravṛttihetupratītiḥ / na ca so 'nya iṣṭābhyupāyatāyāḥ / na khalu dṛṣṭasāmarthye 'kasmādvinā hetunāheturiti yuktimat / na hi taṃ parityajya laukikamalaukikakalpane pramāṇamasti / kutaśca? nābhidhānataḥ / na khalvalaukikasyābhidhānaṃ saṃbhavati, saṃbandhāgrahādityuktam / atha vā tato hyadhyavasāyaprārambhānuṣṭhānaparisamāpanāḥ, apekṣitopāyatvāt / tatsadbhāva eva niyuktapravṛtteḥ yasya kasyacinniyogādapravṛtteḥ /

[kks_118] syādetat --- ‘kartavyam'; iti pratyayātpravartate / anyathā kartavyaṃ na kṛtaṃ syāt / tacca na, nākasmātkartavyapratyayotpādaḥ / sa hi svārthāvāptinimittaḥ / syādetat --- śabdādeva kartavyatābuddhiḥ / tatrocyate --- nābhidhānataḥ / na śabdātkartavyatābuddhiḥ / niyogo hi śabdārthaḥ / sa hi niyoktṛdharmaḥ svatantro vā syāt / kartavyatā tu viṣayadharmaḥ / atha viṣayadharmaṃ niyogaṃ brūyāt, prāptamapekṣitopāyatvam / atha niyogātkartavyatā syāt / evamapi na tasyāṃ śabdaḥ pramāṇam,sākṣāttasya niyogābhidhāyitvāt / nāpyarthāt, akartavye 'pyanāptaniyogadarśanāt / atha niyogasya kāryatā gamyate / tanniṣpattyadhīneti viṣaye kartavyatāvagamaḥ / tadasat, viṣaye kāryatāpratīterloke / tathā hi ‘gaurduhyatāṃ tvayā'; iti niyoge anyena dugdhāyāṃ na punardohamārabhate, viṣayasya kāryatāpratīteḥ tasya niṣpāditatvāt / na cānyenaiva niyogo niṣpāditaḥ, tasyāniyuktatvāt / tatra niyogasiddhaye punardohārambhaḥ syāt / vistareṇa cāyamartho vidhiviveke vicārita ityalamatiprasaṅgena /

syādetat --- asya jñānasya mokṣasādhanatvādvidhānam / vidyāsādhyo hi mokṣaḥ śrūyate ‘vidyayā tadārohanti'; ‘vidyayāmṛtamaśnute'yastamātmānamanuvidya vijānāti sa sarvāṃśca kāmān'; tathā ‘sa yadi pitṛlokakāmo bhavati saṃkalpādevāsya pitaraḥ samuttiṣṭhanti'; ityādi / na ca sādhyatve 'pyantavattvam, śabdagamyatvādanāvṛtteḥ --- ‘na ca punarāvartate'; iti / na hyeṣa tarkagamyaḥ / yena tarkeṇāsya tattvaṃ vyavasthāpyeta / śabdagamyasya tu śabdādeva tattvavyavasthā / [kks_119] anantavidyāsādhyatvādvānantatvam / kṣaṇikatve 'pi ca vijñānasya saṃtatirūpeṇānantatvam / tatrāhuḥ ---
na ca mokṣaḥ phalaṃ tasya sādhyo mokṣo na cāparaḥ
units.translation:
Determination and the like do not arise without cause or simply from verbal expression. We do not say that knowledge of reality arising from words is itself enjoined. Rather, what is at issue is the apprehension that the distinction between knower and known has subsided. Nonduality is the absence of cognition of a second thing of that kind, or the absence of the pair of knower and known. The means by which such an extraordinary cognition arises from another means of knowledge is not understood; therefore its arising is prescribed along with means such as tranquility, self-control, reflection, meditation, and celibacy.

Someone argues that the truth of the Self is not the object of verbal cognition: a word that is a sentence is the means of knowledge, and its subject matter is a connection among the meanings of several words, since understanding follows that connection. How could the Self, which is free of all manifestation of a manifold and untouched even by a trace of duality, be within the scope of that cognition, whose appearance is joined with the bare meanings of diverse objects? That is also unsound. The cognition of the Self as nondual, untouched by even a trace of duality, is its own nature, free from the illusion of limitation. Through the stain of imagined limitation, it appears as something other than the Self; but no other kind of knowledge exists. Scripture says, “Brahman is truth, knowledge, and infinite.” The nature of the Self is free from the evils of the entire world, such as sorrow, and scripture calls it “free from sin.” It shines forth as unsurpassed bliss: “Brahman is consciousness and bliss”; and, “This is its supreme bliss; other beings live by a fraction of this very bliss.” Abiding in that nature is therefore the highest human goal: all the evils of the world cease, and unsurpassed delight is attained. It is said, “There is no higher good than the attainment of the Self.”

It is not reasonable to say that a person will not act toward a human goal if the means are unknown, because desire is the first form of activity. Instruction about the means can therefore be given through desire for the goal, as in “Now, therefore, the desire to know dharma,” and in the saying, “Whatever one desires, one undertakes.” Furthermore, if a person cannot act when the means are unknown, the person must be prompted to act toward the goal by being taught the means. That alone establishes the activity; it is not necessary to assume that an injunction has some separate operation in this respect. It was said, “Its defining mark is the desire to attain it.” The injunction’s operation concerns the means to a result.

Someone may object that activity toward a result is already indicated by the object, so where does the injunction operate? The reply is that it operates in the particular manner of acting. This is not sound: just as activity follows naturally from a general understanding of a means, it can follow from a general understanding of the manner of acting. A means that receives no support from anything else is not effective. If someone must be prompted toward a particular means, the same applies to a particular way of acting.

Moreover, injunction means knowledge of a means that is needed to attain what one wants. Its defining feature is prompting someone who is not already acting; and the word “injunction” refers to the dharma that causes action. There is no other cause of activity besides the desirability of the goal and the fact that a particular means produces it. The desirability of the goal is understood through other means of knowledge, and the person acts spontaneously: the person already knows, “I should do this for myself.” The desirability of the goal is therefore not what prompts someone who is inactive. But when the means to the desired goal is not known through another means of knowledge and can be known through words alone, it is the words that cause the inactive person to act. Therefore it is called an injunction, because it is established through words as a means of knowledge. The means that one is to perform is what prompts the person who carries it out; it is not something whose efficacy is already established by nature. Thus the injunction concerns the means to be performed, and it is known from the word that enjoins it.

Those who explain injunction as determination, intention, the first activity, mere activity without reference to the three times, or the previously unknown relation between an action and its agent are not correct. The cause of determination and the like must be sought here, and it is no other than understanding a means that is required. These states are not without a cause. Someone may say that verbal expression is their cause. That is not so: a verbal expression may give rise to understanding of them, but not to their actual production. It has already been explained in the analysis of injunction that cognition alone does not make things such as pots into causes of action. Alternatively, it is not from verbal expression...

...as explained there: words do not produce determination and the like. If they did, they would merely indicate it, and the problem of untrained action arising without an injunction would follow. Or consider the one who says that determination means the thought, “I should do this,” and that injunction means the thought, “I have been enjoined.” The answer is that both arise precisely because a means to what one wants is needed. In ordinary life a person thinks “I should do this” when it is a means to something desired; when it is not, the thought is “I should not do this.” The difference between the two is evident from their relation to the object. Likewise, “I have been enjoined” means, “I have been prompted to act”: one understands that something has become the cause of one’s own activity. That cause is nothing other than the fact that the action is a means to a desired goal. It is not reasonable to suppose that something whose efficacy is already observed suddenly becomes causeless or ineffective. Nor is there evidence to set that ordinary account aside and invent an extraordinary one. Why? Not because of verbal expression, since, as has been said, a nonordinary verbal meaning cannot be established when the relation of the word to it is not known.

It is because an action is understood as a required means that determination, beginning, undertaking, and completion of effort arise. Only when such a means is present does someone act in response to an injunction; otherwise, no injunction of any kind makes that person act. Someone may say, “I act because of the cognition that this ought to be done.” But a cognition of what ought to be done does not arise without a cause; it arises because doing so is a means to attaining what one desires. Someone may say that the cognition of duty itself arises from words. The reply is that it does not arise merely from verbal expression. Injunction is the meaning of the word. An injunction must either be a property of the person who enjoins, or be something independent. But “ought to be done” is a property of the object being enjoined. If injunction means that property of the object, then it means that the action is a required means. If “ought to be done” arises from an injunction, even then the word is not a means of knowledge about it: the word directly conveys an injunction, not the property of being obligatory. Nor is that property conveyed indirectly, because one also sees unreliable people enjoin what ought not be done. Perhaps the property of being obligatory is inferred from the fact that an injunction is fulfilled through the completion of the action. But the sense of obligation belongs to the object itself in ordinary usage. For example, when a person is told, “The cow should be milked by you,” and someone else milks the cow, the listener does not begin milking again, because the task is already complete. It is not that someone else has fulfilled the injunction: the other person was not enjoined. The task itself was completed. The analysis of this point has been given at length in the work on injunction; enough of this digression.

Someone may object that knowledge is enjoined because it is a means to liberation. Scripture says that liberation is attained through knowledge: “Through knowledge they ascend there,” “Through knowledge one attains immortality,” and, “After knowing and understanding the Self, one attains all desires.” It also says, “If he desires the world of the ancestors, by his resolve alone the ancestors rise before him,” and so on. Even though liberation is something to be attained, it is not finite, since scripture says that one who reaches it does not return. It is not something established by reasoning, by which its nature could be determined; its nature is established from words alone. Or liberation may be endless because it is attained through endless knowledge. Even if cognition is momentary, it may be endless in the form of a continuum. The reply is:

“Liberation is not its result; liberation is not something to be attained,
nor is it something else...”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 106
units.deva: अविद्यास्तमयो मोक्षः सा संसार उदाहृता । विद्यैव चाद्वया शान्ता तदस्तमय उच्यते
units.iast:
avidyāstamayo mokṣaḥ sā saṃsāra udāhṛtā /
vidyaiva cādvayā śāntā tadastamaya ucyate
units.translation: The setting of ignorance is liberation; that [ignorance] is called bondage. Knowledge alone is nondual and peaceful, and its setting is called release.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 107
units.deva:
कः पुनरेष मोक्षः? यद्यनागतदेहेन्द्रियबुद्ध्यनुत्पादः ‘अशरीरं वावसन्तं न प्रियाप्रिये स्पृशतःऽ; --- इति दर्शनात्, स प्रागभावो न साध्यः । अथ ब्रह्मप्राप्तिः, सा चैत्रग्रामयोरिव वा स्याज्जीवब्रह्मणोर्मार्गश्रुतिभ्यः ---

ऽशतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यस्तासां मूर्धानमभि निस्सृतैका । तयोर्ध्वमायन्नमृतत्वमेति ---

‘स यावत्क्षिप्येन्मनस्तावदादित्यं गच्छत्येतद्वै खलु लोकद्वारम्ऽ; तथा ‘ते ऽर्चिषमभिसंभवति अर्चिषो ऽहःऽइत्यादि । यथा वा मधुनि नानाकुसुमरसानां समुद्रे च नदीनां प्राप्तिरविभागलक्षणा तथा स्यात्, ‘यथा लोके मधुकृतो मधु कुर्वन्तिऽ; इतिऽ; ‘यथा सोम्येमा नद्यःऽ; इति दर्शनात् । कार्यस्य वा कारणभावापत्तिः, ‘तथा विद्वान् पुण्यपापे विधूय निरञ्जनः परमं साम्यमुपैतिऽइति श्रुतेः । तद्रूपपरिणामलक्षणा वा योगव्याघ्रवत्, ‘स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवतिऽ; इति दर्शनात् ‘ब्रह्म संपद्यतऽ; इति च । स्फटिकस्येव रागापकर्षणेन [क्क्स्_120] स्वरूपप्राप्तिलक्षणा, ‘परं ज्योतिरुपसंपद्य स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यतेऽ; इति श्रवणात् । तत्र न तावत्प्रथमः कल्पः, सर्वगतत्वात् --- ‘तदन्तरस्य सर्वस्यऽ; ‘नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतम्ऽ; इति । अनन्यत्वाच्च, तद्विज्ञानेन सर्वविज्ञानोपदेशात्, ‘तत्त्वमसिऽ; इति साक्षात्प्रतिपादनात्, प्रत्यगात्मवृत्तिना च सर्वत्रात्मशब्देन निर्देशात्, ‘अथ यो ऽन्याम्ऽ; इति भेददर्शनापवादात् । अत एव च न द्वितीयः, निरवयवत्वाच्च, ‘निष्कलं निष्क्रियम्ऽइति परस्परावयवसंभेदलक्षणस्याविभागस्यानुपपत्तेः । नापि तृतीयः, कार्यस्य सर्वदा कारणत्वात् । अथ कार्यरूपनाशः, उच्छेदात्मताप्रसङ्गो मोक्षस्य । तत्र ‘विद्ययामृतमश्नुतेऽ; इति विरोधः, विद्ययैवोच्छेदप्रसङ्गात् । आत्मोच्छेदस्य चानिष्टत्वादफलत्वम् । प्रतिषिद्धश्च ‘अक्षरम्ऽइत्यत्र मुख्यः कार्यकारणभावः ‘वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयम्ऽइति विकारानृतत्वप्रतिपादनाच्छ्रुत्या । न चतुर्थः, अनन्यत्वादेव, चैतन्यस्य च ब्रह्मरूपस्याविशेषात् । अथ विज्ञानात्मनां शोकमोहाद्यभावो विशिष्यत इति चेत्तत्रापि शोकादयश्चेदात्मानो विज्ञानात्मनाम्, अनुच्छेद्याः । अथ गुणा अर्थान्तरमागमापायिनः क्षणिकाः, क्षणिकत्वादेव चोच्छिद्यन्त इति न तत्साधनमपेक्ष्यम् । न चागामिनामनुत्पत्तये ऽपेक्ष्यत इत्युक्तम् । अथ ऐश्वर्यविशेषो ब्रह्मणि । तत्प्राप्तिस्तद्रूपपरिणामो मोक्षः, ‘स स्वराड् भवतिऽ; इति श्रुतेः । तदसत्, अनेकेश्वरानुपपत्तेः । ब्रह्मणो न्यूनं समं वा विज्ञानात्मनाम् [क्क्स्_121] ऐश्वर्यं स्यात्? न्यूनत्वेन ब्रह्मरूपापत्तिर्न स्वाराज्यम् । तथा हि --- ब्रह्मशब्दवाच्यः परमेश्वरस्तेषामधिपतिः स्यात् । तथा चान्यराजता । तत्र चान्तवत्वं श्रूयते --- ‘अथ ये ऽन्यथातो विदुः, अन्यराजानस्ते क्षय्यलोका भवन्तिऽ; इति । उपपद्यते च परमेश्वरेच्छया न्यूनैश्वर्याणामैश्वर्यप्रच्युतिदर्शनाल्लोके । ‘समत्वस्य त्वनपपत्तिरेव युगपत् । एकश्चेत्सर्वाधिपतिः सर्वस्य प्रशासिता, परः किं कुर्वन्नीशः स्यात्? विरोधाच्च । न खल्वेषामेकमतित्वे हेतुरस्ति । तत्रैकस्मिन् वस्तुनि विरुद्धाभिप्राययोरेकाभिप्रायानुविधायित्वे तस्येतरस्यानीश्वरत्वम् । उभयानुप्रायानुविधानं न, विरोधात् । उभयोरननुविधाने ऽनीश्वरत्वमुभयोः । कार्यासिद्धश्चेदैकमत्ये हेतुः परिषद्वत्, अन्यथा तस्यासिद्धेरिति चेत्, प्रत्येकमनीश्वरत्वम् । अथ पर्यायेणैश्वर्यमविरोधायोच्यते, अन्तवत्ता । जगत्सर्गस्य चासंभवान्न ब्रह्मतुल्यमैश्वर्यम् । यतः पर एव जगत्सर्गे श्रूयते । तदुपासनेन सर्गोत्तरकालो ऽपवर्ग इति । तस्मात्स्फटिकस्येव रागाद्यपकर्षणेन स्वरूपाविर्भावो ब्रह्मप्राप्तिः, ब्रह्मरूपत्वाद्विज्ञानात्मनः । तथा च ‘परं ज्योतिरुपसंपद्य स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यतेऽइत्युक्तम्, अन्यरूपनिष्पत्तौ स्वशब्दानुपपत्तेः । निष्पद्यमानस्याभेदात्संबन्धाद्वोपपत्तिरिति चेत् । न, विशेषणानर्थक्यात्सर्वस्य तस्य निष्पद्यमानस्य स्वत्वात् । तत्र यथा मलापगमे शुक्लमेव सद्वस्त्रं ‘शुक्लं जातम्ऽइत्युच्यते तथा मोहावरणविगमे स्वरूपाविर्भावे ‘स्वेन रूपेणाभिनिष्पद्यतेऽ; इत्युच्यते । तथा ‘ब्रह्मैव सन् ब्रह्माप्येतिऽ; इति । तदेवं स्वरूपस्थितिलक्षणत्वान्मोहस्य न कार्यता, प्रागपि स्वरूपस्य भावात् । आगन्तुकस्यास्वरूपत्वात् । न चान्यत्वम्, यतो ऽविद्यापगम एवोक्तेन प्रकारेण मुक्तिः । अविद्या संसारः । विद्यैव चाविद्यानिवृत्तिः यद्यग्रहणमविद्या, यतो भाव [क्क्स्_122] एवाभावव्यावृत्तिः । अथ विपर्यासः, तथापि विरोधिततत्त्वज्ञानोदय एव तन्निवृत्तिः । न हि शुक्तिकाज्ञानोत्पादादन्या रजतज्ञाननिवृत्तिस्तत्साध्या प्रयत्नान्तरसाध्या वा, तयोर्यौगपद्यात्प्रयत्नान्तरानपेक्षणाच्च । तथा च विद्याब्रह्मप्राप्त्योस्तुल्यकालता श्रूयते --- ‘ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवतिऽ; इति, तथा ‘आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्, न बिभेतिऽ; ‘तदात्मानमेवावेदहं ब्रह्मास्मीति । तस्मात्तत्सर्वमभवत्ऽ; ‘तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतःऽ; वेद -- भवति, विद्वान् -- न बिभेति, को मोहः -- पश्यत इति पौर्वापर्याश्रवणात् । यत्तु क्वचित्पौर्वापर्यं तत् ‘व्यादाय स्वपितिऽइति यथा । नन्वेकत्वे तुल्यकालताप्यनुपपन्ना । न, एकस्यापि वस्तुनो भावाभावरूपेण व्यपदेशात्, तथा --- ‘यदा घटो नश्यति तदा कपालानि जायन्तेऽ; इति । कथं तर्हि मार्गाविभागसर्गाप्ययैश्वर्यश्रुतयः? तत्राहुः --- न मार्गश्रुतयो निरुपाधिविशुद्धब्रह्मविद्याविषयाः । यत्र हि सर्वोपाधिविशुद्धमस्थूलादिकं ब्रह्मोपास्यम्, तत्र ‘ब्रह्मैव सन् ब्रह्माप्येतिऽ; ‘न तस्मात्प्राणा उत्क्रामन्ति, अत्रैव समवनीयन्तेऽ; इति प्राणानुत्क्रमणेन विज्ञानात्मन एवागतिरुच्यते । न हि तदगमने तदुपाधेस्तस्य ब्रह्मणो भेदेन विज्ञानात्मत्वम् । यत्र तु ‘मनोमयः प्राणशरीरो भारूपःऽ; इति सोपाध्युपास्यम्, तद्विषयास्ताः । यत्रैतच्छ्रूयते --- ‘अरश्च ह वै ण्यश्चार्णवौ ब्रह्मलोके तृतीयस्यामितो [क्क्स्_123] दिवि तदैरंमदीयं सरस्तदश्वत्थः सोमसवनस्तदपराजिता पूर्ब्रह्मणः प्रभुविमितं हिरण्मयं वेश्मऽ; इति । तथा चाब्रह्मविदामपि तद्गतिश्रवणम् --- ‘ये चामी अरण्ये श्रद्धां सत्यं तप इत्युपासतेऽ; इति । परब्रह्मप्राप्तिस्तु नाब्रह्मविदां युज्यते,

‘विद्यया तदारोहन्ति यत्र कामाः परागताः । न तत्र दक्षिणा यान्ति नाविद्वांसस्तपस्विनःऽ; ॥ इति, तथा ‘तमेव विदित्वाति मृत्युमेतिऽ; इति वचनात् । अपुनरावृत्ति श्रुतिस्तर्हि कथम्? अत्र केचिन्मन्यते --- क्रममुक्त्याश्रयणात्तत्प्राप्य तत्रोत्पन्ननिरुपाधितत्त्वज्ञानाः परं पदमश्नुवते । यथोक्तम् ---

‘वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः
संन्यासयोगाद्यतयः शुद्धसत्त्वाः । ते ब्रह्मलोकेषु परान्तकाले
परामृताः परिमुच्यन्ति सर्वेऽ; ॥ ब्रह्मलोकेष्विति कार्यब्रह्मलोकनिर्देशः, बहुवचनात्तत्रावयवद्वारेण बहुत्वोपपत्तेः । परान्तकालो महाप्रलयो ब्रह्मणः स्वाधिकारपर्यवसानम्, तस्मिन् परामृताः परब्रह्मरूपेणामृताः सन्तः संन्यासयोगाद्भेदेन परमेश्वरे स्वकृतानां कर्मणां फलानां च संन्यासाद्योगाच्च सर्वमिदं कर्त्रादि ब्रह्म इत्युपासनात् । तथा च स्मृतिः ---

‘ब्रह्मणा सह ते सर्वे संप्राप्ते प्रतिसंचरे । परस्यान्ते कृतात्मानः प्रविशन्ति परं पदम्ऽ; ॥ अन्ये तु मन्यते --- यथा चन्द्रलोके यावत्संपातमुषित्वा स्थित एव तस्मिन् भुक्तभोगा आवर्तन्ते नैवं स्थित एव ब्रह्मलोके तत आवृत्तिः । किं तु तत्प्रलयपर्यवसाना [क्क्स्_124] तत्र स्थितिः । तत्प्रलये हि न तत आवृत्तो भवति । ततश्चानावृत्तिः श्रूयते । तथा च ‘इमं मानवमावर्तं नावर्तन्तेऽ; इति ‘इमम्(?, इम् एदितिओन्), इहऽइति विशेषणम् ‘अमृतत्वमेतिऽइत्यमृतत्वमापेक्षिकम्, यथा --- ‘अमृता देवाःऽ; इति । तथा च पौराणिकस्मरणम् --- ‘आभूतसंप्लवं स्थानममृतत्वं हि भाष्यतेऽ; इति । यत्तु मन्यते --- सर्वगतत्वे ऽपि ब्रह्मणो विकृताविकृतभेदः । ततश्च देशभेदः । तथा चाविकृतस्य ब्रह्मणो देशभेदः श्रूयते --- ‘अथ यदतः परो दिवो ज्योतिर्दीप्यतेऽ; इति । अतो ऽविकृतस्य नियतदेशस्य ब्रह्मणः प्राप्तये युज्यते मार्गविशेषः । तत्संप्रधार्यम् । न तावदनुत्पन्नाद्वयविशुद्धविद्यस्यायं मार्गः, ब्रह्मविदः श्रवणात् । नापि विद्यावतः । विद्योदये निखिलभेदोच्छेदादिति । मधुनदीनिदर्शनाविभागश्रुतिरपि विवेकज्ञानाभावपरा, न तु तद्विध एवाविभागः । सर्गश्रुतयो ऽपि न सर्गपराः । किं तर्हि? एकात्मतत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिप्रधानाः । ततस्तदनुगुणतयैव तासामर्थव्यवस्थानम्, न तु तद्विरोधेन । तथा हि --- कस्मिन्नु भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवति? ‘सदेव सोम्येदमग्र आसीदेकमेवाद्वितीयम्ऽ; इत्येकत्वेनोपक्रमात् ‘ऐतदात्म्यमिदं सर्वम् । तत्सत्यम्, स आत्मा, तत्त्वमसिऽइत्युपसंहारादेकत्वेनैवैकात्म्यतत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिपरमेकमिदं वाक्यं गम्यते । तत्र यद्यपरस्तेजःप्रभृतितत्त्वसर्गः सत्यतया विधीयेत, वाक्यभेदः स्यात् । अतो यथोपांशुयाजवाक्ये ऽजामित्वोपक्रमोपसंहारे ‘विष्णुरुपांशु यष्टव्यःऽइत्यादीनि वचांसि [क्क्स्_125] वाक्यभेददोषात्पृथग्विधित्वमलभमानानि तादर्थ्यात्तदानुकूल्येन स्तुत्यर्थतया व्यवतिष्ठन्ते, तथा सर्गश्रुतयो ऽप्येकत्वोपायतया । न च विपरीतं शक्यं वक्तुम् --- एकत्वश्रुतिरेव भेदप्रतिपत्त्यर्थेति, सर्वत्रैकत्वेनोपक्रमात् उपसंहाराच्च । येनोपक्रम्यते येन चोपसंह्रियते स वाक्यार्थः । भेदप्रतिपत्तेश्चाफलत्वात् । एकत्वप्रतिपत्तेस्तु दृष्टं श्रुतं च फलं शोकादिनिवृत्तः, विशुद्धैकात्म्यदर्शनेन तदवगमात् ‘तत्र को मोहः कः शोक एकत्वमनुपश्यतःऽ; इति श्रवणात् । फलवदङ्गता चाफलस्य । उपायत्वं च । न चेदं जगदसन्मूलम् । किं तर्हि? अद्वितीयैकसन्मूलम् । कारणाव्यतिरेकाच्च कार्यस्य सदेकमेवेदम्, घटादिवत् । मृद्रूपेण हि घटादयो नैकत्वमतिक्रामन्ति । नन्वेवं मुख्य एव कार्यकारणभाव उक्तः स्यात् । नैतत्, एकत्वावतारोपायमात्रत्वात् । न खल्वत्र कार्यकारणभाव एव प्रतिपाद्यः, येनासौ यथाशब्दं मुख्य एव गृह्येत । एकत्वोपायत्त्वादित्युक्तम् । एकत्वं चानेनोपायेनावतार्यते पुरुषः । स च मुख्यः प्रधानविरोधी । ‘एकमेवाद्वितीयम्ऽइति पुनः पुनः श्रुतेः सर्वभेदनिरासपरत्वान्न शक्यं वक्तुम् --- कारणात्मनैकत्वम्, कार्यात्मना नानात्वम् --- ‘तत्सत्यम्, स आत्माऽ; इति च कारणस्यैव सत्यत्वावधारणात् । अन्यत्र चऽ; ‘इन्द्रो मायाभिःऽ; इति भेदस्य मायागम्यत्वश्रुतेः । साक्षाच्च भेदाभावस्य श्रवणात् --- ‘नेह नानास्ति किञ्चनऽ; इति । भेदाभेदयोश्च विरोधात्प्रागनुपपत्तेर्वर्णितत्वात् । तदविरोधेन वर्ण्यते तदुपादानमात्रतया भेदविकल्पस्य, बिम्बप्रतिबिम्बवद्वर्णपदवाक्यादिवच्च । यथा हि न बिम्बात्प्रतिबिम्बानामुत्पत्तिर्नानारूपाणाम्, बिम्बोपादानमात्रतया प्रतिबिम्बभेदविकल्पस्य । न हि बिम्बात् [क्क्स्_126] परस्परतो वा व्यावृत्तानि कानिचिद्वस्तूनि प्रतिबिम्बानि । बिम्बोपादानं तु तन्नाना निर्भासमात्रम् । तथा न वर्णेभ्यः पदवाक्यप्रकरणादीनि कानिचिद्वस्तूनि सन्ति, तदुपादानमात्रत्वात्तत्कल्पनायाः ‘वर्णेभ्यः पदानि निष्पद्यन्ते, पदेभ्यो वाक्यम्ऽ; इत्युच्यते । अपि च स्वप्ने ऽपि सृष्टिः श्रूयते --- ‘न तत्र रथा न रथयोगा न पन्थानो भवन्ति, अथ रथान् रथयोगान् पथः सृजतेऽइति, तद्वदेषा स्यात्, अन्यपरत्वात् । स्वयमेव ‘वाचारम्भणं विकारो नामधेयम्ऽ; इति विकारासत्यतया न पारमार्थिकीत्युक्तम् । ऐश्वर्यश्रुतिष्वपि स्वगुणविद्याविपाको ऽयं श्रूयते --- ‘स एकधा भवति त्रिधा भवतिऽ; ‘सर्वांश्च कामानाप्नोतिऽ; ‘स स्वराड् भवतिऽ; इति, न तु मोक्षः । स हि निरुपाधिब्रह्मविद्यानिमित्त एव । यदपि क्वचिदपुनरावृत्तिश्रवणम्, तस्यापि द्वयी गतिर्व्याख्यातेत्येकं दर्शनम् । अन्ये तु मन्यन्ते --- आविर्भूतब्रह्मरूपो ब्रह्मणः सर्वात्मत्वात्सर्वेशितृत्वाच्च सर्वोपभोगानां च भोक्तृत्वात्तदानन्दमात्रारूपत्वाद्देवाद्यानन्दानां ‘स सर्वांश्च लोकानाप्नोति सर्वांश्च कामान्ऽ; ‘स स्वराड् भवतिऽइति तस्य तत्संकीर्तनं ब्रह्मरूपाविर्भावलक्षणमोक्षप्रशंसार्थम् । ननु सर्वात्मत्वेन सर्वकामावाप्तौ सर्वशोकमोहाद्याप्तिरपि स्यात् । न, तेषामब्रह्मरूपत्वादविद्याध्यस्तत्वात् । ज्ञानैश्वर्यानन्दभोगास्तु ब्रह्मणो रूपम्, ‘विज्ञानमानन्दं ब्रह्मऽ; ‘नान्यो ऽतो ऽस्ति द्रष्टाऽ; ‘एतस्यैवानन्दस्यान्यानि भूतानि मात्रामुपजीवन्तिऽ; [क्क्स्_127] ‘सर्वस्येशानःऽ; ‘एतस्य वा अक्षरस्य प्रशासने गार्गिऽइत्यादिश्रुतिभ्यः । तथा च यत्किञ्चिदीश्वरत्वं यच्च विज्ञानं यश्चानन्दो ब्रह्मादिषु स्थावरान्तेषु भूतेषु ब्रह्मणि तानि । तान्याविर्भूतब्रह्मस्वरूपः समश्नुत इति युक्तम् । लोकादयस्त्वविद्याध्यस्ता न ब्रह्मरूपम् । ते कथमाविर्भूतब्रह्मस्वरूपमास्कन्देयुः? ननु प्रपञ्चशून्यस्याद्वैतस्य ब्रह्मरूपस्य ज्ञेयाभावादीशितव्याभावाच्च विज्ञानमैश्वर्यं चानुपपन्नम् । तत्र ‘सर्वज्ञःऽ; ‘सर्वेश्वरःऽ; इत्यपि श्रुती समाधेये एव । नैतत्सारम् । यतो नेशितव्यकृतमीश्वरत्वम्, ज्ञेयकृतं वा ज्ञातृत्वम् । किं तु सिद्धेन ज्ञानरूपेण सिद्धया चेशनशक्त्या ज्ञेयमवाप्नोति, ईशितव्यं च विनियुङ्क्ते प्रशास्ति च प्रकाशदाहवत् । सिद्धेन हि प्रकाशरूपेण प्रकाश्यं प्रकाशयति विवस्वान् । न तु प्रकाश्याधीनं तस्य प्रकाशरूपम्, दाह्याधीना वा अग्नेर्दाहशक्तिः । तथा च तच्चैतन्येनैव कृत्स्नस्य प्रपञ्चस्यावभासनात् ‘तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभातिऽ; ‘नान्यो ऽतो ऽस्ति द्रष्टाऽइत्यादिश्रुतेः सर्वज्ञत्वम् । सर्वेश्वरत्वमपि तदैश्वर्येण यथायथमीश्वरैरीशितव्यानामीशनात् । एवं च ‘एष भूताधिपतिःऽ; ‘एष लोकपालःऽइति ब्रह्मेन्द्रयमादीनां चैश्वर्यमुक्तम् । सर्वकामावाप्तिश्च तदीयत्वाद्देवाद्यानन्दस्य । कामेष्वानन्दप्राप्त्या कामा आप्ता भवन्ति, न स्वरूपेण । एवं ‘स तत्र पर्येति जक्षन् क्रीडन् रममाणः स्त्रीभिर्वाऽ; इति वर्णनीयम्, [क्क्स्_128] तद्विषयानन्दभोगात्, न तु स्त्र्यादियोगः । यथा ‘आत्मरतिरात्मक्रीड आत्ममिथुनःऽ; इति, न हि मुख्यमात्मक्रीडत्वमात्ममिथुनत्वं वा संभवति । यतश्चानवच्छिन्नानि तदीयान्येव सर्वभूतेषु ज्ञानादीनि कल्पितावच्छेदानि, अतो यत्र यत्र नात्यन्तमवच्छेदः समुत्कर्षात्तेषां तानि तानि प्रत्यासत्तेर्भूतान्यात्मत्वेन भगवानुक्त्वा --- ‘मुनीनामप्यहं व्यासःऽइत्यादि, उपसंजहार --- ‘यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वम्ऽ; इति । तथा ‘अदृष्टं द्रष्टृ, अश्रुतं श्रोतृऽइत्यादि, सर्वभूतदर्शनादीनां तच्चैतन्यनिबन्धनत्वात् । अन्ये त्वाहुः --- यावान् कश्चित्परस्मिन्नामरूपाश्रयो व्यपदेशः सर्वो ऽसावाध्यानाय । यथा ‘यो ऽसावादित्ये पुरुषःऽ; ‘हिरण्यश्मश्रुःऽ; इत्यादि । न हि स्वमहिमप्रतिष्ठस्य परस्य देशविशेषावरोधः, सर्वविशेषातिगस्य च रूपविशेषयोगः । परश्चैषः, सर्वपाप्मोदयश्रुतेः --- ‘उदितः सर्वेभ्यः पाप्मभ्यःऽ; इति, आध्यानं तु तथा विधीयते । तथा सर्वज्ञत्वादपि द्रष्टव्यमिति । तदेवं ब्रह्मात्मनस्तद्रूपाविर्भावस्तत्प्राप्तिः, स मोक्षः । सा च विद्यैव । तस्मान्न साध्यो मोक्षः, न च विद्यया अन्य इति पुष्कलम् । अथ मतम् --- मा भून्मोक्षः साध्यः । बन्धहेतुक्षयस्तु साध्यते । तत्साधनमात्मदर्शनं स्यात् । श्रूयते च तस्य फलं बन्धहेतूनां कर्मणां क्षयः --- ‘क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन् दृष्टे परावरेऽ; । तथा ‘तद्यथेषीकातूलमग्नौ प्रोतं प्रदूयेत एवं हास्य सर्वे पाप्मानः प्रदूयन्तेऽ; ‘पाप्मशब्देन पुण्यमपि संगृहीतम्, सावद्यफलत्वात्, । अन्यत्र च ‘नैतं सेतुमहोरात्रे तरतो न जरा न मृत्युर्न शोको न सुकृतं न दुष्कृतम्ऽ; इत्युपक्रम्य [क्क्स्_129] ‘सर्वे पाप्मानो ऽतो निवर्तन्तेऽइत्युपसंहारात् । न च तत्क्षयमन्तरेण क्षेमप्राप्तिः । अतो ऽवश्यकर्तव्यः । न चादत्तफलस्य कर्मणो न क्षयः, प्रायश्चित्तानां दोषसंयोगेन चोद्यमानानां तत्क्षयफलत्वात् । तस्मात्प्रायश्चित्तैरिव विद्यया बन्धहेतुक्षयः साध्यते । सैव च मुक्तिः, बन्धनविश्लेषार्थत्वान्मुचेः । एवं च नान्तवत्वदोषः, प्रध्वंसस्य कार्यस्याप्यविनाशात् । तत्रोच्यते ---

प्रायश्चित्तदिशा बन्धहेतूच्छेदो ऽपि नो ततः । सर्वाविद्याप्रविलये न च्छेद्यमवशिष्यते
