units.deva: अदृष्टत्वादप्रवृत्तिः शुक्तिकाशकले समा । दृष्टं तद्येन रूपेण तत्प्रवृत्तेरकारणम्
units.iast:
adṛṣṭatvādapravṛttiḥ śuktikāśakale samā /
dṛṣṭaṃ tadyena rūpeṇa tatpravṛtterakāraṇam
units.translation: Failure to act because an object has not been seen is the same in the case of the shell-fragment; that by which it was seen is not a cause for acting toward it.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 121
units.deva: दृष्टस्मृताविवेकाच्चेदिदमत्र परीक्ष्यताम् । तत्त्वबोधादथातत्त्वाबोधाद्रजतवेदनात्
units.iast:
dṛṣṭasmṛtāvivekāccedidamatra parīkṣyatām /
tattvabodhādathātattvābodhādrajatavedanāt
units.translation: If this is said to arise from failure to distinguish what is seen from what is remembered, let this be examined: does knowledge of truth or mistaken knowledge give rise to the cognition “silver”?

gloss.en: between what is seen and what is remembered

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 122
units.deva: दृष्टे प्रवृत्तिः पूर्वस्मिन्विपरीतार्थता मतेः । न दृष्टादृष्टयोर्भेदः परस्मिन्नोपयोगिनी
units.iast:
dṛṣṭe pravṛttiḥ pūrvasminviparītārthatā mateḥ /
na dṛṣṭādṛṣṭayorbhedaḥ parasminnopayoginī
units.translation: In the first case, action follows from what is directly seen, while cognition takes the opposite form. There is no difference between what is seen and unseen that would be useful in the other case.

gloss.en: between what is seen and unseen

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 123
units.deva: स्वयोगदर्शने ते हि समारोपोपयोगिनी । नादृष्टे ऽसंप्रयुक्ते वा चाक्षुषः स्याद्विपर्ययः
units.iast:
svayogadarśane te hi samāropopayoginī /
nādṛṣṭe 'saṃprayukte vā cākṣuṣaḥ syādviparyayaḥ
units.translation: For error depends on superimposition in those cases where one sees the alignment [of the senses with an object]. A visual error cannot arise when the object has not been seen or is not in sensory contact.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 124
units.deva: यदि चक्षुषा संप्रयुक्तं शुक्तिशकलं ‘न रजतम्ऽ; इति प्रतीयात्, रजतं वा तथा, न शुक्तिकाशकल आदित्सया प्रवर्तेत रजतार्थी, तस्य ‘रजतम्ऽ; [क्क्स्_138] इत्यनवगतेर्लोष्टादिवत् । न च स्मर्यमाणे रजते सा प्रवृत्तिः, तद्देशासंनिधेः । न हि प्रतीतिमुपगते ऽपि वस्तुनि यत्र तस्यासंनिधिस्तत्र तेनार्थी प्रवर्तते । स्यादेतत् --- रजतस्य प्रतीतेरसंनिधेश्चाप्रतीतेस्तत्र प्रवृत्तिः । तन्न, शुक्तिकाशकल एव प्रवृत्तेः । तत्रैव तु प्रवृत्तिस्तत्संनिधिनिबन्धना । रजतमात्रप्रतीतेः स्मृतिविवेकशून्यत्वाच्च प्रवृत्तिरन्यत्रापि स्यात्, असंनिधानाग्रहणस्य तत्राप्यविशेषात् । अथ मतम् --- अन्यदेशेषु वस्तुषु सविशेषप्रत्यक्षावगतेषु रजताद्विवेकग्रहणादप्रवृत्तिः, शुक्तिकाशकले तु रजतसाधारणशुक्लभास्वररूपमात्रप्रतीतेर्विशेषात्प्रत्ययाच्च स्मृतिविपरिवर्तिनो रजताद्विवेकग्रहणात्प्रवृत्तिः । एवमप्यदृष्टेषु लोकादिषु ततो ऽन्यतानवधारणात्प्रवृत्तिः स्यात् । अथ न तेषु रजतावगमः, इतरत्रापि न । भावे वा विपरीता ख्यातिरभ्युपगता स्यात् । अथादृष्टत्वादेवादृष्टेषु न प्रवर्तते, शुक्तावपि न प्रवर्तेत । ननु यत्तु तथा रजतरूपम्, न तेनावगमः । स यथा चक्षुषासंप्रयुक्तस्य नास्ति, तथा संप्रयुक्ताया अपि शुक्तेः । यदि मन्येत --- दृश्यमानस्मर्यमाणयोगविवेकाच्चक्षुःसंप्रयुक्त एव प्रवर्तते, नेतरस्मिन् । तत्रापीदं विचार्यम् --- विवेकग्रहणस्य विवेककृतो ऽभावात्संनिधिप्रतीतेरभेदबोधस्ततो वा प्रवृत्तिः, भेदावबोधाभावमात्राद्वा? पूर्वस्मिन्विपर्ययः, उत्तरस्मिन् दृश्यमानादृश्यमानयोः संप्रयुक्तासंप्रयुक्तयोर्वा न विशेषः, भेदाग्रहणस्य तुल्यत्वात् । न हीन्द्रियसंयोगस्य दर्शनस्य वा कश्चिदग्रह उपयोगः, अभूतसमारोपे त्वस्ति । न कथञ्चिदगृहीते ऽसंप्रयुक्ते वैन्द्रियकः समारोप उपपद्यते । स्मृतं प्रत्यक्षतो भिन्नं स्वज्ञानादेव चेत्कुतः । [क्क्स्_139] अविवेको ऽन्यथा तु स्यात्सदा सामान्यदर्शने
units.iast:
yadi cakṣuṣā saṃprayuktaṃ śuktiśakalaṃ ‘na rajatam'; iti pratīyāt, rajataṃ vā tathā, na śuktikāśakala āditsayā pravarteta rajatārthī, tasya ‘rajatam'; [kks_138] ityanavagaterloṣṭādivat / na ca smaryamāṇe rajate sā pravṛttiḥ, taddeśāsaṃnidheḥ / na hi pratītimupagate 'pi vastuni yatra tasyāsaṃnidhistatra tenārthī pravartate / syādetat --- rajatasya pratīterasaṃnidheścāpratītestatra pravṛttiḥ / tanna, śuktikāśakala eva pravṛtteḥ / tatraiva tu pravṛttistatsaṃnidhinibandhanā / rajatamātrapratīteḥ smṛtivivekaśūnyatvācca pravṛttiranyatrāpi syāt, asaṃnidhānāgrahaṇasya tatrāpyaviśeṣāt / atha matam --- anyadeśeṣu vastuṣu saviśeṣapratyakṣāvagateṣu rajatādvivekagrahaṇādapravṛttiḥ, śuktikāśakale tu rajatasādhāraṇaśuklabhāsvararūpamātrapratīterviśeṣātpratyayācca smṛtiviparivartino rajatādvivekagrahaṇātpravṛttiḥ / evamapyadṛṣṭeṣu lokādiṣu tato 'nyatānavadhāraṇātpravṛttiḥ syāt / atha na teṣu rajatāvagamaḥ, itaratrāpi na / bhāve vā viparītā khyātirabhyupagatā syāt / athādṛṣṭatvādevādṛṣṭeṣu na pravartate, śuktāvapi na pravarteta / nanu yattu tathā rajatarūpam, na tenāvagamaḥ / sa yathā cakṣuṣāsaṃprayuktasya nāsti, tathā saṃprayuktāyā api śukteḥ / yadi manyeta --- dṛśyamānasmaryamāṇayogavivekāccakṣuḥsaṃprayukta eva pravartate, netarasmin / tatrāpīdaṃ vicāryam --- vivekagrahaṇasya vivekakṛto 'bhāvātsaṃnidhipratīterabhedabodhastato vā pravṛttiḥ, bhedāvabodhābhāvamātrādvā? pūrvasminviparyayaḥ, uttarasmin dṛśyamānādṛśyamānayoḥ saṃprayuktāsaṃprayuktayorvā na viśeṣaḥ, bhedāgrahaṇasya tulyatvāt / na hīndriyasaṃyogasya darśanasya vā kaścidagraha upayogaḥ, abhūtasamārope tvasti / na kathañcidagṛhīte 'saṃprayukte vaindriyakaḥ samāropa upapadyate /

smṛtaṃ pratyakṣato bhinnaṃ svajñānādeva cetkutaḥ /
[kks_139] aviveko 'nyathā tu syātsadā sāmānyadarśane
units.translation:
If a shell-fragment joined to the eye were apprehended as “not silver,” or silver were apprehended in that way, a person seeking silver would not set out to pick up the shell-fragment for the sake of silver: for silver would not be known there, just as a clod and the like are not. Nor does that action arise toward silver merely as remembered, since it is not present in that place. Even when an object has been apprehended, a person seeking it does not act toward a place where it is absent. One might say: action there comes from apprehending silver and not apprehending its absence. No: the action occurs toward the shell-fragment itself. It occurs precisely there because that object is present. If there were merely an apprehension of silver, with no discernment between memory and perception, action could occur elsewhere too, since failure to apprehend the silver’s absence would be the same there.

Suppose instead that, when other objects are directly perceived with their distinguishing features, one does not act because one apprehends that they differ from silver; but with the shell-fragment one perceives only a white, shining appearance shared with silver, and because this perception is distinctive and turns the remembered silver into something present, one fails to discern the difference from silver and therefore acts. Even so, one would act toward unseen objects such as distant regions, since their difference from silver has not been ascertained. If one replies that silver is not apprehended in those unseen places, the same is true in the other case as well. Or, if silver is apprehended there, one must accept the theory that what is apprehended is something mistaken for another thing. If one argues that no action toward unseen things occurs precisely because they have not been seen, then there should be no action toward the shell either.

But the silver-form that is present there is not apprehended as silver. Just as there is no apprehension of it when it is not joined to the eye, so too there is none when the shell itself is joined to the eye. If one holds that action occurs only where the eye contacts an object, because the seen and remembered are not discriminated, and not toward what is elsewhere, this too must be examined: does action follow from apprehending presence and thereby failing to discern a difference, or merely from the absence of awareness of difference? On the first account, the result is the opposite of what is intended. On the second, there is no distinction between what is seen and unseen, or between what is in contact with the senses and what is not, because failure to grasp the difference is equal in both cases. Neither sensory contact nor seeing has any useful role here; what matters is the superimposition of something that is not there. A sensory superimposition upon something not apprehended at all is in no way possible when it is not in contact with the senses.

“If what is remembered is distinct from what is perceived simply through its own cognition, how could there be confusion? Otherwise confusion would arise whenever a general feature is seen.”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 125
units.deva: विपर्ययो ऽन्यं स्मरतो न च संशयदर्शनात् । स्मृतद्वयाविवेकोत्थं संशयं यदि मन्यते
units.iast:
viparyayo 'nyaṃ smarato na ca saṃśayadarśanāt /
smṛtadvayāvivekotthaṃ saṃśayaṃ yadi manyate
units.translation: There is no error from remembering something else, since doubt is also observed. If one holds that doubt arises from failing to distinguish two remembered things…

gloss.en: arising from failure to distinguish two memories

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 126
units.deva: तन्नोभयोरपि यतः स्मृतौ दृष्टो विपर्ययः । विशेषज्ञानतो ऽध्यक्षे स्मृतं यदि विविच्यते
units.iast:
tannobhayorapi yataḥ smṛtau dṛṣṭo viparyayaḥ /
viśeṣajñānato 'dhyakṣe smṛtaṃ yadi vivicyate
units.translation: No, because error is observed in both cases. If what is remembered is distinguished from what is directly perceived through knowledge of a particular feature…

gloss.en: through knowledge of a distinguishing feature

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 127
units.deva: न स्वज्ञानादसत्यस्मिन्द्विस्मृतौ कथमेकधीः । एकत्वमेव स्मरतः प्राग्रूपं शशिनि स्फुटम्
units.iast:
na svajñānādasatyasmindvismṛtau kathamekadhīḥ /
ekatvameva smarataḥ prāgrūpaṃ śaśini sphuṭam
units.translation: If the object is unreal, how could one cognition arise from two memories without distinguishing them by their own cognitions? The moon’s earlier form appears clearly to one who remembers only its unity.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 128
units.deva: तिमिरादिप्रदोषेण कथं ते द्वित्वविभ्रमः । पिपासतश्च सलिलं शुक्तिकाहितचेतसः
units.iast:
timirādipradoṣeṇa kathaṃ te dvitvavibhramaḥ /
pipāsataśca salilaṃ śuktikāhitacetasaḥ
units.translation: How could the illusion of seeing two moons be caused by a defect such as eye disease? And why would a thirsty person whose mind is fixed on a shell see water?

gloss.en: through a defect such as eye disease
for one whose mind is fixed on a shell

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 129
units.deva:
विपर्ययो न हि भवेद्भवन्वा सलिले भवेत् । अपि चेदं तत्र भवान् व्याचष्टाम् --- स्मर्यमाणं दृश्यमानात्स्वज्ञानादेव विविच्यते, न वा --- स्मृतिज्ञानस्य स्वरूपमेव तादृशं यत्प्रमातव्याद्भेदेनावभासयति, स्वरूपमात्रनिष्ठं वा । तत्र पूर्वस्मिन् स्मरणगोचरयोरविवेकः कुतः, स्वज्ञानादेव विविक्तत्वात्? इतरस्मिन्नपि सदा स्मृतौ विपर्ययः स्यात्, सामान्यदर्शने चान्यस्मृतावविवेकात् । न च तत्तथा, संशयस्यापि दर्शनात् । अथ मतम् --- एकस्मृतौ विपर्ययः, ततो ऽविवेकात् । अनेकस्मृतौ तु संशयः । नैकस्मादविवेकात् । तदसत् । अनेकस्मरणे ऽपि हि दृश्यते विपर्ययः । यदि च प्रत्यक्षे ऽर्थे विशेषज्ञानात्स्मर्यमाणं विविच्यते, न स्वज्ञानात् । असति तत्र विशेषज्ञाने च द्वयोः स्मृतौ संशय एव स्यात्, नैकावभासो विपर्ययः । अथ तु स्वज्ञानात्स्मृतं विविच्यते, स्मृतिविपर्ययभेदश्चाभ्युपगम्यते । तदानेकस्मरणे ऽपीन्द्रियदोषविशेषाद्युक्तो विपर्ययः । दर्शितं चेदम् --- सामान्यदर्शने ऽपि कदाचिदेकां कोटिं स्मरतो न संशयो न विपर्ययः, दोषाणामपुष्टेः । अतः स्वज्ञानादेव तदा स्मृतं विविच्यते, न दृश्यविशेषपरिच्छेदात् । एवं चेत्कुतो दृश्यमानस्मर्यमाणाविवेकः?

[क्क्स्_140] अपि च अन्यदेव स्मरतः पूर्वरूपमेकत्वं शशिनि द्वित्वविभ्रमः, न स्मर्यमाणाविवेकजः । न च ज्ञानेन्द्रियवृत्तिभेदाविवेकात्, तयोरप्रत्यक्षत्वात्स्मर्यमाणत्वाच्च । शुक्तिकाहितचेतसश्च सलिलं पिपासतो न स्याद्विपर्ययः । सलिलाभासो वा, स्मर्यमाणस्य स्वज्ञानविवेकात् । न च सर्वा नियोगेन भ्रान्तिः सादृश्यबन्धना
units.iast:
viparyayo na hi bhavedbhavanvā salile bhavet /
api cedaṃ tatra bhavān vyācaṣṭām --- smaryamāṇaṃ dṛśyamānātsvajñānādeva vivicyate, na vā --- smṛtijñānasya svarūpameva tādṛśaṃ yatpramātavyādbhedenāvabhāsayati, svarūpamātraniṣṭhaṃ vā / tatra pūrvasmin smaraṇagocarayoravivekaḥ kutaḥ, svajñānādeva viviktatvāt? itarasminnapi sadā smṛtau viparyayaḥ syāt, sāmānyadarśane cānyasmṛtāvavivekāt / na ca tattathā, saṃśayasyāpi darśanāt / atha matam --- ekasmṛtau viparyayaḥ, tato 'vivekāt / anekasmṛtau tu saṃśayaḥ / naikasmādavivekāt / tadasat / anekasmaraṇe 'pi hi dṛśyate viparyayaḥ / yadi ca pratyakṣe 'rthe viśeṣajñānātsmaryamāṇaṃ vivicyate, na svajñānāt / asati tatra viśeṣajñāne ca dvayoḥ smṛtau saṃśaya eva syāt, naikāvabhāso viparyayaḥ / atha tu svajñānātsmṛtaṃ vivicyate, smṛtiviparyayabhedaścābhyupagamyate / tadānekasmaraṇe 'pīndriyadoṣaviśeṣādyukto viparyayaḥ / darśitaṃ cedam --- sāmānyadarśane 'pi kadācidekāṃ koṭiṃ smarato na saṃśayo na viparyayaḥ, doṣāṇāmapuṣṭeḥ / ataḥ svajñānādeva tadā smṛtaṃ vivicyate, na dṛśyaviśeṣaparicchedāt / evaṃ cetkuto dṛśyamānasmaryamāṇāvivekaḥ?

[kks_140] api ca anyadeva smarataḥ pūrvarūpamekatvaṃ śaśini dvitvavibhramaḥ, na smaryamāṇāvivekajaḥ / na ca jñānendriyavṛttibhedāvivekāt, tayorapratyakṣatvātsmaryamāṇatvācca / śuktikāhitacetasaśca salilaṃ pipāsato na syādviparyayaḥ / salilābhāso vā, smaryamāṇasya svajñānavivekāt /
na ca sarvā niyogena bhrāntiḥ sādṛśyabandhanā
units.translation:
Mistaken cognition cannot arise if that distinction is present; and if it does arise, it would arise in water as well. But let the opponent explain this: is what is remembered distinguished from what is seen by the cognition’s own character, or not? Is the very nature of memory-cognition such that it appears different from what is to be known, or does it simply rest on its own form? On the first account, how could memory and perception be confused, since each is distinguished by its own cognition? On the second, there would always be error in memory, and when a general feature is seen there would be confusion with every other memory. Yet this is not so, since doubt is also observed.

One might say that error occurs with a single memory because the two are not distinguished, while when there are several memories there is doubt, not failure to distinguish from a single one. That is not correct: error is observed even when several things are remembered. And if what is remembered is distinguished from the directly perceived object by knowing a particular feature of that object, rather than by the cognition’s own character, then in the absence of such knowledge of a particular feature there should be doubt between the two memories, not the error in which one thing alone appears. But if the remembered thing is distinguished by its own cognition, and a distinction is accepted between memory and mistaken cognition, then even with multiple memories error is possible through a particular defect of the senses. It has also been shown that even when a general feature is seen, a person sometimes remembers just one of several possibilities without either doubt or error, because the defects are weak. Therefore the remembered object is distinguished at that time by its own cognition, not by determining a particular feature of what is seen. If so, how can there be confusion between what is seen and what is remembered?

Moreover, in the case of the moon, a person remembering its former appearance sees it as double; this is not caused by confusion with the remembered thing. Nor is it caused by a failure to distinguish the different operations of the cognitive senses, since those operations are not directly perceived but are themselves objects of memory. Nor would the thirsty person, whose mind is fixed on a shell, mistake water for silver; or there would be an appearance of water, since the remembered object is distinguished by its own cognition. And not every error necessarily arises from a connection with similarity.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 130
units.deva: श्वेते पीतभ्रमो दृष्टो मधुरे तिक्तविभ्रमः । किञ्चित्सादृश्यतो हि स्यान्न कश्चित्तत्र न भ्रमः
units.iast:
śvete pītabhramo dṛṣṭo madhure tiktavibhramaḥ /
kiñcitsādṛśyato hi syānna kaścittatra na bhramaḥ
units.translation: One sees the illusion of yellow in something white and of bitterness in something sweet. If these arose from some degree of similarity, nothing would be free from error.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 131
units.deva: तस्मादिन्द्रियदोषाणां सामर्थ्यस्य विभागतः । भ्रमेषु नियमो दोषादग्रहे न भ्रमे यमः
units.iast:
tasmādindriyadoṣāṇāṃ sāmarthyasya vibhāgataḥ /
bhrameṣu niyamo doṣādagrahe na bhrame yamaḥ
units.translation: Therefore errors occur in determinate ways because the defects in the senses differ in power. But where there is mere non-apprehension, a defect does not determine a regular error.

gloss.en: of the defects of the senses

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 132
units.deva: यदि च सदृशदर्शनात्सदृशस्मृतेर्भ्रमः, कथं श्वेते पीतभ्रमः मधुरे वा तिक्तभ्रान्तिः? आन्तरपित्तसंवेदने ऽव्यापारयतो ऽपि बहिरिन्द्रियं स्यात्, अञ्जनवच्चाक्षिगतस्य तद्गतकृष्णिमादिवच्चादृश्यत्वात् । किञ्चित्सादृश्ये सर्वप्रकारभ्रमप्रसंगः । तस्मादिन्द्रियदोषसामर्थ्यभेदान्नियता विपर्ययोत्पत्तिः । अग्रहमात्रे तु दोषव्यापारे कामिलादिदोषाद्भ्रान्तिनियमो न स्यात् । न हि सादृश्यनिमित्तः, असदृशे ऽपि भ्रान्तिदर्शनात् । विशेषस्मरणान्नापि स्मृतावपि तदग्रहः । देशकालविशेषाच्च न स्मृतं प्रविविच्यते
units.iast:
yadi ca sadṛśadarśanātsadṛśasmṛterbhramaḥ, kathaṃ śvete pītabhramaḥ madhure vā tiktabhrāntiḥ? āntarapittasaṃvedane 'vyāpārayato 'pi bahirindriyaṃ syāt, añjanavaccākṣigatasya tadgatakṛṣṇimādivaccādṛśyatvāt / kiñcitsādṛśye sarvaprakārabhramaprasaṃgaḥ / tasmādindriyadoṣasāmarthyabhedānniyatā viparyayotpattiḥ / agrahamātre tu doṣavyāpāre kāmilādidoṣādbhrāntiniyamo na syāt / na hi sādṛśyanimittaḥ, asadṛśe 'pi bhrāntidarśanāt /

viśeṣasmaraṇānnāpi smṛtāvapi tadagrahaḥ /
deśakālaviśeṣācca na smṛtaṃ pravivicyate
units.translation: If an illusion arises from seeing something similar and remembering something similar, how can a white thing be mistaken for yellow, or something sweet for bitter? The external sense would then have to operate even when one does not experience inner bile; yet bile located in the eye, like collyrium or the blackness within the eye, is invisible. If the slightest similarity were enough, every kind of error could occur. Therefore mistaken cognitions arise in determinate ways from differences in the power of defects in the senses. But if a defect acted merely by preventing apprehension, there would be no regular pattern to errors caused by conditions such as jaundice. Error is not caused by similarity, since illusions occur even when there is no similarity. Nor is it caused by recalling a particular feature, since that feature may also be remembered without error. Nor is what is remembered distinguished from what is seen merely by differences of place and time.

gloss.en: like its inner blackness and the like
every kind of error would follow
because the power of sensory defects differs
because of differences in place and time

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 133
units.deva: अनेकदेशाधिगतं विविक्तं न पुनस्ततः । स्मृतिरित्यपि विज्ञानं स्मृतेरन्यदुदाहृतम्
units.iast:
anekadeśādhigataṃ viviktaṃ na punastataḥ /
smṛtirityapi vijñānaṃ smṛteranyadudāhṛtam
units.translation: It is known in many places and is distinct; yet this cognition is not memory. Memory has been described as something different.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 134
units.deva: न च मानफलाद्भिन्नात्तत्सिद्ध्यति फलादृते । सति स्मृतिविवेके च प्रत्यभिज्ञानविभ्रमः
units.iast:
na ca mānaphalādbhinnāttatsiddhyati phalādṛte /
sati smṛtiviveke ca pratyabhijñānavibhramaḥ
units.translation: That is not established by a result distinct from the means of knowledge; without the result it cannot be established. And even when memory is distinguished, the illusion of recognition remains.

gloss.en: from the result of a means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 135
units.deva: अथानसंनिहितो व्यर्थो वेद्यः संनिधिमत्तया । अविविक्तस्मृतेरेवं विपरीतार्थता भवेत्
units.iast:
athānasaṃnihito vyartho vedyaḥ saṃnidhimattayā /
aviviktasmṛterevaṃ viparītārthatā bhavet
units.translation: Otherwise, an object not actually present would be pointless, even though it appears present. In the same way, memory not distinguished from perception would lead to a mistaken cognition.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 136
units.deva: मनसो ऽनुपघाताच्च नासंनिध्यपरिग्रहः । दोषो ह्यग्रहणे हेतुरिन्द्रियाणामुदाहृतः
units.iast:
manaso 'nupaghātācca nāsaṃnidhyaparigrahaḥ /
doṣo hyagrahaṇe heturindriyāṇāmudāhṛtaḥ
units.translation: Since the mind has not been disturbed, one cannot accept mere absence as the cause. A defect of the senses is given as the cause of non-apprehension.

gloss.en: because it has not been disturbed

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 137
units.deva: [क्क्स्_141] प्रवृत्तिनियमो न स्यादिति चात्र निवेदितम् । सर्वज्ञानानि मिथ्या च प्रसज्यन्ते ऽत्र कल्पने
units.iast:
[kks_141] pravṛttiniyamo na syāditi cātra niveditam /
sarvajñānāni mithyā ca prasajyante 'tra kalpane
units.translation: It has already been explained here that there would be no rule governing action; and on this theory, all cognitions would necessarily be false.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 138
units.deva: सर्वात्मनार्थो ज्ञानेन केनचिन्न हि गृह्यते । तथाज्ञातविवेकस्य द्विचन्द्रादिविपर्ययात्
units.iast:
sarvātmanārtho jñānena kenacinna hi gṛhyate /
tathājñātavivekasya dvicandrādiviparyayāt
units.translation: No cognition apprehends an object in every respect. In the same way, without discerning that distinction, one falls into error, as with the appearance of two moons.

gloss.en: for one who has not discerned the distinction
as in the error of seeing two moons and the like

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 139
units.deva: अनुवृत्तिमतः पश्यन् कस्य स्वात्मापनिह्नुते । अथ मतम् --- स्वज्ञानादेव स्मृतं विविच्यते । कदाचित्तु तत्र प्रत्यक्ष इव विशेषाग्रहस्ततो ऽविवेकः । सतो तु विशेषग्रहण इन्द्रियसंयुक्ते सामान्यदर्शने ऽपि नाविवेकः, तत उभयकोटिस्मरणे न संशयः, एकस्मृतौ न संशयो न विपर्ययः । एवमपि द्वयोः स्मरणे न विपर्ययः स्यात् । न च स्मृतौ विशेषग्रहणम्, विशेषस्मरणात् । अथ देशकालविशेषात्स्मर्यमाणं विविच्यते, तत्र देशकालभेदाग्रह इति । तन्न, अनन्तदेशकालभेदावगतं तद्देशावगतं च दृश्यात्स्मर्यमाणं विविक्तं गम्यते । न च देशकालभेदग्रहणात्, अनन्तस्मरणानुपपत्तेः, तद्देशावगते च देशभेदाभावात् । अथ स्मर्यमाणतया अग्रहणादविवेकः स्मर्यमाणताज्ञानाच्च विवेकः, तस्मात् ‘स्मरामिऽ; इति ज्ञानशून्यानि रजतादिज्ञानानि भ्रान्तिहेतवः । परिपूर्णैव तर्हि स्मृतिः, न तया स्वविषयस्य किञ्चिन्न गृहीतम् । स्वयमेव सा स्वविषयं दृश्याद्विविनक्तीति नास्ति दृश्यमानस्मर्यमाणयोरविवेकः । यतः स्मरामि इति ज्ञानमन्यदेव दर्शनस्मरणविवेककारि स्मृतेः । तत्रेदं विचार्यम् --- स्मृतिः स्वविषयं विविनक्ति वा न वा? यदि विविनक्ति, तदा विपर्ययाभावः । अथ न स्मृतिः स्वविषयं विविनक्ति, तदा सामान्यदर्शने चान्यस्मृतौ विपर्ययः स्यादित्युक्तम् । न ‘स्मरामिऽइति विवेकाच्चेत्, स एव स्मृतेः स्वयमविवेचकत्वेन स्यात्, कार्यगम्यस्य हि ज्ञानस्य भेदः कार्यविशेषोन्नेयः । न चेत्स्मृतेः प्रमाणकार्यात्कार्यं विविक्तं स्यात्, केन सा विविक्ता गम्येत? सत्यपि स्मृतिविवेके दृष्टः प्रत्यभिज्ञाभ्रमः ‘स एवऽ; इति न च प्रत्यक्षस्याविवेकः, एकविवेकेनोभयोर्विकारात्स्मृतादविवेकाच्च स्मृतिविभ्रमः स्यात्, न प्रत्यक्षभ्रमः । तस्मान्न ‘स्मरामिऽइति प्रमोषादविवेकः । अथासंनिहितस्य [क्क्स्_142] संनिहितात्मना प्रतीतिरविवेकः, स्मृतेर्विपरीतार्थत्वप्रसंगः । अथासंनिध्यग्रहणात्, भवतु स स्वप्नज्ञाने, नत्विन्द्रियजायां भ्रान्तौ । मनसो ऽनुपघातादुपघातहेतुत्वाच्चाग्रहणस्य । न चेत्थं प्रवृत्तिनियमः स्यादित्युक्तम् । सति च वस्तुग्रहे कस्यचिदंशस्याग्रहाद्भ्रान्तौ सर्वज्ञानभ्रमत्वम् । न हि कस्यचिज्ज्ञानस्य सर्वात्मना वस्तु विषय इति । सत्यपि च विवेकज्ञाने प्रमाणान्तराद् द्विचन्द्रदिङ्मोहाद्यनुगतिर्दृष्टेति नाग्रहणमात्रं विपर्ययः । प्रसक्तप्रतिषेधात्मा ख्यातिः प्राप्तौ प्रकल्पते
units.iast:
anuvṛttimataḥ paśyan kasya svātmāpanihnute /
atha matam --- svajñānādeva smṛtaṃ vivicyate / kadācittu tatra pratyakṣa iva viśeṣāgrahastato 'vivekaḥ / sato tu viśeṣagrahaṇa indriyasaṃyukte sāmānyadarśane 'pi nāvivekaḥ, tata ubhayakoṭismaraṇe na saṃśayaḥ, ekasmṛtau na saṃśayo na viparyayaḥ / evamapi dvayoḥ smaraṇe na viparyayaḥ syāt / na ca smṛtau viśeṣagrahaṇam, viśeṣasmaraṇāt / atha deśakālaviśeṣātsmaryamāṇaṃ vivicyate, tatra deśakālabhedāgraha iti / tanna, anantadeśakālabhedāvagataṃ taddeśāvagataṃ ca dṛśyātsmaryamāṇaṃ viviktaṃ gamyate / na ca deśakālabhedagrahaṇāt, anantasmaraṇānupapatteḥ, taddeśāvagate ca deśabhedābhāvāt / atha smaryamāṇatayā agrahaṇādavivekaḥ smaryamāṇatājñānācca vivekaḥ, tasmāt ‘smarāmi'; iti jñānaśūnyāni rajatādijñānāni bhrāntihetavaḥ / paripūrṇaiva tarhi smṛtiḥ, na tayā svaviṣayasya kiñcinna gṛhītam /

svayameva sā svaviṣayaṃ dṛśyādvivinaktīti nāsti dṛśyamānasmaryamāṇayoravivekaḥ / yataḥ smarāmi iti jñānamanyadeva darśanasmaraṇavivekakāri smṛteḥ / tatredaṃ vicāryam --- smṛtiḥ svaviṣayaṃ vivinakti vā na vā? yadi vivinakti, tadā viparyayābhāvaḥ / atha na smṛtiḥ svaviṣayaṃ vivinakti, tadā sāmānyadarśane cānyasmṛtau viparyayaḥ syādityuktam / na ‘smarāmi'iti vivekāccet, sa eva smṛteḥ svayamavivecakatvena syāt, kāryagamyasya hi jñānasya bhedaḥ kāryaviśeṣonneyaḥ / na cetsmṛteḥ pramāṇakāryātkāryaṃ viviktaṃ syāt, kena sā viviktā gamyeta? satyapi smṛtiviveke dṛṣṭaḥ pratyabhijñābhramaḥ ‘sa eva'; iti na ca pratyakṣasyāvivekaḥ, ekavivekenobhayorvikārātsmṛtādavivekācca smṛtivibhramaḥ syāt, na pratyakṣabhramaḥ / tasmānna ‘smarāmi'iti pramoṣādavivekaḥ / athāsaṃnihitasya [kks_142] saṃnihitātmanā pratītiravivekaḥ, smṛterviparītārthatvaprasaṃgaḥ / athāsaṃnidhyagrahaṇāt, bhavatu sa svapnajñāne, natvindriyajāyāṃ bhrāntau / manaso 'nupaghātādupaghātahetutvāccāgrahaṇasya / na cetthaṃ pravṛttiniyamaḥ syādityuktam / sati ca vastugrahe kasyacidaṃśasyāgrahādbhrāntau sarvajñānabhramatvam / na hi kasyacijjñānasya sarvātmanā vastu viṣaya iti / satyapi ca vivekajñāne pramāṇāntarād dvicandradiṅmohādyanugatirdṛṣṭeti nāgrahaṇamātraṃ viparyayaḥ /
prasaktapratiṣedhātmā khyātiḥ prāptau prakalpate
units.translation:
“Seeing what continues, whose own nature does one conceal?” Someone may say that memory itself distinguishes its object from what is seen. But sometimes, as though it were direct perception, a specific distinction is not grasped in memory, and confusion follows. If the particular feature of a present object is grasped through the senses, however, even a general perception does not confuse it with something remembered. If both alternatives are remembered, there is no doubt; and if only one is remembered, there is neither doubt nor error. Even when two things are remembered, there need be no error. Memory does not grasp their particular features; it is only their particular features that are remembered.

Perhaps what is remembered is distinguished from what is seen by a difference of place and time. That is not so: something remembered is understood as distinct from what is seen whether or not one apprehends the countless differences of place and time; there is no difference of place in what is understood as present here. Someone may say that confusion arises from failing to grasp that the object is remembered, while knowledge that it is remembered distinguishes it. Then cognitions of silver that occur without the thought “I remember” would be causes of error. But memory is complete: it does not fail to grasp some part of its own object. It distinguishes its object from what is seen by itself, so there is no confusion between what is seen and what is remembered.

The cognition “I remember” is itself another cognition that distinguishes memory from perception. This must be examined: does memory distinguish its own object, or not? If it does, there can be no mistaken perception. If memory does not distinguish its own object, then there should be error whenever there is a general perception and some other memory; this has already been explained. Perhaps the distinction arises from the separate cognition “I remember.” But if memory itself cannot distinguish things, the other cognition would have to do so. A cognition is known by its effect; the specific difference among cognitions is inferred from the particular effects they produce. If memory does not produce the effect of distinguishing its own object, what would establish that it is distinct from another cognition? Even when memory is distinguished, one still sees errors of recognition such as “that very same thing.” And the error is not in perception: if one cognition establishes the distinction, the error would arise from a modification of both cognitions together, because of memory and a failure to distinguish memory, not from perception alone. Therefore confusion does not arise simply from the failure of the cognition “I remember.”

Perhaps the error is that something not present is perceived as though it were present. That would mean memory has the wrong object. Perhaps it is instead a failure to recognize that the object is absent. That may be so in a dream, but not in a sensory illusion, where the senses are functioning and the mind is not impaired. The rule governing activity would otherwise fail; it has already been explained. Further, if an object is really perceived but some aspect of it is not grasped, then every cognition would be false, since no cognition presents an object in every respect. Even when one has a distinguishing cognition from another means of knowledge, a perception of two moons or confusion about the directions may persist. Thus error cannot consist merely in non-apprehension.

A false cognition whose form is the negation of something anticipated arises when that thing is encountered...

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 140
units.deva: नाग्रहः प्रापको ऽभावः प्रापिका विपरीतधीः । ये च ख्याती तु रजतश्चक्षुःसंयुक्तवस्तुनोः
units.iast:
nāgrahaḥ prāpako 'bhāvaḥ prāpikā viparītadhīḥ /
ye ca khyātī tu rajataścakṣuḥsaṃyuktavastunoḥ
units.translation: Non-apprehension does not bring the object to the mind; a mistaken cognition of the opposite does. These two appearances—the silver and the object in contact with the eye—…

gloss.en: a mistaken cognition of the opposite
and of an object in contact with the eye

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 141
units.deva: नायं तदुपनीतार्थप्रतिषेधो ऽवगम्यते । न चाग्रहणमेवैषा प्रतीतिरपबाधते
units.iast:
nāyaṃ tadupanītārthapratiṣedho 'vagamyate /
na cāgrahaṇamevaiṣā pratītirapabādhate
units.translation: This is not understood as a negation of the meaning presented by the words. Nor does mere non-apprehension invalidate this cognition.

gloss.en: a negation of the meaning presented by that

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 142
units.deva: सर्वा ह्यग्रहबाधेन जन्म न स्यात्तथेदृशी । विवेकविज्ञानमिदं न प्रसक्तनिषेधधीः
units.iast:
sarvā hyagrahabādhena janma na syāttathedṛśī /
vivekavijñānamidaṃ na prasaktaniṣedhadhīḥ
units.translation: Then every cognition would arise in this way, through the removal of non-apprehension. This knowledge of distinction is not a cognition of negation that was already present.

gloss.en: a cognition negating something already present

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 143
units.deva: इति ब्रुवाणो वैयात्यात्स्वां प्रतीतिमपह्नुते । न क्रमे यौगपद्ये वा विवेकमतिरीदृशी
units.iast:
iti bruvāṇo vaiyātyātsvāṃ pratītimapahnute /
na krame yaugapadye vā vivekamatirīdṛśī
units.translation: A person who speaks this way denies their own experience out of prejudice. Such discernment does not occur either successively or all at once.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 144
units.deva: प्राप्ते स्यादैक्यसंवित्तौ न भेदस्यानिरूपणे । रजतस्य स्मरंश्चक्षुःसंयुक्तस्य च वस्तुनः
units.iast:
prāpte syādaikyasaṃvittau na bhedasyānirūpaṇe /
rajatasya smaraṃścakṣuḥsaṃyuktasya ca vastunaḥ
units.translation: If unity is apprehended, difference would remain undetermined, even though silver is remembered and the object is in contact with the eye…

gloss.en: of what is in contact with the eye

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 145
units.deva: सामान्यदृष्ट्या रजतादबुद्ध्वा च विविक्तताम् । पश्चाद्विविञ्चन् प्रत्येति नैवं सामान्यदर्शने
units.iast:
sāmānyadṛṣṭyā rajatādabuddhvā ca viviktatām /
paścādviviñcan pratyeti naivaṃ sāmānyadarśane
units.translation: After seeing a general feature without discerning that it differs from silver, one may later discern the difference and know the thing. But this does not happen merely from seeing a general feature.

gloss.en: through perception of a common feature
in perception of a common feature

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 146
units.deva: कोटिद्वयस्मृत्यभावे संशयो न नियोगतः । विवेकग्रहणाभावात्कालसंनिधिसंविदः
units.iast:
koṭidvayasmṛtyabhāve saṃśayo na niyogataḥ /
vivekagrahaṇābhāvātkālasaṃnidhisaṃvidaḥ
units.translation: Doubt does not invariably arise because two possible things are remembered. It can arise because the cognition fails to distinguish them through awareness of their time and place.

gloss.en: when there is no memory of both alternatives
because of failure to apprehend the distinction
from cognition of time and proximity

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 147
units.deva: तद्वदाभासनात्प्राप्ताविष्टः स्यादन्यथाग्रहः । तत्राग्रहो निमित्तं स्यादथवा संनिधिग्रहः
units.iast:
tadvadābhāsanātprāptāviṣṭaḥ syādanyathāgrahaḥ /
tatrāgraho nimittaṃ syādathavā saṃnidhigrahaḥ
units.translation: If the desired object is attained because it appears in that form, then if it is apprehended otherwise, there is error. In that case, either non-apprehension is the cause, or apprehension of presence is.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 148
units.deva: भेदग्रहापवादेन रहितो भावरूपतः । विपर्ययानभ्युपाये भ्रमो ऽग्रहनिबन्धनः
units.iast:
bhedagrahāpavādena rahito bhāvarūpataḥ /
viparyayānabhyupāye bhramo 'grahanibandhanaḥ
units.translation: When apprehension of difference is absent, and there is no rejection of the real object, error may be based on non-apprehension.

gloss.en: with the apprehension of difference set aside
when mistaken cognition is not admitted

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 149
units.deva: [क्क्स्_143] शब्दैकगम्य उक्तः स्यादग्रहो ऽग्रहबन्धनः । ‘नेदं रजतम्ऽइति प्रसक्तप्रतिषेधरूपा प्रतीतिर्नाग्रहणे ऽवकल्पते, प्रसङ्गाभावात् । न खल्वग्रहणं कस्यचित्प्रसञ्जकम् । अभावो हि सः । विपरीता तु ख्यातिः संनिहितस्य रजततामभूतां रजतस्य वा संनिहिततामादर्शयन्ती प्रसञ्जयति । ननु च रजतनयनघटितवस्तुनोः ख्याती स्तः । ते एव प्रसञ्जिके । सत्यम् । न तु तदुपनीतयोरियं निषेधावगतिः । न हि ‘नेदं रजतम्ऽइति रजतमात्रं चक्षुःसंयुक्तवस्तुमात्रं वा निरस्यमानमवस्यामः । किं तु चक्षुःसंयुक्तस्य तु रजततां रजतस्य वा चक्षुसंयुक्ताम् । न चैतयोरग्रहणं प्रापकम्, अग्रहणत्वादेव । तस्मादवश्यं प्रतिषेध्यप्राप्तये विपरीतख्यातिरुपासनीया । न च ‘नेदम्ऽइत्यग्रहणमेव वार्यते, सर्वज्ञानेषु ताद्रूप्यप्रसंगात् । सर्वज्ञानानामग्रहबाधेनोत्पत्तौ च विवेकज्ञानमात्रमिदं न प्रसक्तप्रतिषेधरूपमिति प्रतीत्यनुसारिणो ऽनुरूपम् । न हि रजतशुक्तिकाशकलयोर्युगपद्विविक्तयोर्ग्रहणे ईदृशी प्रतीतिर्न क्रमेण । अविविक्तयोर्ग्रहण ईदृशी स्यादिति चेत् । युक्ता, विविक्तयोर्ग्रहणे ऽविवेकप्रतिषेधरूपत्वात् । विविक्तयोर्ग्रहणे प्राप्त्यभावयुक्ता । अपि च भवति कदाचित् --- यः स्मरति च रजतस्य, चक्षुःसंयुक्तस्य वस्तुनः सामान्यमात्रदर्शी, न रजताद्विवेकं गृह्णाति, पुनश्चक्षुःप्रसादात्प्रत्येति । न च तदा तथा प्रतीतिरविवेकग्रहणाभावात् । ननु सामान्यदर्शने न चेद्विपर्ययः, संशयः स्यात् । तदपनोदि च निर्णयज्ञानमीदृशमेव । नैतत्सारम् । न ह्यसति कोटिद्वयस्मरणे सामान्यदर्शने ऽपि संशयः, न च विपर्ययः । भवति हि पुरो ऽवस्थिते भास्वररूपमात्रप्रतीतिः, रजते च स्मृतिः । न च तयोरन्यत्वं प्रतिपद्यते, नैकत्वं च । तत्र न विवेकज्ञानमेवंरूपम्, एकत्वाप्रतिपत्तेः । अथ मतम् --- विवेकाग्रहणात्कालसंनिधिप्रतीतेश्च रजतं वा चक्षुःसंप्रयुक्तवदवभासते, चक्षुःसंयुक्तं वा रजतवत् । अतः प्राप्तिरिति प्रतिषेधोपपत्तिः । अभ्युपेता तर्हि विपरीतख्यातिः । न ह्यन्या सा, अतदात्मनस्तथावभासनात् । कामं [क्क्स्_144] तत्त्वाज्ञाननिमित्ता स्यात् । न हि सा तत्त्वज्ञाने सत्युदेति, विरोधादिति । तत्रापि संनिधिख्यातिरेव निबन्धनम् । तस्यास्तु विवेकग्रहो ऽपवादः । अग्रहणे निरपवादा सैव कारणम्, नाभावः । विपरीतख्यात्यनभ्युगमे चाग्रहणनिबन्धनो भ्रम इत्यग्रहणमग्रहणनिबन्धनमिति सुव्याहृतम् । स्वप्ने च द्वितीयाभावात्कुतो ऽविवेकः, स्मृतत्वेनाविविक्तस्य तथा विवेके धर्मिणि प्रतिपन्ने धर्मान्तरप्रतिपन्ने धर्मान्तरप्रतिपत्तेर्बाधकत्वं पूर्वस्याश्च भ्रान्तित्वं स्यातामिति । यः प्रतीतिविरोधस्तु स स्वदोष उदाहृतः
units.iast:
[kks_143] śabdaikagamya uktaḥ syādagraho 'grahabandhanaḥ /
‘nedaṃ rajatam'iti prasaktapratiṣedharūpā pratītirnāgrahaṇe 'vakalpate, prasaṅgābhāvāt / na khalvagrahaṇaṃ kasyacitprasañjakam / abhāvo hi saḥ / viparītā tu khyātiḥ saṃnihitasya rajatatāmabhūtāṃ rajatasya vā saṃnihitatāmādarśayantī prasañjayati / nanu ca rajatanayanaghaṭitavastunoḥ khyātī staḥ / te eva prasañjike / satyam / na tu tadupanītayoriyaṃ niṣedhāvagatiḥ / na hi ‘nedaṃ rajatam'iti rajatamātraṃ cakṣuḥsaṃyuktavastumātraṃ vā nirasyamānamavasyāmaḥ / kiṃ tu cakṣuḥsaṃyuktasya tu rajatatāṃ rajatasya vā cakṣusaṃyuktām / na caitayoragrahaṇaṃ prāpakam, agrahaṇatvādeva / tasmādavaśyaṃ pratiṣedhyaprāptaye viparītakhyātirupāsanīyā / na ca ‘nedam'ityagrahaṇameva vāryate, sarvajñāneṣu tādrūpyaprasaṃgāt / sarvajñānānāmagrahabādhenotpattau ca vivekajñānamātramidaṃ na prasaktapratiṣedharūpamiti pratītyanusāriṇo 'nurūpam / na hi rajataśuktikāśakalayoryugapadviviktayorgrahaṇe īdṛśī pratītirna krameṇa / aviviktayorgrahaṇa īdṛśī syāditi cet / yuktā, viviktayorgrahaṇe 'vivekapratiṣedharūpatvāt / viviktayorgrahaṇe prāptyabhāvayuktā / api ca bhavati kadācit --- yaḥ smarati ca rajatasya, cakṣuḥsaṃyuktasya vastunaḥ sāmānyamātradarśī, na rajatādvivekaṃ gṛhṇāti, punaścakṣuḥprasādātpratyeti / na ca tadā tathā pratītiravivekagrahaṇābhāvāt / nanu sāmānyadarśane na cedviparyayaḥ, saṃśayaḥ syāt / tadapanodi ca nirṇayajñānamīdṛśameva / naitatsāram / na hyasati koṭidvayasmaraṇe sāmānyadarśane 'pi saṃśayaḥ, na ca viparyayaḥ / bhavati hi puro 'vasthite bhāsvararūpamātrapratītiḥ, rajate ca smṛtiḥ / na ca tayoranyatvaṃ pratipadyate, naikatvaṃ ca / tatra na vivekajñānamevaṃrūpam, ekatvāpratipatteḥ / atha matam --- vivekāgrahaṇātkālasaṃnidhipratīteśca rajataṃ vā cakṣuḥsaṃprayuktavadavabhāsate, cakṣuḥsaṃyuktaṃ vā rajatavat / ataḥ prāptiriti pratiṣedhopapattiḥ / abhyupetā tarhi viparītakhyātiḥ / na hyanyā sā, atadātmanastathāvabhāsanāt / kāmaṃ [kks_144] tattvājñānanimittā syāt / na hi sā tattvajñāne satyudeti, virodhāditi / tatrāpi saṃnidhikhyātireva nibandhanam / tasyāstu vivekagraho 'pavādaḥ / agrahaṇe nirapavādā saiva kāraṇam, nābhāvaḥ / viparītakhyātyanabhyugame cāgrahaṇanibandhano bhrama ityagrahaṇamagrahaṇanibandhanamiti suvyāhṛtam / svapne ca dvitīyābhāvātkuto 'vivekaḥ, smṛtatvenāviviktasya tathā viveke dharmiṇi pratipanne dharmāntarapratipanne dharmāntarapratipatterbādhakatvaṃ pūrvasyāśca bhrāntitvaṃ syātāmiti /
yaḥ pratītivirodhastu sa svadoṣa udāhṛtaḥ
units.translation:
The verse says:

“If non-apprehension were bound by non-apprehension,
it would have to be understood through words alone.”

The cognition “This is not silver” has the form of denying an error that has just been suggested. It cannot arise from mere non-apprehension, because nothing would have suggested the error in the first place. Non-apprehension does not make anything appear; it is an absence. A mistaken appearance, by contrast, makes something nearby appear as silver when it is not, or makes silver appear to be nearby, and thereby suggests an error.

One may object that there are two appearances: the appearance of silver and the appearance of an object in visual contact. Those are precisely what suggest the error. That is true, but the cognition of negation does not deny either of those things by itself. When one says, “This is not silver,” one does not deny only silver, nor only the object connected with sight. One denies that the object connected with sight is silver, or that the silver is the object connected with sight. Mere non-apprehension of either of those objects cannot suggest that relation, since non-apprehension is only non-apprehension. Therefore, a mistaken appearance must be accepted to account for the error that is denied.

Nor is the cognition “This is not silver” simply the removal of non-apprehension, since that would apply to every cognition. If all cognitions arose by removing non-apprehension, this one would be only a cognition of difference, not the distinctive cognition that denies an anticipated error. The form of cognition should be understood in accordance with how it appears. When the shell and silver are clearly distinguished, whether grasped at once or in sequence, this kind of cognition does not arise. Someone may say it would arise if they were not clearly distinguished. That is reasonable: when they are not distinguished, the cognition has the form of denying that confusion. When they are distinguished, there is no confusion to be denied.

Sometimes someone remembers silver and sees only the general quality of brightness in an object connected with sight, without grasping its difference from silver; later, through clearer vision, the person recognizes it. At that point the cognition does not have this form, because there is no grasp of non-difference. Someone may object that if the general perception is not mistaken, it should instead be doubtful; a decisive cognition that removes that doubt would then be just such a denial. This is not sound. Without recollection of both alternatives, there is no doubt even when one sees only a general quality. A bright form is perceived in front, and silver is remembered, but the person does not understand either that they are different or that they are the same. This is neither a cognition of difference nor a mistaken cognition of identity.

Someone may say that failure to grasp the distinction, together with the appearance of proximity, makes the silver appear to be the object in visual contact, or makes the object in visual contact appear to be silver. Then there is an appearance of identity and something to deny, so the negation is explained. But that accepts a mistaken cognition: something that is not one thing appears as that thing. Let it be caused by ignorance of reality, if one wishes; it does not arise when reality is correctly known, since the two oppose one another. Here too the appearance of proximity is the basis of error; the grasp of difference removes it. If one does not accept mistaken cognition, then the error must be based on non-apprehension; yet that would make non-apprehension itself the cause of non-apprehension, which is a contradiction.

And how could there be non-discrimination in a dream when there is no second thing? If one recognizes an attribute of an actual person and then an incompatible attribute, the later recognition of the different attribute sublates the earlier one; the earlier cognition is then shown to have been false. The conflict with perception that was mentioned is therefore due to the defect already explained.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 150
units.deva: सामानाधिकरण्येन बोधाद्रूप्यमिदं मितम् । ऽइदं शुक्लं रजतम्ऽइति सामानाधिकरण्येन प्रतीतेरात्मोपालम्भः परस्मिन्नासज्यते प्रतीतिविरोधः, ज्ञानभेदकल्पनायाः प्रमाणाभावात् । अनाश्वासो ज्ञायमाने ज्ञानेनैवापबाध्यते
units.iast:
sāmānādhikaraṇyena bodhādrūpyamidaṃ mitam /
'idaṃ śuklaṃ rajatam'iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena pratīterātmopālambhaḥ parasminnāsajyate pratītivirodhaḥ, jñānabhedakalpanāyāḥ pramāṇābhāvāt /
anāśvāso jñāyamāne jñānenaivāpabādhyate
units.translation: This cognition of a shared property is established through words in the same grammatical case. When one perceives “This is white silver,” applying the same grammatical case gives rise to the appearance of one thing; to impose the Self’s apprehension upon something else contradicts experience, since there is no means of knowledge for imagining two distinct cognitions. Uncertainty in what is being known is removed by cognition itself.

gloss.en: through being in the same grammatical case

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 151
units.deva: व्यभिचारादसामर्थ्यं न तत्कार्यस्य लाभतः । व्यभिचारात्प्रमेयत्वे कार्यमेव न लभ्यते
units.iast:
vyabhicārādasāmarthyaṃ na tatkāryasya lābhataḥ /
vyabhicārātprameyatve kāryameva na labhyate
units.translation: A cause’s failure is not established merely from irregularity, since its effect may still be obtained. But if the object’s knowability were irregular, the effect itself would not be obtained.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 152
units.deva: यो हि ज्ञायमाने ऽर्थे ऽन्यथापि स्यादित्यनाश्वासस्तस्य तेनैव ज्ञानेन तथात्वपरिच्छेदिनोत्पत्तिर्निरुध्यते । तथा हि --- अनाश्वासनिवृत्तये तद्विधं ज्ञानमेवापेक्ष्यते । तच्चास्त्येव । न च व्यभिचारदोषादसमर्थप्रमाणं ज्ञानमिति युज्यते, प्रमाणकार्यस्य परिच्छेदस्य ज्ञानरूपादेव सिद्धत्वात् । परिच्छेदतो हि प्रामाण्यम् । अतन्त्रता तु व्यभिचाराव्यभिचारयोः, असति तस्मिन् धूमादेरव्यभिचारस्याप्यप्रमाणत्वात्, व्यभिचारवतो ऽपि च सितासितादिषु चक्षुषः सति तस्मिन् प्रामाण्यात् । न च व्यभिचारो बाधहेतुर्दोषवत् प्रामाण्योपघाती क्वचिद् दृष्टः, चक्षुरादौ व्यभिचारवति प्रमाणत्वात् । ननु दृष्टो व्यभिचारः प्रामाण्योपघाती प्रमेयत्वोर्ध्वत्वादौ । नैतत्सारम् । न [क्क्स्_145] तत्र व्यभिचारादप्रामाण्यम्, अपि तु परिच्छेदकार्याभावात् । तदभावश्च हेत्वभावात् । अव्यभिचाराद्धि लिङ्गाल्लिङ्गिपरिच्छेदः । यत्र त्वव्यभिचारो न कारणं तत्र व्यभिचारे ऽपि सति परिच्छेदे प्रामाण्यमविवादम् । अक्षेषु तद्वदेव च ज्ञानं परिच्छेदनिमित्तम्, न लिङ्गवत् । न च संशयोत्पत्त्या व्यभिचारः प्रामाण्यमुपहन्ति, सम्यक्परिच्छिन्ने द्वैविद्ध्यस्यासंशयहेतुत्वात् । न निश्चिते स्थाणावूर्ध्वत्वेन संशेरते । उत्पत्त्यैव ज्ञानमर्थमवधारयति । अनवधारकं तु नैवेहाधिकृतम् । एवं चावधारणादेवानवधारणमिति विप्रतिषिद्धम् । य एव त्वव्यभिचारमर्थयते ज्ञानस्याश्वासार्थं तस्यैवानाश्वासः, अव्यभिचारज्ञाने ऽप्यनाश्वासात् । न हि तदसिद्धव्यभिचारमात्मनि ज्ञानान्तरेषु चाश्वासकारणम् । ज्ञानान्तरात्सिद्धावनवस्था । अपि च ज्ञानरूपाच्चेन्नार्थाश्वासः, तस्यासिद्धौ केन सहाव्यभिचारो ज्ञानस्य गृह्येत? किं च ज्ञानरूपादेवाव्यभिचारो ऽपि कथ्यते, विपरीतख्यातौ तद्विरोधात् । तथा सति तदेव विषयस्य साधकम्, व्यर्थो ऽव्यभिचारः । न च व्यभिचारः प्रामाण्यमुपहन्तीत्युक्तम् । अपि चाग्रहणे ऽभीष्टं यद्विवेकनिबन्धनम् । न पराणुद्यते दण्डैस्तद्विपर्ययदर्शने
units.iast:
yo hi jñāyamāne 'rthe 'nyathāpi syādityanāśvāsastasya tenaiva jñānena tathātvaparicchedinotpattirnirudhyate / tathā hi --- anāśvāsanivṛttaye tadvidhaṃ jñānamevāpekṣyate / taccāstyeva / na ca vyabhicāradoṣādasamarthapramāṇaṃ jñānamiti yujyate, pramāṇakāryasya paricchedasya jñānarūpādeva siddhatvāt / paricchedato hi prāmāṇyam / atantratā tu vyabhicārāvyabhicārayoḥ, asati tasmin dhūmāderavyabhicārasyāpyapramāṇatvāt, vyabhicāravato 'pi ca sitāsitādiṣu cakṣuṣaḥ sati tasmin prāmāṇyāt / na ca vyabhicāro bādhaheturdoṣavat prāmāṇyopaghātī kvacid dṛṣṭaḥ, cakṣurādau vyabhicāravati pramāṇatvāt / nanu dṛṣṭo vyabhicāraḥ prāmāṇyopaghātī prameyatvordhvatvādau / naitatsāram / na [kks_145] tatra vyabhicārādaprāmāṇyam, api tu paricchedakāryābhāvāt / tadabhāvaśca hetvabhāvāt / avyabhicārāddhi liṅgālliṅgiparicchedaḥ / yatra tvavyabhicāro na kāraṇaṃ tatra vyabhicāre 'pi sati paricchede prāmāṇyamavivādam / akṣeṣu tadvadeva ca jñānaṃ paricchedanimittam, na liṅgavat / na ca saṃśayotpattyā vyabhicāraḥ prāmāṇyamupahanti, samyakparicchinne dvaividdhyasyāsaṃśayahetutvāt / na niścite sthāṇāvūrdhvatvena saṃśerate / utpattyaiva jñānamarthamavadhārayati / anavadhārakaṃ tu naivehādhikṛtam / evaṃ cāvadhāraṇādevānavadhāraṇamiti vipratiṣiddham / ya eva tvavyabhicāramarthayate jñānasyāśvāsārthaṃ tasyaivānāśvāsaḥ, avyabhicārajñāne 'pyanāśvāsāt / na hi tadasiddhavyabhicāramātmani jñānāntareṣu cāśvāsakāraṇam / jñānāntarātsiddhāvanavasthā / api ca jñānarūpāccennārthāśvāsaḥ, tasyāsiddhau kena sahāvyabhicāro jñānasya gṛhyeta? kiṃ ca jñānarūpādevāvyabhicāro 'pi kathyate, viparītakhyātau tadvirodhāt / tathā sati tadeva viṣayasya sādhakam, vyartho 'vyabhicāraḥ / na ca vyabhicāraḥ prāmāṇyamupahantītyuktam /

api cāgrahaṇe 'bhīṣṭaṃ yadvivekanibandhanam /
na parāṇudyate daṇḍaistadviparyayadarśane
units.translation:
Someone who fears that something known may turn out otherwise has that lack of confidence removed when a cognition arises that determines it to be just so. A cognition of this kind is indeed required to remove uncertainty. It is not reasonable to say that cognition is incapable of establishing what is real because of the defect of deviation: the means of knowledge produces the result of determining the object, and that determination itself arises from the form of cognition. Authority consists in this determination. Whether cognition does or does not deviate is not decisive: without determination, even smoke, though it never deviates, would not be a means of knowledge; with determination, the eye is a means of knowledge despite deviations in some cases, such as in distinguishing white from dark. No one has seen deviation itself as a defect that destroys authority, as one sees other defects, since the eye is authoritative about other objects even when it sometimes deviates.

Someone may object that deviation is observed to destroy authority in cases such as cognition of what is knowable, tall, and the like. That is not sound. Authority fails there not because of deviation but because the cognition does not determine its object; and the failure to determine comes from the absence of its cause. An inference determines the signified object because the sign does not deviate. Where non-deviation is not itself the cause of determination, the presence of deviation does not destroy authority once determination has occurred. Cognition through the senses is a cause of determination in that way; it is not like inference, where a sign is the basis.

Nor does the arising of doubt destroy the authority of cognition: when the object has been properly determined, the possibility of two forms is itself a cause for there being no doubt. Cognition determines its object at the moment it arises; a cognition that does not determine is not at issue here. Thus a person who demands an infallible cognition in order to have confidence in knowledge has no means of gaining confidence: even cognition that it does not deviate could itself be doubted. It is not the case that one establishes non-deviation through another cognition, since that would lead to endless regress. If the cognition’s own determination is not enough, what establishes that it does not deviate? If its form alone is enough, then non-deviation is unnecessary. And if non-deviation is an object of cognition, it would itself need to be established.

What is sought in the absence of something is a distinction based on what is absent; that distinction cannot simply be removed by force when the contrary appearance arises...

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 153
units.deva: नोद्रेकहेतवो दोषाः कार्यसामर्थ्यघातिनः । ग्रहाग्रहविभागः स्यादतस्तत्सदसत्त्वतः
units.iast:
nodrekahetavo doṣāḥ kāryasāmarthyaghātinaḥ /
grahāgrahavibhāgaḥ syādatastatsadasattvataḥ
units.translation: Defects do not intensify when they destroy the power of an effect. Therefore the distinction between apprehension and non-apprehension depends on whether the object is existent or nonexistent.

gloss.en: the distinction between apprehension and non-apprehension
on the basis of that object's existence or nonexistence

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 154
units.deva: विपर्यये हि नितरामुपघातः प्रकल्पते । इष्टकार्योपरोधेन विपरीतोदयेन च
units.iast:
viparyaye hi nitarāmupaghātaḥ prakalpate /
iṣṭakāryoparodhena viparītodayena ca
units.translation: In mistaken cognition, the disturbance is especially pronounced: it obstructs the desired result and brings about the opposite.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 155
units.deva: तस्मात्तत्सदसत्त्वाभ्यां विवेको ऽत्रापि कल्पते । दोषे ऽसत्यग्रहाशङ्का कथं च विनिवर्तते
units.iast:
tasmāttatsadasattvābhyāṃ viveko 'trāpi kalpate /
doṣe 'satyagrahāśaṅkā kathaṃ ca vinivartate
units.translation: Therefore, even here, difference is imagined on the basis of that thing’s being existent or nonexistent. If there is no defect, how could the suspicion of non-apprehension be removed?

gloss.en: by that object's existence or nonexistence

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 156
units.deva: [क्क्स्_146] न हि कारणसद्भावे कार्यसत्ता नियोगतः । प्रत्यक्षं कार्यमेवं च हेतुनानुमितं भवेत्
units.iast:
[kks_146] na hi kāraṇasadbhāve kāryasattā niyogataḥ /
pratyakṣaṃ kāryamevaṃ ca hetunānumitaṃ bhavet
units.translation: The effect does not necessarily exist whenever its cause exists. Thus the effect may be directly known, while the cause is inferred from it.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 157
units.deva: विपर्यये फलाभावो हेत्वभावात्तु युज्यते । विवेकोपायश्च दोषाभावभावौ ग्रहणाग्रहणयोर्न दण्डवारितौ । विपर्यये विपर्ययहेतवो ऽभ्युपघातकाः, सुतरामिष्टकार्योपरोधाद्विपरीतोदयाच्च । न चादुष्टेष्वपीन्द्रियादिषु अग्रहाशङ्कानिवृत्तिः, यतो हेतुभावे ऽपि न नियोगतः कार्यम्, विपर्ययश्च स्यात् । प्रत्यक्षासंवित्तिर्हेतुनानुमीयेत । फलात्तु हेतोर्हेतुभावानुमानम् । दोषाभावात्तु विपर्ययकार्यासत्त्वं युक्तानुमानम्, हेत्वभावे कार्यानुत्पादात् । अनालम्बनतापत्तिर्यथाकारान्तरार्पणम्
units.iast:
viparyaye phalābhāvo hetvabhāvāttu yujyate /
vivekopāyaśca doṣābhāvabhāvau grahaṇāgrahaṇayorna daṇḍavāritau / viparyaye viparyayahetavo 'bhyupaghātakāḥ, sutarāmiṣṭakāryoparodhādviparītodayācca / na cāduṣṭeṣvapīndriyādiṣu agrahāśaṅkānivṛttiḥ, yato hetubhāve 'pi na niyogataḥ kāryam, viparyayaśca syāt / pratyakṣāsaṃvittirhetunānumīyeta / phalāttu hetorhetubhāvānumānam / doṣābhāvāttu viparyayakāryāsattvaṃ yuktānumānam, hetvabhāve kāryānutpādāt /
anālambanatāpattiryathākārāntarārpaṇam
units.translation: In the case of error, the absence of a result is reasonable because the cause is absent. The means of discernment is the presence or absence of defects, which is not prevented either in apprehension or in non-apprehension. In mistaken cognition, the causes of error are disruptive; all the more so when they obstruct the desired result and produce the opposite. But even when the senses and other faculties are not defective, one cannot rule out a failure to apprehend, since the presence of a cause does not invariably produce its effect, and error may still occur. The absence of direct perception may be inferred from its cause; the presence of a cause is inferred from its effect. From the absence of defects, it is reasonable to infer the absence of error, since without a cause the effect does not arise. The consequence is that cognition would have no object, just as when one presents it in the form of another object…

gloss.en: because they obstruct the desired result
even when there is no defect
in the senses and the like
removal of the possibility of non-apprehension
the inference of its causal role
absence of the result of error
because the effect does not arise
as when another form is imposed

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 158
units.deva: स्वरूपानर्पणादेवं भवेदग्रहणे ऽपि ते । कस्यचित्त्वर्पणं तुल्यमथ तत्र न तत्तथा
units.iast:
svarūpānarpaṇādevaṃ bhavedagrahaṇe 'pi te /
kasyacittvarpaṇaṃ tulyamatha tatra na tattathā
units.translation: In this way there would be non-apprehension because the object does not present itself. But if something does present itself to someone, that case is not the same.

gloss.en: because it does not present its own nature

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 159
units.deva: परस्यापि हि तत्रैवमथ तत्र तथा स्थितेः । सर्वत्र स्यात्तथाभावः स्यादेवं ग्रहणे ऽपि ते
units.iast:
parasyāpi hi tatraivamatha tatra tathā sthiteḥ /
sarvatra syāttathābhāvaḥ syādevaṃ grahaṇe 'pi te
units.translation: If this also holds for the other person, and the thing is situated in that way, then the same state would occur everywhere; thus it would occur even in apprehension.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 160
units.deva: यथा तत्रानिमित्तत्वात्सम्यज्ञाने ऽनिमित्तता । शङ्क्यते ग्रहणे ऽप्येवमग्रहे सा निरूपिता
units.iast:
yathā tatrānimittatvātsamyajñāne 'nimittatā /
śaṅkyate grahaṇe 'pyevamagrahe sā nirūpitā
units.translation: Just as, in that case, the lack of a cause in correct cognition is suspect, so too, in apprehension, the lack of a cause has been shown.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 161
units.deva:
ज्ञानादेव निमित्तत्वमन्येषां न विशिष्यते । आलम्बनत्वहानं च यथाकारान्तरावभासे चक्षुःसंयुक्तस्य तथाग्रहणे ऽपि, स्वरूपानर्पणस्य तुल्यत्वात् । अथ कस्यचित्सामान्यरूपस्य स्वाकारत्वात् --- अथ कानिचिच्चक्षुःसंयुक्तानि वस्तूनि स्वेन रूपेण गृह्यन्त इति कस्यचिदग्रहणे ऽपि नानालम्बनत्वम् --- तुल्यम् । आकारान्तरावभासे ऽपि केषाञ्चित् [क्क्स्_147] स्वाकाराणामवभासनात् । अथाग्रहणे नैव चक्षुःसंयुक्तस्यालम्बनत्वमिष्यते, परो ऽपि नैव विपर्यय इच्छति । एवं ह्युक्तम् ---

ऽतस्माद्यदन्यथा सन्तमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते । तन्निरालम्बनं ज्ञानमभावालम्बनं च तत्ऽ; ॥ अथ विपर्यये चक्षुःसंयुक्तस्यालम्बनत्वादन्यत्राप्यनालम्बनताशङ्का, अग्रहणे ऽपि तुल्या । यथा खलु विपर्ययज्ञाने चक्षुःसंप्रयुक्तवस्तुस्वभावनिरपेक्षता दृष्टा सम्यग्ज्ञाने ऽपि शङ्क्यते ज्ञानत्वसामान्यात्तथा चक्षुःसंप्रयुक्तमपि वस्तु नाविकलरूपं गृह्यते, तेनानालम्बनं भवति, सदृशस्मृतिहेतुतां च प्रतिपद्यते --- इत्यग्रहणे दृष्टानालम्बनता ग्रहणेष्वपि कस्मान्न शङ्क्यते? दोषाभावादिति चेत्, विपर्यये ऽपि तुल्यम्, न चान्यथालम्बने निरालम्बनत्वम् । चक्षुस्त्वन्यथापि नालम्ब्यते । आलम्बनार्थश्च रजतव्यवहारयोग्यता शुक्तेः, तथा हि रजतार्थी तामादत्ते । घटस्यापि हि नैवान्यत्स्वज्ञानालम्बनत्वमन्यत्र व्यवहारयोग्यतायाः, यतो न विषयाकारं ज्ञानम् । तत्र शुक्तिः स्वरूपेण नालम्बिता रजतज्ञानेन, तन्निबन्धनव्यवहारभावात् । रजतरूपेण तु तन्निबन्धनस्योपादानव्यवहारस्य तत्र भावादिति । क्रियानिष्ठे ऽपि विधौ वस्तुस्वरूपसिद्धये कश्चिदाह ---
अवघातप्रोक्षणादेर्यथा द्रव्यार्थता स्थिता
units.iast:
jñānādeva nimittatvamanyeṣāṃ na viśiṣyate /
ālambanatvahānaṃ ca yathākārāntarāvabhāse cakṣuḥsaṃyuktasya tathāgrahaṇe 'pi, svarūpānarpaṇasya tulyatvāt / atha kasyacitsāmānyarūpasya svākāratvāt --- atha kāniciccakṣuḥsaṃyuktāni vastūni svena rūpeṇa gṛhyanta iti kasyacidagrahaṇe 'pi nānālambanatvam --- tulyam / ākārāntarāvabhāse 'pi keṣāñcit [kks_147] svākārāṇāmavabhāsanāt / athāgrahaṇe naiva cakṣuḥsaṃyuktasyālambanatvamiṣyate, paro 'pi naiva viparyaya icchati / evaṃ hyuktam ---

'tasmādyadanyathā santamanyathā pratipadyate /
tannirālambanaṃ jñānamabhāvālambanaṃ ca tat'; //

atha viparyaye cakṣuḥsaṃyuktasyālambanatvādanyatrāpyanālambanatāśaṅkā, agrahaṇe 'pi tulyā / yathā khalu viparyayajñāne cakṣuḥsaṃprayuktavastusvabhāvanirapekṣatā dṛṣṭā samyagjñāne 'pi śaṅkyate jñānatvasāmānyāttathā cakṣuḥsaṃprayuktamapi vastu nāvikalarūpaṃ gṛhyate, tenānālambanaṃ bhavati, sadṛśasmṛtihetutāṃ ca pratipadyate --- ityagrahaṇe dṛṣṭānālambanatā grahaṇeṣvapi kasmānna śaṅkyate? doṣābhāvāditi cet, viparyaye 'pi tulyam, na cānyathālambane nirālambanatvam / cakṣustvanyathāpi nālambyate / ālambanārthaśca rajatavyavahārayogyatā śukteḥ, tathā hi rajatārthī tāmādatte / ghaṭasyāpi hi naivānyatsvajñānālambanatvamanyatra vyavahārayogyatāyāḥ, yato na viṣayākāraṃ jñānam / tatra śuktiḥ svarūpeṇa nālambitā rajatajñānena, tannibandhanavyavahārabhāvāt / rajatarūpeṇa tu tannibandhanasyopādānavyavahārasya tatra bhāvāditi /

kriyāniṣṭhe 'pi vidhau vastusvarūpasiddhaye kaścidāha ---
avaghātaprokṣaṇāderyathā dravyārthatā sthitā
units.translation:
That knowledge alone is the cause of the other cognition makes no distinction. The loss of the object’s status as an object occurs both when another form appears and when the thing is not apprehended, since in either case it does not present itself as it is. If one says that some common feature is presented in its own form—or that some objects in contact with the eye are apprehended in their own form, so that even when something else is not apprehended there is no loss of the object—the same applies in the other case: even when another form appears, some of the things’ own forms are also presented. Or one might say that, when the thing in contact with the eye is not apprehended, it is not accepted as the object at all. The other side does not accept mistaken cognition either. For it has been said:

“Therefore, the cognition that apprehends a thing that exists in one way as existing in another way has no object; it takes as its object what does not exist.”

But if, in mistaken cognition, the thing in contact with the eye is the object, then one may suspect that there is no object elsewhere too. This suspicion is equally applicable when the thing is not apprehended. Just as, in mistaken cognition, independence from the nature of the object in contact with the eye has been observed, one may suspect the same of correct cognition because both are cognition. Thus the object in contact with the eye is not apprehended in its complete form; it therefore has no role as an object and merely becomes the cause of a similar memory. If this lack of an object, seen in cases of non-apprehension, is not suspected even in cases of apprehension, why should it be? If one says that there is no defect, the same is true of mistaken cognition; and there is no lack of an object merely because it is apprehended in a different way.

Nor is the eye itself what is taken as the object. The meaning of “object” here is that the shell is fit to support the practical activity directed toward silver: indeed, a person seeking silver picks it up. A pot too has no status as the object of its cognition apart from being fit to support practical activity, since cognition does not take the form of its object. In the cognition of silver, therefore, the shell is not the object in its own nature, because the practical activity based on that cognition does not occur on that basis. But it is the object in the form of silver, because the act of picking it up, founded on that cognition, does occur there.

Even when an injunction is directed toward action, someone says that the reality of an object is established in the following way—

“Just as the objecthood of a substance is established for acts such as pounding and sprinkling…”

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 162
units.deva: ज्ञानं स्वभावाद्द्रव्यार्थं कर्मत्वाच्चात्मनस्तथा । भवत्वेवं तथापीष्टरूपसिद्धिः कुतो मता
units.iast:
jñānaṃ svabhāvāddravyārthaṃ karmatvāccātmanastathā /
bhavatvevaṃ tathāpīṣṭarūpasiddhiḥ kuto matā
units.translation: Knowledge, by its nature, is directed toward an object, and in its role as an action it is directed toward the Self. Let that be so; how then is the desired nature [of the Self] established?

gloss.en: because it functions as an action
the establishment of the desired nature

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 163
units.deva: शब्दस्तदर्थकार्यत्वे तावज्ञानस्य निष्ठितः । ज्ञानाज्ज्ञेयस्य को ऽन्यो ऽर्थः स्वरूपप्रतिभासनात्
units.iast:
śabdastadarthakāryatve tāvajñānasya niṣṭhitaḥ /
jñānājjñeyasya ko 'nyo 'rthaḥ svarūpapratibhāsanāt
units.translation: A word culminates in knowledge of its object; what further purpose could there be beyond knowledge, when the object’s own nature shines forth?

gloss.en: when its function is to convey that meaning
of what is to be known
because its own nature shines forth

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 164
units.deva: अदृष्टकल्पना युक्ता न च दृष्टस्य संभवे । [क्क्स्_148] तस्माद्यथा प्रोक्षणादिविधेर्व्रीहिषु गम्यते
units.iast:
adṛṣṭakalpanā yuktā na ca dṛṣṭasya saṃbhave /
[kks_148] tasmādyathā prokṣaṇādividhervrīhiṣu gamyate
units.translation: It is reasonable to posit an unseen result when no directly visible result can account for it. Thus, from an injunction such as “He sprinkles the rice grains,” one understands…

gloss.en: the positing of an unseen result
from an injunction to sprinkle and the like

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 165
units.deva: अदृष्टा संस्कृतिर्ज्ञानविधे रूपं तथात्मनः । यथा अवघातप्रोक्षणादयः स्वरूपेणैव द्रव्यार्थाः, द्वितीयया च द्रव्यस्य कर्मत्वेन निर्देशात्, तथा ज्ञानमपि स्वरूपेण परार्थम् । कर्मत्वेन चात्मनो निर्देशात्तदर्थम् । अतो ज्ञानविषयो ऽपि विधिरात्मरूपं संस्पृशति, न ज्ञानमात्रे पर्यवस्यति, ज्ञानस्यात्मरूपार्थत्वेन कर्तव्यतावगमाज्ज्ञाननियोगेनैवात्मरूपस्याक्षेपात् । स्यादेतत् --- भवतु ज्ञानस्यात्मार्थताभिप्रेता । अपहतपाप्मादिरूपात्मप्रतीतौ तु प्रमाणं वाच्यम् । शब्दस्तावदेवंविधात्मज्ञानकर्तव्यतायां पर्यवसितः --- ‘एवंविधात्मोद्देशेन ज्ञानं कुर्यात्ऽ; न तु ‘एवंविध आत्माऽ; इति । तत्रोच्यते --- न हि तत्राकिञ्चित्करस्य तादर्थ्येन कर्तव्यता युज्यते । ज्ञानस्य च कर्मणि नान्यत्फलं तद्रूपसंवित्तेः, न हि तस्यां दृष्टायामन्यस्यादृष्टस्य कल्पना । तत्र यथा ‘व्रीहीन् प्रोक्षतिऽइति प्रोक्षणविधेरेव व्रीहिष्वदृष्टसंस्कारावगमः प्रोक्षणविषयादपि । नान्यथा व्रीह्यर्थे प्रोक्षणे कर्तव्यता युज्यते । न हि तत्र किञ्चिदकुर्वत्प्रोक्षणं तदर्थं कृतं स्यादित्येवं विधेरेवादृष्टसंस्कारसद्भावसिद्धिः, यथा ‘स्वर्गकामो यजेतऽ; इति । नान्यथा स्वर्गकामस्य यागकर्तव्यताप्रतीतिर्युज्यते यदि न स्वर्गोपायो यागः । अनुपाये चेन्नियुज्यते, न स्वर्गकामो नियुक्तो भवति । अनुष्ठितो ऽपि न स्वर्गकामेनानुष्ठितो भवतीति क्रियाविषयादपि विधेः साध्यसाधनभावावगमः शाब्दः --- तथा ज्ञानविषयादपि विधेरात्मरूपबोधः । न हि तद्विधमात्मानमुद्दिश्यज्ञाननियोगो युज्यते, अतद्विधश्चेदात्मा तेन ज्ञानेन प्रतीयत इति । उक्तोत्तरमिदं यस्मादरूपेणापि भासकम्
units.iast:
adṛṣṭā saṃskṛtirjñānavidhe rūpaṃ tathātmanaḥ /
yathā avaghātaprokṣaṇādayaḥ svarūpeṇaiva dravyārthāḥ, dvitīyayā ca dravyasya karmatvena nirdeśāt, tathā jñānamapi svarūpeṇa parārtham / karmatvena cātmano nirdeśāttadartham / ato jñānaviṣayo 'pi vidhirātmarūpaṃ saṃspṛśati, na jñānamātre paryavasyati, jñānasyātmarūpārthatvena kartavyatāvagamājjñānaniyogenaivātmarūpasyākṣepāt / syādetat --- bhavatu jñānasyātmārthatābhipretā / apahatapāpmādirūpātmapratītau tu pramāṇaṃ vācyam / śabdastāvadevaṃvidhātmajñānakartavyatāyāṃ paryavasitaḥ --- ‘evaṃvidhātmoddeśena jñānaṃ kuryāt'; na tu ‘evaṃvidha ātmā'; iti / tatrocyate --- na hi tatrākiñcitkarasya tādarthyena kartavyatā yujyate / jñānasya ca karmaṇi nānyatphalaṃ tadrūpasaṃvitteḥ, na hi tasyāṃ dṛṣṭāyāmanyasyādṛṣṭasya kalpanā / tatra yathā ‘vrīhīn prokṣati'iti prokṣaṇavidhereva vrīhiṣvadṛṣṭasaṃskārāvagamaḥ prokṣaṇaviṣayādapi / nānyathā vrīhyarthe prokṣaṇe kartavyatā yujyate / na hi tatra kiñcidakurvatprokṣaṇaṃ tadarthaṃ kṛtaṃ syādityevaṃ vidherevādṛṣṭasaṃskārasadbhāvasiddhiḥ, yathā ‘svargakāmo yajeta'; iti / nānyathā svargakāmasya yāgakartavyatāpratītiryujyate yadi na svargopāyo yāgaḥ / anupāye cenniyujyate, na svargakāmo niyukto bhavati / anuṣṭhito 'pi na svargakāmenānuṣṭhito bhavatīti kriyāviṣayādapi vidheḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvāvagamaḥ śābdaḥ --- tathā jñānaviṣayādapi vidherātmarūpabodhaḥ / na hi tadvidhamātmānamuddiśyajñānaniyogo yujyate, atadvidhaścedātmā tena jñānena pratīyata iti /
uktottaramidaṃ yasmādarūpeṇāpi bhāsakam
units.translation:
The unseen refinement produced by an injunction concerning knowledge is the nature of the Self. Just as acts such as pounding and sprinkling are directed toward a substance in their own right, while the second-case grammatical form marks the substance as the object of the action, so knowledge too is, in its own nature, for the sake of something else; and because the Self is designated as its object, knowledge is for the sake of the Self. Thus an injunction whose subject is knowledge also reaches the nature of the Self; it does not end with cognition alone. Since knowledge is understood as serving the Self, its obligatoriness is apprehended, and through the injunction to know the Self’s nature is implied.

One might object: let it be intended that knowledge is for the sake of the Self. But what means of knowledge establishes the apprehension that the Self is free from evil and so forth? The words culminate only in a duty to produce knowledge of a Self of that kind: “One should produce knowledge directed toward a Self of this kind”; they do not say, “The Self is of this kind.”

We reply: it is not reasonable to enjoin an action as being for the sake of something that accomplishes nothing. And the only result of the act of knowing is awareness of the Self’s nature; once that is directly seen, one need not posit some other unseen result. Just as from the injunction “He sprinkles the rice grains,” one understands an unseen refinement of the rice from the injunction to sprinkle, even though the rice is the object of the sprinkling, so an obligation to know something for the sake of the Self is reasonable only if the injunction itself establishes an unseen refinement of the Self. Sprinkling that accomplishes nothing for the rice could not be performed for its sake. Likewise, from the injunction “One who desires heaven should sacrifice,” one understands that sacrifice is a means to heaven; otherwise it would not be reasonable to enjoin sacrifice for someone who desires heaven. If an act were enjoined without being a means to that end, the person desiring heaven would not truly be enjoined to perform it, and even if performed, it would not have been performed by one who desires heaven. Thus, from an injunction whose subject is an action, scripture teaches the relation between means and end. In the same way, from an injunction whose subject is knowledge, it teaches the apprehension of the Self’s nature. It would not be reasonable to enjoin knowledge directed toward a Self that had no such nature; and if the Self lacked that nature, it could not be apprehended through that knowledge. This objection has already been answered, since the words can illuminate even without presenting a form.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 166
units.deva: ज्ञानं प्रदर्शितं न स्यादन्यथा तद्विधेः फलम् । लयो निवर्त्यो न तथा विक्षेपो हि यथासुखः
units.iast:
jñānaṃ pradarśitaṃ na syādanyathā tadvidheḥ phalam /
layo nivartyo na tathā vikṣepo hi yathāsukhaḥ
units.translation: Otherwise, the result of that injunction would not have been demonstrated. Absorption must be overcome; distraction, however, is as pleasurable as one wishes.

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 167
units.deva: [क्क्स्_149] लयविक्षेपभेदश्च न स्यादग्रहमात्रके । नन्वरूपावभासे स्याददृष्टफलकल्पना
units.iast:
[kks_149] layavikṣepabhedaśca na syādagrahamātrake /
nanvarūpāvabhāse syādadṛṣṭaphalakalpanā
units.translation: If there were merely non-apprehension, there would be no distinction between absorption and distraction. One might object that when no form appears, an unseen result should be posited.

gloss.en: the distinction between absorption and distraction
the positing of an unseen result

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 168
units.deva: रूपावभासे दृष्टं तु फलं तत्सिद्धिलक्षणम् । न दृष्टमात्राद् दृष्टार्थं पुरुषार्थानुगं तु तत्
units.iast:
rūpāvabhāse dṛṣṭaṃ tu phalaṃ tatsiddhilakṣaṇam /
na dṛṣṭamātrād dṛṣṭārthaṃ puruṣārthānugaṃ tu tat
units.translation: A directly visible result is observed in the appearance of a form; that is the mark by which it is established. But not everything directly seen serves a human purpose; it is that [result] which does.

gloss.en: is the mark of its establishment

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 169
units.deva: न भिद्यते च तद्भावो रूपारूपावभासयोः । यथा प्रपञ्चशून्यत्वे तत्त्वे ज्ञानावभासिते
units.iast:
na bhidyate ca tadbhāvo rūpārūpāvabhāsayoḥ /
yathā prapañcaśūnyatve tattve jñānāvabhāsite
units.translation: Its nature does not differ between an appearance with form and one without form, as when truth is illumined by cognition in which the manifold world is absent.

gloss.en: between appearances with and without form

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 170
units.deva: दुःखकर्मक्लेशहानमतत्त्वे ऽपि तथा भवेत् । एतच्चात्र भवेद्युक्तं प्रत्यक्षाद्यविरोधतः
units.iast:
duḥkhakarmakleśahānamatattve 'pi tathā bhavet /
etaccātra bhavedyuktaṃ pratyakṣādyavirodhataḥ
units.translation: The destruction of suffering, action, and affliction would occur even without knowing the truth. This is reasonable here, since it does not conflict with perception and the other means of knowledge.

gloss.en: the ending of suffering, action, and affliction
because it does not conflict with perception and the other means of knowledge

units.sectionTitle: Kāṇḍa 2 · Niyoga — whether Vedānta knowledge depends on injunction
units.label: Kāṇḍa 2 · 171
units.deva:
अनौपचारिकार्थाश्च स्युः कर्मविषयो यतः । आत्मार्थज्ञानविधेरेतावद्गम्यते --- ज्ञानेन सो ऽवभास्यते, आलम्ब्यते, व्यवहारयोग्यतामापद्यते । तच्चावभासनं स्वरूपेण च दृष्टम्, पररूपेण च । रजतात्मना शुक्तिकायाः । प्रतिपादितमेतत् --- नाग्रहमात्रमेतत्, अन्यथाख्यातिस्तु । तत्रोभयथा संभवे कुत एतत् --- तत्त्वप्रतिपत्तिरवश्याभ्युपेया, नातस्मिंस्तत्ख्यातिः? अन्यथा नात्मज्ञानविधिः फलवान् स्यात् । स खल्वनात्मरूपप्रविलयार्थः । अनात्मरूपविलयेन हि वस्तुनो ऽवगतिर्दृष्टेति । यदि च नात्मनो नामरूपप्रपञ्चरूपेण प्रकाशनम्, किं प्रविलाप्येत? अथ मतम् --- द्विप्रकारेयमविद्या, प्रकाशस्याच्छादिका विक्षेपिका च । स्वप्नजागरितयोर्विक्षेपिका, सुषुप्त आच्छादिका लयलक्षणा । तत्राच्छादकाविद्यानिवृत्तिर्ज्ञानविधेः फलम् । तच्चासत् । यतो नाच्छादिकाया अविद्याया निवृत्तिः पुरुषेणार्थ्यते तथा यथा विक्षेपस्य । स हि विविधदुःखात्मकः । लयस्तु विविधदुःखनिवृत्तेरसकृदानन्दत्वेन श्रुतौ गीतः प्रत्युतार्थनीयः स्यात् । अपि च विपर्यासमनिच्छतो ऽविद्याभेद एव न स्यात्, अवस्थात्रये ऽप्यग्रहणमात्रत्वात् । तस्मादग्रहणविपर्ययग्रहणे द्वे अविद्ये कार्यकारणभावेनावस्थिते । [क्क्स्_150] स्वप्नजागरितयोरुभे, कारणभूताग्रहणलक्षणा सुषुप्त इत्यविद्याप्रविभाग उपपद्यते । तदुक्तम् ---

कार्यकारणबद्धौ ताविष्येते विश्वतैजसौ । प्राज्ञः कारणबद्धस्तु द्वौ तु तुर्ये न सिध्यतःऽ; ॥ नन्वन्यथायं भेदः --- अग्रहणसम्यग्ग्रहणाभ्याम् । अग्रहणलक्षणाच्छादिका सुषुप्ते, असम्यग्ग्रहणमितरयोः । तथा हि --- अभिन्नस्य वस्तुनो ऽप्रदेशस्य ग्रहणे तथाभावस्य चाग्रहणात्पृथक्त्वेन प्रत्यवभासः । नैतत्सारम् । यदि तावदसम्यग्ग्रहणमात्रं तदपटुत्वं वा ज्ञानस्य केनचिद्द्रूपेण वा ग्रहणम्, न सर्वात्मना । तत्र दूरस्थे सूक्ष्मे च भवत्यपटु ज्ञानं सामान्यज्ञानम् । न च तदविद्या । न च किञ्चिज्ज्ञानं सर्वात्मनार्थस्य ग्राहकमिति सर्वज्ञानमिथ्यात्वापातः । अभेदस्याग्रहणे ऽपि भेदस्यावर्तने ऽपि भेदस्यासंवित्तेर्न निवर्तनीयमस्ति विद्यया । न खल्वभेदाग्रहणं निवर्तनीयम् । न हि तत्किञ्चिदपराध्यति । भेदस्तु विविधदुःखायतनम् । अथासम्यग्ग्रहणं पृथक्प्रत्यवभासो ऽपृथगात्मनः, अभ्युपेता तर्हि विपर्ययख्यातिः --- अपृथक् पृथक् प्रकाशत इति । अथोच्येत --- न ब्रूमः पृथक् प्रकाशते, किं तु पृथगिव प्रकाशत इति । क इवार्थः? यदि यथा पृथग्भूतमप्रकाशमानैकत्वं प्रकाशते तथैकमप्यात्मतत्त्वमगृह्यमाणैकत्वं प्रकाशत इति । केनचिदंशेन ग्रहणं सर्वात्मना चाग्रहणमुक्तं भवति, तत्र चोक्तम् । अथ प्रकाशत इव, न तु प्रकाशते । प्रकाशने क उपमार्थः? तन्निबन्धनव्यवहारप्रवृत्तिः । तन्निबन्धनश्चेद्व्यवहारः । प्राप्तं प्रकाशनम् --- नासति कारणे कार्यं भवतीति । अथाभेदाग्रह एव पृथक्त्वग्रहाभिमानः । तदसत्, अग्रहणस्याभावस्य स्वरूपेण पररूपेण वा ग्रहणानभ्युपगमात् । अप्रकाशमाने च पृथक्त्वे कुतस्तदवग्रहः? अभिन्ने च भेदाभिमानं परित्यज्याभेदाग्रहणे भेदग्रहाभिमानमूरीकुर्वता किं परिहृतं स्यात्? तस्मात्सुष्ठूच्यते --- ‘लयविक्षेपभेदश्च न स्यादग्रहमात्रकेऽ; इति । [क्क्स्_151] नन्वनात्मरूपेण प्रतिपत्तेर्न दृश्यते किञ्चित्फलम् । तत्रादृष्टकल्पना स्यात् । आत्मरूपप्रतिपत्तेस्तु दृष्टं फलं तत्स्वरूपसिद्धिः । उच्यते --- न यस्य कस्यचिद्दर्शनाद् दृष्टार्थता, किं तु पुरुषार्थसंस्पर्शिनः । तेन हि तद्विधिर्निराकाङ्क्षा भवति । न च पुरुषार्र्हभेदस्तत्त्वातत्त्वप्रतिपत्त्योः । यथा हि विशुद्धमद्वैतमात्मानं प्रतिपद्यमानस्तथाभूतो न शोकेन संस्पृश्यते, शोचनीयाभावात् । न कर्माशयमुपचिनोति, कर्तव्याभावात् । न क्वचिद्द्रज्यति किञ्चिद् द्वेष्टि वा, विषयाभावात् । ‘एवं जीवन्नेव विद्वान्विमुक्तो भवति । तथा अतथाभूतमपि तथाभावनापुरःसरं साक्षादिव प्रतिपद्यमानः । अभूतो ऽप्यर्थः परिभावनातिशयाद्भूतव्यवहारहेतुर्भवति । इदमेव चात्र युज्यते, प्रत्यक्षादीनामविरोधात्, कर्मविधीनां च भूतार्थत्वात् । परमार्थे हि प्रपञ्चशून्यत्वे प्रत्यक्षादीनि प्रमाणानि बाध्येरन् । कर्मविधयश्चाभूतकल्पनोपादानव्यवहारसिद्धार्थगोचराः स्युः । तस्मादपरमार्थेनैवाद्वैतात्मज्ञानविधिर्युज्यते । जानातिस्तत्त्वबोधे चेन्न मिथ्यादिविशेषणात्
units.iast:
anaupacārikārthāśca syuḥ karmaviṣayo yataḥ /
ātmārthajñānavidheretāvadgamyate --- jñānena so 'vabhāsyate, ālambyate, vyavahārayogyatāmāpadyate / taccāvabhāsanaṃ svarūpeṇa ca dṛṣṭam, pararūpeṇa ca / rajatātmanā śuktikāyāḥ / pratipāditametat --- nāgrahamātrametat, anyathākhyātistu / tatrobhayathā saṃbhave kuta etat --- tattvapratipattiravaśyābhyupeyā, nātasmiṃstatkhyātiḥ? anyathā nātmajñānavidhiḥ phalavān syāt / sa khalvanātmarūpapravilayārthaḥ / anātmarūpavilayena hi vastuno 'vagatirdṛṣṭeti / yadi ca nātmano nāmarūpaprapañcarūpeṇa prakāśanam, kiṃ pravilāpyeta? atha matam --- dviprakāreyamavidyā, prakāśasyācchādikā vikṣepikā ca / svapnajāgaritayorvikṣepikā, suṣupta ācchādikā layalakṣaṇā / tatrācchādakāvidyānivṛttirjñānavidheḥ phalam / taccāsat / yato nācchādikāyā avidyāyā nivṛttiḥ puruṣeṇārthyate tathā yathā vikṣepasya / sa hi vividhaduḥkhātmakaḥ / layastu vividhaduḥkhanivṛtterasakṛdānandatvena śrutau gītaḥ pratyutārthanīyaḥ syāt / api ca viparyāsamanicchato 'vidyābheda eva na syāt, avasthātraye 'pyagrahaṇamātratvāt / tasmādagrahaṇaviparyayagrahaṇe dve avidye kāryakāraṇabhāvenāvasthite / [kks_150] svapnajāgaritayorubhe, kāraṇabhūtāgrahaṇalakṣaṇā suṣupta ityavidyāpravibhāga upapadyate / taduktam ---

kāryakāraṇabaddhau tāviṣyete viśvataijasau /
prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhastu dvau tu turye na sidhyataḥ'; //
